In the famous collection by al-Hariri, written around 1100, each episode follows the same pattern: a narrator arrives in a new city, meets a clever wanderer named Abu Zayd, and watches him trick a crowd out of money with a dazzling speech. Each episode ends with Abu Zayd leaving town, and the next one begins somewhere else. Because no episode depends on events from an earlier one, a reader of al-Hariri's collection ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: would need to read the episodes in their original order to follow Abu Zayd's story.
would find that Abu Zayd's speeches grow longer as the collection goes on.
would discover that the narrator and Abu Zayd become close friends by the final episode.
could begin with almost any episode and still understand what happens in it.
g.explanation: 지문은 어떤 에피소드도 이전 에피소드의 사건에 의존하지 않는다고 분명히 말하므로, 독자는 아무 에피소드부터 읽어도 이해할 수 있다는 D가 정답이다. A는 순서대로 읽어야 한다고 하여 '서로 독립적'이라는 단서와 정반대이다. B는 연설 길이의 변화를 말하지만 지문에는 그런 정보가 없다. C는 에피소드를 넘나드는 관계의 발전을 가정하는데, 이는 각 에피소드가 독립적이라는 진술과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The passage states that no episode depends on events from an earlier one, so a reader could start with almost any episode and still follow it, which is choice D. Choice A says the episodes must be read in order, which is the opposite of what the passage says about their independence. Choice B talks about speeches getting longer, but the passage gives no information about that. Choice C assumes a relationship that builds across episodes, which doesn't fit the claim that each episode stands on its own.
g.design: 이 문항은 '이전 에피소드에 의존하지 않는다'는 명시적 단서 하나에서 한 단계만 추론하면 풀리도록 easy 수준으로 설계했다. 오답은 모두 같은 'would…' 문장 틀을 쓰며, 연재 서사를 떠올리게 하는 전형적인 오개념으로 구성했다.

g.passage: In Edo-period Japan, ukiyo-e prints such as Utagawa Hiroshige's landscape series were made through a division of labor. An artist drew the design, a carver cut it into blocks of cherry wood, and a printer pressed paper onto the inked blocks one color at a time. Because a single set of carved blocks could be inked and printed again and again, a publisher could produce thousands of copies of one design without asking the artist to redraw it. This method helps explain why Hiroshige's prints sold for roughly the price of a bowl of noodles: since the costly work of designing and carving was done only once for each image, ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the expense of making each additional copy remained low.
the expense of hiring skilled carvers rose with every copy printed.
the expense of the prints depended mainly on how famous the artist was.
the expense of cherry wood made each print costlier than a painting.
g.explanation: 지문은 디자인과 조각처럼 비용이 큰 작업이 이미지마다 한 번만 이루어지고, 같은 목판으로 계속 인쇄할 수 있었다고 말한다. 따라서 추가로 찍는 한 장의 비용은 낮았고, 이것이 싼 가격을 설명하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 조각이 한 번만 이루어진다는 내용과 모순된다. C는 지문이 제시한 제작 방식과 무관한 설명이고, D는 판화가 싸게 팔렸다는 사실과 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the costly design and carving work happened only once per image, and the same blocks could be printed again and again. So each extra copy cost little to make, which explains the low price. That makes A correct. B contradicts the point that carving happened only once. C brings in the artist's fame, which has nothing to do with the production method the passage describes. D contradicts the fact that the prints were cheap.
g.design: 한 단계 추론(일회성 고정비 → 추가 사본 비용 낮음)으로 풀리게 했다. 오답은 모두 같은 'the expense of...' 틀을 쓰고, 흔히 하는 오해를 담았다.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 주장과 이유를, 텍스트 2는 같은 주제의 다른 접근을 각각 짧게 제시하되 서로를 언급하지 않게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자라면 텍스트 1의 주장에 어떻게 반응할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 2의 전제에서만 도출되는 반응으로 만들고, 오답 3개는 텍스트 1의 내용을 반복하는 선택지, 텍스트 2의 결론만 되풀이하는 선택지, 텍스트 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점을 끌어온 선택지로 만든다.
c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Phonetic alphabet and Phoenician writing system alphabetic innovation syllabic simplification historical linguistics

g.passage:
Text 1
Many historians credit the Phoenicians with the decisive step toward the alphabet. By reducing the hundreds of signs used in Egyptian and Mesopotamian scripts to roughly twenty-two consonant symbols, Phoenician scribes made writing far easier to learn. On this view, the alphabet's essential innovation was sheer simplification: fewer signs meant that literacy could spread beyond a narrow class of trained specialists.

Text 2
Some linguists argue that the number of signs in a script tells us little about what makes it alphabetic. Several syllabaries, such as the one later devised for Cherokee, use a modest inventory of symbols, yet each symbol still stands for a whole syllable. What distinguishes a true alphabet, these linguists contend, is the analytical principle of assigning separate symbols to individual consonants and vowels—a principle first applied systematically when Greek writers repurposed some Phoenician signs to represent vowels.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 about what made the Phoenician script innovative?
options: By agreeing that the Phoenicians' reduction of signs to about twenty-two was what allowed literacy to extend beyond trained specialists
By objecting that a small set of signs, by itself, does not make a script alphabetic, so Text 1 identifies the wrong feature as the alphabet's defining advance
By insisting that the true alphabet emerged only when Greek writers adapted Phoenician signs to stand for vowels
By questioning whether literacy actually spread more widely in Phoenician society than in Egypt or Mesopotamia
g.explanation: 정답 B: Text 2는 체로키 음절문자처럼 기호 수가 적어도 알파벳이 아닐 수 있다는 전제를 제시한다. 따라서 '기호 축소'를 핵심 혁신으로 보는 Text 1에 대해, 기호 수는 알파벳의 정의적 특징이 아니라고 반박할 것이다. A: Text 1의 내용을 반복할 뿐 Text 2의 관점과 맞지 않는다. C: Text 2의 결론(그리스의 모음 표기)을 되풀이할 뿐, Text 1의 '단순화' 주장이 왜 틀렸는지에 대한 반응이 되지 못한다. D: 실제 문해율 확산 여부는 Text 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점이다.
g.explanation_en: B is correct: Text 2 points out that syllabaries like Cherokee have small sign inventories yet aren't alphabets, so its author would reject Text 1's idea that reducing the number of signs was the alphabet's essential innovation. A just repeats Text 1's claim, which Text 2 undercuts. C restates Text 2's conclusion about Greek vowels but doesn't address the actual flaw in Text 1's reasoning, which is treating sign count as the defining feature. D brings in whether literacy really spread, an issue Text 2 never discusses.
g.design: Text 2 never mentions Phoenician simplification directly; the rebuttal must be inferred from its premise that small inventories don't make a script alphabetic. The distractors are a restatement of Text 1, a repetition of Text 2's conclusion only, and an issue neither text takes up.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 하나의 결론을 이끄는 주장을, 텍스트 2는 그 주장의 핵심 근거를 약하게 만들 수 있는 별개의 관찰이나 연구를 제시한다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자가 텍스트 1의 어느 부분에 가장 이의를 제기할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 1의 결론이 아니라 그 결론이 기대는 가정으로 하고, 오답 3개는 결론 자체, 텍스트 1의 부수적 세부, 텍스트 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분으로 만든다.
c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Scholiast marginal commentary and classical text annotation medieval Byzantine scholarly interpretation manuscript tradition

g.passage:
Text 1
Byzantine scholia, the marginal notes that surround many medieval manuscripts of Homer and Sophocles, have long been prized as windows into lost ancient criticism. Some historians argue that the scholia's value as evidence lies chiefly in their consistency: because the same explanatory note often appears, nearly word for word, in manuscripts copied in different centuries and monasteries, the note must descend from a single authoritative ancient commentary. On this view, a note's wide distribution is itself evidence of its antiquity, and scholars can reconstruct Hellenistic scholarship simply by collecting the scholia that recur most often.

Text 2
A recent study of twelfth-century manuscripts from Constantinople complicates this picture. Examining ownership marks and handwriting, researchers found that a small circle of teachers lent their annotated copies widely, and students routinely transcribed those teachers' own marginal remarks into new books. Several notes that appear in dozens of later manuscripts can be traced to one twelfth-century schoolmaster, not to any ancient source. The study's authors do not dispute that some scholia preserve genuine Hellenistic material, but they caution that classroom copying could spread a medieval comment just as efficiently as an ancient one.
g.question: Based on the texts, which element of the reasoning described in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely challenge?
options: The conclusion that Byzantine scholia are worth studying as sources for ancient literary criticism
The observation that the scholia accompany medieval manuscripts of authors such as Homer and Sophocles
The premise that a note recurring across many manuscripts must have originated in a single ancient commentary
The claim that at least some scholia transmit material that originated in Hellenistic scholarship
g.explanation: 정답 C: Text 1의 결론(가장 자주 반복되는 주석으로 헬레니즘 학문을 재구성할 수 있다)은 '널리 퍼진 주석은 고대 단일 출처에서 왔다'는 가정에 기댄다. Text 2는 12세기 교사의 주석이 수업 필사를 통해 수십 개 사본에 퍼졌음을 보여 주어, 널리 퍼졌다는 사실이 고대성을 보장하지 않는다고 지적한다. 즉 결론이 아닌 그 가정을 공격한다. A: 결론 자체에 해당하는 넓은 주장이다. Text 2는 스콜리아의 가치를 부정하지 않으므로 이의를 제기하지 않는다. B: 지문의 부수적 세부일 뿐 논증의 핵심이 아니며, Text 2는 이에 대해 아무 말도 하지 않는다. D: Text 2의 저자들은 일부 스콜리아가 진짜 헬레니즘 자료를 보존한다는 점을 오히려 명시적으로 인정한다.
g.explanation_en: C is correct. Text 1's method (rebuilding Hellenistic scholarship from the notes that show up most often) depends on one assumption: if a note is widely shared, it must come from one ancient source. Text 2 shows that a twelfth-century schoolmaster's remarks spread to dozens of manuscripts through classroom copying. So a note being widespread doesn't prove it's ancient, and that undercuts the assumption, not the conclusion. A is wrong because it's the broad conclusion. Text 2 never says scholia are worthless as sources. B is wrong because it's a side detail that Text 2 doesn't address at all. D is wrong because Text 2's authors openly agree that some scholia preserve genuine Hellenistic material.
g.design: Text 1 reaches its conclusion through the hidden assumption that a widely spread note must be ancient. Text 2 gives a case where a medieval note spread just as widely. The correct answer targets that assumption. The wrong answers are the conclusion itself, a side detail, and a point Text 2 agrees with, and all four use the same "The ___ that..." sentence frame.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1의 저자가 좋은 설명이나 해결책의 기준(예: 재현 가능성, 단순성, 장기적 효과)을 분명히 드러내게 쓰고, 텍스트 2는 그 기준과 어긋날 수 있는 결론을 내리게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 1의 저자의 기준에서 텍스트 2의 결론을 어떻게 평가할 것인가'로 한다. 오답 3개는 텍스트 2 저자의 기준으로 평가한 결과, 두 저자의 기준을 섞은 평가, 일반 상식에 따른 평가로 만든다.
c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Kasuga mandala and Japanese religious art architectural painting Mount Kasuga deity representation devotional imagery

g.passage:
Text 1
Scholars often read Kasuga shrine mandalas, the medieval Japanese paintings that show the Kasuga Shrine compound beneath the slopes of Mount Kasuga, as straightforward topographic records. Art historian Mai Tanabe argues that any account of such images must be checked against how they were actually handled. In her view, an interpretation counts as persuasive only if it is backed by evidence of use, such as temple inventories, ritual manuals, or wear on the scrolls themselves, and not by visual resemblance alone.

Text 2
In many Kasuga mandalas, the deer, the shrine buildings, and the forested mountain are placed in a pattern that closely matches the arrangement of Buddhist deities in mandalas of the Esoteric Buddhist tradition. Given how strong this parallel is, one scholar concludes that the paintings were designed to make viewers see the landscape itself as a sacred body of buddhas. On this reading, they were made as objects of devotion, not as maps.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Tanabe (Text 1) most likely evaluate the conclusion reached by the scholar in Text 2?
options: She would find it convincing, since the close match between the painted landscape and the arrangement of Esoteric Buddhist deities is precisely the kind of pattern that shows what the paintings were meant to do.

She would find it partly convincing, since the visual parallel shows the paintings' devotional function, though their topographic accuracy would still need to be checked against the actual shrine site.
She would find it unconvincing, since medieval painters were generally trying to show real places accurately, which makes a devotional reading of these landscape scenes unlikely.
She would find it insufficiently supported, since the scholar infers what the paintings were for from their composition without pointing to any record of how they were kept or used.
g.explanation:
정답 D: Tanabe의 기준은 해석이 시각적 유사성만이 아니라 사용의 증거(사찰 목록, 의례 지침서, 두루마리의 마모)로 뒷받침되어야 한다는 것이다. Text 2의 학자는 구도의 유사성만으로 신앙 대상이라는 결론을 내리므로, Tanabe는 결론이 틀렸다고 단정하기보다 근거가 부족하다고 평가할 것이다.
A: Text 2 저자의 기준(시각적 패턴의 강한 일치)으로 평가한 것이다. Tanabe는 바로 이런 근거만으로는 부족하다고 본다.
B: 두 기준을 섞었다. 시각적 유사성으로 기능을 인정하면서 현장과의 지형 대조를 덧붙이는데, 지형 대조는 Tanabe가 요구하는 사용 증거가 아니다.
C: 일반 상식(중세 화가는 사실적 재현을 추구했다)에 기댄 평가로, 지문 어디에도 근거가 없다. Tanabe는 오히려 지형 기록으로 읽는 해석에도 비판적이다.
g.explanation_en:
D is correct. Tanabe's standard is that an interpretation is persuasive only when it rests on evidence of use, such as inventories, ritual manuals, or wear on the scrolls, and not on visual resemblance alone. The scholar in Text 2 draws a conclusion about the paintings' devotional purpose purely from how they are composed. So Tanabe wouldn't necessarily say the conclusion is false. She would say it lacks the kind of support she requires.
A judges the conclusion by Text 2's own standard, the strength of the visual parallel. That is exactly the kind of evidence Tanabe considers insufficient.
B mixes the two standards. It accepts the visual parallel as proof of function and then adds a check of the topography against the site. Comparing the painting to the site is still not evidence of how the paintings were used.
C relies on a general assumption that medieval painters aimed for accuracy, and nothing in either text supports it. Tanabe actually questions reading these paintings as topographic records in the first place.
g.design: Text 1에 '사용 증거' 기준을 명시하고 Text 2는 시각적 유사성만으로 결론을 내리게 했다. 오답은 각각 Text 2의 기준, 두 기준을 섞은 평가, 일반 상식에 따른 평가로 구성했다.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Rhetoric epideictic praise and Isocrates ancient Greek oratory formal ceremonial discourse philosophical tradition

g.passage:
Text 1
Many scholars treat epideictic speech, the ancient Greek oratory of praise performed at festivals and funerals, as mere decoration. In their view, these ceremonial speeches simply flattered famous people and taught listeners nothing of real importance.

Text 2
The Athenian teacher Isocrates used speeches of praise to shape his students' values. When he praised a leader's fairness or courage, he was showing young citizens which qualities deserved admiration and imitation. For Isocrates, ceremonial oratory was a serious tool for moral education.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the view of the scholars described in Text 1?
options: By arguing that the scholars overlook the way such speeches could teach listeners which virtues to value
By arguing that the scholars overlook the way such speeches were performed only at funerals rather than festivals
By arguing that the scholars overlook the way such speeches avoided praising any famous people
By arguing that the scholars overlook the way such speeches were valued mainly for their decorative style
g.explanation: Text 1의 학자들은 찬양 연설이 아무것도 가르치지 않는 장식에 불과하다고 본다. Text 2는 이소크라테스가 찬양 연설로 학생들에게 존경하고 본받을 덕목을 보여 주어 도덕 교육에 사용했다고 말하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Text 2가 연설 장소를 구분하지 않으므로 틀렸다. C는 Text 2에서 이소크라테스가 지도자를 칭찬했다고 하므로 맞지 않는다. D는 오히려 Text 1의 '장식' 관점에 동조하는 내용이라 Text 2의 반응이 될 수 없다.
g.explanation_en: The scholars in Text 1 say praise speeches were only decoration and taught nothing important. Text 2 says Isocrates used praise to show students which qualities deserved admiration and imitation, so it treats these speeches as moral education. That makes A correct. B is wrong because Text 2 never separates funerals from festivals. C contradicts Text 2, where Isocrates does praise a leader. D actually agrees with Text 1's "decoration" view, so it can't be how Text 2's author would push back.
g.design: Text 2가 Text 1의 주장을 직접 반박하므로, 한 단계만 추론하면 풀 수 있다. 오답들은 같은 문장 틀을 쓰지만 세부 내용을 잘못 읽었거나 Text 1의 입장을 그대로 되풀이한다.

g.passage:
Text 1
Many scholars describe tsukumogami, the household objects in Japanese folklore said to come alive after about a hundred years, as a product of ancient animism. On this view, the stories simply reflect a very old belief that spirits live in all things, including tools and utensils.

Text 2
Tsukumogami do not appear in the oldest Japanese writings. They show up mainly in picture scrolls and tales made centuries after the Heian period, often as comic figures. These stories seem less like ancient belief and more like later entertainment that warned people not to waste or carelessly throw away old objects.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the view of tsukumogami presented in Text 1?
options: By arguing that tsukumogami stories actually come from the very oldest Japanese writings
By suggesting that the stories are better explained as a later creation than as an ancient belief
By agreeing that tsukumogami stories mainly record an old belief that spirits live in all things
By claiming that tsukumogami stories were meant to encourage people to throw away old objects
g.explanation: Text 1은 츠쿠모가미를 고대 애니미즘의 산물로 보지만, Text 2는 이 이야기들이 가장 오래된 문헌에는 없고 훗날의 오락물에 가깝다고 말한다. 따라서 Text 2의 저자는 츠쿠모가미가 후대에 만들어졌다고 반박할 것이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 가장 오래된 문헌에 등장하지 않는다고 한 말과 정반대이다. C는 Text 2가 반대하는 Text 1의 입장을 그대로 반복한 것이다. D는 이야기가 오래된 물건을 버리지 말라고 경고했다는 Text 2의 내용을 거꾸로 뒤집었다.
g.explanation_en: Text 1 treats tsukumogami as a product of ancient animism, while Text 2 says the stories don't appear in the oldest writings and look more like later entertainment. So the author of Text 2 would push back by saying the stories were made later, which makes B correct. A contradicts Text 2's point that tsukumogami are missing from the oldest writings. C just repeats the Text 1 view that Text 2 disagrees with. D flips Text 2's claim around, because Text 2 says the stories warned people not to throw old objects away.
g.design: Text 2가 Text 1의 주장을 직접 반박하는 구조로 만들어 한 단계 추론만으로 풀리게 했다. 오답은 흔한 오개념(사실 왜곡, Text 1 입장 동조, 내용 뒤집기)으로 구성했다.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Sgraffito scratched decoration and Italian Renaissance earthenware ceramic surface technique decorative pottery production

g.passage: In sgraffito, a technique widely used by potters in fifteenth-century northern Italy, a reddish earthenware vessel was coated with a thin layer of pale slip (liquid clay), and the decorator then scratched designs through the slip to expose the darker body beneath. Because the slip dried quickly, the design had to be scratched in a single session, and lines could not be erased once cut. Art historian Lucia Ferrante has examined a group of sgraffito bowls from a workshop near Padua whose borders show nearly identical interlaced patterns, while the central figures—birds, coats of arms, profile portraits—vary widely in subject and quality. Ferrante notes that the borders show almost no hesitation marks or corrected strokes, whereas several central figures show doubled or abandoned lines. Given the constraints of the technique, these observations suggest that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the workshop's decorators preferred interlaced patterns to figural images because borders could be scratched more quickly than central figures could be.
the slip used on the bowls' central areas dried more slowly than the slip on the borders, which allowed decorators to revise the figures.
the borders were probably cut by practiced hands repeating a familiar design, while the figures were improvised individually and sometimes by less experienced decorators.
the bowls with corrected central figures were probably made later than the others, after the workshop had stopped training its decorators in sgraffito.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Zeugma rhetorical device semantic word joining and multiple meaning simultaneity in classical Latin poetry compression

g.passage:
Text 1
Classical Latin poets prized zeugma, in which a single verb governs two objects in different senses, as in a line where a figure "lost her sandal and her composure." Many commentators argue that the device was chiefly ornamental: poets used it to display wit, and its function was to amuse a learned audience rather than to carry meaning that plainer phrasing could not.

Text 2
Latin verse was bound by strict metrical patterns, so every syllable had to earn its place. Zeugma let a poet make one verb do the work of two, joining a concrete and an abstract sense in a single slot. When Ovid has a character carry "arms and grief," the reader must hold both senses at once, and the pairing implies that the physical burden and the emotional one are inseparable—a claim that two separate verbs would weaken.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the commentators' view described in Text 1?
options: By arguing that the device served a purpose beyond displaying wit, since it conveyed a connection between ideas that separate phrasing would not convey as well
By arguing that the device served mainly to entertain educated readers, since metrical rules left poets little room for serious content
By arguing that the device served poets only as a way to fill out metrical lines, since its meaning could easily be restated in plainer terms
By arguing that the device served Ovid differently than it served other poets, since he alone paired concrete and abstract senses
g.explanation: Text 1의 논평가들은 zeugma가 재치를 보여 주는 장식일 뿐이고 평이한 표현이 전달하지 못하는 의미는 없다고 본다. Text 2는 zeugma가 운율 제약 속에서 두 의미를 동시에 담아, 별개의 동사로 쓰면 약해질 '육체적 짐과 감정적 짐의 불가분성'을 표현한다고 말하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Text 1의 입장을 그대로 따르는 것이라 Text 2와 맞지 않는다. C는 운율 언급은 맞지만 평이하게 바꿔 말할 수 있다는 부분이 Text 2의 주장과 정반대다. D는 Ovid 예시만 들었을 뿐 Ovid만 그렇게 했다는 주장은 Text 2에 없다.
g.explanation_en: In Text 1, the commentators treat zeugma as ornament: it shows off wit but carries no meaning that plainer wording couldn't. Text 2 argues that zeugma packs two senses into a single metrical slot and suggests a connection, here that physical and emotional burdens can't be separated, which two separate verbs would weaken. That makes A the answer. B simply repeats Text 1's view, so it doesn't fit the author of Text 2. C gets the meter part right but claims the meaning could easily be restated, which is the opposite of what Text 2 says. D overreaches: Text 2 uses Ovid as one example and never says only Ovid paired concrete and abstract senses.
g.design: To answer, you have to link Text 1's claim that zeugma adds no meaning to Text 2's example about inseparable burdens. The wrong options reuse true details from the passage, like meter and Ovid, so a quick skim makes them tempting.

g.passage:
Text 1
Scholars have long described the pre-Islamic qasida as following a fixed three-part sequence: the nasib, in which the poet mourns at the abandoned campsite of a beloved; the rahil, a desert journey on camelback; and a closing section of tribal boast or praise. Because nearly every surviving ode from the Jahiliyya period seems to move through these stages, many critics conclude that poets composed by filling in an inherited template, and that the form's single rhyme, sustained across dozens of lines, served mainly to hold these loosely joined parts together.

Text 2
The tidy three-part outline of the qasida owes more to later Abbasid-era critics, especially Ibn Qutayba in the ninth century, than to the poems themselves. Many early odes skip the journey entirely, reverse the order of sections, or linger on one theme for most of their length. What does run through every one of them is the monorhyme, and poets plainly used it with care: a rhyme chosen in the opening line constrained every later word choice, so audiences heard each new section as an answer to the first. The unity of these poems, in other words, was built line by line rather than borrowed from a plan.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the critics' conclusion described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that poets relied on an inherited template but arguing that the monorhyme mattered more to audiences than the template did
By arguing that the critics depend on a scheme imposed after the fact and underrate the monorhyme as a deliberate means of making a poem cohere
By arguing that the critics overstate the role of the monorhyme, since later scholars such as Ibn Qutayba showed that the three sections were what unified each ode
By agreeing that the sections of most odes were loosely joined but arguing that this looseness reflects the influence of Abbasid-era revisions to the poems
g.explanation: Text 2는 세 부분 구조가 후대 아바스 시대 비평가들이 만들어 낸 틀이라고 보며, 모노라임이 단순히 부분들을 묶어 두는 장치가 아니라 시를 한 줄씩 통일하는 의도적 기법이었다고 주장한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 모노라임 강조는 맞지만, Text 2는 틀을 물려받았다는 주장 자체를 부정한다. C는 Ibn Qutayba를 언급하지만 Text 2의 논지를 뒤집는다. D는 '느슨하게 연결되었다'는 점과 아바스 시대 개정 모두 Text 2가 주장하지 않는 내용이다.
g.explanation_en: Text 2 treats the three-part outline as a scheme later Abbasid critics laid over the poems. It also says the monorhyme was not just glue for loosely joined parts but a careful way of building unity line by line, so B is correct. A gets the emphasis on the monorhyme right, but Text 2 rejects the idea that poets used an inherited template at all. C mentions Ibn Qutayba but flips Text 2's argument, since Text 2 says his outline doesn't fit the poems. D is wrong because Text 2 never agrees that the sections were loosely joined, and it describes critics, not revisions to the poems themselves.
g.design: To answer, students must link two claims in Text 2: the template came from later critics, and the monorhyme was used on purpose. A and C each reuse one real detail from the texts but distort it, and D sounds plausible but is unsupported.

g.passage:
Text 1
Anglo-Saxon law codes such as those of King Æthelberht list precise payments, or wergeld, owed for killing or injuring a person, with sums scaled to the victim's social rank. Some historians read these tariffs as evidence that early English communities had largely replaced blood feud with orderly monetary settlement. On this view, the codes describe how disputes were actually resolved: a killing triggered a fixed payment, and the matter closed.

Text 2
Old English poetry complicates that picture. In Beowulf, the poet repeatedly shows wergeld being offered and accepted, yet the settlements rarely hold; the Finnsburg episode and the tale of Ingeld both depict compensation agreements collapsing into renewed violence once old grievances are stirred. Such scenes suggest that audiences understood payment as a fragile truce rather than a final resolution, and that the tidy tariffs of the codes record an ideal more than a routine practice.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the historians' view described in Text 1?
options: By arguing that the law codes' payment schedules were invented by later scribes and did not exist in early English communities
By agreeing that the codes reflect actual practice, since Beowulf shows wergeld being offered and accepted on many occasions
By suggesting that the codes may present an aspiration toward settlement rather than an accurate account of how conflicts typically ended
By contending that the poetry shows payments were scaled to the victim's rank even more strictly than the codes indicate
g.explanation: Text 1의 역사가들은 법전의 배상 규정이 실제 분쟁 해결 방식을 기술한다고 본다. Text 2는 Beowulf에서 배상이 받아들여져도 다시 폭력으로 무너지는 장면을 들어, 법전이 일상적 관행보다 이상을 기록한다고 주장하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 법전의 존재 자체를 부정하지 않으므로 지나치다. B는 배상이 제안·수용된다는 부분적 사실만 취하고 그 합의가 지켜지지 않았다는 핵심을 놓쳤다. D는 신분에 따른 액수 차이를 언급하지만 Text 2는 이를 논하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The historians in Text 1 treat the law codes as a description of how disputes were actually settled. Text 2 points to scenes in Beowulf where compensation is accepted but then breaks down into renewed violence, and it concludes that the codes record an ideal more than routine practice, so C is correct. A goes too far, because Text 2 never says the codes were invented or didn't exist. B picks up the true detail that wergeld is offered and accepted in the poem, but it ignores Text 2's main point that these settlements fall apart. D brings in rank-based payment amounts, which Text 2 never discusses.
g.design: To answer, students must connect Text 1's claim that the codes show actual practice with Text 2's claim that they record an ideal. B and D reuse true details from the texts to trap students who skim, and A is an overstatement that still sounds plausible.

g.passage:
Text 1
Art historians often treat the mudras of Buddhist sculpture as a fixed visual vocabulary. The earth-touching gesture, in which the Buddha's right hand reaches toward the ground, is read as a direct citation of a single scriptural moment: his calling the earth to witness his enlightenment. On this view, a sculptor's task was simply to transcribe a meaning already settled in Sanskrit texts, and any viewer who knew the texts could decode the gesture exactly.

Text 2
Surviving temple records from medieval Bengal complicate this picture. Workshop manuals there list gestures alongside regional ritual instructions that appear in no canonical Sanskrit source, and the same earth-touching pose is labeled differently in different monasteries. Some patrons commissioned it to signal protection from floods rather than enlightenment. Texts certainly supplied a core meaning, but local practice continually layered new significance onto the hands.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the view of sculptors described in Text 1?
options: By arguing that Sanskrit texts had no real influence on how gestures such as the earth-touching pose were understood
By agreeing that viewers familiar with scripture could decode gestures exactly, since workshop manuals preserved canonical meanings
By claiming that the earth-touching gesture originally signified protection from floods and was only later linked to enlightenment
By suggesting that the view overlooks how regional settings added meanings to gestures beyond those fixed in scripture

A는 Text 2가 "Texts certainly supplied a core meaning"이라고 인정한 점과 모순된다. B는 매뉴얼에 정전에 없는 지시가 있다는 Text 2의 내용과 반대된다. C는 홍수 보호 의미가 원래 의미였다고 하지만, Text 2는 그것을 나중에 덧붙여진 지역적 의미로 제시할 뿐 기원을 주장하지 않는다.

B is wrong because the second sentence isn't an example of indirect phrasing; it describes the opposite approach. C is wrong because using indirect phrasing doesn't cause other negotiators to prefer directness. D is wrong because the two behaviors aren't similar; they're opposite.

g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 노동계층 아이들이 많은 것을 생략하는 '제한 코드'를 쓴다고 하고, 뒤 문장은 중산층 아이들이 의미를 모두 풀어 말하는 '정교 코드'를 쓴다고 한다. 서로 다른 두 집단의 반대되는 언어 습관을 나란히 놓으므로 대조를 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 사례일 때 쓰지만, 중산층 아이들은 노동계층 아이들의 예가 아니다. C는 인과 관계를 나타내지만, 한 집단의 말투가 다른 집단의 말투를 일으키지 않는다. D는 같은 방향의 정보를 더할 때 쓰므로 반대되는 내용에는 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence says working-class children used a "restricted code" that leaves much unsaid. The next sentence says middle-class children used an "elaborated code" that spells meanings out in full. These two groups have opposite speech habits, so the transition has to show contrast, and that makes B correct. A doesn't work because the middle-class children are not an example of the working-class children's speech. C doesn't work because one group's way of talking did not cause the other group's. D is for adding similar information, so it can't link two opposite ideas.

She found that airlines trained attendants to stay cheerful and calm with every passenger, even rude ones, and to keep smiling for hours at a time. ______ many attendants told Hochschild that they began to feel cut off from their own real emotions, both at work and at home.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 승무원들이 몇 시간씩 억지로 밝은 감정을 유지하도록 훈련받았다는 원인을 제시하고, 뒤 문장은 그 때문에 자신의 진짜 감정과 단절된 느낌을 받았다는 결과를 말한다. 따라서 결과를 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 앞 내용의 구체적 사례를 들 때 쓰는데, 뒤 문장은 훈련의 사례가 아니라 그 영향이다. B는 대조를 나타내지만 두 문장은 서로 반대되지 않는다. D는 비슷한 내용을 하나 더 덧붙일 때 쓰지만, 뒤 문장은 비슷한 사실이 아니라 결과이다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentences describe a cause: attendants were trained to stay cheerful for hours, even with rude passengers. The last sentence describes what happened because of this training: the attendants felt cut off from their real emotions. Since that is a cause-and-effect relationship, C is correct. A introduces a specific instance, but the last sentence is an effect of the training, not an example of it. B signals contrast, and the two ideas don't oppose each other. D adds a parallel point, but the last sentence is a consequence, not a similar fact.
g.design: 원인(감정 유지 훈련)→결과(감정 단절)가 명확한 한 단계 관계로 만들고, 오답은 예시·대조·유사 관계의 전환어로 구성했다.

g.passage: In the 1980s, psychologist Sherry Turkle interviewed children who played with early electronic toys and computers. She found that the children did not treat these machines as simple objects like blocks or balls. Instead, many children ______ the devices with feelings and intentions, saying that a game "wanted" to win or that a toy could be "sad" when it was switched off.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 아이들이 기기가 무언가를 "원한다"거나 "슬플" 수 있다고 말했다고 하므로, 아이들이 기기에 감정과 의도가 있다고 여겼다는 뜻의 단어가 필요하다. D의 credited는 "credit A with B" 구조로 'A에 B가 있다고 여기다'라는 뜻이어서 정답이다. A의 repaired(수리했다)는 감정을 부여하는 것과 관련이 없다. B의 compared는 비교를 뜻할 뿐, 기기에 감정이 있다고 믿었다는 뜻을 전달하지 못한다. C의 replaced(교체했다)는 지문 내용과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the children claimed a game "wanted" to win or a toy could be "sad," so the blank needs a word meaning the children thought the devices had feelings and intentions. Choice D, "credited," fits the pattern "credit A with B," which means to believe that A has B, so D is the best answer. Choice A, "repaired," means fixed and has nothing to do with giving the devices feelings. Choice B, "compared," only means looking at similarities and doesn't say the children believed the devices had feelings. Choice C, "replaced," doesn't match what the passage describes.
g.design: 단서(“wanted”, “sad”)가 빈칸 바로 뒤에 직접 제시되어 한 단계 추론으로 credit A with B를 고르게 했고, 오답은 같은 동사 과거형 틀로 구성했다.

g.passage: In his 1975 book Discipline and Punish, philosopher Michel Foucault examined the panopticon, a prison design in which a central tower allows a guard to watch every cell. Because prisoners cannot see into the tower, they never know whether they are being watched at a given moment. Foucault argued that this uncertainty leads prisoners to ______ their own behavior: acting as though a guard is always present, they follow the rules even when no one is actually looking.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 빈칸 뒤 콜론 다음 내용이 단서이다. 수감자들은 감시자가 늘 있는 것처럼 행동하며 아무도 보지 않을 때도 규칙을 지킨다고 했으므로, 스스로 행동을 '통제한다'는 뜻의 A가 정답이다. B(버리다)는 행동을 그만둔다는 뜻이라 규칙을 지킨다는 내용과 맞지 않는다. C(과장하다)는 행동을 부풀린다는 뜻이라 규칙 준수라는 단서와 관련이 없다. D(잊다)는 자기 행동에 신경 쓰지 않는다는 뜻이 되어, 늘 감시를 의식한다는 설명과 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: The clue comes after the colon: the prisoners act as though a guard is always present and follow the rules even when no one is watching. That means they control their own behavior, so A is correct. B means to give up the behavior entirely, which doesn't fit with prisoners carefully following rules. C means to make the behavior bigger or more extreme, and nothing in the text suggests that. D would mean the prisoners stop paying attention to how they act, which is the opposite of always being aware they might be watched.
g.design: 콜론 뒤에 '스스로 규칙을 지킨다'는 직접 단서를 두어 한 단계 추론으로 regulate를 고르게 했다. 오답은 모두 '자기 행동에 무언가를 하는' 같은 문장 틀에 들어가는 동사로 구성했다.

In her turn-taking analyses, a speaker's overlapping comments ______ frequently meant as signs of enthusiastic support rather than as attempts to take control of the discussion.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 동사의 주어는 단수 소유격 "a speaker's"가 아니라 복수 명사 "comments"이다. 따라서 복수 동사가 필요하고, 지문 전체가 현재 시제(suggests, is)이므로 B "are"가 정답이다. A "is"는 단수 동사로, 바로 앞의 "speaker's"에 맞춘 오류이다. C "has been"과 D "was"도 모두 단수형이라 복수 주어 "comments"와 수가 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the verb in the blank is the plural noun "comments." It is not the singular possessive "a speaker's," which only describes the comments. A plural subject needs a plural verb, and the text uses the present tense ("suggests," "is"), so B, "are," is correct. A, "is," is singular, so it wrongly agrees with "speaker's." C, "has been," and D, "was," are also singular forms, so neither one agrees with the plural subject "comments."
g.design: This question tests one rule: subject-verb agreement. A short singular possessive ("a speaker's") comes right before the plural subject, and all three wrong answers are singular verbs that look correct next to that nearby singular word.

A student researcher hypothesizes that, consistent with Goffman's view, listeners are more likely to offer this kind of help when the speaker shows visible embarrassment than when the speaker shows none.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the student researcher's hypothesis?

In recorded conversations, speakers who appeared calm after a slip made just as many slips overall as speakers who blushed or stammered.
In recorded conversations, listeners made a joke or shifted the topic about equally often after slips, whether or not the speaker blushed or stammered.
In recorded conversations, speakers who blushed or stammered after a slip were more likely to apologize than speakers who appeared calm.
g.explanation: 가설은 화자가 당황한 모습을 보일 때 청자가 상황 수습을 더 자주 돕는다는 것이다. A는 당황한 화자 쪽에서 청자의 도움(농담, 화제 전환) 비율이 훨씬 높다고 보여 주므로 가설을 직접 뒷받침한다. B는 실수 횟수에 관한 것이고 청자의 반응은 다루지 않는다. C는 차이가 없다고 하므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다. D는 청자가 아니라 화자 자신의 행동(사과)에 관한 것이다.
g.explanation_en: The hypothesis says listeners help repair a slip more often when the speaker looks embarrassed. A shows listeners joking or changing the subject much more often after slips by embarrassed speakers, so it directly supports the hypothesis. B is about how many slips speakers make, not how listeners respond. C finds no difference, so it would actually weaken the hypothesis. D describes what the speakers did (apologizing), not what the listeners did.
g.design: 이 문항은 가설의 비교 대상(당황한 화자 vs. 침착한 화자)과 측정 대상(청자의 도움)을 맞게 짚는 한 단계 규칙만으로 풀린다. 오답은 측정 대상이 다르거나(B, D) 결과 방향이 반대인(C) 전형적 오개념이고, 질문 문장에는 정답의 핵심어를 쓰지 않았다.

g.passage: Linguist Deborah Cameron has argued that differences between "men's talk" and "women's talk" are not fixed traits that speakers carry from birth or early childhood. Women in a large survey reported that they talk about their feelings more often than men do, and their answers stayed the same across ten years.

g.explanation_en: Cameron claims that speech style depends on the setting and the speaker's role more than on gender. g.passage: In nineteenth-century Lucknow, reciting Urdu qasida poetry was more than a literary pastime. Courtiers who mastered its ornate Persian-derived vocabulary used the form to signal refinement and to mark themselves off from lower-ranking groups. Linguistic anthropologists describe this as a register, a style of speech that listeners link to a particular social identity. Performing the qasida well did not simply reflect a speaker's elite ______ it helped create and maintain that status in the eyes of others.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Performing the qasida well did not simply reflect a speaker's elite status"와 뒤 "it helped create and maintain that status..."는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문장부호가 전혀 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 등위접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 붙어 표준 구두점에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "Performing the qasida well did not simply reflect a speaker's elite status," form an independent clause, and so do the words after it, "it helped create and maintain that status..." A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence. D adds an extra comma after the conjunction "and," and Standard English doesn't put a comma there.
g.design: 빈칸 양쪽이 모두 독립절이라는 점이 바로 보이게 썼고, 오답은 흔한 실수인 쉼표 스플라이스, 무종지문, 접속사 뒤 쉼표로 구성했다.

A와 D는 정동사라는 점은 맞지만 복수형('were', 'have')이므로 삽입구 속 'features'에 끌린 일치 오류이다. B의 분사 'functioning'은 수 일치 문제는 피하지만 that절에 정동사가 없게 만들어 문장이 불완전해진다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the that-clause is the singular noun "choice." The phrase "along with ... 'nothing,'" is an interrupting modifier, so it doesn't change the subject's number. The clause therefore needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, and C, "functioned," does that. A and D are finite verbs, but they're plural ("were," "have"), which means they mistakenly agree with "features" inside the interrupting phrase. B, the participle "functioning," avoids the agreement problem but leaves the that-clause with no main verb, so the sentence is incomplete.
g.design: A long "along with" modifier that contains a plural noun separates the singular subject from the verb. Students have to make two checks, finite verb vs. participle and singular vs. plural, before only one choice remains.

B는 지문이 규범적 영향과 정보적 영향을 대비하고 있어 대조처럼 보이지만, 뒤 문장은 앞 문장을 반박하지 않고 그 결과를 이어 간다. C는 지문 앞부분의 일반론 뒤에 연구가 나오기 때문에 그럴듯해 보이지만, 마지막 문장은 사례가 아니라 사례에서 나온 추론이다. g.design: There are no wording cues. The cause-result link comes from the detail about private answers. C and D get partial support from the general-then-specific setup, and B gets partial support from the normative-vs-informational contrast.

c.seed: social science research — Actor-observer bias and perspective differences in attribution errors favoring situational actor explanations

g.passage: When people explain their own missteps, they tend to point to circumstances: a late train, a confusing set of instructions, an unusually demanding week. When they explain the identical missteps of others, however, they more often cite character traits such as carelessness or laziness. Psychologists Edward Jones and Richard Nisbett called this pattern the actor-observer bias and proposed that it stems partly from perspective: actors look outward at the situation, while observers look at the actor. In a test of this idea, researchers videotaped conversations and then showed participants a recording filmed from their partner's vantage point, so that participants watched themselves as an observer would. ______ these participants explained their own behavior much as observers typically do, emphasizing personal dispositions over situational pressures.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 마지막 문장은 바로 앞에서 설명한 실험 조건(상대방 시점에서 찍은 영상으로 자신을 관찰자처럼 봄)에서 나타난 결과를 제시하므로, 그 조건을 가리키는 B가 정답이다. 이 결과는 관점 가설을 뒷받침하는 예상된 결과이므로, 예상과의 대조를 나타내는 A와 C는 맞지 않는다. 행위자 자신이 성향적 설명을 했다는 점이 일반적 경향과 달라 보여 A·C가 그럴듯해 보이지만, 지문의 논리상 이 결과는 가설이 예측한 바이다. D는 영상을 본 뒤의 결과를 그 이전의 일로 잘못 배치한다.
g.explanation_en: The final sentence reports what happened in the experimental setup just described, where participants watched themselves from their partner's viewpoint, so B correctly ties the result to that condition. The result supports the perspective hypothesis, so it is exactly what the researchers predicted, which rules out the contrast transitions A and C. A and C can look tempting because actors describing themselves in terms of traits seems to go against the usual pattern, but in this passage that outcome is what the hypothesis predicts. D is wrong because it places the result before the viewing, even though the explanations came after watching the recording.
g.design: 자기 설명이 성향적으로 바뀐 '반전처럼 보이는' 결과를 제시해 대조 전환어(A, C)가 끌리게 하되, 실제로는 가설이 예측한 조건별 결과임을 파악해야 B를 고를 수 있게 했다.

c.seed: social science research — Terror management theory mortality salience and worldview defense coping with existential death anxiety

g.passage: Terror management theory proposes that people cope with the awareness of their own mortality by clinging more tightly to cultural worldviews that promise lasting meaning. In a classic test of the idea, researchers asked some participants to write about their own death before judging a person who had criticized the participants' country; other participants wrote about a neutral topic. Those reminded of death rated the critic far more harshly, a pattern the researchers called worldview defense. __Yet later studies found that when participants were asked to think about death in vivid, concrete detail rather than abstractly, the harsh judgments often weakened or disappeared.__ This finding has led some theorists to argue that worldview defense is triggered not by death thoughts in general but specifically by death thoughts that linger just outside conscious attention.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a result that confirms the classic study's finding that reminders of death lead people to judge critics of their country more harshly.
It presents a methodological flaw that led researchers to reject the claim that awareness of mortality influences people's judgments.
It presents a result that complicates the classic finding and prompts a narrower account of when worldview defense occurs.
It presents an example of worldview defense that participants showed when they wrote about a neutral topic instead of death.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작하며, 죽음을 구체적으로 생각하게 하면 가혹한 판단이 약해진다는 결과를 제시한다. 이는 고전적 발견을 복잡하게 만들고, 바로 다음 문장에서 의식 밖에 머무는 죽음 생각에 한정하는 더 좁은 설명으로 이어지므로 C가 정답이다. A는 이 결과가 고전적 발견을 단순히 확인한다고 보지만, 실제로는 대비되는 결과다. B는 이론을 기각했다고 하지만, 지문은 이론을 버리지 않고 범위를 좁혔을 뿐이다. D는 중립 주제 집단을 다루는데, 밑줄 문장은 그 집단과 관계가 없다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence starts with "Yet" and reports that thinking about death in vivid, concrete detail weakened the harsh judgments. That result complicates the classic finding, and the next sentence uses it to support a narrower account based on death thoughts that stay outside conscious attention, so C is correct. A says the result confirms the classic finding, but the sentence actually sets up a contrast with it. B claims the theory was rejected, but the text only narrows the theory and doesn't abandon it. c.seed: social science research — Hyperbolic discounting temporal preferences and preference reversal favoring immediate smaller rewards over delayed larger

g.passage: Standard economic models assume that people discount future rewards at a constant rate, so that someone who prefers $110 in 31 days to $100 in 30 days should also prefer $110 tomorrow to $100 today. Behavioral economists have repeatedly found otherwise. In surveys and laboratory tasks, many participants choose the larger, later reward when both options lie weeks away, yet switch to the smaller, sooner reward once the earlier option becomes immediate. __This reversal is difficult to reconcile with constant discounting, because the one-day delay separating the two rewards is identical in both choices.__ Researchers have therefore proposed hyperbolic models, in which the perceived value of a reward drops steeply over short delays and more gradually over long ones, as a better account of how people actually weigh time.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why participants in laboratory tasks tend to prefer larger rewards when both options are distant.
It introduces the hyperbolic model by describing how perceived value declines over short and long delays.
It questions whether survey and laboratory findings about reward choices accurately reflect real-world behavior.
It identifies why a pattern of observed choices poses a problem for an established assumption, setting up the alternative that follows.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 앞서 서술한 선호 역전이 두 선택 모두 지연 간격이 하루로 같다는 이유로 일정 할인 가정과 맞지 않음을 지적하고, 이어지는 쌍곡선 모형 제안의 근거가 된다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 먼 미래 선택만 다루며, 밑줄 문장은 선호 이유가 아니라 모순을 설명한다. B는 마지막 문장의 기능이지 밑줄 문장의 기능이 아니다. C는 실험 결과의 타당성을 의심한다고 하지만, 지문은 그 결과를 받아들이고 오히려 기존 모형을 문제 삼는다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence points out that the preference reversal conflicts with constant discounting because the one-day gap is the same in both choices, and that conflict is what leads into the hyperbolic model proposed next. So D is correct. A covers only the distant-choice behavior, and the sentence isn't explaining why people prefer anything. It's showing a contradiction. B describes the final sentence, not the underlined one. C says the sentence doubts the experimental findings, but the text accepts those findings and uses them to challenge the standard model.
g.design: To answer, students must connect the reversal pattern to the constant-discounting assumption and also see how the sentence leads into the next one. B is tempting because it borrows from the neighboring sentence, and A is tempting because it repeats a detail from the earlier one.

c.seed: social science research — Availability heuristic memory accessibility and probability estimation overweighting easily recalled examples

g.passage: In a 1973 study of the availability heuristic, the tendency to judge how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind, psychologists Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman asked participants whether the letter K appears more often as the first letter of English words or as the third. Most participants picked the first position, a judgment that seems sensible at first glance______ words with K in the third position are actually about twice as common, but they are much harder to recall.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Most participants picked ... at first glance"는 긴 동격구가 붙어 있지만 독립절이고, 뒤의 "words with K ... are actually about twice as common..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 이어야 하며, 전환어 "in fact" 뒤에는 쉼표를 붙이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 "in fact"를 쉼표로 감싸 삽입어처럼 보이지만 결국 쉼표만으로 두 절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C도 쉼표로만 절을 이어 같은 오류가 있고, "in fact" 뒤 쉼표까지 빠졌다. D는 두 절 사이에 아무 문장부호도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The part before the blank, "Most participants picked ... at first glance," is an independent clause, even with the long appositive phrase attached to it. The part after it, "words with K ... are actually about twice as common...," is also an independent clause. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, and a transition like "in fact" takes a comma after it, so A is correct. B puts commas around "in fact" so it looks like an interrupter, but that still leaves only a comma joining the two clauses, which is a comma splice. C has the same comma splice and is also missing the comma after the transition. D has no punctuation at all between the clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: The long appositive ("a judgment that seems sensible...") hides the fact that the sentence before the blank is a complete clause. B and C look plausible because they set off "in fact" with commas, so students have to notice that a transition alone can't join two clauses.

Rather than moderating their positions, the participants rated the report that matched their prior beliefs as more rigorous and scrutinized the opposing report for ______ many left the experiment more convinced of their original views than when they arrived.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Rather than ... flaws"는 주어 participants와 동사 rated·scrutinized를 갖춘 독립절이고, 뒤의 "many left the experiment ..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 나누고, 접속부사 as a result 뒤에는 쉼표를 써야 하므로 B가 맞다. A는 접속부사 앞뒤에 쉼표만 써서 두 독립절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스이다. C도 쉼표만으로 두 절을 이어 같은 오류가 생긴다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 절이 붙은 런온 문장이고, as a result가 앞 절의 scrutinized를 꾸미는 것처럼 잘못 읽힌다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "Rather than ... flaws," is an independent clause with the subject "participants" and the verbs "rated" and "scrutinized." The text after it, "many left the experiment ...," is also an independent clause. Two independent clauses can be separated with a semicolon, and the conjunctive adverb "as a result" then takes a comma after it, so B is correct. A puts only commas around "as a result," which creates a comma splice. C also joins the two clauses with just a comma, making the same error. D has no punctuation between the clauses, so it is a run-on, and it makes "as a result" seem to modify "scrutinized" in the first clause.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "Members"이고, 긴 삽입구 "assuming ... consensus" 뒤에 동사 "withhold"가 와서 첫 번째 독립절이 끝난다. 그다음 "the group interprets ..."는 주어와 동사를 갖춘 또 하나의 독립절이므로, 두 절을 이어 주는 세미콜론을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. B는 "쉼표+and" 형태가 겉보기엔 맞아 보이지만, 앞의 삽입구 쉼표들과 겹치면서 "assuming that ... and that ..., and the group"처럼 읽혀 and가 삽입구 안의 that절을 계속 나열하는 것으로 오해될 수 있다. 무엇보다 문맥상 두 번째 절은 앞 절의 결과를 해석하는 내용이라 대등한 덧붙임보다 세미콜론의 긴밀한 연결이 더 알맞다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다.
g.explanation_en: The subject here is "Members," and after the long "assuming ..." phrase, the verb "withhold" finishes the first independent clause. "The group interprets ..." has its own subject and verb, so it is a second independent clause, and the semicolon in C joins the two correctly. A connects two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B's comma plus "and" looks acceptable on its own, but coming right after the parenthetical commas, it reads as if "and" continues the list of "that" clauses inside the "assuming" phrase. The context also calls for the semicolon's tighter link, because the second clause explains what the members' silence leads to rather than just adding a parallel point. D runs the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, making a run-on sentence.
g.design: A long participial phrase between subject and verb hides where the first clause ends, so the reader has to find the main verb before choosing a boundary. A and D are standard traps, and B looks partly correct, so the reader has to compare it with C in context.

g.design: 빈칸 앞에 'a disaster in which...'라는 긴 동격 수식어를 두어 그 수식어가 문장 중간 삽입처럼 보이게 만들고, 실제로는 'Weick examined...'가 완결된 독립절임을 파악해야 두 독립절 사이 경계를 판단할 수 있게 했다.
g.explanation: 'Weick examined the 1949 Mann Gulch fire'는 완결된 독립절이고, 'a disaster in which ... minutes'는 fire를 꾸미는 동격어구일 뿐이다. 빈칸 뒤 'his conclusion was that...'도 독립절이므로 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 하며, 따라서 A가 정답이다. g.explanation_en: "Weick examined the 1949 Mann Gulch fire" is already a complete independent clause, and "a disaster in which ... minutes" is just an appositive describing the fire. B joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, creating a comma splice; it's tempting because the comma looks like it's closing off the appositive. C has no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on sentence. D uses the coordinating conjunction "and," but leaves out the comma that should come before "and" when it joins two independent clauses.

After "however," a new independent clause begins ("replication attempts have..."), so you need a boundary mark that can join two independent clauses. In C, the colon works because the second clause explains the claim that the effect has been hard to reproduce. A closes the appositive correctly as well, and a semicolon can also join two clauses, so A is the closest distractor. Watch that difference carefully: the mark you choose has to fit both the grammar and the logical link between the clauses. B puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, and its comma after "however" creates a comma splice. D fails because it leaves out the comma that closes the appositive.

g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "the pseudopatients ... behaved normally"와 뒤 "hospital staff nonetheless interpreted ..."는 각각 독립절이므로 둘을 이으려면 쉼표+등위접속사나 세미콜론이 필요하다. g.passage: In a classic study of post-decision attitude change, participants rated several household appliances and then chose between two items they had rated almost equally. When they rated the appliances again, they gave the item they had chosen a higher score and the rejected item a lower one. Researchers argue that this shift reflects an effort to ______ the discomfort of having given up an attractive option: by making the chosen item look better and the rejected one worse, participants made their decision seem obviously correct and eased the tension between "I chose this" and "the other one was just as good."

g.explanation: 지문은 참가자들이 선택한 물건은 더 좋게, 포기한 물건은 더 나쁘게 평가해 결정이 옳아 보이게 만들고 긴장을 "eased"했다고 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 불편함을 '덜다'라는 뜻이 필요하고 A(alleviate)가 정답이다. B(conceal)는 불편함을 다룬다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 지문에 나온 것은 남에게 감정을 숨기는 것이 아니라 태도를 바꿔 불편함 자체를 줄이는 과정이다. C(anticipate)는 결정과 관련된 감정이라는 점은 맞지만, 평가 변화는 선택을 한 뒤에 일어났으므로 불편함을 '예상하는' 것과는 맞지 않는다. D(intensify)는 불편함을 더 키운다는 뜻이어서 "eased"와 정반대다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says participants rated the chosen item higher and the rejected item lower so their decision would seem correct, and that this "eased the tension." So the blank needs a word meaning "reduce," and that makes A (alleviate) the answer. B (conceal) is tempting because it also deals with discomfort, but the participants didn't hide their feelings from anyone; they changed their attitudes so the discomfort itself got smaller. C (anticipate) does connect to feelings about a decision, but the ratings changed after the choice was made, so they weren't predicting a feeling in advance. D (intensify) means making the discomfort stronger, which is the opposite of "eased."
g.design: I used Brehm's free-choice study of post-decision attitude change. To get the answer, you have to connect the blank to the later phrase "eased the tension." B and C each match part of the passage, so you have to compare them carefully to rule them out, while D is the opposite meaning.

g.explanation_en: The wearers predicted that about half of the observers noticed the shirt, but only about a quarter actually did. That means people overestimate how much others pay attention to them, and the phrase "largely imaginary" audience backs this up, so B is correct. A does point to a mistaken judgment, but the study measured how much attention people received, not the reasons for it. C fits the idea of being self-absorbed, but it leaves out the key point of the passage: a wrong estimate. D also describes a wrong estimate, but in the opposite direction, which contradicts the finding that predictions were higher than reality.
g.design: To answer, students must connect the numbers in the passage (half predicted vs. a quarter actual) to the direction of the error. Two distractors are partly supported: A names a misjudgment, and D names an estimation error in the wrong direction. C is a plausible reaction for someone absorbed in their own appearance.

B would mean they learned from the delays, but the passage says they ignored them and made optimistic predictions. g.explanation_en: The passage says confidence "grows" because of encouraging feedback and rehearsal, even though memory doesn't improve. So the blank has to describe these influences making confidence bigger without good reason, and D, "inflate," does exactly that. A, "verify," fits the investigative setting, but feedback doesn't check confidence; it distorts it no matter how accurate the witness is. B, "diminish," gets the idea of distortion right but points the wrong way, because the passage says confidence increases. C, "document," means recording, which isn't something these influences do to confidence.
g.design: The distractors are traps for skimmers: B gets the distortion idea but the wrong direction, and A borrows the legal context. You have to tie the blank back to the word "grows" earlier in the passage. The answer word doesn't appear on the surface of the passage.

g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

g.explanation_en: The text says that misremembering a source leads people to trust weakly supported information as if it had been vetted, so the misattribution must inflate, or unjustifiably increase, their confidence. c.seed: social science research — Milgram obedience experiments cultural variation and authority compliance differences across Japan Germany Australia

g.passage: Replications of Stanley Milgram's obedience experiment conducted outside the United States have produced strikingly different compliance rates: some studies in Germany reported that most participants delivered the maximum shock, while a study in Australia found far lower rates, especially among women. Some researchers have attributed these differences to national cultures that vary in their general respect for authority. Social psychologist Ilse Brandt proposes another explanation. She argues that the replications differed in how much legitimacy the experimenter appeared to have—such as whether the study was linked to a prestigious university or took place in a plain office building—and that this perceived legitimacy, rather than national culture, mainly accounts for the variation in compliance.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Brandt's explanation?
options: Within a single country, participants tested at a well-known university obeyed at much higher rates than participants given the identical procedure in a rented storefront by an unaffiliated researcher.
Across several countries, participants who scored high on a survey measuring general respect for authority obeyed at higher rates than participants who scored low on that survey.
In both the German and the Australian replications, participants who obeyed fully reported feeling more stress during the session than participants who refused to continue.
Replications conducted in Japan produced compliance rates that fell between those found in the German and the Australian studies, regardless of where the sessions were held.
g.explanation: Brandt의 주장은 국가 문화가 아니라 실험자의 인지된 정당성(소속 기관의 권위 등)이 복종률 차이를 설명한다는 것이다. A는 국가(문화)를 고정한 채 정당성만 달리했을 때 복종률이 크게 달라졌음을 보여 주므로 이 주장을 가장 직접 뒷받침한다. B는 개인의 권위 존중 성향이 복종을 예측함을 보여 주어 오히려 문화·성향 설명 쪽에 가깝다. C는 스트레스와 복종의 관계일 뿐 정당성과 무관하다. D는 장소와 무관하게 국가별 차이가 유지된다는 뜻이므로 오히려 문화 설명을 지지하고 Brandt의 주장을 약화한다.
g.explanation_en: Brandt claims that the experimenter's perceived legitimacy, not national culture, mainly explains the differences in compliance. Choice A holds the country constant and changes only the institutional setting, and obedience still shifts sharply, so it most directly supports her view. Choice B shows that a person's general respect for authority predicts obedience, which fits the cultural explanation better than Brandt's. Choice C connects stress to obedience but says nothing about legitimacy. Choice D suggests national differences hold no matter the setting, which actually weakens Brandt's explanation.
g.design: To get the answer, students must see that Brandt's claim rules out culture, so the right evidence has to hold nationality fixed while legitimacy changes. B and D tempt students because they deal with authority and national comparisons.

c.seed: social science research — Rosenhan pseudopatient study diagnostic bias and psychiatric labeling effects in mental health institutional settings

g.passage: In 1973, psychologist David Rosenhan reported that eight mentally healthy volunteers gained admission to psychiatric hospitals by claiming to hear voices. Once admitted, they stopped reporting any symptoms and behaved normally, yet staff often interpreted ordinary actions—such as taking notes—as signs of illness. Rosenhan argued that the diagnostic label itself, rather than anything in the patients' behavior, shaped how staff perceived them: once a person was labeled "schizophrenic," staff read even normal conduct through that label. Critics have proposed a different explanation, suggesting that staff were simply following cautious hospital routines that applied to every patient regardless of diagnosis.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Rosenhan's explanation over the critics' explanation?
options: Staff at the hospitals recorded detailed behavioral notes on all patients, including those admitted for conditions unrelated to psychosis, at the same rate.

When staff were shown identical descriptions of a patient's calm note-taking, those told the patient was diagnosed with schizophrenia described the behavior as symptomatic far more often than those told the patient had no diagnosis.
Several of the pseudopatients reported that other patients on the ward suspected they were not actually ill, even though staff did not.
Hospitals in the study required every newly admitted patient to remain under observation for a minimum period before any discharge could be considered.

A와 D는 진단과 무관하게 모든 환자에게 똑같은 절차가 적용됐음을 보여 주므로 오히려 비판자들의 설명을 지지한다. C는 직원과 다른 환자의 인식 차이를 보여 줄 뿐, 그 차이가 꼬리표 때문인지 관행 때문인지 구별하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: Rosenhan claims the diagnostic label, not behavior, shaped staff perceptions, while critics say uniform hospital routines explain the staff's actions. Choice B holds behavior constant and changes only the label, and the interpretation shifts—direct evidence of a label effect that uniform routines can't explain. Choices A and D show that procedures were applied equally to all patients regardless of diagnosis, which actually supports the critics. Choice C shows that staff and fellow patients saw things differently, but it doesn't tell you whether labels or routines caused that difference.
g.design: To pick the right answer, students have to (1) see what separates the two explanations (label vs. uniform routine) and (2) find the finding that isolates the label variable. A and C seem relevant but don't separate the two explanations.

g.passage: For much of the twentieth century, many criminologists assumed that publicly identifying someone as a rule-breaker, through arrest, conviction, or expulsion, would make that person less likely to break rules again, since the shame of the label would serve as a warning. In the 1960s, however, sociologist Howard Becker and other labeling theorists argued that the stigma attached to such a label often cuts people off from jobs, schools, and law-abiding friends, pushing them toward groups that accept the deviant identity. On this view, official labeling frequently ______ the very behavior it is meant to stop.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 정답 C(entrenches, 굳어지게 하다): 'however' 뒤에서 Becker는 낙인이 사람을 정상적 기회에서 밀어내고 일탈 집단 쪽으로 몰아간다고 주장한다. 그러니 낙인은 막으려던 행동을 오히려 굳히고 강화한다. 이는 통념(억제한다)과 정반대 방향이다. A(discourages): 전환 앞에 나온 통념, 즉 낙인이 재범을 억제한다는 견해를 그대로 옮긴 말이다. B(eradicates): 전환어를 놓치고 통념과 같은 방향(줄이다)을 더 극단적인 강도로 표현한 말이다. D(documents): '기록하다'는 공식 절차와 연관되어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 낙인이 행동을 늘리느냐 줄이느냐라는 논점과 상관없는 제3의 의미다.
g.explanation_en: C (entrenches) is correct. After "however," the text says the stigma of a label shuts people out of jobs, schools, and law-abiding friendships and pushes them toward groups that accept a deviant identity. So labeling ends up strengthening and locking in the behavior it was supposed to stop. That is the opposite of the earlier assumption. A (discourages) just repeats the older view that the shame of a label deters future rule-breaking. B (eradicates) misses the contrast signal: it points the same way as the old view (reducing the behavior), only more strongly. D (documents) fits the idea of official procedures, but it says nothing about whether labeling increases or decreases the behavior, and that is the point the passage is making.
g.design: 'However' 앞에는 통념(낙인이 억제한다)을, 뒤에는 이를 뒤집는 낙인 이론을 두었고, 빈칸은 뒤집힌 결론(강화)을 나타내게 했다. 오답은 통념 어휘, 같은 방향에서 강도만 센 어휘, 논점과 무관한 어휘로 구성했다.
