c.seed: history and civics — Magna Carta 1215 and English feudal rights establishing precedent for limited monarchy constitutional governance

g.passage: The Magna Carta, a charter that King John sealed in 1215 after a coalition of rebellious barons forced him to negotiate with them at Runnymede, ______ the principle that even a monarch was bound by written law, an idea that later framers of constitutional governments would repeatedly invoke.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'The Magna Carta'이고, 'a charter ... at Runnymede'는 주어를 설명하는 긴 동격어구일 뿐이므로 문장에는 정동사가 필요하다. B의 'established'는 단수 주어와 맞는 과거 시제 정동사로서 1215년이라는 과거 맥락과도 어울린다. A와 D는 분사형이라 정동사가 없어 문장이 완성되지 않는다(문장 조각). C는 정동사이긴 하지만 복수형이어서, 바로 앞의 'barons'나 'them'에 끌려 고르기 쉬운 오답이며 단수 주어 'Magna Carta'와 수가 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The Magna Carta." Everything from "a charter" to "Runnymede" is a long appositive describing it, so the sentence still needs a main verb. Choice B, "established," is a finite past-tense verb that works with a singular subject and fits the 1215 setting. Choices A and D are participles, so with either one the sentence has no main verb and becomes a fragment. Choice C is a finite verb, but it is plural. It seems to agree with the nearby "barons" or "them," but it doesn't agree with the singular subject "Magna Carta."

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 관계절이 주어 "The General Act"와 동사를 떼어 놓아, 정동사가 필요하다는 점과 단수 주어에 맞춘 수 일치를 함께 판단해야 한다. 바로 앞 복수 명사 "states/regions"가 B를 고르도록 유도한다.
g.explanation: 주어는 "The General Act"이고, "which required ... coastal regions"는 주어를 꾸미는 삽입 관계절이므로 빈칸에는 이 단수 주어의 정동사가 와야 한다. C의 과거형 "accelerated"는 수 제한이 없고 1880년대 사건을 다루는 문맥에도 맞으므로 정답이다. g.explanation_en: The subject of the sentence is "The General Act," and the clause "which required ... coastal regions" is just a modifier set off by commas, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with that singular subject. Choice A is a participle, which leaves the sentence with no main verb. Choice B is a finite verb, but it is plural, matching the nearby nouns "states" and "regions" instead of the singular subject "Act." g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

A는 과거 시제는 맞지만 단수형이라, 바로 앞의 단수 명사 'Klan'이나 'Black citizens' 근처를 주어로 착각하게 만든 오답이다. B는 분사구라 문장에 정동사가 없게 되고, C는 단수형이면서 현재 시제라 과거 문맥과도 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun phrase "The Enforcement Acts," and the long which-clause is just a modifier sitting between the subject and its verb. That means you need a plural main verb, and it also has to be in the past tense, since "1870 and 1871" and "began withdrawing" place the events in the past. D meets both requirements. A has the right tense, but it's singular, so it only seems correct if you mistake a nearby singular noun like "Klan" for the subject. B is a participle, which leaves the sentence with no main verb, and C is both singular and in the present tense, so it doesn't fit the past-tense context.

When Britain and France, acting in secret coordination with Israel, launched a military operation to retake the waterway that autumn, the reaction from Washington and Moscow ______ swift: both superpowers demanded a ceasefire, and within weeks the invading forces had begun to withdraw, a retreat many historians regard as a turning point in the decline of European imperial power.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 주어 'the reaction'과 빈칸 사이에 복수 명사구 'Washington and Moscow'를 두어 수 일치 함정을 만들고, 분사형 오답으로 정동사 필요성까지 판단하게 했다.
g.explanation: 이 주절의 주어는 단수 명사 'the reaction'이고, 'from Washington and Moscow'는 그 주어를 꾸미는 전치사구일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 정동사가 필요하므로 A의 'was'가 정답이다. B의 'were'는 바로 앞의 복수처럼 보이는 'Washington and Moscow'에 맞춘 것이어서 주어-동사 수 일치가 틀린다. C의 'being'과 D의 'having been'은 분사라서 정동사가 아니므로, 콜론 앞의 절이 동사 없는 불완전한 절이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this main clause is the singular noun "the reaction." The phrase "from Washington and Moscow" is just a prepositional phrase describing that subject. So you need a singular finite verb, which makes A, "was," the answer. B, "were," agrees with "Washington and Moscow," which sounds plural, so the subject and verb don't agree. C, "being," and D, "having been," are participles, not finite verbs, so the clause before the colon would be left without a main verb.

g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The program." The clause "whose grants ... West Germany" just sits between the subject and its verb. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, which makes B correct. A is a finite verb, but it's plural, likely pulled that way by the nearby plural nouns like "grants" and "countries," so it doesn't agree with "program." C (a participle) and D (an infinitive) aren't finite verbs, which would leave the sentence without a main verb.
g.design: A long relative clause full of plural nouns separates the singular subject from its verb. The wrong choices test both agreement and finite versus nonfinite verbs, so getting it right takes two steps: finding the subject and confirming the sentence needs a main verb.

g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "assault." The long phrase "on senior party officials, many of whom ... Red Guards" just sits between the subject and its verb. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, and since the events happened in 1966-1967, C, "weakened," is correct. g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'release'이고, 그 뒤의 'the so-called "smoking gun" tape ...' 부분은 긴 동격 수식어구이므로 빈칸에는 단수 주어에 맞는 정동사가 와야 한다. 'within days'와 'resigned'가 과거 사건을 나타내므로 단순과거 D(eroded)가 정답이다. g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "release." B is a finite verb, but it's plural, which matches the nearby plural nouns "aides" or "conversations" rather than the singular subject. C is also plural, and its present perfect tense doesn't fit the past-time narration.
g.design: I put a long appositive containing plural nouns (conversations, aides) between the singular subject and the blank. g.passage: The Treaty of Utrecht, signed in 1713 after years of tense negotiation between British and French diplomats over colonial territories in North America and the Mediterranean, ______ Britain control of Gibraltar, Minorca, and much of Newfoundland, strategic holdings that helped secure British naval supremacy for nearly a century.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The Treaty of Utrecht'이고, 긴 분사구 'signed in 1713 ... Mediterranean'은 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이므로 빈칸에는 주어와 수가 일치하는 정동사가 와야 한다. B의 'granted'는 단수 주어와 함께 쓸 수 있는 과거형 정동사이므로 정답이다. A의 'granting'과 D의 'having granted'는 분사여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 문장이 완성되지 않는다. C의 'have granted'는 정동사이긴 하지만 복수형이어서, 바로 앞의 'diplomats'나 'territories'와 잘못 일치시킨 형태이다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The Treaty of Utrecht." The long phrase "signed in 1713 ... Mediterranean" only modifies that subject, so the blank needs a main verb that agrees with a singular subject. Choice B, "granted," is a past-tense main verb that works with a singular subject, so it is correct. Choices A ("granting") and D ("having granted") are participles, which means the sentence would have no main verb and wouldn't be complete. Choice C ("have granted") is a main verb, but it is plural, so it wrongly agrees with nearby nouns like "diplomats" or "territories" instead of the real subject.
g.design: A long participial modifier full of plural nouns separates the singular subject from the blank. The student has to see that a main verb is needed (which rules out A and D) and then check agreement with the real subject (which rules out C).

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 긴 수식어구/도치 뒤의 주어-동사 일치, 병렬 구조, 수식어 위치(dangling modifier), 정동사 vs 분사/부정사 선택처럼 구조 파악이 필요한 문제.
c.seed: history and civics — Tanzimat Ottoman reforms 1839-1876 and centralization modernization attempts to save declining Ottoman imperial power

g.passage: The Tanzimat reforms, a series of legal and administrative measures that Ottoman officials introduced between 1839 and 1876 in an effort to reassert central authority over increasingly autonomous provinces, ______ tax collection, military conscription, and many courts under the direct supervision of ministries in Istanbul.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 주어는 복수 명사 'The Tanzimat reforms'이고, 콤마 사이의 긴 동격 구문을 지나면 이 주어에 대한 정동사가 필요하다. C 'placed'는 정동사이고 복수 주어와 맞으며 1839~1876년이라는 과거 시제와도 어울린다. A 'placing'은 분사여서 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다. B는 동격 구문 뒤에서 주어를 'they'로 다시 써서 주어가 중복된다. D 'places'는 단수 현재형이라 복수 주어와 맞지 않고 과거 맥락과도 어긋나는데, 바로 앞의 단수 명사들에 끌리면 고르기 쉽다.
g.explanation_en: The subject is the plural noun "The Tanzimat reforms." Once you skip over the long appositive between the commas, you can see that this subject still needs a main verb. C, "placed," is a finite verb that agrees with the plural subject and matches the past time frame of 1839-1876. A, "placing," is a participle, so the sentence would have no main verb. B repeats the subject with "they" after the appositive, which gives the sentence a redundant subject. D, "places," is singular and in the present tense, so it doesn't agree with "reforms" and doesn't fit the past context either; it's tempting only if you match it to a nearby singular noun.
g.design: 긴 동격 구문이 주어와 빈칸을 갈라 놓아서, 주어를 다시 찾아내는 판단과 정동사·수·시제를 확인하는 판단, 이렇게 두 단계가 필요하도록 설계했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 긴 수식어구/도치 뒤의 주어-동사 일치, 병렬 구조, 수식어 위치(dangling modifier), 정동사 vs 분사/부정사 선택처럼 구조 파악이 필요한 문제.
c.seed: history and civics — Warsaw Pact formation 1955 and Soviet-aligned Eastern European military alliance countering NATO Western bloc

g.passage: In May 1955, just days after West Germany formally joined NATO, the Soviet Union and seven Eastern European states, including Poland, Hungary, and Czechoslovakia, gathered in the Polish capital to sign a treaty of "friendship, cooperation, and mutual assistance." The resulting Warsaw Pact, often described by historians as Moscow's answer to the Western bloc's growing military integration, ______ the armed forces of its members under a unified command whose top officers were almost always Soviet.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The resulting Warsaw Pact'이고, 삽입된 분사구 'often described ... integration'이 주어와 빈칸을 떼어 놓고 있다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하며, D 'placed'가 이를 충족한다. A 'placing'은 분사여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 불완전한 문장이 된다. B 'have placed'와 C 'were placing'은 정동사이긴 하지만 복수형이라, 바로 앞의 'historians'나 'the Western bloc's'와 연결해 읽을 때만 그럴듯해 보일 뿐 단수 주어와 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun phrase "The resulting Warsaw Pact," and the participial phrase "often described ... integration" separates it from the blank. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, and D, "placed," does that. A, "placing," is a participle, which would leave the sentence without a main verb and make it a fragment. B, "have placed," and C, "were placing," are finite verbs, but they're plural. They only seem to fit if you mistakenly link the verb to a nearby noun like "historians." Neither one agrees with the singular subject.
g.design: 긴 삽입 분사구가 단수 주어와 빈칸을 갈라 놓는다. 그래서 학생은 정동사가 필요한지와 수 일치를 모두 판단해야 한다. 오답 B와 C는 정동사라는 조건은 맞췄지만 복수형이고, A는 수와 상관없는 형태지만 정동사가 아니다.

c.seed: history and civics — Peace of Paris 1783 and American independence recognition establishing United States as sovereign nation

g.passage: The Treaty of Paris, signed in September 1783 by American and British diplomats after nearly two years of difficult negotiation with input from French and Spanish envoys, ______ the thirteen former colonies as a sovereign nation, a status that allowed the United States to conduct its own diplomacy and claim territory extending west to the Mississippi River.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The Treaty of Paris"이고, 쉼표 사이에 긴 분사구(signed ... envoys)가 끼어 있으므로 빈칸에는 주어에 맞는 정동사가 필요하다. A는 과거형 정동사 "recognized"를 써서 완전한 독립절을 만든다. B와 D는 분사 형태여서 정동사 역할을 하지 못하므로 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다. C의 "which"는 관계절을 만들어 주어가 끝내 본동사를 갖지 못하게 하므로, 문장이 불완전한 조각으로 남는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The Treaty of Paris," and a long participial phrase (signed ... envoys) sits between the commas, so the blank needs a finite verb that goes with that subject. A works because the past-tense verb "recognized" turns the sentence into a complete independent clause. B and D are participles, and a participle can't act as the main verb, so the sentence would have no main verb at all. C starts a relative clause with "which," so the subject still never gets a main verb, and the sentence is left as a fragment.
g.design: A long participial phrase separates the subject from the blank, so students have to find the subject and then see that every option except the finite verb leaves the sentence without a main verb. The relative clause and the perfect participle look plausible if you only skim.

c.seed: history and civics — Roman siege of Masada 73-74 CE and Jewish Zealot mass suicide resisting Roman imperial conquest of Judea

g.passage: According to the first-century historian Josephus, the Roman Tenth Legion, after encircling the mountaintop fortress of Masada with a wall and camps, ______ a massive earthen ramp against the plateau's western face, a structure whose remains are still visible today. Some archaeologists, however, question whether the defenders' final collective suicide unfolded exactly as Josephus describes.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "the Roman Tenth Legion"이고, "after encircling ... camps"는 삽입된 수식어구일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 주어에 대응하는 정동사가 필요하며, 과거 사건이므로 B의 "constructed"가 맞다. A의 "building"은 현재분사로 정동사 역할을 하지 못해 문장이 불완전해진다. C의 "having constructed"는 완료 분사로 시점 관계는 그럴듯하지만 역시 정동사가 아니다. D의 "to construct"는 부정사로 목적을 나타낼 수는 있어도 주절의 동사가 될 수 없다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "the Roman Tenth Legion," and "after encircling ... camps" is just an interrupting modifier. So the blank needs a finite verb that goes with that subject, and since the event is in the past, B, "constructed," is correct. A, "building," is a present participle, so it can't serve as the main verb, and the sentence is left incomplete. C, "having constructed," is a perfect participle; its sense of time may seem to fit, but it still isn't a finite verb. D, "to construct," is an infinitive that could express purpose, but it can't act as the main verb of the clause.
g.design: 긴 삽입 수식어구가 주어와 빈칸을 갈라 놓아 정동사가 빠진 구조를 숨긴다. 분사·부정사 오답도 각각 그럴듯한 의미를 갖게 만들었다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: history and civics — Mongol postal relay system Yam routes and communication infrastructure enabling Eurasian empire administrative coordination

g.passage: Established under Genghis Khan and expanded by his successors, the Yam was a network of relay stations spaced roughly a day's ride apart across the Mongol Empire. Each station kept fresh horses, food, and lodging for officially licensed messengers, who could exchange exhausted mounts for rested ones and continue almost without pause. ______ orders issued at the imperial court could reach provincial governors thousands of kilometers away within days rather than the weeks such journeys would ordinarily have required.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 역참마다 새 말이 준비되어 전령이 거의 쉬지 않고 이동할 수 있었다는 원인을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 덕분에 명령이 몇 주가 아닌 며칠 만에 전달되었다는 결과를 말하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 역접인데 빠른 전달은 앞 내용과 상반되지 않고 오히려 그로부터 나온다. B는 예시 관계로 보일 수 있으나, 뒤 문장은 역참 운영 방식의 한 사례가 아니라 그것이 낳은 효과이다. D는 시간상 앞선 일을 나타내지만, 빠른 전달은 Yam이 생긴 뒤의 일이고 그 이전 상황이 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank gives a cause: every station kept fresh horses, so messengers could keep going almost without stopping. The sentence after the blank gives the effect: orders arrived in days instead of weeks. That makes C the answer. A signals a contrast, but fast delivery doesn't go against the earlier point; it follows from it. B might look possible, but the last sentence isn't one example of how the stations worked; it describes what they made possible. D points to an earlier time, but the faster delivery happened because of the Yam, not before it existed.
g.design: 빈칸 앞뒤에 인과를 직접 알려 주는 어휘를 두지 않았다. 학생은 말 교체가 빠른 명령 전달로 이어지는 논리를 스스로 읽어 내야 한다. B는 구체화로, D는 'ordinarily' 같은 시간 표현 때문에 그럴듯해 보이도록 오답을 설계했다.

c.seed: history and civics — Peasants' Revolt 1381 England and Wat Tyler uprising challenging feudal serfdom labor obligations

g.passage: In June 1381, thousands of rebels from Essex and Kent marched on London, demanding that King Richard II abolish serfdom and free them from the unpaid labor they owed their lords. Within days, the rebel leader Wat Tyler was killed at Smithfield, and the king soon revoked the charters of freedom he had granted, executing many of the uprising's organizers. ______ the rebels' central goal was largely realized over the following decades: lords increasingly found that they could not enforce traditional labor services, and by the mid-1400s serfdom had nearly disappeared from much of England.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 반란이 즉각 진압되고 왕이 약속을 철회했다는 실패를 서술하고, 뒤 문장은 그럼에도 반란의 핵심 목표인 농노제 폐지가 결국 실현되었다고 말하므로 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 반란이 장기적으로 영향을 주었다는 배경지식 때문에 그럴듯해 보이지만, 바로 앞 문장의 내용(지도자 사망, 헌장 철회)이 농노제 쇠퇴의 원인이 될 수 없으므로 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. B는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장을 바꿔 말한 것이 아니라 상반된 결과를 제시하므로 틀리다. C는 두 문장이 유사한 사례를 나열하는 관계가 아니라 대조 관계이므로 부적절하다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence describes the revolt's quick failure—Tyler was killed and the king took back his charters—while the next sentence says the rebels' main goal was achieved anyway, so D, which signals a contrast after a concession, is correct. A may seem tempting because the revolt is often linked to serfdom's decline, but the specific events just mentioned (a leader's death and revoked charters) could not cause serfdom to disappear, so the cause-and-effect direction does not work. B is wrong because the second sentence does not restate the first; it reports an opposite outcome. C is wrong because the sentences do not present similar examples; they present a contrast.
g.design: There is no word like "but" to signal the shift. Students have to see that the immediate failure is followed by long-term success. The result-based choice (A) is tempting because of what students may already know about the revolt, so they have to check which events are actually being linked as cause and effect.

c.seed: history and civics — Treaty of Tordesillas 1494 and Portuguese Spanish division of colonial territories in Americas Africa

g.passage: The 1494 Treaty of Tordesillas divided newly encountered lands outside Europe between Spain and Portugal along a meridian drawn roughly 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands. On paper, the arrangement appeared to favor Spain, which was assigned nearly all of the Americas. ______ the line's placement handed Portugal a claim to the eastern bulge of South America, territory that would eventually become Brazil, one of the largest colonies in the Western Hemisphere.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.design: 앞 문장이 '스페인에 유리해 보였다'고 인정한 뒤 다음 문장이 포르투갈의 큰 이익을 제시하는 양보-반전 구조로, 어휘 단서 없이 논리로 판단하게 했다. 인과(B)와 예시(C)는 경계선이 결과를 만들었다는 점, 분할의 한 사례라는 점에서 부분적으로 그럴듯하다.
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 조약이 스페인에 유리해 보였다고 말하고, 뒤 문장은 같은 경계선 때문에 포르투갈이 브라질이라는 거대한 영토를 얻었다고 말하므로, 예상을 인정한 뒤 뒤집는 A가 정답이다. B는 경계선 위치가 결과를 낳았다는 점에서 인과처럼 보이지만, 스페인이 유리했다는 사실에서 포르투갈의 이익이 나오지는 않는다. C는 브라질을 분할의 한 사례로 볼 수 있을 듯하지만, 스페인에 유리했다는 주장의 예가 아니라 오히려 그 주장을 반박한다. D는 두 문장이 서로 비슷한 내용이라고 보는 것인데, 두 문장은 대조된다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence grants that the treaty seemed to favor Spain, and the next sentence shows that the same line gave Portugal a huge territory, Brazil. That's a concession followed by a reversal, so A is correct. B might look right because the line's placement did cause an outcome, but Portugal's gain doesn't follow from Spain being favored. C might seem to work if you read Brazil as an example of the division, but it actually goes against the claim that Spain was favored instead of illustrating it. D treats the two sentences as similar, but they contrast with each other.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: history and civics — St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre 1572 and French religious violence targeting Protestant Huguenots during civil conflict

g.passage: For centuries, the St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre of 1572 was described as a carefully planned royal plot, with Catherine de' Medici supposedly arranging the killing of thousands of Protestant Huguenots across France. Surviving records do confirm that the crown ordered the deaths of a small group of Huguenot military leaders in Paris on the night of August 23–24. ______ the wider slaughter that spread to cities such as Lyon, Rouen, and Toulouse over the following weeks appears to have been carried out largely by local Catholic militias and crowds acting without any written instructions from the king.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 둘째 문장은 왕실이 파리의 소수 지도자 살해를 명령했다는 점을 인정하고(양보), 셋째 문장은 지방으로 번진 대규모 학살이 왕의 명령 없이 지역 민병대에 의해 이루어졌다고 말해 '계획된 왕실 음모'라는 통념을 반박한다. 따라서 양보 뒤에 반전을 표시하는 B가 정답이다. A는 파리 명령이 지방 폭력을 촉발했다는 인과로 읽힐 수 있지만, 셋째 문장의 핵심은 왕의 지시가 없었다는 대비이므로 결과 관계가 아니다. C는 두 사건이 모두 학살이라는 점에서 유사해 보이지만, 지문은 명령 유무를 대조하고 있다. D는 앞 내용을 강화하는 표현인데, 셋째 문장은 왕실 음모설을 강화하지 않고 오히려 그 범위를 제한한다.
g.explanation_en: The second sentence concedes that the crown did order the killing of a few Huguenot leaders in Paris. The third sentence then turns against the old "royal plot" view: it says the larger killings in other cities happened without written orders from the king. A concession followed by a reversal calls for a contrast, so B is correct. A might look logical, since the Paris killings could have set off violence elsewhere, but the third sentence is stressing the lack of royal orders, not describing a result. C and D don't fit either. C points to a similarity, but the text contrasts ordered and unordered violence. D would strengthen the idea of a royal plot, while the third sentence actually narrows it.
g.design: Without any word-level clue, students must see that the second sentence makes a concession and the third reverses the "planned plot" view. Choice A (cause-and-effect) and choice D (emphasis) can each seem right on a quick read.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: history and civics — Jacobite Rising 1745 Scotland and Bonnie Prince Charlie's failed rebellion against Hanoverian British monarchy

g.passage: In December 1745, Charles Edward Stuart's Jacobite army marched south from Scotland and reached Derby, roughly 125 miles from London, prompting a run on the Bank of England and rumors that King George II was preparing to flee. ______ the prince's commanders, noting that the promised uprising of English supporters and the expected French landing had both failed to materialize, voted to turn back toward Scotland, a retreat that ended months later in defeat at Culloden.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 첫 문장은 재커바이트 군이 런던 가까이까지 진격해 큰 공황을 일으켰다는 성공적 국면을 제시하고, 둘째 문장은 그럼에도 지휘관들이 퇴각을 결정했다는 반전을 서술하므로 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 퇴각이 런던의 공황 때문에 일어난 결과처럼 만들지만, 실제 퇴각 이유는 지원군과 프랑스군의 부재이며 진격의 성공이 퇴각을 낳은 것이 아니다. B는 두 문장을 비슷한 사건으로 묶지만 진격과 퇴각은 서로 대조된다. D는 둘째 문장을 첫 문장의 사례로 제시하지만 퇴각은 공황의 예가 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence describes the Jacobite army's apparent success: it got close to London and caused panic. The second sentence describes a reversal, since the commanders chose to retreat anyway, so the concession-then-contrast transition in C fits. A makes the retreat a result of the advance and the panic, but the text says the retreat happened because the English support and the French landing never came. B presents the two events as alike, but advancing and retreating are opposites here. D treats the retreat as an example of the panic, which it isn't.
g.design: This is a concession-then-reversal item with no cue word. A tempts a cause-and-effect reading, so you have to check what actually caused the retreat to rule it out.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: history and civics — Philippine-American War 1899-1902 and American colonial occupation following Spanish-American War

g.passage: After Spain ceded the Philippines to the United States in the 1898 Treaty of Paris, many American officials described the islands' new status as a period of "benevolent assimilation" that Filipinos would welcome. Emilio Aguinaldo and his supporters, who had already declared Philippine independence in June 1898, saw the arrangement very differently. ______ fighting broke out between American and Filipino forces in February 1899, beginning a war that would last officially until 1902 and claim the lives of hundreds of thousands of Filipino civilians.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 이미 독립을 선포한 아기날도 세력이 미국의 통치를 전혀 다르게 받아들였다는 내용이고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 결과로 1899년 전쟁이 발발했다는 내용이므로 인과 관계를 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 지문 전체에 미국의 '환영받을 것'이라는 기대와 실제 충돌 사이의 대비가 있어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 빈칸 바로 앞 문장(필리핀 측의 반대)과 전쟁 발발은 서로 대립하지 않고 오히려 자연스럽게 이어진다. B는 전쟁 발발이 '다르게 보았다'는 견해의 한 사례처럼 읽힐 수 있으나, 실제로는 그 견해에서 비롯된 결과이지 예시가 아니다. C는 앞 문장과 비슷한 내용을 덧붙일 때 쓰는 말인데, 뒤 문장은 비슷한 다른 사례가 아니라 새로 일어난 사건이다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank says that Aguinaldo's supporters, who had already declared independence, saw American rule very differently. The sentence after it describes the war that broke out as a result, so the relationship is cause and effect, and D is correct. A might look tempting because the passage as a whole does contrast American expectations with what actually happened. However, the sentence right before the blank is about Filipino opposition, and the outbreak of fighting follows from that opposition instead of contradicting it. B treats the war as an example of the Filipino view, but the war was a result of that view, not an illustration of it. C would add a similar point, but the final sentence describes a new event that grew out of the earlier one, not a parallel case.
g.design: 빈칸 앞 문장만 정독하면 인과가 분명하지만, 첫 문장의 미국 측 기대와 대비시켜 훑어 읽으면 Nevertheless를 고르도록 설계했고, For instance도 부분적 근거를 갖게 했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: history and civics — Boxer Rebellion 1900 China and anti-foreign peasant uprising against Western imperial missionary influence

g.passage: In 1899 and 1900, a severe drought struck northern China's Shandong and Zhili provinces, leaving many farmers without work or food. Rumors spread through the villages that foreign missionaries and Chinese Christian converts had angered local gods by rejecting traditional rituals, and that this was why the rains had stopped. ______ the Boxers, a loosely organized movement that claimed its martial-arts training made members immune to bullets, found eager recruits among idle young villagers that spring, and its attacks on mission stations spread quickly toward Beijing.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.design: 전환어 단서 없이 가뭄·굶주림·외국인 탓 소문(원인)과 의화단 모집 급증(결과)의 인과 방향을 파악해야 한다. 구체화(C)와 유사(D)는 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯하게 보이도록 배치했다.
g.explanation: 앞 문장들은 가뭄으로 일이 없고 굶주린 농민들, 그리고 가뭄을 선교사 탓으로 돌리는 소문이라는 원인을 제시한다. 빈칸 뒤 문장은 의화단이 한가한 젊은 농민들 사이에서 신병을 쉽게 모은 결과를 서술하므로 인과를 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 역접이지만, 가뭄과 반외세 소문은 모집을 막는 조건이 아니라 오히려 모집을 부추긴 조건이다. C는 뒤 문장이 앞 내용을 구체화한다고 보지만, 의화단 모집은 소문을 자세히 풀어 설명하는 것이 아니라 소문이 낳은 새로운 사건이다. D는 비슷한 사례를 나란히 놓는 표현인데, 뒤 문장은 앞의 내용과 평행한 사례가 아니라 그로 인한 결과다.
g.explanation_en: The earlier sentences give the causes: drought left farmers idle and hungry, and rumors blamed missionaries and converts for the missing rain. The sentence after the blank describes what followed: the Boxers easily recruited idle young villagers. That cause-and-effect relationship makes A correct. B signals contrast, but the hardship and anti-foreign rumors encouraged recruitment rather than working against it. C would mean the next sentence adds detail to the rumors, but the Boxers' recruitment is a new event caused by those conditions, not a closer explanation of them. D sets up a parallel example, yet the final sentence is a result of the earlier conditions, not a similar case.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: history and civics — Sykes-Picot Agreement 1916 and Anglo-French secret partition of Ottoman Middle Eastern territories

g.passage: In 1915 and 1916, British officials exchanged letters with Sharif Hussein of Mecca, suggesting that Britain would support an independent Arab state if he led a revolt against the Ottoman Empire. At the same time, British diplomat Mark Sykes and French diplomat François Georges-Picot secretly agreed to divide much of that same territory into British and French zones of control. After seizing power in Russia in 1917, the Bolsheviks published the secret agreement to expose the wartime deals of the Allied powers. ______ Arab leaders who had trusted British assurances came to view them with deep suspicion, a distrust that shaped negotiations at the postwar peace conferences.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 볼셰비키가 비밀 협정을 공개했다는 원인이고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 아랍 지도자들이 영국의 약속을 의심하게 되었다는 결과이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 지문 전체에 '약속 대 비밀 분할'이라는 대조가 있어 끌리지만, 그 대조는 첫 두 문장 사이의 관계이고 빈칸 앞뒤 문장은 서로 반대되지 않는다. C는 뒤 문장이 '전시 비밀 거래 폭로'의 한 사례가 아니라 그 폭로가 낳은 반응이므로 맞지 않는다. D는 두 문장이 서로 비슷한 사건을 나란히 놓는 관계가 아니므로 배제된다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank gives a cause: the Bolsheviks published the secret agreement. The sentence after it gives the effect: Arab leaders became suspicious of British assurances. That makes B the answer. A is tempting because the passage does contrast Britain's promises with the secret partition, but that contrast is between the first two sentences, and the sentences on either side of the blank don't oppose each other. C doesn't work because the Arab leaders' distrust isn't an example of the Allied deals being exposed; it's a reaction to that exposure. D doesn't fit because the second sentence doesn't describe a similar, parallel event.
g.design: The relationship isn't signaled by a vocabulary clue. Students have to see that the blank links a cause (the treaty is published) to its result (distrust). The passage's overall promise-versus-betrayal contrast makes "However" a trap for students who skim.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: history and civics — Easter Rising 1916 Dublin and Irish republican armed insurrection against British colonial rule

g.passage: When Irish republicans seized the General Post Office and other sites in Dublin on Easter Monday, 1916, many Dubliners reacted with hostility; some jeered the rebels as they were marched away after their surrender six days later. ______ the British authorities' decision to court-martial and execute fifteen of the rising's leaders over the following weeks transformed that mood, turning the executed men into martyrs and swelling support for the republican cause.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 첫 문장은 봉기 직후 더블린 시민들이 반란군에게 적대적이었다는 내용이고, 둘째 문장은 영국 당국의 처형이 그 분위기를 바꿔 공화주의 지지를 키웠다는 내용이므로 대조 관계이다. 그래서 C가 정답이다. A는 처형이 시간상 뒤에 일어나서 결과처럼 보이지만, 시민의 적대감이 처형을 불러온 것이 아니고 둘째 문장은 그 적대감이 뒤집힌 것을 말하므로 틀리다. B는 둘째 문장이 적대감의 사례가 아니라 반대되는 변화이므로 틀리다. D는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용이 아니라 반대되는 내용이므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence says that right after the rising, Dubliners were hostile to the rebels. The second sentence says the British executions changed that mood and built support for the republicans, so the two sentences contrast, and C is correct. A may look right because the executions came afterward, but the public's hostility didn't cause the executions, and the second sentence describes that hostility being reversed. B is wrong because the second sentence isn't an example of hostility; it shows the opposite change. D is wrong because the sentences describe opposite reactions, not similar ones.
g.design: 빈칸 앞뒤 문장에 'but' 같은 어휘 단서를 두지 않았다. 처형이 시간상 뒤에 일어나서 A(결과)가 그럴듯해 보이지만, 정독하면 첫 문장의 분위기가 반전된다는 것을 알아야 정답을 고를 수 있다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: history and civics — Spanish Civil War 1936-1939 and ideological conflict between fascists republicans foreshadowing World War Two

g.passage: Historians frequently describe the Spanish Civil War (1936–1939) as a prelude to the Second World War. Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy sent aircraft and troops to support Francisco Franco's Nationalists, while the Soviet Union supplied the Republican government, and the German bombing of Guernica in 1937 previewed tactics later used across Europe. ______ many of the Spaniards who actually fought saw the conflict in largely domestic terms: as a struggle over land reform, the political power of the Catholic Church, and Catalan and Basque autonomy rather than as one front in a continental clash of ideologies.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 첫 부분은 이 전쟁을 국제적 이념 대결, 즉 제2차 세계대전의 전조로 보는 통설과 그 근거(외국의 개입, 게르니카 폭격)를 제시한다. 빈칸 뒤 문장은 실제 전투원들이 이 전쟁을 국내 문제로 이해했다고 말하며, 앞의 시각과 대비되는 관점을 제시한다. 따라서 앞 내용을 인정하면서 반전시키는 D가 정답이다. A는 뒤 문장이 구체적 쟁점을 나열하므로 그럴듯해 보이지만, 그 쟁점들은 국제적 전조라는 앞 주장의 예시가 아니라 반대 관점이다. B는 외국 개입이 국내적 인식의 원인이 된다는 인과 관계를 잘못 설정하고, C는 앞 주장을 강화하는 표현이어서 대조를 담지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The first part of the text presents the common view that the war was a prelude to World War II and backs it with evidence (foreign intervention, the bombing of Guernica). The sentence after the blank says the Spaniards who fought mostly saw the war as a domestic conflict, which goes against the international framing. So you need a transition that accepts the earlier point and then turns away from it, and that is D. A might look right because the last sentence lists specific issues, but those issues aren't examples of the war as a prelude; they support the opposite view. B wrongly says foreign intervention caused the fighters' domestic view, and C would strengthen the earlier claim instead of setting up a contrast.
g.design: There's no "however"-type cue word in the text. The reader has to see the turn from the scholarly international framing to the fighters' domestic framing. The list of specific issues makes "For example," tempting, and "Indeed," tempts readers who skim.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: history and civics — Appeasement policy 1930s and British French diplomatic concessions to Nazi Germany expansion

g.passage: At the 1938 Munich Conference, British and French leaders allowed Nazi Germany to annex the Sudetenland, a border region of Czechoslovakia, after Adolf Hitler promised that it would be his final territorial demand in Europe. In March 1939, however, German troops occupied the rest of Czechoslovakia, showing that this promise had been empty. ______ the British government dropped its policy of concessions and publicly guaranteed that it would defend Poland's independence if Germany attacked.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 마지막 문장은 1939년 3월 독일이 약속을 어기고 체코슬로바키아 전체를 점령한 데 뒤따라 영국이 보인 반응, 즉 양보 정책을 버리고 폴란드 보장을 선언한 것을 서술하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 약속이 깨졌는데도 예상과 다른 일이 일어났다는 뜻이 되지만, 배신을 당한 뒤 정책을 바꾸는 것은 예상 밖의 일이 아니라 자연스러운 결과다. C는 영국의 정책 변화가 점령보다 먼저 일어났다고 시간 순서를 뒤집어 버린다. D는 폴란드 보장을 앞 문장의 사례로 만들지만, 이는 독일이 약속을 어긴 것의 사례가 아니라 그에 대한 대응이다.
g.explanation_en: The last sentence describes how Britain reacted after Germany broke its promise by occupying all of Czechoslovakia in March 1939: it dropped concessions and guaranteed Poland's independence. That makes A the answer, since it marks Britain's move as a reaction to the occupation. B would mean Britain did something unexpected despite the betrayal, but changing policy after being betrayed is the natural outcome, not a surprise. C flips the timeline by placing Britain's policy change before the occupation. D treats the guarantee to Poland as an example of the broken promise, but the guarantee was a response to that event, not an instance of it.
g.design: There is no vocabulary clue in the passage. Students have to see that the final sentence describes Britain's reaction to the March 1939 betrayal. B looks tempting because the passage includes a contrast ("however"), and C looks tempting because the passage moves through dates, so careless readers can fall for both.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Warsaw Ghetto Uprising 1943 and Jewish resistance against Nazi deportation to Treblinka extermination

g.passage: In January 1943, when German forces entered the Warsaw Ghetto to resume deportations to the Treblinka extermination camp, they met armed resistance from the Jewish Combat Organization (ŻOB) for the first time. The Germans withdrew after several days, having deported far fewer people than they had planned. Historians have long described the larger uprising that began that April as a revolt that had no realistic hope of defeating the German army, and in military terms that description is accurate. __Yet the fighters' own writings suggest that victory on the battlefield was never the measure by which they judged their actions.__ In a letter smuggled out of the ghetto, ŻOB commander Mordecai Anielewicz wrote that his dream had come true: he had seen Jewish self-defense in the ghetto "in all its greatness and glory." For Anielewicz and many others, resisting the deportations was itself the goal, because it refused the Germans the orderly compliance they had counted on.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It questions historians' claim that the uprising was unlikely to succeed by suggesting that the fighters had reason to expect a military victory.
It introduces a different way of judging the uprising, which the text then supports with evidence from a participant's own account.
It explains why German forces withdrew from the ghetto in January 1943 after meeting armed Jewish resistance.
It offers a conclusion about the fighters' goals that the quotation from Anielewicz is then presented as calling into question.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작하며, 역사가들의 군사적 평가(승산이 없었다)를 인정한 뒤 투사들 자신이 쓴 기준은 달랐다는 새로운 관점을 제시한다. 이어지는 Anielewicz의 편지 인용이 그 관점을 뒷받침하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 'Yet'의 대조를 잘못 읽은 것으로, 지문은 군사적 평가가 정확하다고 인정하고 있으며 투사들이 승리를 기대했다고 하지 않는다. C는 1월 철수를 다룬 앞부분 내용으로, 밑줄 문장의 역할이 아니다. D는 인용문이 밑줄 문장의 주장을 반박한다고 하지만, 실제로는 그 주장을 뒷받침한다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence starts with "Yet." The text has just agreed that, in military terms, the uprising could not succeed, and this sentence moves to a different standard: how the fighters themselves judged what they did. Anielewicz's smuggled letter then backs up that new standard, so B is correct. A misreads the contrast. The text accepts the military assessment and never says the fighters expected to win. C describes the January events, which come earlier in the text and are not what the underlined sentence does. D gets the relationship backward: the quotation supports the sentence's claim rather than calling it into question.
g.design: Medium difficulty: you have to catch the contrast signaled by "Yet" and then link the sentence to the quotation that follows it. A and D each get one part right (A notices the contrast with historians, D notices that a conclusion is followed by a quotation), so they can only be ruled out by comparing them closely with the text.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Rape of Nanking 1937 and Japanese military atrocities killing Chinese civilians during invasion

g.passage: Historians reconstructing the Nanjing Massacre, in which Japanese troops killed tens of thousands of Chinese civilians and disarmed soldiers after capturing the city in December 1937, have long relied on records kept by the Nanjing Safety Zone Committee, a group of Western residents who sheltered refugees. These documents are valuable because they were written as events unfolded. Some scholars have argued, however, that the committee's members, confined largely to the zone, could observe only a fraction of the violence. __Yet the diaries of Japanese soldiers, published decades later, describe killings in outlying villages that closely match the committee's reports of refugees arriving with accounts of those same incidents.__ Such convergence suggests that the committee's records, though limited in what members saw directly, captured a broader picture than critics have assumed.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that the committee's records were written later than historians had believed, which weakens their value as accounts made as events unfolded.
It presents evidence that Japanese soldiers' diaries are more reliable than the committee's records, which supports the scholars' doubts about the committee.
It presents evidence from an independent source that matches the committee's records, which limits the force of the scholars' objection.
It presents evidence that the committee's members traveled beyond the zone, which directly disproves the claim that their observations were limited.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해, 위원회가 일부만 보았다는 학자들의 반론에 맞서 독립적인 자료(일본군 일기)가 위원회 기록과 맞아떨어진다는 증거를 내놓는다. 그래서 마지막 문장에서 기록의 범위가 비판자들 생각보다 넓었다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 정답은 C이다. A는 작성 시점이 아니라 일기 출판 시점을 다루고 있으므로 틀렸다. B는 두 자료가 서로 일치한다는 것을 말할 뿐 우열을 따지지 않으며 오히려 반론을 약화시키므로 틀렸다. D는 위원들이 직접 이동했다는 내용이 없고, 지문도 직접 관찰이 제한적이었다는 점은 인정하므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence starts with "Yet," and it pushes back on the scholars' objection that the committee saw only part of the violence. It does this by showing that an independent source, Japanese soldiers' diaries, matches the committee's reports. The final sentence then concludes that the records cover more than critics assumed, so C is correct. A is wrong because the text dates the diaries' publication, not the committee's records. B is wrong because the sentence shows the two sources agree without ranking them, and it weakens the doubts rather than supporting them. D is wrong because members never travel beyond the zone in the text, and the text actually admits their direct observation was limited.
g.design: To pick the answer, students have to connect the sentence's contrast signal with the objection before it and the conclusion after it. Every option starts with "It presents evidence," so the wrong choices can only be ruled out by checking what the evidence is and how it relates to the objection.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: history and civics — Partition of India 1947 and violent Hindu-Muslim communal conflict displacing millions

g.passage: In August 1947, the British boundary commission led by lawyer Cyril Radcliffe, a man who had never before visited India, drew the lines dividing Punjab and Bengal between the new states of India and Pakistan in roughly five weeks. Because the final maps were not published until two days after independence ______ millions of Hindus, Muslims, and Sikhs living near the new borders did not know which country they belonged to, and the resulting panic fueled communal violence that displaced an estimated fifteen million people.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장은 종속절 "Because the final maps ... had been declared"로 시작하고, 주절 "millions of Hindus ... did not know"가 그 뒤에 이어진다. 앞에 오는 부사절과 주절 사이는 쉼표로 구분하므로 D가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론과 C의 콜론은 앞부분이 독립절이어야 쓸 수 있는데, 앞부분은 Because로 시작하는 불완전한 절이다. B는 쉼표+and로 두 독립절을 잇는 형식처럼 보이지만, 그렇게 하면 Because절이 주절과 끊어져 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: This sentence opens with a dependent clause, "Because the final maps ... had been declared," and the main clause, "millions of Hindus ... did not know," follows it. When an introductory adverbial clause comes before the main clause, you separate the two with a comma, so D is correct. A (semicolon) and C (colon) both need a complete independent clause before the mark, but the text before the blank begins with "Because," so it isn't one. B uses comma plus "and," the pattern for joining two independent clauses, but adding "and" here cuts the Because clause off from its main clause, and the sentence falls apart.
g.design: 문장 앞쪽에 동격 수식어(a man who...)와 긴 종속절을 두어 독자가 Because를 잊고 독립절로 착각하게 했다. 그래서 세미콜론, 콜론, 쉼표+and가 그럴듯해 보인다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: history and civics — Korean War 1950-1953 and Cold War proxy conflict between American Soviet-backed regional powers

g.passage: Historians often describe the Korean War as one of the first proxy conflicts of the Cold War. North Korea, armed and advised by the Soviet Union, invaded the South in June 1950, and the United States, acting under a United Nations mandate, quickly sent troops to defend the government in Seoul. The fighting, which ended in an armistice in July 1953 rather than in a formal peace ______ left the peninsula divided near the same line where the war had begun.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The fighting"이고 본동사는 "left"이며, 그 사이의 "which ended ... formal peace treaty"는 쉼표로 열린 비제한적 관계절이다. 따라서 관계절을 닫는 쉼표가 필요하므로 A가 정답이다. B의 세미콜론은 주어와 본동사를 떼어 놓아 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. C는 여는 쉼표만 있고 닫는 쉼표가 없어 삽입절의 끝이 표시되지 않는다. D는 "and left"가 관계절 안의 두 번째 동사가 되어 버려 주어 "The fighting"에 본동사가 남지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The fighting," and its main verb is "left." Between them sits a nonessential relative clause, "which ended ... formal peace treaty," and it opens with a comma. That clause needs a closing comma too, so A is correct. B is wrong because a semicolon would split the subject from its verb, and the words before it can't stand alone as an independent clause. C is wrong because it leaves out the closing comma, so nothing marks where the clause ends. D is wrong because "and left" turns "left" into a second verb inside the relative clause, which leaves "The fighting" with no main verb.
g.design: There's a long nonessential relative clause between the subject and the main verb, so you have to find the sentence's main structure before you can tell that a closing comma is needed. The wrong choices are each plausible in a different way: a semicolon, no punctuation, and comma plus "and."

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: history and civics — Hungarian Revolution 1956 and anti-Soviet uprising crushed by Warsaw Pact tank intervention

g.passage: Imre Nagy, a reform-minded communist who had been forced out of power by Hungary's hard-line leadership the previous year, was reinstated as prime minister in the first days of the 1956 uprising______ he announced Hungary's withdrawal from the Warsaw Pact, a decision that helped prompt Soviet tanks to roll back into Budapest on November 4.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Imre Nagy ... was reinstated ... uprising"은 긴 동격구가 들어 있어도 그 자체로 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 "he announced ..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있고, 도입 부사구 "within days" 뒤의 쉼표도 맞으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 두 절 사이에 아무 문장부호도 없어 run-on 문장이 된다. D는 관계대명사 "which"를 넣었지만 뒤에 주어 "he"가 이미 있어 관계절이 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The part before the blank, "Imre Nagy ... was reinstated ... uprising," is a complete independent clause even though it contains a long appositive. The part after it, "he announced ...," is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, and the comma after the introductory phrase "within days" is correct, so B is the answer. A joins the two clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses, so it is a run-on sentence. D adds "which," but the clause after it already has the subject "he," so the relative clause doesn't work grammatically.
g.design: This is a medium question. The long appositive inside the first clause hides where that clause actually ends, so you first have to see that there are two independent clauses and then choose the right way to join them. A looks plausible because of the commas around the introductory phrase, and D looks plausible because it seems to link the clauses, but both have to be compared with B before you can rule them out.

- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: history and civics — Cuban Missile Crisis 1962 and nuclear standoff between Kennedy Khrushchev bringing world to brink

g.passage: In October 1962, after American U-2 reconnaissance flights photographed Soviet medium-range missile sites being built in western Cuba, President John F. Kennedy and his advisers faced a stark ______ they could order air strikes to destroy the sites before they became operational, accepting the risk of Soviet retaliation, or they could impose a naval "quarantine" of the island and hope that Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev would negotiate.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "President ... faced a stark dilemma"는 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 "they could order air strikes ... or they could impose ..."도 완전한 독립절로서 앞의 'dilemma'의 두 선택지를 구체적으로 설명한다. 따라서 앞 절을 설명·부연하는 콜론을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 세미콜론 뒤에 "that they could..."라는 종속절만 남아 세미콜론 뒤가 독립절이 아니므로 틀린다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "President John F. Kennedy and his advisers faced a stark dilemma," is a complete independent clause. The text after it, "they could order air strikes ... or they could impose ...," is also an independent clause, and it spells out what the dilemma was. A colon is the right way to introduce an explanation like this, so C is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes it a comma splice. B joins them with no punctuation at all, which makes it a run-on sentence. D puts a semicolon before "that they could...," but that is a dependent clause, and a semicolon has to be followed by an independent clause.
g.design: 이 문항에서는 앞에 긴 도입 부사절이 붙은 독립절이 오고 그 뒤에 or로 연결된 두 선택지를 설명하는 절이 이어지도록 해서, 학생이 두 단계로 판단하게 했다. 먼저 빈칸 앞뒤가 모두 독립절인지 확인하고, 그다음 뒷절이 앞절을 설명한다는 관계를 파악해야 한다. 오답은 모두 같은 dilemma + they 틀을 유지해 문장부호만 비교하도록 구성했다.

c.seed: history and civics — Tet Offensive 1968 Vietnam and coordinated North Vietnamese surprise attack shifting American public opinion

g.passage: In late January 1968, during the Lunar New Year holiday known as Tet, North Vietnamese and Viet Cong forces launched coordinated attacks on more than one hundred cities and towns across South Vietnam. Militarily, the offensive was costly for the attackers, who failed to hold most of the positions they ______ the sheer scale of the assault, which included a brief breach of the US embassy compound in Saigon, contradicted official American assurances that the enemy was nearly defeated and deepened public doubts about the war.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Militarily ... seized'와 뒤 'the sheer scale ... contradicted ... doubts'는 각각 독립절이므로 경계에 세미콜론이 필요하고, 'however'는 뒤 절에 속하는 접속부사로 'politically, however,'처럼 앞뒤를 쉼표로 감싸야 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 연결한 comma splice이다. B는 세미콜론을 however 뒤에 두어 'politically, however'가 앞 절에 붙게 되어 의미상 대조(군사적/정치적) 구조가 무너진다. C는 경계는 맞지만 however 뒤 쉼표가 빠져 삽입 요소가 주어 앞에서 제대로 분리되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Militarily ... seized") and the text after it ("the sheer scale ... deepened public doubts about the war") are both independent clauses, so a semicolon has to mark the boundary between them. "However" is a conjunctive adverb that belongs to the second clause, and together with "politically" it is an introductory element, so it needs a comma after it: "politically, however," — that makes D correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. B puts the semicolon after "however," which attaches "politically, however" to the first clause and breaks the military-versus-political contrast. C places the boundary correctly but leaves out the comma after "however," so the introductory element isn't set off from the subject.
g.design: 긴 관계절 뒤 절 경계와 접속부사 위치를 함께 판단하게 했다. B와 C는 각각 경계 부호나 쉼표 하나만 맞아서, 선택지끼리 비교해야 걸러진다.

c.seed: history and civics — Tiananmen Square protest 1989 and Chinese student democracy movement suppressed by government tanks

g.passage: In the spring of 1989, thousands of students gathered in Beijing's Tiananmen Square to call for political reform. Their demonstration, which began as a mourning gathering for Hu Yaobang, a reform-minded official who had died in April, grew to include workers and other citizens over the following ______ on the night of June 3, the government sent troops and tanks into the city to clear the square by force.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 삽입절(which ... April)을 걷어내면 'Their demonstration ... grew ... over the following weeks'가 하나의 독립절이고, 'the government sent troops ...'가 또 하나의 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 이어야 하며 'then'은 접속부사이므로 세미콜론 뒤에 오고 쉼표가 뒤따르는 A가 정답이다. B는 접속부사 then을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 두 절 사이에 아무 경계도 없어 run-on 문장이 된다. D는 세미콜론을 쓰기는 했지만 then 뒤에 붙여 then을 첫째 절에 넣어 버려 'over the following weeks then'이라는 어색한 구조가 되고, 둘째 절의 시간 연결이 깨진다.
g.explanation_en: If you set aside the long nonessential clause (which ... April), "Their demonstration ... grew ... over the following weeks" is one independent clause, and "the government sent troops ..." is a second independent clause. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, and "then" is a conjunctive adverb, so it should come after the semicolon and be followed by a comma. That's choice A, so A is correct. Choice B joins the clauses with only a comma before "then," which makes a comma splice. Choice C puts no punctuation between the clauses at all, so it's a run-on. Choice D does use a semicolon, but it puts the semicolon after "then," which attaches "then" to the first clause ("over the following weeks then") and breaks its time link to the second clause.
g.design: A long appositive and relative clause hide where the first independent clause ends, so students have to find the clause boundary and also figure out which clause the conjunctive adverb "then" belongs to. B and D each get part of the rule right (a comma after "then," or a semicolon), and that makes them tempting.

c.seed: history and civics — Rwandan genocide 1994 and Hutu extremist massacre of Tutsi minority ethnic cleansing

g.passage: During the 1994 genocide in Rwanda, Hutu extremists killed an estimated 800,000 people, most of them members of the Tutsi minority, in about one hundred days. Mass media played a central role in the killing. Radio Télévision Libre des Mille Collines (RTLM), a privately owned station that repeatedly called Tutsi "cockroaches" and read out the names and locations of people to be hunted down by militia members ______ became one of the most notorious tools of the violence. Years later, the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda convicted several of the station's founders of inciting genocide.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "Radio Télévision Libre des Mille Collines (RTLM)"이고 동사는 "became"이다. 그 사이의 "a privately owned station that ... militia members"는 쉼표로 시작된 비필수 동격구이므로 같은 부호인 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론은 두 독립절 사이에만 쓰는데, 여기서는 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞뒤 모두 완전한 절이 되지 않는다. C의 대시도 삽입구를 닫을 수는 있지만, 쉼표로 시작한 삽입구를 대시로 닫으면 부호가 맞지 않는다. D는 동격구를 닫지 않아 "militia members became"처럼 읽혀 militia members가 became의 주어인 것처럼 문장 구조가 잘못 해석된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "Radio Télévision Libre des Mille Collines (RTLM)," and its verb is "became." The phrase in between, "a privately owned station that ... militia members," is a nonessential appositive that opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma too. That makes B correct. A doesn't work because a semicolon belongs only between two independent clauses, and here it would cut the subject off from its verb, so neither side is a complete clause. C is tempting because a dash can close an interruption, but an interruption that opens with a comma can't close with a dash, since the punctuation has to match. D leaves the appositive open, so the sentence reads as "militia members became," as if the militia members were the subject of "became," and that misreads the sentence's structure.
g.design: The appositive opens long before the blank, and a relative clause follows inside it. Students have to find the true subject and verb, then match the punctuation that closes the appositive to the comma that opens it. The dash and no-punctuation options look plausible on a quick read.

c.seed: history and civics — Yugoslav Wars 1991-2001 and Balkan ethnic conflicts dissolving multiethnic Soviet successor state

g.passage: Although Yugoslavia had broken with Moscow in 1948 and was never part of the Soviet bloc, the multiethnic federation still came apart along national lines as communist rule weakened across Eastern Europe. In June 1991, Slovenia and Croatia, two of the federation's six constituent republics, formally declared independence ______ within months, fighting between Croatian forces and Serb-led units of the Yugoslav People's Army had spread across much of Croatia.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Slovenia and Croatia ... formally declared independence"는 삽입된 동격구가 있어도 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 "within months, fighting ... had spread across much of Croatia"도 주어 fighting과 동사 had spread를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 접속 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 관계대명사 which를 넣었지만 뒤 절에 이미 주어 fighting이 있어 which가 문장에서 할 역할이 없으므로 비문이다. D는 "declared independence within months"로 자연스럽게 읽혀 그럴듯해 보이지만, 문장부호 없이 두 독립절이 붙어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The part before the blank, "Slovenia and Croatia ... formally declared independence," is a complete independent clause, even with the appositive phrase in the middle. The part after it, "within months, fighting ... had spread across much of Croatia," is also an independent clause, with the subject "fighting" and the verb "had spread." A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so C is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B adds "which," but the second clause already has its own subject, "fighting," so "which" has no job to do and the sentence is ungrammatical. D might look fine because "declared independence within months" reads smoothly, but it runs two independent clauses together with no punctuation, which makes a run-on sentence.
g.design: The appositive in the middle and the phrase "independence within months," which reads smoothly at first, hide where the clause boundary is. To answer, students have to find the subject and verb of the second clause and then pick the right punctuation.

g.passage: The Slavery Abolition Act of 1833 did not immediately free enslaved people across most of the British Empire. Instead, it created a system of "apprenticeship," under which formerly enslaved adults in colonies such as Jamaica and Barbados were still required to work without pay for their former ______ this arrangement, originally intended to last until 1840, collapsed early under widespread resistance and public pressure, and full emancipation came in 1838.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: enslavers for up to forty-five hours each week,
enslavers, for up to forty-five hours each week
enslavers for up to forty-five hours each week, but,
enslavers for up to forty-five hours each week;
g.design: 빈칸 뒤에 'originally intended to last until 1840'라는 삽입 수식어가 있어 두 번째 독립절의 주어와 동사(arrangement ... collapsed)가 떨어져 있다. 이 때문에 절 경계를 판단하기가 어렵다. 쉼표만 쓴 오답, 아무 부호도 없는 오답, 접속사 뒤에 쉼표를 잘못 붙인 오답을 함께 비교하게 했다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 "under which ... week"는 관계절이지만, 이를 포함한 앞 문장은 "it created a system"을 중심으로 한 독립절이다. 빈칸 뒤의 "this arrangement ... collapsed early"도 삽입구 때문에 주어와 동사가 떨어져 있을 뿐 독립절이다. 따라서 두 독립절을 세미콜론으로 연결한 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. B는 시간 표현 앞에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣고, 두 절 사이에는 아무 부호도 두지 않아 run-on 문장이 된다. C는 등위접속사 but을 쓴 점은 맞지만 but 뒤에 쉼표를 붙여, 접속사와 그 뒤 절을 잘못 끊어 놓았다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank form an independent clause built on "it created a system," even though they contain the relative clause "under which...". The words after the blank, "this arrangement ... collapsed early," are also an independent clause; the inserted phrase "originally intended to last until 1840" just separates its subject from its verb. So you need a semicolon between the two clauses, which makes D correct. A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, so it creates a comma splice. B adds an unneeded comma before the time phrase and puts no punctuation between the two clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence. C is right to use the conjunction "but," but the comma after "but" wrongly cuts the conjunction off from the clause it introduces.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: history and civics — Berlin Blockade 1948-1949 and Soviet attempted starvation of West Berlin defeated by airlift

g.passage: In June 1948, Soviet authorities severed every road, rail, and canal link into West Berlin, an enclave of more than two million residents surrounded on all sides by the Soviet occupation zone______ American and British planners organized an airlift that would eventually deliver over two million tons of coal, flour, and other supplies before the blockade was lifted in May 1949.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격구(an enclave ... zone)로 끝나지만 "Soviet authorities severed..."라는 독립절이 이미 완성되어 있고, 빈칸 뒤 "American and British planners organized..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 run-on이 된다. D는 관계대명사 which를 넣었지만 뒤의 절이 이미 주어와 동사를 모두 갖추고 있어서 which가 할 역할이 없고, 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The long appositive (an enclave ... zone) comes at the end of a complete independent clause, "Soviet authorities severed every road...," and the text after the blank, "American and British planners organized...," is also an independent clause. A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so A is correct. B joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D adds the relative pronoun "which," but the clause after it already has its own subject and verb, so "which" has no job to do and the sentence doesn't work grammatically.
g.design: The long appositive hides where the first independent clause ends, so you have to spot that boundary and then confirm that what follows is a full clause. B and D look plausible because each seems to keep modifying the appositive.

c.seed: history and civics — Mao Great Leap Forward 1958-1962 and catastrophic famine from collectivization policies killing millions

g.passage: Launched in 1958, the Great Leap Forward was meant to transform China from an agrarian society into an industrial power within a few years. Rural households were merged into vast people's communes, and local officials, eager to impress Beijing with record harvests, ______ the state then requisitioned grain on the basis of those inflated numbers, leaving villages with too little to eat. Historians estimate that the resulting famine, which lasted until 1962, killed tens of millions of people.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 "local officials ... routinely exaggerated grain yields"는 쉼표로 둘러싼 삽입구(eager to impress...)를 품은 독립절이고, 뒤의 "the state then requisitioned..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 쉼표+and로 문법적으로 보이지만, 앞 절이 이미 "Rural households were merged..., and local officials..."로 and에 의해 연결되어 있어 세 절이 쉼표+and로 나열되면서 then과 함께 구조가 어색해지고 연결이 중복된다. D는 아무 부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다.
g.explanation_en: Before the blank, "local officials ... routinely exaggerated grain yields" is a complete independent clause, even with the interrupting phrase "eager to impress Beijing with record harvests" inside it. After the blank, "the state then requisitioned grain..." is also an independent clause. A semicolon is the standard way to join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C may look acceptable, but the sentence already uses ", and" to link its first two clauses, so adding another ", and" strings three clauses together awkwardly and makes "then" repeat the linking job; the semicolon sets off the result clearly. D puts no punctuation between the clauses, which makes a run-on sentence.
g.design: 긴 삽입구 뒤에서 절 경계를 찾아야 하며, 쉼표+and(C)를 그럴듯한 오답으로 두어 문장 전체 구조를 확인해야 배제되게 했다.

c.seed: history and civics — Iran-Contra affair 1985-1987 and Reagan administration secret arms sales funding Nicaraguan rebels

g.passage: The Boland Amendment, a series of measures that Congress passed between 1982 and 1984 to restrict US involvement in Nicaragua's civil war, had banned federal agencies from funding the Contra rebels ______ the Reagan administration's secret diversion of profits from covert arms sales to Iran into Contra accounts, revealed to the public in November 1986, therefore directly defied the will of the legislature.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞뒤가 모두 독립절이지만, 앞에는 긴 동격구가 있고 뒤에는 긴 주어와 삽입구가 있어 경계가 잘 보이지 않는다. 오답은 쉼표 단독(comma splice), 관계사(목적어 중복), 쉼표 없는 접속사 'and'로 구성해 'therefore'의 역할을 확인해야 배제되게 했다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'The Boland Amendment ... had banned ... rebels'는 독립절이다. 빈칸 뒤 'the Reagan administration's secret diversion ... therefore directly defied the will of the legislature'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이므로, 두 절을 잇는 세미콜론을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절 두 개를 이어 comma splice가 된다. B는 'which'가 'defied'의 목적어 역할을 해야 하는데 'defied' 뒤에 이미 목적어 'the will'이 있어 관계절이 성립하지 않는다. D는 접속사 'and' 앞에 쉼표가 없고, 뒤 절의 'therefore'가 이미 논리 관계를 나타내므로 앞 절과 매끄럽게 이어지지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "The Boland Amendment ... had banned federal agencies from funding the Contra rebels," is an independent clause. The text after it, "the Reagan administration's secret diversion ... therefore directly defied the will of the legislature," is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb, so C is correct: a semicolon joins the two clauses. A connects the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B doesn't work because "which" would have to be the object of "defied," but "defied" already has an object, "the will." D leaves out the comma that should come before "and" when it joins two long independent clauses, and "therefore" in the second clause already shows how the ideas connect, so the joined sentence is awkward and run-on.

g.passage: In March 1965, civil rights demonstrators twice tried to walk from Selma, Alabama, to the state capitol in Montgomery, a route of roughly fifty-four miles along U.S. Highway 80______ third attempt, protected by federalized National Guard troops, finally reached Montgomery on March 25 with some 25,000 marchers, adding pressure that helped secure passage of the Voting Rights Act that August.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: The blank comes right after a long appositive ('a route of ... Highway 80'), which makes it hard to see where the first independent clause ends. The second clause is also lengthened by the participial phrase 'protected by ...'. A comma splice, a run-on, and a colon+conjunction combination serve as attractive distractors.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'demonstrators twice tried ... Highway 80'는 동격구까지 포함한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'the third attempt ... finally reached ...' 역시 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 되며, 긴 동격구 뒤라서 쉼표가 자연스러워 보일 뿐이다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. C는 콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 'and'를 쓴 비표준 결합이고, 뒤 절이 앞 절을 설명하거나 부연하지도 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, 'demonstrators twice tried ... Highway 80', is an independent clause, even with the long appositive attached. The text after it, 'the third attempt ... finally reached ...', is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so D is correct. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice; the comma only seems natural because it follows the long appositive. B puts no punctuation between the clauses, which makes a run-on sentence. C puts the conjunction 'and' after a colon, a nonstandard combination, and the second clause doesn't explain or expand on the first anyway.

g.passage: On July 14, 1789, crowds of Parisian artisans, shopkeepers, and laborers converged on the Bastille, a medieval fortress that had long held prisoners detained by royal order without trial. The attackers were seeking gunpowder stored inside, but the fortress's fall carried a meaning far greater than its military value. The Bastille, a symbol of the arbitrary power wielded by King Louis XVI and his ______ within days, citizens had begun dismantling its walls stone by stone.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ministers, was quickly targeted for demolition;
ministers was quickly targeted for demolition;
ministers, was quickly targeted for demolition,
ministers; was quickly targeted for demolition,
g.explanation: "a symbol of ... ministers"는 주어 The Bastille에 대한 비필수 동격구이므로 앞뒤에 쉼표가 짝을 이뤄야 하고, 이어지는 "within days, citizens had begun..."은 독립절이므로 두 독립절 사이에 세미콜론이 필요하다. A가 두 조건을 모두 충족한다. B는 세미콜론은 맞지만 동격구를 닫는 쉼표가 빠졌다. C는 동격구는 올바르게 닫았으나 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. D는 주어와 동사 사이에 세미콜론을 넣어 문장을 끊고 뒤에서 쉼표 스플라이스까지 만든다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "a symbol of ... ministers" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject, The Bastille, so it needs a comma on both sides. After that, "within days, citizens had begun..." is an independent clause, so you need a semicolon between the two independent clauses. A meets both requirements. B has the correct semicolon but leaves out the comma that closes the appositive. C closes the appositive correctly, but it joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. D puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, splitting the sentence, and then adds a comma splice later on.
g.design: To answer, the student has to make two decisions: close the appositive with a comma after a long modifier, and mark the boundary between two clauses with a semicolon. B and C each get one of these right, so the student must compare them with A to rule them out.

c.seed: history and civics — Treaty of Versailles 1919 and punitive terms imposed on defeated Germany enabling Hitler rise

g.passage: Historians have long debated how much the Treaty of Versailles contributed to Adolf Hitler's rise. Some argue that the treaty's terms, though harsh, were not unusually severe by the standards of the era. Even these scholars concede, however, that many Germans experienced the war-guilt clause and the heavy reparations as deeply humiliating, and that Hitler skillfully ______ this resentment, presenting himself as the leader who would overturn a dishonorable peace and restore national pride.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에서 히틀러가 굴욕적인 평화를 뒤집을 지도자로 자신을 내세웠다고 하므로, 그가 대중의 분노를 정치적으로 이용했다는 뜻이 필요하다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 분노를 숨겼다는 뜻이 되어 분노를 공개적으로 부추긴 맥락과 반대된다. C는 히틀러도 독일인으로서 그 분노를 함께 겪었다고 볼 수 있어 그럴듯하지만, 'skillfully'와 지도자로서의 자기 연출이라는 능동적·전략적 행동을 담지 못한다. D는 분노를 기록했다는 학자적 행위를 뜻해 정치적 동원이라는 맥락과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text says Hitler presented himself as the leader who would overturn a dishonorable peace, so the blank needs a word meaning he used Germans' resentment for political gain. That makes B correct. A would mean he hid the resentment, which is the opposite of openly stirring it up. C might seem reasonable because Hitler, as a German, also lived through the resentment, but it doesn't fit "skillfully" or the strategic way he presented himself as a leader. D describes recording the resentment, which is what a scholar does, not what a politician mobilizing a population does.
g.design: 빈칸 뒤의 정치적 자기 연출과 'skillfully'를 연결해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. 'endured'와 'documented'는 분노와 관련은 있지만 능동적·전략적 의미가 없어서 정답과 비교해 봐야 배제된다.

A, "dispute," fits partly because the new work did challenge older estimates, but it doesn't describe the precise result that comes from comparing numbers. B, "publicize," sounds plausible for research, but it has nothing to do with the method of comparing records or with precision. g.design: Distractors draw partial support from nearby cues (pirates→defend, power/territory→conquer, tolls→afford); only reading through to the consequence clause confirms "bypass."

g.explanation_en: The phrase after the blank, "placing scripture and prayer manuals within reach of merchants and artisans who had never before owned a book," explains what the blank means, so A, saying the books became available to many people, is correct. B might seem related to the rarity of hand-copied books, but the passage is about spreading books, not preserving them. C describes how the books looked, which has nothing to do with more people owning them. D is tempting because mass printing does create identical copies, but the sentence stresses new readers gaining access, not consistent content.
g.design: 빈칸 뒤 부연 구절과 연결하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. D(대량 인쇄로 인한 균일성)와 B(필사본의 희소성)는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가진 오답으로 설계했다.

C, "postponed," might seem to fit with the timing phrase "from its earliest weeks," but delaying the revolt contradicts the idea that these resources shaped it. D, "publicized," might seem to fit with communication networks, but the passage is about how the revolt was organized internally, not about spreading word of it.
g.design: To answer, you have to link "giving shape to... organized" with the blank and also notice that the idea of borrowing belongs to the view the passage rejects. A, C, and D each tie to one surface clue in the passage (borrowing, timing, communication).

g.passage: Historians once portrayed the Meiji Restoration of 1868 as a clean break in which Japan's new leaders swept away feudal society almost overnight.
