While the government did abolish the samurai class's hereditary stipends and build a conscript army on European models, many former samurai found new roles as bureaucrats, police officers, and factory managers, carrying older habits of hierarchy and discipline into modern institutions. In this view, the Restoration did not erase the feudal order so much as ______ it, turning its personnel and values toward new purposes.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 메이지 유신이 봉건 질서를 지운 것이 아니라 그 인력과 가치를 새로운 목적으로 돌렸다고 말하므로, '다른 용도로 바꿔 쓰다'라는 뜻의 C가 정답이다. A는 '해체하다'로, 'not erase … so much as' 구조가 요구하는 대조를 만들지 못하고 지워 버렸다는 옛 견해를 되풀이한다. B는 옛 관습이 이어졌다는 점에서 일부 맞지만, 그것들이 '새로운 목적'으로 돌려졌다는 변화를 담지 못한다. D는 유럽식 군대 모델에서 연상되는 단어이지만, 봉건 질서를 '모방'했다는 것은 같은 사람과 가치를 직접 다시 썼다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the Restoration took the feudal order's people and values and turned them "toward new purposes," so C, "repurpose," is the most precise choice. A, "dismantle," would mean the same thing as "erase," but the sentence structure "not erase... so much as" needs a contrast, and A just repeats the older view the passage argues against. B, "preserve," fits the idea that old habits carried on, but it misses the key point that those habits were put to new uses. D, "imitate," may bring to mind the European military models, but the government didn't copy feudalism. It reused feudalism's actual people and values directly.
g.design: To get this right, you have to see the contrast set up by "not erase... so much as" and also connect it to the final phrase about continuity plus new purposes. B is partly right (continuity) and A is partly right (change), but only C covers both.

g.passage: Historians often describe Britain's Factory Act of 1833 as a turning point in labor law, but its early effect on mill floors was limited. g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 1833년 법이 이미 제정되었지만 감독관이 너무 적어 공장주들이 법을 어겼고, 이후 감독관을 늘리고 연령 증명을 의무화한 뒤에야 법이 실제로 지켜지게 되었다는 점이다. 따라서 '실제로 집행되다'를 뜻하는 D가 정답이다. A는 법의 초안 작성을 뜻하는데, 1833년 규정은 이미 작성되어 통과된 상태였으므로 맞지 않는다. B는 알리는 것을 뜻하지만, 지문은 공장주들이 법을 알고도 단속이 없어서 어겼다고 하므로 문제는 홍보가 아니었다. C는 '이의를 제기하다'라는 뜻인데, 추가 감독관과 연령 증명은 법에 맞서는 것이 아니라 법을 뒷받침하는 조치이다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the 1833 act had already been passed, but with only four inspectors, mill owners could break it without much risk. Only later acts that added inspectors and required proof of age made the limits actually work in practice, so D, "enforced," is correct. A doesn't fit because the restrictions had already been drafted and passed in 1833. B is wrong because the problem wasn't that people didn't know about the law; the owners knew about it and ignored it because inspections were unlikely. C is wrong because more inspectors and proof-of-age rules supported the law instead of opposing it.
g.design: 'publicized'와 'drafted'는 법 관련 어휘라 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯해 보이지만, 이미 법이 통과되었다는 정보와 공장주들이 법을 알고 있었다는 정보를 함께 읽어야 배제된다. 정답 단어는 지문이나 질문에 직접 나오지 않는다.

g.passage: When the Union Navy began its blockade of Southern ports in 1861, it had too few ships to seal more than 3,500 miles of coastline, and fast blockade runners slipped through often. Historians who judge the strategy only by how many runners were caught miss its broader effect, however. Because the risk of capture drove up shipping insurance and freight costs, imported goods such as salt, medicine, and railroad iron became scarce and expensive across the Confederacy. The blockade did not have to stop every vessel to work; by steadily raising the cost of trade, it ______ the Southern economy over four years rather than defeating it in a single stroke.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 봉쇄가 모든 배를 막지는 못했지만 무역 비용을 '꾸준히' 올려 '4년에 걸쳐' 효과를 냈고, '한 번에 무찌른' 것은 아니라고 설명한다. 따라서 점진적으로 약화시켰다는 뜻의 A(wore down)가 가장 정확하다. B(cut off)는 봉쇄와 관련된 말이라 그럴듯하지만, 지문은 배들이 자주 빠져나갔다고 하므로 완전한 차단을 뜻하는 표현과 맞지 않는다. C(took over)는 연방이 남부 경제를 장악했다는 뜻으로, 지문에 나오지 않는 통제를 암시한다. D(stirred up)는 경제를 자극하거나 활성화한다는 뜻이라 물자 부족과 가격 상승이라는 내용과 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the blockade didn't stop every ship but kept "steadily raising the cost of trade" "over four years," and it didn't defeat the economy "in a single stroke." So you need a phrase meaning gradual weakening, and choice A, "wore down," fits that best. Choice B, "cut off," is tempting because it sounds like what a blockade does, but the text says runners got through often, so the South wasn't fully cut off. Choice C, "took over," suggests the Union took control of the Southern economy, and nothing in the text supports that. Choice D, "stirred up," means stimulating or agitating something, which goes against the scarcity and high prices the text describes.

g.passage: At the Berlin Conference of 1884–1885, delegates from fourteen states, most of them European, set rules for claiming territory in Africa. No African ruler or representative was invited to take part. Historians often point out that the conference did not actually hand out most of the land; that division came later, through treaties and military campaigns. Even so, the meeting's principle of "effective occupation," which held that a claim was valid only if the claiming power kept a real presence there, ______ the scramble that followed: it encouraged rival powers to rush officials and troops inland to secure territory before their competitors could get there.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 콜론 뒤 문장은 이 원칙 때문에 경쟁국들이 경쟁자보다 먼저 영토를 차지하려고 서둘렀다고 설명하므로, 원칙이 쟁탈전을 '가속화했다'는 B가 정답이다. A(끝냈다)는 회의 이후 분할이 이어졌다는 문맥과 반대이다. C(기록했다)는 회의가 원칙을 문서로 정했다는 점에서 그럴듯해 보이지만, 원칙이 이후 행동을 부추겼다는 인과 관계는 담지 못한다. D(예견했다)는 원칙이 나중의 쟁탈전보다 먼저 나왔다는 순서와는 맞지만, '부추겼다'는 능동적 영향은 표현하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The clause after the colon says the principle pushed rival powers to rush inland before their competitors could, so the principle sped up the scramble. That makes B, "accelerated," correct. A ("concluded") contradicts the text, which says the division continued after the conference. C ("documented") sounds plausible because the conference did write down rules, but it misses the cause-and-effect link: the principle drove what came next. D ("anticipated") fits the timeline, since the principle came before the scramble, but it only means the principle predicted the scramble, not that it actively encouraged it.
g.design: 오답 C·D는 각각 '문서화'와 '시간상 선행'이라는 부분적 근거가 있어 콜론 뒤의 인과 관계(encouraged... rush)를 확인해야만 배제할 수 있다. A는 'scramble을 끝냈다'로 표면상 말은 되지만 문맥과 모순된다.

g.passage: Popular accounts often describe the Bolsheviks' seizure of power in October 1917 as the moment that ended tsarist autocracy in Russia. Historian Sheila Fitzpatrick has noted that this framing ______ two distinct episodes: Tsar Nicholas II had already abdicated months earlier, during the February Revolution, and the Bolsheviks took control not from the monarchy but from the Provisional Government that had replaced it.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 대중적 서술이 2월의 차르 퇴위와 10월 볼셰비키의 임시정부 전복이라는 '서로 다른 두 사건'을 하나로 합쳐 버린다고 지적하므로, 별개의 것을 혼동해 하나로 묶는다는 뜻의 C(conflates)가 정답이다. A는 서술이 사실을 과장한다는 뜻이라 그럴듯하지만, 지문이 문제 삼는 것은 규모의 과장이 아니라 두 사건을 하나로 뭉뚱그린 점이다. D는 순서 문제처럼 보이지만, 대중적 서술은 사건의 순서를 뒤바꾸는 것이 아니라 앞선 사건을 뒤의 사건 속에 섞어 버린다. B는 두 사건을 구분한다는 뜻이어서, 지문이 비판하는 내용과 정반대이다.
g.explanation_en: The text says popular accounts treat October 1917 as the end of tsarist rule, even though the tsar's abdication (February) and the Bolsheviks' takeover from the Provisional Government (October) were "two distinct episodes." So the framing merges separate events into one, and that is exactly what C (conflates) means. A may look right because the framing does give October too much credit, but the text's complaint is about blending two events together, not about overstating how big one event was. D suggests the order of events is flipped, but the accounts don't reverse the sequence; they fold the earlier event into the later one. B means the framing keeps the events apart, which is the opposite of the text's criticism.
g.design: To get this right, a student has to link the claim in the first sentence with the phrase "two distinct episodes" in the second sentence. The wrong choices "exaggerates" and "reverses" each match part of the context, so they have to be compared carefully against the answer before they can be ruled out.

g.passage: Textbooks often credit the Peace of Westphalia (1648) with creating the modern system of sovereign states, but some historians argue that this account overstates the treaties' novelty. The agreements did end decades of religious warfare in central Europe, yet many of the principles later associated with them, such as rulers' authority over religion within their own territories, had already been stated in the Peace of Augsburg nearly a century earlier. On this view, Westphalia did less to invent sovereignty than to ______ arrangements that earlier settlements had outlined but had failed to secure.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 웨스트팔리아가 주권을 새로 '발명'했다기보다, 이전 조약이 제시했지만 확고히 하지 못한 질서를 굳혔다고 본다. 따라서 '강화하다, 공고히 하다'를 뜻하는 D가 정답이다. A는 웨스트팔리아가 종교 전쟁을 끝냈다는 점에서 무언가를 없앤 듯 보이지만, 이전 원칙을 계승했다는 맥락과 정반대다. B는 시간 순서가 틀렸다. 그 질서는 이미 이전에 제시되었으므로 '예견했다'고 할 수 없다. C는 '새로 만들어 내다'라는 뜻이어서, 지문이 부정하는 '발명'과 같은 의미가 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text argues that Westphalia didn't invent sovereignty. Instead, it made firm the arrangements that earlier treaties had outlined but failed to secure, so "consolidate" in D is correct. A might seem tempting because the treaties ended religious wars, but the text says Westphalia carried earlier principles forward, which is the opposite of abolishing them. B gets the time order backward: the arrangements already existed, so Westphalia couldn't have anticipated them. C means "to create something new," which is just another way of saying "invent," and the text rejects that idea.
g.design: 이 문항은 두 단계 판단이 필요하도록 만들었다. 학생은 'less to invent ... than to' 대조 구조를 파악하고, 그 뒤에 'outlined but failed to secure'라는 단서와 연결해야 한다. 오답 A는 종교 전쟁 종식, C는 교과서식 통념에 각각 부분적 근거를 두었다. B는 시간 순서 혼동을 노린다.

g.explanation_en: The text's examples show deep, lasting change: maize and potatoes became staples across several continents, and horses and cattle remade economies in the Americas. That is exactly what A means: they fundamentally changed daily life. B doesn't work because the transfers themselves didn't record anything. C is only about positive outcomes, but the text is pushing back against a story of European gain and stresses neutral, sweeping change on both sides. D might seem right if you think of disease, but the examples given describe new staples and rebuilt economies, which is a restructuring, not just a disturbance.
g.design: 빈칸 뒤 예시(주식화·경제 재편)와 앞의 '이익 중심 서술' 반박을 연결해야 하는 두 단계로 설계했다. C와 D는 이 교류의 일부 측면에 맞는 단어여서 문맥과 꼼꼼히 비교해야 배제된다.

g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 자치가 독립이 아니었고, 술탄이 지도자를 임명·해임할 수 있었다고 말하므로 지도자의 권위는 제국의 승인에 '달려 있었다'는 B가 정답이다. A는 공동체가 법정과 징세를 스스로 운영했다는 앞부분의 자율성만 보면 그럴듯하지만, 술탄이 해임할 수 있었다는 내용과 모순된다. C도 자치의 폭을 과장한 해석으로, 'not independence'라는 경고와 정반대다. D는 대신 세금을 걷는 지도자의 권위가 승인 과정과 무관하게 숨겨졌다는 뜻이 되어 문맥상 근거가 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the millet autonomy was not independence and that the sultan could confirm or remove each leader, so the leader's authority depended on imperial approval. C also overstates the autonomy and contradicts the historians' warning that it was "not independence." D suggests the leader's authority was hidden from approval, which nothing in the text supports.
g.design: 앞부분의 자치 서술이 A·C를 그럴듯하게 만들고, 'however'와 해임권을 연결해야 B가 확정되도록 두 단계 판단을 요구했다.

g.passage: Between 1405 and 1433, the Ming admiral Zheng He led seven expeditions across the Indian Ocean, reaching ports from Southeast Asia to the coast of East Africa. Some popular accounts portray the voyages as campaigns of conquest, but historian Edward Dreyer argues that this view ______ the fleet's purpose: although the ships carried thousands of soldiers, they rarely fought, and their main task was to collect tribute and spread awareness of Ming power among foreign rulers.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: Dreyer은 원정의 주된 목적이 정복이 아니라 조공 수집과 위세 과시였다고 보므로, '정복 원정'이라는 견해는 함대의 목적을 잘못 묘사한다(C). A는 부정적 평가라 그럴듯하지만, '과장하다'는 정복이 실제 목적이었는데 규모만 부풀렸다는 뜻이 되어, 목적 자체가 달랐다는 지문의 논지와 맞지 않는다. B는 그 견해가 목적을 정확히 기록한다는 의미가 되어 Dreyer의 반박과 모순된다. D는 견해 자체가 목적을 의심한다는 뜻이 되는데, 그 견해는 목적에 대해 확신에 찬 주장을 할 뿐 의심하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Dreyer argues that the voyages mainly aimed to collect tribute and display Ming power, not to conquer, so the "conquest" view gets the fleet's purpose wrong. That makes C, "misrepresents," the right answer. A sounds tempting because it's also critical, but "exaggerates" would mean conquest really was the purpose and the view just overstates it, while the text says the purpose was something else entirely. B would mean the view records the purpose accurately, which contradicts Dreyer's rebuttal. D doesn't work either: the conquest view makes a confident claim about the fleet's purpose rather than casting doubt on it.
g.design: Distractors A and D share C's critical tone, so students have to notice that the text describes a different purpose, not an overstated or doubted one.

c.seed: history and civics — Spanish Inquisition tribunal system religious persecution targeting Muslims Jews heretics medieval Iberia

g.passage: Established in 1478, the Spanish Inquisition targeted conversos (Jews who had converted to Christianity), moriscos (converted Muslims), and suspected heretics, and it is often pictured as a single, all-seeing apparatus. Historian Henry Kamen's work in tribunal archives complicates that image. Some district tribunals, such as Toledo's, heard many cases a year. Others, short of officials and money, went long stretches with almost no trials, and rural areas far from a tribunal seat often saw inquisitors only rarely. The Inquisition's grip on Spanish society, Kamen suggests, was therefore ______: fierce in some places and periods, faint in others.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 어떤 재판소는 사건을 많이 다룬 반면 다른 재판소는 인력과 자금이 부족해 거의 재판을 열지 못했다고 설명하고, 콜론 뒤에서 "어떤 곳과 시기에는 강하고 다른 곳에서는 약했다"고 정리한다. 따라서 지역과 시기에 따라 차이가 났다는 뜻의 D(uneven)가 가장 정확하다. A(absolute)는 지문이 반박하는 '전지적 기구'라는 통념과 맞을 뿐 지문의 결론과는 반대이다. B(secretive)는 종교재판이 실제로 비밀스럽게 운영되었다는 배경지식과는 맞지만, 지문이 말하는 지역 간 차이를 설명하지 못한다. C(hostile)는 박해 대상에 대한 태도로는 그럴듯하지만, 강하기도 하고 약하기도 했다는 콜론 뒤 설명과 연결되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text contrasts busy tribunals like Toledo's with others that held almost no trials, and the part after the colon sums this up: "fierce in some places and periods, faint in others." The word you need has to describe power that changed by place and time, so D (uneven) is the most precise choice. A (absolute) fits the "all-seeing" image that the text says Kamen's research complicates, so it's the opposite of the conclusion. B (secretive) might match what you already know about how the Inquisition operated, but it doesn't explain the regional differences the text describes. C (hostile) works as a description of the Inquisition's attitude toward the people it persecuted, but it doesn't match the idea of a grip that was strong in some places and weak in others.

B mentions Republican senators, but it concerns a time before the ruling and has no connection to the tapes. C shows a change after the ruling, but it is about newspaper coverage, not the senators whose votes mattered.
g.design: 오답 B·C는 각각 주장의 한 요소(상원의원 / 판결 이후 변화)만 담아 부분적으로 맞아 보이며, 정답만이 테이프 내용과 상원의원 입장 변화를 둘 다 연결한다. 질문에 정답의 핵심어는 쓰지 않았다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Fall of Berlin Wall 1989 symbolic collapse Cold War division reuniting Germany peacefully

g.passage: Popular accounts often portray the opening of the Berlin Wall on November 9, 1989, as the direct result of mass street protests in East Germany. Historian Mary Elise Sarotte, however, has argued that the precise timing of the opening owed much to bureaucratic confusion: according to this view, a poorly prepared announcement by East German official Günter Schabowski, who mistakenly stated that new travel rules took effect "immediately," prompted crowds to gather at the border crossings that very night, before the government had any plan for how the rules would actually be carried out.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the view about the timing of the Wall's opening described in the text?
options: Internal East German documents show that the travel regulations had been scheduled to begin the following morning, with border guards receiving no instructions about them before crowds appeared at the checkpoints.

Internal East German documents show that the number of protesters in Leipzig had grown steadily during the weeks before November 9, with officials expressing alarm about the size of the demonstrations.

Internal East German documents show that Schabowski had been given the text of the new travel regulations only shortly before his press conference, though he read it aloud exactly as it had been written.
Internal East German documents show that the government had spent months preparing detailed procedures for processing exit visas, which border guards began applying on the evening of November 9.
g.explanation: 이 견해의 핵심은 샤보프스키의 잘못된 '즉시' 발표 때문에 정부가 실행 계획을 세우기 전에 군중이 국경에 모였다는 것이다. A는 규정이 원래 다음 날 아침부터 시행될 예정이었고 경비병이 지침을 받지 못했다고 보여 주므로, 발표 실수와 계획 부재를 모두 뒷받침한다. B는 시위대의 영향력을 강조하는 대중적 설명에 더 가깝다. C는 준비가 부족했음을 보여 주지만, 발표문을 그대로 읽었다면 '실수'라는 핵심 요소가 약해진다. D는 정부가 철저히 준비했다는 내용이라 오히려 이 견해를 약화한다.
g.explanation_en: The view claims two things: Schabowski made a mistake when he said the rules took effect "immediately," and crowds showed up before the government had any plan for carrying the rules out. Choice A backs up both points. The rules were really meant to start the next morning, so "immediately" was an error, and the guards had no instructions, so there was no plan. Choice B is about protest crowds, which fits the popular account instead. Choice C does show poor preparation, but if Schabowski read the text exactly as written, he made no mistake, and that is the core of the claim. Choice D describes careful planning, so it would actually weaken the view.
g.design: To support the view, a finding has to connect two parts of it: the announcement was a mistake, and there was no plan in place. C confirms only the poor-preparation part and undercuts the mistake. B fits the rival account, and D sounds plausible but works against the view.

c.instruction: 지문에 '한때 ~라고 여겨졌으나(통념)' 다음 'however/but/실제로는' 류의 전환어와 함께 이를 뒤집는 새 증거나 반박 문장을 제시하고, 빈칸이 그 반박된 결과를 표현하도록 한다. 정답은 통념과 정반대 방향의 의미를 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 통념 쪽 단어를 그대로 쓴 것, (2) 전환어를 못 읽고 통념과 같은 방향이지만 강도만 다른 단어, (3) 반박 대상과 무관한 제3의 의미 단어로 구성한다. 전환 지점 앞뒤 문장만으로 답이 결정되게 하고 문장 길이나 어휘 난이도는 중간 수준을 유지한다.
c.seed: history and civics — Treaty of Utrecht 1713 Anglo-French colonial negotiations establishing British naval maritime supremacy

g.passage: Historians long portrayed the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht as a document whose colonial clauses mattered little to Britain's rise at sea; the territorial transfers in North America and the Mediterranean, the argument went, were minor concessions that diplomats traded away with little thought. Recent archival work on the Anglo-French negotiations, however, shows that British envoys fought hardest over exactly these terms, insisting on Gibraltar, Minorca, and Newfoundland's coasts because each offered harbors and fishing grounds that could sustain a permanent navy. Far from being incidental, the colonial provisions were ______ to the maritime supremacy Britain would enjoy for the rest of the century.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 정답 B(foundational): 'however' 뒤의 새 증거를 보면 영국 사절들은 해군을 유지할 항구와 어장 때문에 바로 이 식민지 조항들을 두고 가장 치열하게 협상했다. 'Far from being incidental'도 통념을 뒤집으므로, 빈칸에는 이 조항들이 해상 패권의 기반이었다는 뜻이 들어가야 한다. A(peripheral)는 '부차적'이라는 통념을 그대로 옮긴 단어이다. C(somewhat marginal)는 전환어를 놓친 선택지로, 통념과 같은 방향에서 강도만 약하게 한 표현이다. D(ceremonial)는 '의례적'이라는 뜻으로, 조항이 중요했느냐 사소했느냐는 논점과 관계없는 제3의 의미이다.
g.explanation_en: B (foundational) is correct. After "however," the passage gives new evidence: British envoys fought hardest for these exact colonial terms, because those places offered harbors and fishing grounds that could support a permanent navy. The phrase "Far from being incidental" also reverses the old view. So the blank must say that these clauses were the basis of Britain's naval supremacy. A (peripheral) simply repeats the old view that the clauses were minor. C (somewhat marginal) misses the reversal. It points the same way as the old view and only softens how strongly it says so. D (ceremonial) adds an unrelated idea, ritual or formality, when the real issue is whether the clauses were important or minor.
g.design: 통념(조항은 사소함)을 'however'로 뒤집었다. 오답은 통념 단어, 같은 방향의 약한 표현, 무관한 의미 단어 하나씩으로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 지문에 'is not X, but rather Y' 또는 'it isn't that A; instead B' 형태로 부정어 뒤에 대조 표현이 이어지는 문장을 만들고, 빈칸이 그 대조 표현(B) 자리에 오게 한다. 정답은 부정된 개념(X)과 반대 극성을 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 부정어를 무시하고 X와 같은 의미 단어, (2) 부정 구조를 이중으로 잘못 해석해 극성을 다시 뒤집은 단어, (3) 대조 구조와 무관한 유사 발음/철자 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: history and civics — Tanzimat Ottoman reforms 1839-1876 centralization modernization attempts saving declining Ottoman imperial power

g.passage: Many European observers in the mid-nineteenth century treated the Ottoman Tanzimat reforms (1839–1876) as proof that the sultan was losing control of his empire, since the reforms brought new provincial councils and legal guarantees for subjects. Historian Ali Yaycıoğlu and others have challenged this reading. They argue that the reforms were not a dilution of imperial authority but rather its ______: by replacing semi-independent tax farmers with salaried officials who answered to Istanbul, and by putting provincial courts under codified imperial law, the reformers pulled power that had long been spread among local notables back toward the center.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation:
정답 C(consolidation, 강화·통합). 'not A but rather B' 구조라서 빈칸에는 부정된 '권위의 희석(dilution)'과 반대되는 말이 와야 한다. 콜론 뒤의 근거도 이를 뒷받침한다. 징세청부인을 이스탄불에 보고하는 봉급 관리로 바꾸고, 지방 법원을 성문화된 제국법 아래 두어 흩어져 있던 권력을 중앙으로 다시 모았다고 했으므로 '권위의 강화·통합'이 맞다.
A(attenuation, 약화): 부정어 not을 무시하고 dilution과 같은 뜻의 단어를 고른 경우다. 지문이 부정한 해석을 그대로 되풀이한다.
B(decentralization, 분권화): 부정을 한 번 더 뒤집어 읽은 오류다. 지문 앞부분의 '지방 의회'에 이끌리면 고르기 쉽지만, 권력이 중앙으로 다시 모였다는 근거와 정면으로 충돌한다.
D(consolation, 위로): 철자와 발음이 정답과 비슷할 뿐 대조 구조와 아무 관련이 없다. '권위의 위로'라는 표현은 말이 되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en:
Choice C is correct. The "not A but rather B" structure means the blank must be the opposite of the rejected idea, a "dilution" of imperial authority. The evidence after the colon supports this. Tax farmers were replaced with salaried officials who answered to Istanbul, and provincial courts were put under imperial law. Both changes pulled scattered power "back toward the center," which is a consolidation of authority.
Choice A ("attenuation") ignores the word "not." It means about the same thing as "dilution," so it repeats the very reading the historians reject.
Choice B ("decentralization") flips the meaning back again. The earlier mention of provincial councils might pull you toward it, but it contradicts the evidence that power moved to the center.
Choice D ("consolation") only looks and sounds like "consolidation." It has nothing to do with the contrast, and "its consolation" makes no sense when applied to authority.
g.design: The blank is the B part of "not a dilution of imperial authority but rather its ______," so the answer has the opposite meaning of "dilution." The wrong answers are built from three errors: ignoring the negation (attenuation), flipping the meaning back again (decentralization, which the mention of provincial councils makes tempting), and picking a word that only looks and sounds like the answer (consolation).

c.instruction: 지문을 두 단계(예: 상황 묘사 후 화자의 숙고, 또는 기존 주장 소개 후 저자의 반박/선언)로 구성하고, 빈칸을 두 번째 단계의 시작 지점에 배치해 앞 단계와 다른 서술 기능을 하도록 한다. 정답은 두 번째 단계의 기능(숙고, 반박, 선언 등)에 맞는 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 첫 번째 단계에 어울리는 단어, (2) 두 단계 어디에도 맞지 않는 중립적 단어, (3) 의미는 비슷하나 문장이 요구하는 품사/기능이 다른 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: history and civics — Peasants' Revolt 1381 England Wat Tyler uprising challenging feudal serfdom labor obligations

g.passage: Medieval chroniclers such as Thomas Walsingham described the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 as a sudden outburst of rage: a crowd with no real leaders, angered by a third poll tax, that followed Wat Tyler toward London. Many later historians repeated this picture and focused on the burned manors and the royal officials who were killed. Yet this account ______ what the rebels actually demanded at Mile End and Smithfield: an end to serfdom, an end to forced labor for lords, and land rents fixed at fourpence an acre. These were demands of a coherent challenge to the feudal order, not just fury.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation:
지문은 두 단계로 되어 있다. 앞부분은 연대기 작가와 후대 역사가들이 반란을 '분노의 폭발'로 그린 기존 서술을 소개하고, 'Yet'부터는 저자가 이를 반박한다. 빈칸 뒤에는 농노제 폐지, 강제 노역 폐지, 지대 고정 같은 구체적인 요구가 나오고, 이를 근거로 반란이 '단순한 분노'가 아니었다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 빈칸에는 기존 서술이 이 요구들을 '가려 버린다'는 비판이 들어가야 하므로 D 'obscures'가 정답이다.
A 'documents'(기록하다)는 앞 단계의 묘사에 어울리는 단어이다. 하지만 기존 서술이 요구를 기록했다면 저자가 반박할 이유가 없어진다.
B 'concerns'(~에 관한 것이다)는 중립적인 단어라서 'Yet'이 요구하는 반박의 기능을 하지 못한다.
C 'dismissive of'는 '무시하는'이라는 비슷한 뜻을 담고 있지만 형용사구이다. 주어 'this account' 뒤에는 동사가 와야 하므로 문법적으로 들어갈 수 없다.
g.explanation_en:
The text has two stages. First, it presents the traditional view of chroniclers and later historians, who described the revolt as an outburst of rage. Then, starting with "Yet," the author pushes back against that view. After the blank, the author lists the rebels' specific demands (an end to serfdom, an end to forced labor, fixed rents) and uses them to argue that the revolt was more than fury. So the blank needs a verb showing that the traditional account hides these demands. That makes "obscures" (D) the answer.
(A) "Documents" fits the first, descriptive stage. But if the account recorded the demands, the author would have no reason to object.
(B) "Concerns" is neutral and doesn't do the critical work that "Yet" calls for.
(C) "Dismissive of" has a similar meaning, but it's an adjective phrase. The subject "this account" needs a verb after it, so this choice doesn't work grammatically.
g.design: I placed the blank at the start of the second stage, right after "Yet," where the author's rebuttal begins. Each wrong answer matches one of the required traps: "documents" fits the first stage, "concerns" is a neutral word, and "dismissive of" has a similar meaning but the wrong part of speech.

c.instruction: 학술적 소재(연구, 인물, 현상 등)에 대한 3~4문장의 짧은 지문을 만들고, 마지막 문장은 앞 내용 중 특정 목적이나 강조점(예: 결과가 아니라 의도, 수치가 아니라 방향성)에 부합하는 전환어를 골라야 정답이 되게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)앞 문장의 결과·부수적 사실과는 맞지만 지문의 핵심 강조점과는 어긋나는 전환어, (2)방향은 맞지만 논리관계(원인/대조 등)가 틀린 전환어, (3)전혀 다른 내용과 연결되는 전환어로 구성하라. 지문에 여러 개의 정보가 나열되되 그중 한 가지만 답과 직결되도록 설계한다.
c.seed: history and civics — Treaty of Tordesillas 1494 Portuguese Spanish division colonial territories Americas Africa Asia

g.passage: Signed in 1494, the Treaty of Tordesillas drew a north-south line 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, assigning newly encountered lands west of it to Spain and those east of it to Portugal. Because navigators of the era could not reliably measure longitude, the line's exact position was disputed for decades, and its placement later gave Portugal an unexpected claim to part of Brazil. Historians stress, however, that the negotiators were not trying to map the world precisely; their goal was to keep the two Catholic crowns from going to war over overseas territory. ______ the treaty is better judged by whether it prevented open conflict between Lisbon and Madrid than by the accuracy of its line—and on that measure, it largely succeeded.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Like the papal decree before it,
g.explanation:
정답 A: 바로 앞 문장은 협정의 '의도'(정밀한 지도 작성이 아니라 전쟁 방지)를 강조한다. 마지막 문장은 그 의도에 맞춰 협정을 평가해야 한다(선의 정확성이 아니라 분쟁을 막았는지로 판단)고 결론짓기 때문에, 목적에 부합함을 나타내는 'In keeping with that purpose'가 자연스럽다.
B: 경도 측정이 부정확했다는 것은 지문에 나오는 부수적 사실이다. 하지만 마지막 문장이 선의 정확성으로 평가하지 말자고 하는 이유는 부정확성이 아니라 협정의 목적이다. 그러므로 원인으로 이어지지 않는다.
C: '목적'을 가리킨다는 점은 맞지만 양보·대조 관계를 나타낸다. 마지막 문장은 그 목적을 따르는 결론이므로 논리 관계가 반대다.
D: 교황 칙서는 지문에 전혀 나오지 않는다. 유사성을 나타내는 연결도 근거가 없다.
g.explanation_en:
Answer A: The sentence just before the blank stresses what the negotiators intended: they weren't trying to map the world precisely, they were trying to prevent a war. The final sentence then judges the treaty by that goal, asking whether it stopped open conflict rather than whether its line was accurate. "In keeping with that purpose" correctly links this conclusion to the stated goal.
B: The longitude problem really is in the passage, but it's a side detail. The text says to set aside the line's accuracy because of the treaty's purpose, not because the line was imprecise. So this cause-and-effect link is wrong.
C: This choice points to the right thing (the purpose), but it signals contrast. The final sentence follows from the purpose instead of going against it.
D: The passage never mentions a papal decree, so a comparison with one has no support in the text.
g.design: The passage lists several facts: where the line was drawn, the trouble measuring longitude, and the claim to Brazil. Only the negotiators' purpose leads directly to the final sentence. The wrong answers are built on (1) the longitude detail, (2) the right reference point with the wrong logical relationship (contrast), and (3) something the passage never mentions.

c.instruction: 서로 배치되거나 상반된 것처럼 보이는 두 가지 관찰(실험 결과, 사례, 수치)이 제시된 짧은 지문을 만들고, 두 관찰을 종합했을 때 나오는 결론을 마지막 문장에서 올바른 전환어로 연결해야 정답이 되게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)한쪽 관찰만 반영한 전환어, (2)두 관찰이 상반된다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 전환어, (3)종합 결론과 무관한 전환어로 구성하라. 계산이나 복잡한 수치 없이 정성적 진술만으로 구성한다.
c.seed: history and civics — Venetian Republic Arsenal shipyard 1104-1797 and industrial assembly line production revolutionizing medieval naval construction

g.passage: Accounts of the Venetian Arsenal, the state shipyard that operated from the twelfth century until 1797, often stress its speed: during crises, workers could complete and launch war galleys in a matter of days. Yet the Arsenal's own ledgers show that in peacetime, partly built hulls frequently sat untouched for long stretches. ______ the shipyard's famous speed depended on its slow periods, when stockpiled hulls and standardized parts waited to be rapidly assembled once the republic needed a fleet.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Taken together, these records suggest that
g.explanation:
정답 B: 지문의 두 관찰, 즉 위기 때의 빠른 진수와 평시에 방치된 선체를 종합하면, 평시의 비축이 위기 때의 속도를 가능하게 했다는 결론이 나온다. "Taken together"가 바로 이 종합을 표시한다.
A(Thus): 바로 앞 문장(평시 방치)만 근거로 삼는 인과 연결이다. 방치만으로는 '빠른 속도'라는 결론이 나오지 않으므로 한쪽 관찰만 반영한 것이다.
C(Nevertheless): 두 관찰이 상반된다는 점만 보고 대조로 처리했다. 하지만 마지막 문장은 앞 내용에 맞서는 진술이 아니라 두 관찰을 조화시키는 결론이다.
D(Meanwhile): 동시에 일어난 별개의 사실을 덧붙일 때 쓰는 말로, 마지막 문장의 종합 결론과는 관계가 없다.
g.explanation_en:
B is correct. The text gives two observations that seem to conflict: the Arsenal built galleys very fast in crises, but its peacetime ledgers show half-built hulls sitting idle. The last sentence brings these together: the idle stockpiles are what made the fast crisis assembly possible. "Taken together, these records suggest that" signals this synthesis.
A ("Thus,") treats the conclusion as following only from the previous sentence about idle hulls. Idleness alone does not explain the speed, so this uses just one observation.
C ("Nevertheless,") sees only that the two observations clash and treats the last sentence as a contrast. In fact, that sentence reconciles them.
D ("Meanwhile,") adds a separate fact happening at the same time and has nothing to do with drawing a combined conclusion.
g.design: 상충해 보이는 관찰 두 개(위기 때의 속도, 평시의 방치)를 제시하고 마지막 문장에서 둘을 종합하게 했다. 오답은 한쪽 관찰만 반영한 Thus, 단순 대조인 Nevertheless, 무관한 Meanwhile로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 한 문장 안에서 수식어구나 비교 표현이 인접한 명사가 아니라 문장 앞부분의 다른 요소(주어나 앞 문장의 대상)를 가리키도록 설계된 짧은 지문을 만들고, 이 실제 지시 관계를 올바르게 파악해야 정답 전환어를 고를 수 있게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)인접한 명사를 지시 대상으로 잘못 본 전환어, (2)문법적으로는 자연스럽지만 실제 지시관계와 어긋나는 전환어, (3)전혀 다른 요소를 지시 대상으로 삼은 전환어로 구성하라. 문장은 짧고 단순한 구조를 유지한다.
c.seed: history and civics — Barbary Wars 1801-1815 American naval conflict against North African pirate states protecting Mediterranean commerce

g.passage: In the 1790s, the United States paid tribute to the Barbary states of North Africa so that pirates would not seize American merchant ships. Thomas Jefferson, unlike many members of Congress, who considered the payments cheap insurance, had condemned the practice since the 1780s. When he became president in 1801 and Tripoli demanded more money, he sent warships to the Mediterranean instead. ______ his decision continued a position he had long held rather than marking a change of heart.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: "had condemned the practice since the 1780s"의 주어는 바로 옆 명사 Congress가 아니라 문장 앞의 Jefferson이다. 'unlike many members of Congress' 삽입구는 Jefferson과 의회를 대비하는 말이다. 따라서 Jefferson은 오래전부터 공납에 반대해 왔고, 1801년 함대를 보낸 결정은 그 입장을 이어간 것이므로 결론을 이끄는 "Thus,"가 맞다. A "Surprisingly,"는 공납을 값싼 보험으로 여긴 쪽(의회)의 견해를 Jefferson의 견해로 잘못 본 선택이다. 그렇게 읽으면 함대 파견이 뜻밖의 방향 전환처럼 보인다. B "In contrast,"는 앞 문장에 대비 표현(unlike)이 있어 문법적으로는 자연스러워 보인다. 하지만 마지막 문장은 앞 내용과 대조되지 않고 앞 내용에서 따라 나오는 결론이므로 틀리다. D "Even so,"는 지시 대상을 Tripoli의 추가 요구라는 전혀 다른 요소로 잡은 선택이다. 그 요구에도 '불구하고'라는 양보 관계를 만들지만, 지문에는 그런 양보 관계가 없다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "had condemned the practice since the 1780s" belongs to Jefferson, the subject at the start of the sentence. It does not describe Congress, the noun right next to it. The phrase "unlike many members of Congress" sets Jefferson against Congress. So Jefferson had opposed tribute for a long time, and sending warships in 1801 carried that view forward. The last sentence is a conclusion drawn from these facts, so "Thus," is correct. A ("Surprisingly,") gives Jefferson the view of the nearby noun, Congress, which saw tribute as cheap insurance. Read that way, the warships would look like an unexpected reversal. B ("In contrast,") sounds natural because the sentence before it uses "unlike." But the final sentence agrees with what comes before it and does not contrast with it. D ("Even so,") links the final sentence to a different element, Tripoli's demand. That creates a "despite this" relationship that the passage doesn't support.
g.design: 삽입된 비교구 때문에 'had condemned'의 주어가 바로 옆 Congress로 잘못 읽히기 쉽다. 실제 주어 Jefferson을 찾아야만 '이전 입장의 연속'이라는 결론 관계("Thus,")를 고를 수 있다.

c.instruction: 지문에 두 변수 사이의 이론적 관계(예: A가 클수록 B도 커진다, 정직한 신호일수록 비용이 크다)를 제시하고, 이 이론을 새로운 구체적 집단이나 사례에 적용했을 때 나올 결론을 빈칸으로 묻는다. 정답은 이론이 제시한 방향을 그대로 새 사례에 적용한 것이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 관계의 방향을 반대로 뒤집기, 원인과 결과를 바꾸기, 이론과 무관한 제3의 요인을 결론으로 제시하기의 실제 오개념을 사용해 만든다.
c.seed: history and civics — Scottish Enlightenment intellectual movement 1707-1790 and philosophical empiricism challenging continental rationalist traditions

g.passage: Historians of the Scottish Enlightenment (roughly 1707–1790) often contrast its thinkers with continental rationalists, who tried to derive knowledge from first principles through reasoning alone. One historian goes further and proposes a graded relationship: the more heavily a moral philosopher grounded arguments in recorded observation of actual human conduct, the more readily that philosopher treated conclusions as provisional and open to change when new cases emerged. To test this, the historian compares surviving lecture notes from two eighteenth-century Edinburgh professors. The first professor's notes are filled with detailed accounts of merchants' bargaining, parish disputes, and travelers' reports, while the second professor's notes proceed almost entirely by deduction from a few stated axioms. If the historian's proposal is correct, then a comparison of successive versions of each professor's lectures over several decades should reveal that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the second professor's conclusions changed more often from one version to the next than the first professor's conclusions did.
the first professor's habit of frequently changing conclusions was what led that professor to start filling the notes with recorded observations.
the professor whose university received more funding from Edinburgh's merchant community changed conclusions more often between versions.
the first professor's conclusions changed more often from one version to the next than the second professor's conclusions did.
g.explanation: 이 역사가의 가설은 관찰에 더 많이 의존할수록 결론을 잠정적인 것으로 보고 더 쉽게 고친다는 것이다. 관찰 기록이 풍부한 사람은 첫 번째 교수이므로, 강의 판본이 바뀔 때마다 결론이 더 자주 달라지는 쪽도 첫 번째 교수여야 한다. 그래서 정답은 D이다. A는 관계의 방향을 뒤집어 연역 위주인 두 번째 교수가 더 자주 바꾼다고 말한다. B는 원인과 결과를 바꾸었다. 가설에서는 관찰 의존이 원인이고 결론 수정이 결과인데, B는 결론 수정이 관찰을 낳았다고 한다. 게다가 B는 두 교수를 비교하지도 않는다. C는 상인 공동체의 재정 지원이라는 이 이론과 무관한 요인을 결론으로 내세운다. 지문에는 이 요인에 대한 근거가 없다.
g.explanation_en: The historian's claim is that the more a philosopher relies on recorded observation, the more readily that philosopher treats conclusions as provisional and revises them. The first professor relies heavily on observation, so the first professor should show more changes across versions. That makes D correct. A reverses the direction of the relationship by giving the deductive professor more revisions. B swaps cause and effect: in the theory, relying on observation is the cause and revising is the effect, but B says revising caused the observing. B also doesn't compare the two professors. C points to an outside factor, merchant funding, which the theory never mentions and the text gives no support for.
g.design: This item gives a graded theory (the more a philosopher relies on observation, the more readily conclusions are revised) and applies it to two new professors. Each wrong answer uses a different mistake: A reverses the direction, B swaps cause and effect, and C brings in an unrelated third factor (funding). All four choices use the same sentence frame, and the question doesn't repeat any key words from the answer.

c.instruction: 짧은 표나 그래프 하나와 이를 설명하는 가설 문장 하나를 함께 제시하고, 두 정보를 결합해야만 답할 수 있는 결론을 빈칸으로 묻는다. 정답은 시각 자료의 특정 수치와 가설 문장을 연결해야 나오고, 오답 3개는 각각 시각 자료만 보고 가설을 무시한 결론, 가설 문장만 보고 시각 자료를 무시한 결론, 시각 자료의 다른 항목을 잘못 짝지은 결론으로 만든다.
c.seed: history and civics — Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth 1569-1795 and elected monarchy system balancing religious tolerance with aristocratic privilege

g.passage:
Historian Marta Kowalczyk studies royal elections in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth (1569–1795), in which the nobility (szlachta) chose each king. Every elected king had to swear to the Henrician Articles and the pacta conventa, which bound him to protect noble privileges and to uphold the 1573 Warsaw Confederation's guarantee of religious peace. Kowalczyk hypothesizes that this toleration pledge mattered to electors only when Protestant nobles made up a large share of those present: in her view, a candidate's Catholic zeal hurt his chances only at elections where Protestants made up at least 15 percent of the voting nobles. The table shows her estimates for four elections.

Election | Protestant share of voting nobles | Winner viewed as a zealous Catholic?
1573 | 22% | No
1587 | 17% | No
1648 | 9% | Yes
1697 | 4% | Yes

If Kowalczyk's hypothesis is correct, the table suggests that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: a candidate's reputation for Catholic zeal would likely have been a disadvantage in 1587 but not in 1648.
a candidate's reputation for Catholic zeal would likely have been a disadvantage in 1648 but not in 1587.
a candidate's reputation for Catholic zeal would likely have been a disadvantage at every election, since every king swore to uphold religious peace.
a candidate's reputation for Catholic zeal would likely have been a disadvantage in 1697 but not in 1573.
g.explanation: 가설: 개신교 귀족 비율이 15% 이상인 선거에서만 가톨릭 열성이 불리했다. 표에서 1587년은 17%(기준 이상), 1648년은 9%(기준 미만)이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 표에서 1648년 열성 가톨릭 군주가 당선된 사실만 보고 가설의 15% 기준을 무시한 결론이다(오히려 순서가 뒤집힘). C는 모든 왕이 종교 평화를 맹세했다는 서술만 보고 표의 수치를 무시한 결론이다. D는 표의 항목을 잘못 짝지은 것으로, 1697년(4%)과 1573년(22%)의 관계를 거꾸로 적용했다.
g.explanation_en: The hypothesis says Catholic zeal hurt a candidate only when Protestants were at least 15 percent of the voting nobles. The table shows 17% in 1587 (above the threshold) and 9% in 1648 (below it), so zeal would have been a disadvantage in 1587 but not in 1648. That makes A correct. B reverses this. It relies only on the fact that zealous Catholics won in 1648 and ignores the 15% threshold. C uses only the passage's point that every king swore the toleration pledge and ignores the table's numbers, which the hypothesis says matter. D pairs the wrong rows: 1697 (4%) falls below the threshold and 1573 (22%) is above it, so the conclusion is backward.
g.design: To get the answer, you have to apply the hypothesis's 15% threshold to specific values in the table. Each wrong answer has a different flaw: B uses the table only, C uses the hypothesis only, and D mismatches the table's rows.

c.instruction: 하나의 결론이나 가설을 먼저 제시한 뒤, 그것을 뒷받침/약화/무관하게 만드는 추가 사실 하나를 골라야 하는 빈칸 문제를 만든다. 정답은 가설의 핵심 조건을 직접 충족하거나 위배하는 사실이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 표면적으로만 관련 있어 보이지만 실제로는 무관한 사실, 가설과 반대 방향으로 작용하는 사실을 지지 사실인 것처럼 제시한 것, 결론과 무관한 배경 정보를 결론 지지처럼 위장한 것으로 만든다.
c.seed: history and civics — Tokugawa shogunate sakoku isolation policy 1633-1853 and Japan's deliberate trade restrictions maintaining internal stability

g.passage: Historians have long described the Tokugawa shogunate's sakoku policies (1633–1853) as a near-total closure of Japan. Some scholars, however, argue that the restrictions were less about shutting out foreign goods than about controlling who profited from them: by confining Dutch and Chinese trade to Nagasaki under direct shogunal supervision, the regime kept wealthy regional lords (daimyo) from building independent commercial ties that could fund challenges to central authority. If this argument is correct, then the strongest support for it would come from evidence showing that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: imported Chinese silk and medicinal herbs continued to be sold in Edo markets throughout the period, often at prices well above those of domestic equivalents.
daimyo whose domains lay near Nagasaki were barred from trading directly with Dutch or Chinese merchants, while the shogunate's own officials set prices and collected the proceeds.
the number of Dutch ships allowed to dock at Nagasaki each year was gradually reduced, which lowered the total volume of foreign goods reaching Japan.
Japanese scholars of 'Dutch learning' (rangaku) studied European medicine and astronomy from books obtained through the Nagasaki trade.
g.explanation: 이 가설의 핵심은 무역 제한의 목적이 외국 물품 차단이 아니라 이익의 통제, 즉 다이묘가 독자적인 무역 관계를 맺지 못하게 하고 수익을 막부가 갖는 데 있었다는 것이다. B는 나가사키 인근 다이묘까지 직접 거래를 금지당했고 가격 결정과 수익 징수는 막부 관리가 맡았다는 내용이다. 가설의 두 조건(다이묘 배제, 중앙의 이익 독점)을 모두 직접 충족하므로 정답이다. A: 외국 물품이 계속 유통되었다는 사실은 '완전 폐쇄'가 아니었다는 점만 보여 준다. 누가 이익을 얻었는지는 말해 주지 않으므로 겉으로만 관련 있어 보이는 사실이다. C: 무역량이 줄었다는 것은 물품 자체를 차단했다는 전통적 해석 쪽을 가리킨다. 가설과 반대 방향으로 작용하는 사실을 지지 근거처럼 제시한 오답이다. D: 난학(蘭學)은 무역의 문화적 배경 정보일 뿐, 이익을 누가 통제했는지와는 관련이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The hypothesis says the main goal of the restrictions was to control who profited from foreign trade, not to keep foreign goods out. Under this view, the shogunate kept regional lords (daimyo) from forming their own trade ties and kept the profits for itself. Choice B shows both parts directly: even daimyo near Nagasaki were barred from trading with foreigners, and shogunal officials set the prices and collected the proceeds. That makes B the correct answer. Choice A only shows that foreign goods still reached Japan. It says nothing about who controlled the profits, so it's related on the surface but doesn't test the claim. Choice C, a falling trade volume, fits the traditional "keep goods out" reading better, so it actually works against the hypothesis even though it's worded like support. Choice D is cultural background about Dutch learning and has nothing to do with control of trade profits.
g.design: I stated a hypothesis about the purpose of a policy (controlling profit, not shutting out goods). The correct answer directly meets both of its conditions. The three wrong answers are, in order: a surface-related but irrelevant fact, a fact that pushes in the opposite direction, and background information dressed up as support.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — African diaspora slave trade resistance 1518-1865 and maroon settlements established by escaped enslaved peoples

g.passage: Maroon communities were settlements founded by people who escaped slavery in the Americas between the 1500s and the 1800s. Historians studying one maroon community in the mountains of Jamaica have found that its founders chose a site surrounded by steep cliffs and thick forest, reachable only by a single narrow trail. Colonial soldiers sent to recapture the residents could approach only in a slow single-file line, which made them easy to spot from far away. Because of these features, historians conclude that the founders most likely picked the location in order to ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: make it easier to trade crops with nearby colonial towns.
make it easier to grow large plantations of sugarcane.
make it easier to defend themselves against attackers.
make it easier to welcome visitors arriving by sea.
g.explanation: 지문은 가파른 절벽, 울창한 숲, 좁은 길 하나 때문에 병사들이 한 줄로 천천히 다가와야 했고 멀리서도 쉽게 보였다고 설명한다. 이런 특징은 모두 공격을 막는 데 유리하므로, 정착지는 방어를 위해 선택되었다는 C가 정답이다. A는 고립된 지형이 이웃 마을과의 교역을 오히려 어렵게 만드므로 틀렸다. B는 절벽과 숲이 대규모 농장에 맞지 않고 지문에 농업 이야기가 없으므로 틀렸다. D는 산속 지형이 바다로 오는 방문객과 관련이 없고, 지문은 사람들을 막는 것에 초점을 두므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the site had steep cliffs, thick forest, and only one narrow trail, so soldiers had to come slowly in single file and could be spotted from far away. All of these features help people protect themselves, so C is correct: the founders picked the site for defense. A is wrong because an isolated site would make trade with colonial towns harder, not easier. B is wrong because cliffs and forest don't suit large plantations, and the passage never mentions farming. D is wrong because a mountain site has nothing to do with visitors arriving by sea, and the passage is about keeping people out.
g.design: 지형 특징이 방어에 유리하다는 단서 하나로 목적을 한 단계 추론하게 했다. 선택지는 모두 같은 'make it easier to ~' 틀을 쓰고, 오답은 그럴듯한 정착지 선택 동기(교역, 농업, 접근성)로 구성했다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Scientific Revolution telescopic observations 1610-1687 and heliocentric model challenging Catholic Church astronomical doctrine

g.passage: In 1610, Galileo Galilei pointed his telescope at Jupiter and saw four small moons circling the planet. At the time, the Catholic Church supported the traditional view that every object in the heavens moves around Earth. Galileo's observation was important because it showed something that this view said could not happen: objects in the sky orbiting a body other than Earth. Therefore, the moons of Jupiter suggested that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Earth must be the only planet in the solar system that has moons of its own.
Jupiter must be located much closer to Earth than astronomers had once believed.
the telescope must have been too weak to show the heavens as they really are.
Earth might not be the center around which all heavenly bodies move.
g.explanation: 지문은 교회가 지지한 전통적 견해가 '모든 천체는 지구 주위를 돈다'는 것이었고, 목성의 위성은 지구가 아닌 다른 천체를 도는 물체였다고 말한다. 따라서 이 관측은 지구가 모든 천체 운동의 중심이 아닐 수 있음을 시사하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 목성에도 위성이 있다는 관측 내용과 정면으로 모순된다. B는 거리에 관한 내용으로, 지문은 목성까지의 거리를 전혀 언급하지 않는다. C는 관측을 신뢰하지 않는 결론인데, 지문은 이 관측을 전통적 견해에 맞선 중요한 증거로 제시한다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the traditional view held that every heavenly object moves around Earth, but Jupiter's moons were objects orbiting something other than Earth. So the observation suggests that Earth might not be the center of all heavenly motion, which makes D correct. A contradicts the observation itself, since Jupiter was seen to have moons. B is about distance, and the passage never discusses how far away Jupiter is. C throws out the observation, but the passage treats it as important evidence against the traditional view.
g.design: 추론은 '전통 견해: 모든 천체가 지구를 돈다' + '목성 주위를 도는 위성'이라는 한 단계 반례 논리로만 이루어진다. 오답은 같은 문장 틀을 쓰면서 관측과 모순되거나, 지문과 무관하거나, 증거를 부정하는 흔한 오개념으로 만들었다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Janissary corps Ottoman military institution 1363-1826 and devshirme recruitment system converting Christian boys into elite soldiers

g.passage: From the late fourteenth century onward, the Ottoman state filled the ranks of its elite Janissary infantry through the devshirme, a system that took boys from Christian families in the Balkans, converted them to Islam, and trained them as soldiers. Because these recruits were separated from their birth families and were legally considered servants of the sultan, they had no local family ties or inherited estates to draw their loyalty elsewhere. Historians therefore argue that the sultans valued the devshirme largely because it ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: produced soldiers whose allegiance was owed to the ruler rather than to any rival power base.
produced soldiers who remained closely connected to the villages where they had been born.
produced soldiers who could pass their military positions and lands on to their own sons.
produced soldiers who were recruited mainly from established Muslim noble families.
g.explanation: 지문은 신병들이 가족과 분리되었고 술탄의 종으로 간주되어 충성심을 다른 곳으로 돌릴 가족 유대나 상속 재산이 없었다고 말한다. 따라서 술탄이 이 제도를 중시한 이유는 통치자에게만 충성하는 병사를 얻었기 때문이라는 A가 논리적이다. B는 출신 마을과의 분리라는 진술과 모순된다. C는 상속 재산이 없었다는 점과 어긋나며, D는 기독교 가정 출신이라는 사실과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the recruits were cut off from their families and counted as the sultan's servants, so they had no family ties or inherited estates to pull their loyalty elsewhere. That means the sultans would value the system because it gave them soldiers loyal only to the ruler, which is choice A. Choice B is wrong because the boys were separated from their home communities. Choice C is wrong because the recruits had no inherited estates, and choice D is wrong because they came from Christian families, not Muslim noble ones.
g.design: 이 문항은 한 단계 추론만 필요하다. 가족 유대와 상속 재산이 없었다는 단서에서 통치자에게만 충성했다는 결론을 끌어낸다. 오답 세 개는 지문의 명시적 사실과 하나씩 모순되며, 네 선택지 모두 같은 문장 틀을 쓴다.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 주장과 이유를, 텍스트 2는 같은 주제의 다른 접근을 각각 짧게 제시하되 서로를 언급하지 않게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자라면 텍스트 1의 주장에 어떻게 반응할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 2의 전제에서만 도출되는 반응으로 만들고, 오답 3개는 텍스트 1의 내용을 반복하는 선택지, 텍스트 2의 결론만 되풀이하는 선택지, 텍스트 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점을 끌어온 선택지로 만든다.
c.seed: history and civics — American Revolution Declaration of Independence 1776 and natural rights philosophy inspiring subsequent democratic revolutions worldwide

g.passage:
Text 1
Historians tracing the spread of democratic revolutions after 1776 often credit the Declaration of Independence as their spark. Its claim that all people possess unalienable rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness, this view holds, gave reformers from Paris to Caracas a universal principle to invoke, and the document's influence can therefore be measured by how often later revolutionaries quoted or echoed its language.

Text 2
Historian David Armitage, examining foreign printings of the Declaration, notes that readers abroad were drawn less to its opening philosophy of rights than to its closing assertion that the colonies were "Free and Independent States." For many later movements, the document served chiefly as a model of how a people might announce sovereignty to other nations, a template copied in dozens of independence declarations that said little about individual rights.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the method of gauging influence described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that counting echoes of the Declaration's rights language is the most reliable way to show that natural rights philosophy inspired revolutions from Paris to Caracas
By cautioning that tracking only echoes of the rights passage would miss the document's widest influence, which came through imitation of its announcement of statehood
By insisting that later declarations of independence were copied from the Declaration and therefore said little about individual rights
By arguing that the Declaration's influence abroad was weakened because foreign translations often distorted the meaning of its original wording
g.explanation: 정답 B: Text 2는 해외 독자들이 권리 철학보다 '독립국가' 선언 부분에 주목했고, 주권 선언의 틀로 모방되었다고 본다. 이 전제에서 보면 Text 1처럼 권리 문구의 인용 빈도로 영향력을 재는 방법은 가장 널리 퍼진 영향 경로(주권 선언 형식의 모방)를 놓친다. A: Text 1의 주장을 그대로 반복할 뿐이고 Text 2의 관점과 충돌한다. C: Text 2의 결론을 되풀이할 뿐 Text 1의 측정 방법에 대한 반응이 아니다. D: 번역의 왜곡은 Text 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점이며, Text 2는 영향력이 약했다고 말하지도 않는다.
g.explanation_en: B is correct. Text 2 says readers abroad cared less about the Declaration's rights philosophy than about its claim to statehood, and that later movements copied it as a way to announce sovereignty. From that starting point, measuring influence only by echoes of the rights language would miss the main way the document spread, so the author of Text 2 would warn that Text 1's method leaves things out. A just repeats Text 1's view, which Text 2's evidence undercuts. C restates Text 2's own conclusion without responding to how Text 1 measures influence. D brings in distorted translations, which Text 2 never mentions, and it wrongly says the document's influence was weakened.
g.design: Neither text mentions the other. The answer comes from applying Text 2's idea (the Declaration spread as a model for announcing sovereignty) to Text 1's method of measuring influence. The three wrong answers are: a repeat of Text 1, a restatement of Text 2's conclusion, and an issue Text 2 never raises (translation).

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 하나의 결론을 이끄는 주장을, 텍스트 2는 그 주장의 핵심 근거를 약하게 만들 수 있는 별개의 관찰이나 연구를 제시한다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자가 텍스트 1의 어느 부분에 가장 이의를 제기할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 1의 결론이 아니라 그 결론이 기대는 가정으로 하고, 오답 3개는 결론 자체, 텍스트 1의 부수적 세부, 텍스트 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분으로 만든다.
c.seed: history and civics — Transiberian Railway construction 1891-1916 and Russian imperial expansion connecting Moscow to Pacific ports

g.passage:
Text 1
Historians often describe the Trans-Siberian Railway, built between 1891 and 1916, as an engine of imperial expansion. Because Russian settlement in Siberia surged in the years after the line's sections opened, many scholars conclude that the railway itself drew millions of peasants eastward. On this view, the state's decision to link Moscow with Pacific ports such as Vladivostok was what turned Siberia into a settled frontier of the empire.

Text 2
Records of migration from European Russia show that the eastward flow of peasants had already begun to rise sharply in the 1880s, years before construction started. Many migrants traveled by river boat and cart, and surveys of new villages found that most families chose sites far from the tracks, near arable land that had been opened through the 1889 resettlement law and the expanded land allotments that followed. The railway clearly carried freight and officials, but its link to peasant settlement is less obvious.
g.question: Based on the texts, which part of the reasoning described in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely challenge?
options: The claim that the railway turned Siberia into a settled frontier of the Russian Empire
The claim that the railway connected Moscow with Pacific ports such as Vladivostok
The claim that the timing of the settlement surge shows the railway caused it
The claim that Russian settlement in Siberia increased greatly around the time the line opened
g.explanation:
정답 C: Text 1은 '노선 개통 이후 정착이 급증했다'는 시간적 순서를 근거로 철도가 이주를 일으켰다고 추론한다. Text 2는 이주 증가가 착공 전인 1880년대에 이미 시작됐고, 이주민은 강·마차로 이동해 철로와 먼 곳에 정착했으며 1889년 재정착법 등 다른 요인이 있었다고 제시해, 바로 이 '시기 일치=인과' 가정을 약화시킨다.
A: 결론 자체이다. Text 2는 철도의 역할을 '덜 분명하다'고 할 뿐 시베리아가 정착지가 되었다는 사실을 부정하지 않으며, 핵심 공격 대상은 결론이 기대는 추론 고리이다.
B: 부수적 세부이다. Text 2는 노선 경로를 문제 삼지 않고 오히려 철도가 화물과 관리를 실어 날랐다고 인정한다.
D: Text 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분이다. Text 2도 이주가 급격히 늘었다고 기록하며, 다만 그 시작 시점과 원인을 다르게 본다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, C: Text 1 reasons from timing. Settlement surged after sections of the line opened, so the railway must have caused it. Text 2 attacks that link directly. It shows the surge started in the 1880s, before construction began. It also notes that migrants traveled by river and cart, that they settled far from the tracks, and that other causes existed, such as the 1889 resettlement law.
A is wrong because it's the conclusion. Text 2 doesn't deny that Siberia became settled. It disputes the reasoning that credits the railway for it.
B is wrong because it's a side detail. Text 2 never questions the route, and it even agrees that the railway carried freight and officials.
D is wrong because Text 2 agrees with it. Text 2 also reports a sharp rise in migration. It only disagrees about when the rise began and what caused it.
g.design: Text 1은 '개통 후 정착 급증'이라는 시간적 순서에서 인과를 끌어내고, Text 2는 착공 전부터 이주가 늘었고 다른 원인이 있었다는 증거로 그 가정을 약화시킨다. 오답은 결론(A), 부수적 세부(B), Text 2가 동의하는 사실(D)이며, 네 선택지 모두 같은 'The claim that…' 문장 틀로 썼다.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1의 저자가 좋은 설명이나 해결책의 기준(예: 재현 가능성, 단순성, 장기적 효과)을 분명히 드러내게 쓰고, 텍스트 2는 그 기준과 어긋날 수 있는 결론을 내리게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 1의 저자의 기준에서 텍스트 2의 결론을 어떻게 평가할 것인가'로 한다. 오답 3개는 텍스트 2 저자의 기준으로 평가한 결과, 두 저자의 기준을 섞은 평가, 일반 상식에 따른 평가로 만든다.
c.seed: history and civics — Westward expansion Indian Removal Act 1830 and forced Cherokee Trail of Tears displacement westward

g.passage:
Text 1
Historians who explain the Cherokee removal of 1838–1839 often credit a single cause, such as Andrew Jackson's personal hostility toward Native nations. In my view, an explanation of the Trail of Tears is persuasive only if it accounts for why removal happened when it did. Causes that existed for decades before 1830 cannot, by themselves, explain why forced displacement suddenly became federal policy in that particular decade.

Text 2
The roots of Cherokee removal lie in a settler hunger for land that stretched back to the colonial era. From the 1700s onward, white Americans steadily pressed westward, and each generation demanded more Cherokee territory. The Indian Removal Act of 1830 and the march west that followed were, in this sense, simply the culmination of a long-standing desire that had shaped frontier politics for nearly a century.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the explanation offered in Text 2?
options: As convincing, because tracing settler demand across several generations shows that the Removal Act grew out of deep and lasting pressures rather than one leader's attitudes
As partly convincing, because it avoids blaming a single individual, though it would be stronger if it also included Jackson's personal hostility as one of the causes
As convincing, because demand for land is widely recognized as the central force behind westward expansion and the conflicts it produced
As insufficient, because a desire that persisted for nearly a century does not by itself show why forced removal became federal policy in the 1830s
g.explanation: Text 1 저자의 기준은 '왜 하필 그 시점에 일어났는가'를 설명해야 한다는 것이며, 1830년 이전 수십 년간 존재한 원인만으로는 부족하다고 명시한다. Text 2는 거의 한 세기 지속된 토지 욕구를 원인으로 제시하므로, 바로 그 기준에 미달한다(D). A는 Text 2 저자 자신의 기준(장기적 뿌리의 깊이)으로 평가한 것이다. B는 두 기준을 섞은 평가로, Text 1이 단일 원인론을 비판한 점만 취하고 시기 기준은 빠뜨린 채 오히려 잭슨 요인을 더하라고 한다. C는 '토지 욕구가 서부 팽창의 핵심'이라는 일반 상식에 기댄 평가로 Text 1의 기준과 무관하다.
g.explanation_en:
Text 1's author sets a clear test: a good explanation of the Trail of Tears has to account for why removal happened when it did. The author also says that causes present for decades before 1830 can't explain the timing on their own. Text 2 points to land hunger that lasted nearly a century. That is exactly the kind of long-running cause Text 1 calls insufficient, so D is correct.
- A judges Text 2 by Text 2's own standard, which values deep, long-term roots.
- B mixes the two authors' standards. It picks up Text 1's criticism of single-cause explanations but drops the timing test, and it even suggests adding Jackson's hostility.
- C relies on common knowledge that land demand drove westward expansion, not on Text 1's stated test.
g.design: Text 1 states a timing-specific criterion; Text 2 gives a long-duration cause. The wrong answers apply Text 2's standard (A), a blend of the two standards (B), and common knowledge (C).

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Ottoman siege of Constantinople 1453 and Mehmed II's conquest ending Byzantine Empire thousand-year history

g.passage:
Text 1
Many popular accounts claim that Constantinople fell in 1453 mainly because of Mehmed II's enormous cannons. According to this view, the giant guns smashed the city's ancient walls, and the thousand-year Byzantine Empire simply could not survive against such new weapons.

Text 2
Mehmed II's cannons did damage the walls of Constantinople, but the guns were slow to reload, and defenders often repaired the broken sections overnight. Historians point out that the city had only about seven thousand defenders facing a much larger Ottoman army. Mehmed also moved ships overland into the Golden Horn, cutting the city off by sea. These factors together, not cannons alone, explain the conquest.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the popular accounts described in Text 1?
options: By arguing that these accounts give too much weight to a single cause and overlook other important reasons for the city's fall
By arguing that these accounts are correct because the cannons destroyed the walls faster than the defenders could repair them
By arguing that these accounts exaggerate the age of the Byzantine Empire and the strength of its walls
By arguing that these accounts wrongly suggest that Constantinople was ever conquered by the Ottomans
g.explanation: Text 1의 대중적 설명은 함락의 주된 원인을 대포로 본다. Text 2는 대포가 피해를 주긴 했지만 방어군이 밤사이 보수했다고 하며, 적은 방어 병력과 배를 육로로 옮긴 봉쇄 같은 다른 요인을 들어 대포만으로는 설명할 수 없다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 Text 2가 대포가 장전이 느렸고 성벽이 보수되었다고 말한 것과 반대된다. C는 Text 2가 제국의 역사나 성벽의 강도를 문제 삼지 않으므로 틀리고, D는 Text 2가 정복 자체는 인정하므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: Text 1 describes accounts that treat Mehmed II's cannons as the main reason Constantinople fell. Text 2 agrees that the cannons did damage, but it notes that defenders repaired the walls overnight, then points to other factors: the small number of defenders and the ships moved overland to block the city by sea. Its conclusion is that these factors together, not cannons alone, explain the conquest, so A is correct. B is wrong because Text 2 says the guns were slow to reload and the walls were repaired, which is the opposite of B's claim. C is wrong because Text 2 never questions how old the empire was or how strong its walls were. D is wrong because Text 2 clearly accepts that the conquest happened.
g.design: 이 문항은 한 단계 추론으로 푸는 easy 문항이다. Text 2가 마지막 문장에서 단일 원인론을 직접 반박하므로 정답 단서가 지문에 명시되어 있다. 오답은 '대포 원인론에 동의', '엉뚱한 세부 사항 반박', '정복 자체 부정'이라는 흔한 오개념으로 구성했고, 정답과 같은 'By arguing that these accounts...' 문장 틀을 썼다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Abolition movement anti-slavery activism 1780-1865 and transatlantic campaigns culminating in American Thirteenth Amendment

g.passage:
Text 1
Many popular accounts of the end of slavery in the United States focus on lawmakers in Washington. In these accounts, the Thirteenth Amendment, ratified in 1865, was mainly the achievement of skilled politicians who guided it through Congress.

Text 2
The Thirteenth Amendment did not come from Congress alone. For decades before 1865, formerly enslaved speakers such as Frederick Douglass, along with ordinary petition signers in the United States and Britain, built the public pressure that made the amendment possible. Without that long campaign, lawmakers would likely never have acted.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the popular accounts described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that the amendment was achieved mostly through the skill of politicians in Congress
By arguing that these accounts overlook the years of activism that pushed lawmakers to act
By arguing that these accounts give too much credit to British supporters of the amendment
By agreeing that petition signers played only a minor role in ending slavery
g.explanation: Text 1은 수정헌법 제13조를 주로 의회 정치인들의 업적으로 보는 통속적 서술을 소개하고, Text 2는 수십 년간의 노예제 폐지 운동이 만든 압력이 없었다면 의원들이 움직이지 않았을 것이라고 말한다. 따라서 Text 2의 저자는 그런 서술이 활동가들의 역할을 빠뜨렸다고 반박할 것이므로 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 Text 2가 명시적으로 부정하는 '정치인 중심'·'청원자 역할 미미' 관점에 동의하는 것이라 틀리다. C는 Text 1이 영국 지지자를 언급조차 하지 않으므로 근거가 없다.
g.explanation_en: Text 1 describes popular accounts that credit the Thirteenth Amendment mainly to skilled politicians in Congress. Text 2 says decades of activism by speakers and petition signers created the pressure that made lawmakers act, so its author would say those accounts leave out that activism, which is B. A and D are wrong because they agree with the politician-centered view that Text 2 directly rejects. C is wrong because Text 1 never mentions British supporters, so there is no extra credit for Text 2 to complain about.
g.design: Text 2가 Text 1의 견해를 직접 반박하는 단일 관계만 파악하면 되도록 구성했고, 오답은 동의/엉뚱한 대상 비판이라는 전형적 오개념으로 만들었다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Enlightenment salons Paris 1750-1789 and women intellectual gatekeepers promoting philosophe radical political ideas

g.passage: Historians have long credited the hostesses of Parisian salons, such as Julie de Lespinasse and Marie-Thérèse Geoffrin, with spreading the radical political ideas of the philosophes between 1750 and 1789. Historian Dena Goodman argues that these women did more than provide a meeting place: they set the rules of conversation, deciding who could speak and steering debates away from personal quarrels. But a closer look at salon records complicates the claim that hostesses actively promoted radical politics. Geoffrin, for instance, regularly barred discussion of current government policy at her gatherings and dropped guests whose writings drew the attention of royal censors, yet her salon remained one of the most important places where philosophes met to read and critique one another's unpublished work. Taken together, these facts suggest that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Geoffrin's rules of conversation kept radical political ideas from circulating among the philosophes who attended her salon.
Geoffrin promoted radical political ideas more effectively than other hostesses did because she controlled which guests could attend.
a hostess's influence on Enlightenment thought may have come more from supporting the exchange of ideas in general than from championing radical political positions.
the philosophes valued salons mainly as places to escape the attention of royal censors rather than as forums for critiquing new work.
g.explanation: 지문은 Geoffrin이 정치 논의를 막고 검열 대상이 된 손님을 배제했지만, 그녀의 살롱은 여전히 철학자들이 미발표 원고를 비평하는 중요한 장소였다고 말한다. 이 두 사실을 합치면, 살롱 주인의 영향력은 급진적 정치를 옹호하는 데서보다 사상 교류 전반을 지원하는 데서 나왔을 수 있다는 C가 가장 논리적이다. A는 정치 논의 금지라는 사실에는 맞지만, 그녀의 살롱이 사상 교류의 중심이었다는 점을 무시하고 급진 사상의 유통이 막혔다고 지나치게 단정한다. B는 손님 통제라는 사실을 근거로 삼지만, 그 통제가 오히려 급진 정치를 피하는 쪽으로 쓰였다는 점과 정반대다. D는 검열이라는 소재를 쓰지만, Geoffrin이 검열을 끄는 손님을 배제했다는 사실과 맞지 않고 비평 기능도 부정한다.
g.explanation_en: The passage tells you Geoffrin banned talk about current policy and dropped guests who caught the censors' attention, yet her salon was still a key place for philosophes to critique one another's unpublished work. Put those two facts together and C follows best: a hostess's influence may have come from supporting the exchange of ideas in general, not from championing radical politics. A fits the ban on policy talk, but it ignores the salon's role as a center of exchange and claims too much when it says radical ideas were stopped from circulating. B points to Geoffrin's control over guests, but she used that control to avoid radical politics, which is the opposite of what B says. D brings up censorship, but Geoffrin actually pushed out guests the censors were watching, and D also downplays the critiquing that the passage stresses.
g.design: To answer, you have to connect two facts: Geoffrin limited political talk, but her salon was still central to intellectual exchange. Wrong choices A, B, and D each grab one detail (the rules, control over guests, the censors) and are ruled out only by comparing them with the other fact.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: history and civics — Triangular trade Atlantic commerce 1500-1800 and three-way economic system exchanging manufactured goods enslaved peoples sugar

g.passage: Historians have long described Atlantic commerce between roughly 1500 and 1800 as a "triangular trade": European ships carried manufactured goods such as textiles and firearms to West Africa, transported enslaved Africans across the Atlantic to plantations in the Americas, and returned to Europe laden with sugar and other plantation crops. Economic historian Nuala Prendergast notes, however, that shipping records from Liverpool and Bristol show that many vessels completing the transatlantic crossing with enslaved people sailed home with little or no cargo, while most sugar reaching Europe arrived aboard separate ships that shuttled directly between Caribbean ports and Europe. If these records are representative, then the familiar image of single ships tracing all three legs of the route ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: shows that the slave trade made up only a minor part of Atlantic commerce during the period.
suggests that sugar was less valuable to European merchants than the manufactured goods shipped to West Africa.
indicates that Liverpool and Bristol played a smaller role in Atlantic commerce than historians have assumed.
may describe the overall pattern of goods exchanged better than it describes how individual voyages were actually organized.
g.explanation: 지문은 세 지역 간 상품 교환이 있었다는 점은 부정하지 않고, 다만 한 척의 배가 세 구간을 모두 운항했다는 이미지가 기록과 맞지 않는다고 지적하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 노예 무역의 규모를 다루지만 기록은 배의 운항 방식만 보여줄 뿐 규모가 작았다는 근거는 없다. B는 설탕이 별도 선박으로 운송되었다는 점을 가치가 낮았다는 뜻으로 잘못 확대한다. C는 기록의 출처인 항구를 언급하지만 두 항구의 역할이 작았다는 내용은 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: The passage doesn't deny that goods moved among the three regions. It only says the records don't fit the idea of one ship sailing all three legs, so D is correct. A is about how big the slave trade was, but the records only show how ships traveled, not that the trade was small. B treats the fact that sugar came on separate ships as proof that sugar was worth less, which the passage never says. C mentions the ports where the records came from, but nothing in the passage suggests those ports mattered less than historians thought.
g.design: 이 문항은 두 정보를 연결해야 풀 수 있습니다. 세 지역 간 교환이라는 패턴과 배가 실제로 따로 운항했다는 기록을 합쳐야 하며, 각 오답은 지문의 세부 사항(노예 무역, 설탕, 항구)을 가져와 지나치게 확대 해석하도록 만들었습니다.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: history and civics — Byzantine iconoclasm controversy 726-843 CE and religious conflict over religious image veneration in Eastern Christianity

g.passage:
Text 1
Historians have long explained Byzantine iconoclasm, the campaign against religious images that began under Emperor Leo III in 726 CE, as a theological dispute. On this view, Leo and his successors sincerely believed that venerating painted images of Christ and the saints amounted to idolatry, and the policy's eventual reversal in 843 CE reflected the triumph of a rival theology defending images.

Text 2
Surviving sources for the early phase of iconoclasm were written almost entirely by the image-venerating side after its victory, and they portray the iconoclast emperors as fanatics. Yet the few iconoclast documents that remain, such as the decrees of the council of 754 CE, do engage seriously with doctrine. What the victors' accounts obscure is how closely the emperors' policy tracked military fortune: images fell from favor after defeats by Arab armies and returned as the empire recovered, suggesting that rulers read battlefield results as signs of divine approval or anger.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the historians' explanation described in Text 1?
options: By granting that iconoclasts held real doctrinal convictions while arguing that this account overlooks how political circumstances shaped the policy's course
By granting that the policy changed over time while arguing that the iconoclast emperors held no genuine doctrinal convictions at all
By granting that doctrine shaped the policy while arguing that the council of 754 CE opposed the emperors' theology
By granting that image-venerating writers misrepresented the emperors while arguing that the controversy ended because Arab armies were finally defeated
g.explanation: Text 2의 저자는 754년 공의회 문서가 교리를 진지하게 다룬다고 인정하므로 신학적 동기를 부정하지 않으면서도, 정책이 군사적 성패에 따라 오르내렸다는 점을 Text 1이 놓쳤다고 본다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 Text 2가 황제들을 광신자로 그린 승자 측 서술을 비판하고 교리적 진지함을 인정하므로 틀리다. C는 754년 공의회가 황제의 신학에 반대했다는 근거가 없으며, 오히려 성상파괴 측 문서이다. D는 앞부분은 맞지만, Text 2는 제국의 회복을 성상 복귀와 연결할 뿐 아랍 군대의 최종 패배로 논쟁이 끝났다고 말하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The author of Text 2 admits that the council of 754 CE documents engage seriously with doctrine, so the author doesn't reject the theological motive. Instead, the author argues that Text 1's account misses how the policy rose and fell with military fortunes. That makes A the correct answer. B is wrong because Text 2 criticizes the victors' picture of the emperors as fanatics and acknowledges that they took doctrine seriously. C is wrong because the 754 council was an iconoclast source, and nothing in Text 2 says it opposed the emperors. D starts out plausibly, but Text 2 only links the empire's general recovery to the return of images; it never claims the controversy ended because Arab armies were finally defeated.
g.design: To get this right, you have to combine two clues from Text 2: its concession about doctrine and its added political explanation. B and D each match part of Text 2 but distort the rest, and C misreads which side the council was on.
