c.seed: history and civics — Indian indentured servitude colonial 1834-1920 and contracted Asian labor replacing slavery in Caribbean plantations

g.passage:
Text 1
After Britain abolished slavery in 1834, plantation owners in Trinidad and British Guiana turned to indentured laborers recruited from India. Some historians describe this system as fundamentally a free labor market: workers signed contracts, received wages, and were promised return passage after five years. On this view, indenture marked a genuine break from slavery, since laborers entered the arrangement by choice.

Text 2
Historian Madhavi Kale and others have examined the records of recruiters in Indian districts and magistrates in the colonies. Recruiters often misled villagers about destinations and pay, and many signers could not read the contracts. Once on plantations, workers who left without passes could be jailed under colonial labor laws, and wages were frequently withheld through fines. Such evidence suggests that the formal features of a contract tell us little about how much freedom workers actually had.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the historians' view described in Text 1?
options: By arguing that the view understates how much indentured workers earned, since wage records show that their pay often exceeded what they could earn in India
By arguing that the view relies too heavily on the terms written into contracts, since the way workers were recruited and held on plantations limited their choices
By arguing that the view ignores how quickly the system ended, since the colonies abandoned indenture soon after abolition took effect
By arguing that the view correctly identifies consent as decisive, since the records confirm that most workers understood the contracts they signed
g.explanation: Text 1의 역사가들은 계약·임금·귀환 약속 같은 형식적 요소를 근거로 계약노동을 자유노동으로 본다. Text 2는 모집 과정의 기만, 문맹, 통행증 없는 이탈 시 투옥, 벌금으로 인한 임금 공제를 들어 계약의 형식이 실제 자유를 보여주지 못한다고 하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 임금 문제를 언급하지만 오히려 임금이 원천징수되었다고 하므로 반대 방향이다. C는 제도 종료 시점을 다루지 않는다(오히려 1920년까지 지속). D는 Text 2가 많은 서명자가 계약을 읽지 못했다고 하므로 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: The historians in Text 1 treat indenture as free labor because of its formal features: contracts, wages, and promised return passage. Text 2 points to deceptive recruiting, workers who couldn't read their contracts, jailing for leaving without passes, and wages withheld through fines, and it concludes that a contract's formal terms reveal little about real freedom, so B is correct. A mentions wages, but Text 2 says wages were withheld, not that they were high. C is wrong because Text 2 never discusses when the system ended. D contradicts Text 2, which says many signers could not read the contracts.
g.design: To answer, students have to connect Text 1's reliance on formal contract terms with Text 2's evidence about actual conditions. A and D reuse details from Text 2 (wages, consent, records) but get their meaning backward, and C is a plausible historical claim that neither text supports.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).

c.seed: economics and business — Medieval Hanseatic League merchant network and Baltic trade monopoly in grain timber furs exchange

g.passage: During the 1300s, merchants of the Hanseatic League won special trading rights from rulers in many Baltic port cities. These rights allowed League members alone to buy and sell grain, timber, and furs in those markets. ______ merchants from outside the League were largely shut out of the region's most profitable trade.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 한자 동맹 상인만 곡물·목재·모피를 사고팔 수 있었다는 원인을 말하고, 마지막 문장은 그 때문에 외부 상인이 배제되었다는 결과를 말한다. 따라서 인과를 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 앞 내용의 구체적 사례를 들 때 쓰지만, 외부 상인의 배제는 사례가 아니라 결과이다. B는 대조를 나타내지만 두 문장은 서로 반대되지 않는다. D는 비슷한 다른 상황을 덧붙일 때 쓰지만, 여기서는 같은 상황이 낳은 결과를 말하고 있다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence gives a cause: only League members could buy and sell grain, timber, and furs in those markets. The last sentence gives the effect: outside merchants were shut out. A cause-and-effect transition fits, so C is correct. A introduces an example, but being shut out is a consequence, not an example of the rights. B signals contrast, yet the two sentences don't oppose each other. D adds a similar but separate situation, while this sentence describes what followed from the same situation.
g.design: 'alone'라는 명시적 단서로 독점이 외부 상인 배제로 이어지는 인과 관계를 한 단계 추론으로 파악하게 했다. 오답은 예시·대조·유사로 서로 다른 관계를 나타낸다.

c.seed: economics and business — Antwerp diamond trade fifteenth-century cutting techniques and gemstone valuation pricing standardization

g.passage: In the fifteenth century, diamond cutters in Antwerp adopted new polishing wheels that allowed them to shape stones into regular, symmetrical facets. Because these cuts followed consistent patterns, merchants could compare one stone with another far more easily than before. ______ buyers across Europe began to rely on shared standards when setting prices, and Antwerp grew into a major center of the diamond trade.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 규칙적인 연마 방식 덕분에 상인들이 보석을 쉽게 비교할 수 있게 되었다고 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 때문에 구매자들이 공통 기준으로 가격을 정하게 되었다는 결과를 제시한다. 따라서 원인-결과 관계를 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 대조를 나타내지만 두 문장은 서로 반대되지 않는다. B는 예시를 나타내지만 뒤 문장은 비교가 쉬워졌다는 사실의 구체적 사례가 아니라 그로 인해 생긴 결과이다. C는 유사한 사례를 덧붙일 때 쓰지만 뒤 문장은 앞 문장과 비슷한 별개의 상황이 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank says that regular cuts made diamonds easier to compare, and the sentence after it describes what happened because of that: buyers began using shared pricing standards. That is a cause-and-effect relationship, so D is correct. A signals contrast, but the two sentences don't oppose each other. B introduces an example, but the second sentence is a consequence, not a specific instance of stones becoming easier to compare. C points to a similar, separate case, but the second sentence follows directly from the first rather than paralleling it.

c.seed: economics and business — South Sea Bubble 1720 financial speculation and joint-stock company stock price manipulation scandal

g.passage: In 1720, shares in Britain's South Sea Company rose from about £128 to nearly £1,000 in just a few months. Company directors spread exaggerated stories about future trade profits, and many investors bought shares hoping to sell them quickly at even higher prices. By autumn, however, confidence collapsed and the share price ______, falling back below £200 and leaving thousands of investors with heavy losses.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 빈칸 바로 뒤의 "falling back below £200"과 "heavy losses"는 주가가 갑자기 크게 떨어졌다는 것을 직접 보여 주므로, '급락하다'라는 뜻의 A가 정답이다. B는 '안정되다'라는 뜻으로 가격이 급격히 떨어진 상황과 맞지 않는다. C는 '치솟다'라는 뜻이어서 하락이라는 내용과 정반대이며, 앞부분의 상승 이야기만 보고 고르기 쉬운 오답이다. D는 '오르내리다'라는 뜻이어서 한 방향으로 급격히 떨어졌다는 의미를 정확히 담지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: Right after the blank, the text says the price was "falling back below £200" and left investors with "heavy losses." That tells you the price dropped sharply, so A, which means "fell suddenly and steeply," is correct. B means "became steady," which doesn't match such a dramatic drop. C means "rose rapidly," the opposite of falling; it's tempting only if you focus on the earlier part of the story, when prices went up. D means "moved up and down," which misses the clear one-way collapse the text describes.
g.design: 빈칸 직후 "falling back below £200"이라는 명시적 단서 하나로 방향(급락)을 판별하게 했고, 오답은 같은 품사의 가격 변동 동사로 구성했다.

c.seed: economics and business — Scottish banking system nineteenth-century free banking and note-issuing competition without central regulation

g.passage: From the early 1700s until 1845, Scotland had no central bank controlling its money. Instead, many private banks competed with one another, and each printed its own paper notes. Some observers expected such a system to collapse. In fact, Scottish banking proved remarkably ______: bank failures were rare, and people holding the notes of a failed bank almost never lost their money.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 콜론 뒤의 설명(은행 파산이 드물었고 지폐 보유자가 돈을 거의 잃지 않았다)이 빈칸의 의미를 직접 알려 주며, 'In fact'는 붕괴할 것이라는 예상과 반대되는 결과를 나타낸다. 따라서 '안정적인'을 뜻하는 B가 정답이다. A는 중앙 규제가 없으면 혼란스러울 것이라는 예상에는 맞지만, 지문이 반박하는 바로 그 예상이다. C와 D는 비용이나 비밀성에 관한 말로, 파산이 드물고 손실이 적었다는 근거와 관련이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The words after the colon explain the blank: bank failures were rare, and noteholders almost never lost money. "In fact" also tells you the result went against the prediction that the system would collapse. So B, "stable," is correct. A fits what the doubters expected, but the passage says that expectation was wrong. C and D are about cost and secrecy, and the evidence about rare failures and small losses says nothing about either one.
g.design: The clue for the blank sits right after the colon and takes one step to use. The wrong answers include the common belief that "unregulated means chaotic" plus two plausible words about the banking system that don't fit the clue.

c.seed: economics and business — Japanese silk standardization Meiji period and quality grading export market competitiveness silk filature

g.passage: During Japan's Meiji period (1868–1912), many silk filatures, the factories where silk thread is reeled from cocoons, began following national inspection rules so that they could compete in foreign markets. Under this system, each batch of thread was graded by its evenness and strength. The grading standards for raw silk ______ buyers in New York and Lyon a reliable way to compare thread from different Japanese mills, which helped Japan become the world's leading silk exporter by the early twentieth century.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 "standards"이다. "for raw silk"는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이므로 동사는 복수형이어야 하고, 따라서 C "give"가 정답이다. A "gives", B "has given", D "is giving"은 모두 단수 동사형이다. 이 선택지들은 동사 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "silk"에 동사를 맞춘 경우로, 복수 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "standards." The phrase "for raw silk" only describes the subject, so the verb has to be plural, which makes C ("give") correct. A ("gives"), B ("has given"), and D ("is giving") are all singular verb forms. They match the singular noun "silk," which sits right before the blank, instead of the actual plural subject, so they don't agree in number.
g.design: 짧은 전치사구 수식어가 붙은 복수 주어에 대해 주어-동사 수 일치 규칙 하나만 묻는다. 오답 3개는 모두 근처 단수 명사에 끌린 단수형이다.

c.seed: economics and business — Cork industry Portugal and wine bottle stopper manufacturing monopoly market dominance

g.passage: Portugal produces roughly half of the world's cork, much of it stripped by hand from the bark of cork oak trees in the Alentejo region. The country's largest cork company, along with its many smaller suppliers, ______ millions of wine stoppers each year, a level of output that has given Portugal a dominant position in the global market.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'company'이고, 'along with its many smaller suppliers'는 삽입된 수식어일 뿐 주어를 복수로 만들지 않는다. 따라서 단수 동사가 필요하며, D의 'manufactures'가 올바르다. A, B, C는 각각 복수 동사(manufacture, are manufacturing, have manufactured)로, 바로 앞의 'suppliers'나 'along with'를 'and'처럼 보고 주어를 복수로 착각한 오답이다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "company." The phrase "along with its many smaller suppliers" is just an added modifier, so it doesn't make the subject plural. That means the sentence needs a singular verb, and D, "manufactures," is correct. A, B, and C all use plural verbs ("manufacture," "are manufacturing," "have manufactured"). Those choices fall for the trap of treating the nearby word "suppliers," or the phrase "along with," as though it made the subject plural the way "and" would.
g.design: 주어와 동사 사이의 짧은 'along with' 수식어 하나만 넘기면 되는 단일 수 일치 규칙 문제로, 오답은 모두 복수 동사로 구성했다.

c.seed: economics and business — Swiss watchmaking precision manufacturing and temporal standardization enabling railway schedule coordination

g.passage: In the mid-1800s, Swiss workshops began producing pocket watches with interchangeable, machine-made parts, which made accurate watches far cheaper than before. Economic historian Lena Marti argues that this drop in price helped railways run on tighter schedules: once ordinary station workers and conductors could afford reliable watches, she claims, trains could be coordinated to the minute rather than only roughly.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marti's claim?
options: Railway lines whose staff bought low-cost Swiss watches reported fewer late departures than lines whose staff did not have such watches.
Swiss watch exports to wealthy collectors rose sharply during the same decades that new railway lines were built.
Some railway companies printed their timetables in larger type after the 1860s so that passengers could read them easily.
Watchmakers in other countries also experimented with machine-made parts, though their watches remained costly.
g.explanation: Marti의 주장은 '값싼 정확한 시계를 철도 직원이 갖게 되면서 열차 운행이 더 정밀하게 조정되었다'는 것이다. A는 저가 스위스 시계를 산 직원이 있는 노선이 지연 출발이 더 적었다는 발견으로, 시계 보급과 일정 정확성을 직접 연결해 주장을 지지한다. B는 부유한 수집가 대상 수출이라 일반 직원의 시계 보유와 무관하다. C는 시간표 인쇄 방식의 변화일 뿐 시계와 관련이 없고, D는 다른 나라 시계에 관한 내용이라 철도 일정과 연결되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Marti claims that once railway workers could afford reliable, cheap watches, trains could be scheduled more precisely. Choice A directly connects workers owning low-cost Swiss watches with fewer late departures, so it supports the claim. Choice B is about wealthy collectors, not ordinary railway staff. Choice C describes a change in how timetables were printed, which has nothing to do with watches, and Choice D concerns watches from other countries without linking them to railway timing.
g.design: Easy: the claim links two things (cheap watches for staff → precise schedules), and only A connects both; distractors share one topic word but miss the link.

c.seed: economics and business — Optical lens manufacturing patents and industrial espionage in nineteenth-century German optical instrument firms

g.passage: In the nineteenth century, German optical firms competed fiercely to make better lenses for microscopes and telescopes. Some firms protected their glass recipes with patents, which made the recipes public but legally barred others from copying them for a set period. Other firms kept their recipes as closely guarded workshop secrets. Economic historian Lena Hartmann argues that secrecy, not patenting, was the more effective way for these firms to protect their lens-making knowledge from rivals during this period.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Hartmann's claim?
options: Firms that patented their glass recipes usually employed more workers than firms that kept their recipes secret.
Firms that kept their glass recipes secret were copied by rivals far less often than firms that patented their recipes.
Firms that patented their glass recipes often sold their lenses in more foreign countries than firms that kept their recipes secret.
Firms that kept their glass recipes secret spent more money on workshop equipment than firms that patented their recipes.
g.design: 하나의 규칙(주장의 핵심은 '경쟁사로부터 지식을 보호하는 효과')만으로 풀리도록 했고, 오답은 같은 비교 틀을 쓰되 직원 수·수출·장비 지출처럼 보호 효과와 무관한 지표를 비교하게 만들었다.
g.explanation: Hartmann은 경쟁사로부터 렌즈 제조 지식을 지키는 데 특허보다 비밀 유지가 더 효과적이었다고 주장한다. B는 비밀을 유지한 회사가 경쟁사에게 훨씬 덜 모방당했다고 하므로 '보호 효과'를 직접 보여 주어 주장을 지지한다. A는 회사 규모를 다룰 뿐 지식 보호와는 관계가 없다. C는 해외 판매 범위에 관한 것이라 모방 방지 효과를 보여 주지 못한다. D는 장비 지출에 관한 것으로, 돈을 더 썼다고 해서 지식이 더 잘 보호되었다는 뜻은 아니다.
g.explanation_en: Hartmann claims that keeping recipes secret protected lens-making knowledge from rivals better than patenting did. B says secret-keeping firms were copied far less often than patenting firms, and that directly shows better protection, so it supports her claim. A is about how many workers a firm had, which tells you nothing about protecting knowledge. C is about how many foreign markets a firm sold in, not about whether rivals copied it. D is about spending on equipment, and spending more money doesn't show that a firm's knowledge was better protected.

c.seed: economics and business — Kenyan tea auction system Mombasa and price discovery mechanism for smallholder farmer cooperative sales

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Mombasa Tea Auction in Kenya is one of the largest tea auctions in the world.
- It is run by the East African Tea Trade Association, founded in 1957.
- Each week, buyers bid on lots of tea, and the highest bid sets the price for that lot.
- This bidding process lets prices reflect current demand for different teas.
- Many Kenyan smallholder farmers sell their leaves through cooperatives whose tea is sold at the auction.
g.question: The student wants to explain how prices are determined at the Mombasa Tea Auction. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Mombasa Tea Auction, one of the largest tea auctions in the world, is run by the East African Tea Trade Association.
Many Kenyan smallholder farmers sell their leaves through cooperatives, and that tea is sold at the Mombasa Tea Auction.
At the Mombasa Tea Auction, buyers bid on lots of tea each week, and the highest bid sets each lot's price, so prices reflect current demand.
The East African Tea Trade Association, which runs the Mombasa Tea Auction, was founded in 1957.
g.design: 목표가 가격 결정 방식을 다룬 메모 3·4와 직접 대응하는 쉬운 문항이다. 오답들은 같은 경매를 다루는 다른 메모(규모, 운영 기관, 소농 협동조합)를 사용한다.
g.explanation: 목표는 경매에서 가격이 어떻게 정해지는지 설명하는 것입니다. C는 구매자들이 입찰하고 가장 높은 입찰가가 가격이 되며, 그 결과 가격이 수요를 반영한다고 설명하므로 정답입니다. A는 경매의 규모와 운영 기관만 소개하고, D는 운영 기관의 설립 연도만 제시합니다. B는 소농이 차를 어떻게 판매하는지를 설명할 뿐 가격 결정 방식에는 답하지 않습니다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain how prices are set at the auction. C does this: buyers bid, the highest bid sets each lot's price, and so prices reflect demand. A only gives the auction's size and who runs it, and D only gives the year the association was founded. B describes how smallholder farmers sell their tea, but it never explains how the price is set.

c.seed: economics and business — Filipino copra trade coconut oil production and colonial extraction economic dependency patterns

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Copra is the dried meat, or kernel, of the coconut.
- Coconut oil is pressed from copra and was used in soap, margarine, and candles.
- In the early 1900s, the Philippines was under United States colonial rule.
- During that period, much of the copra grown in the Philippines was shipped abroad for processing.
- As a result, many Filipino farming communities relied on a single export crop whose price was set by foreign buyers.
g.question: The student wants to explain what copra is to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In the early 1900s, copra was grown in the Philippines while the country was under United States colonial rule.
Copra grown in the Philippines was often shipped abroad, leaving farmers dependent on prices set by foreign buyers.
Copra was a crop that many Filipino farming communities relied on as their single export.
Copra, the dried kernel of the coconut, is the source of an oil once used in soap, margarine, and candles.

Its members collectively own a share of Divine Chocolate, a company that sells chocolate bars made from their beans. Because of this arrangement, farmers receive more than just a price for their cocoa ______ they also earn a portion of the company's profits and hold seats on its board.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "farmers receive more than just a price for their cocoa"와 뒤 "they also earn ... board"는 각각 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 연결하려면 세미콜론이 필요하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 쉼표 스플라이스이다. C는 아무 부호 없이 이어 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 "and" 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 있고 "they"가 중복되어 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("farmers receive more than just a price for their cocoa") and the text after it ("they also earn ... board") are both independent clauses. Two independent clauses joined without a conjunction need a semicolon, so A is correct. B links the two clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between them, so it's a run-on sentence. D puts an unnecessary comma after "and" and repeats "they," so the sentence doesn't work.

The invention allowed his small Austrian firm to supply sparkling stones to fashion jewelers at a fraction of the usual ______ costume jewelry soon became affordable to shoppers who could never have bought diamonds.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 독립절 두 개 사이 경계를 묻는 기본 문제로, 연결부사 'as a result'를 접속사로 착각하는 전형적 오개념(쉼표 스플라이스·무구두점 연결)을 오답으로 삼았다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'The invention allowed ... usual price'와 뒤 'costume jewelry soon became affordable ...'는 각각 독립절이다. 'as a result'는 접속사가 아닌 연결부사이므로 두 독립절은 마침표로 나누어야 하며, B가 이를 지킨다. A와 D는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 구두점 없이 두 독립절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("The invention allowed ... usual price") form an independent clause, and so do the words after it ("costume jewelry soon became affordable ..."). "As a result" is a transitional phrase, not a conjunction, so the two clauses need to be split with a period, and that's what B does. A and D join the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all between the clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence.

g.passage: The city of Tiruppur in southern India produces a large share of the country's knitted cotton garments. Thousands of small firms there each specialize in a single step, such as dyeing, knitting, or stitching ______ by sharing work among these firms, the cluster can fill large export orders quickly.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Thousands of small firms ... stitching"과 뒤 "by sharing work ... the cluster can fill large export orders quickly"는 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 마침표로 나누는 것이 맞으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 부호 없이 이어 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 접속사 and 뒤에 쉼표가 잘못 붙어 있고, 뒤 절의 도입구 "by sharing work among these firms" 다음에 이미 쉼표가 있어 문장이 어색해진다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("Thousands of small firms ... stitching") and the words after it ("by sharing work ... the cluster can fill large export orders quickly") are both independent clauses. Two independent clauses can be separated with a period, so C is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B uses no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D puts a comma after the conjunction "and," which is incorrect, and the introductory phrase in the second clause already ends with its own comma, so the sentence reads awkwardly.
g.design: It's an easy item because the boundary between the two independent clauses is easy to see. The wrong answers are the typical mistakes: a comma splice, a run-on sentence, and a misplaced comma after a conjunction.

g.passage: After the United Nations imposed sanctions on Rhodesia in 1966, the colony's tobacco trade, which had previously supplied a large share of the leaf bought by British cigarette manufacturers, ______ to survive by routing harvests through intermediaries in neighboring countries and selling them under falsified certificates of origin.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "trade"이고, which로 시작하는 관계절은 수식어일 뿐이므로 주절에는 정동사가 필요하다. D의 "attempted"는 단수 주어와 맞는 과거 정동사이므로 문장이 완성된다. A의 "attempting"과 C의 "having attempted"는 분사라서 주절에 정동사가 없게 되어 문장이 불완전해진다. B의 "were attempting"은 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "manufacturers"에 수를 맞춘 복수형이어서 단수 주어 "trade"와 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "trade." The "which" clause is only a modifier, so the main clause still needs a finite verb. D, "attempted," is a finite past-tense verb that works with a singular subject, so it completes the sentence correctly. A ("attempting") and C ("having attempted") are participles, which means the main clause would have no finite verb and the sentence would be a fragment. B ("were attempting") is a finite verb, but it's plural, as if it agreed with the nearby noun "manufacturers," so it doesn't agree with the singular subject "trade."
g.design: 긴 관계절이 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 복수 명사 manufacturers가 동사 바로 앞에 오도록 했다. 그래서 학생은 정동사가 필요한지와 주어-동사 수 일치를 두 단계로 판단해야 한다.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'arrangements'이고, 'which ~ landowner'는 주어를 꾸미는 삽입 관계절이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 정동사이지만 빈칸 바로 앞의 단수 명사 'landowner'에 수를 맞춘 것이어서 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C와 D는 분사 형태라 정동사 역할을 할 수 없어서, 문장에 본동사가 없는 비문이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "arrangements," and the clause "which often require... landowner" just interrupts between the subject and its verb. The blank therefore needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject, so A is correct. B is a finite verb, but it is singular because it matches the nearby noun "landowner" rather than the real subject. C and D are participle forms, which can't serve as the main verb, so either one would leave the sentence without a main verb.
g.design: 긴 삽입 관계절이 주어와 동사 사이를 떼어 놓고, 빈칸 바로 앞에 단수 명사를 두어 수 일치 함정을 만들었다. 이와 함께 정동사인지 분사인지도 판단해야 하도록 구성했다.

g.passage: After Croatia's independence, the state-owned shipyards of Split, Rijeka, and Pula faced competitors in South Korea and China that could build vessels far more cheaply. In 2013, as a condition of joining the European Union, the government agreed to privatize the yards and end the subsidies that had kept them afloat. The restructuring plans, which required the yards to cut capacity and shed thousands of jobs, ______ intended to make the industry competitive without state support, but several yards later entered bankruptcy proceedings.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수형 "The restructuring plans"이고, 쉼표 사이의 관계절은 주어를 꾸미는 삽입 어구일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 복수 주어에 맞는 정동사가 필요하므로 B "were"가 정답이다. A "was"는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "capacity"나 "job"에 끌려 고른 단수형이어서 주어와 수가 맞지 않는다. C "having been"과 D "being"은 분사형이라 주어에 대응하는 정동사가 없어지고, 결국 주절이 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "The restructuring plans," and the relative clause set off by commas just describes that subject. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject, which makes B, "were," correct. A, "was," is a finite verb, but it's singular, probably chosen because nearby words like "capacity" or "jobs" are distracting, so it doesn't agree with the subject. C, "having been," and D, "being," are participles, which leaves the subject without a main verb, so the main clause isn't complete.

g.passage: For decades, most of the raw cashew nuts harvested in Tanzania were shipped abroad, primarily to India and Vietnam, where they were shelled, roasted, and packaged for sale. Economists have long argued that this arrangement leaves farming regions with only a small share of the crop's final value. Recently, however, a cooperative of growers in the Mtwara region, along with several private investors seeking to capture more of that value at home, ______ a series of local processing plants that handle every stage from drying to vacuum-sealing.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'a cooperative'이고, 'along with several private investors...'는 삽입된 수식어구라서 주어의 수에 영향을 주지 않는다. 문장에는 아직 정동사가 없으므로 단수 정동사가 필요하고, 따라서 C 'has opened'가 정답이다. A는 정동사이지만 바로 앞의 'investors'나 'home'에 맞춘 복수형이어서 단수 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다. B와 D는 분사 형태라 정동사가 될 수 없으므로 문장이 완성되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "a cooperative." Since the sentence doesn't have a main verb yet, you need a singular finite verb, which makes C, "has opened," the answer. A is a finite verb, but it's plural, matching the nearby "investors" rather than the actual subject. B and D are participles, and a participle can't act as the main verb, so either one would leave the sentence incomplete.

g.passage: Founded in Gothenburg, Sweden, in 1907, the company SKF built its reputation on the self-aligning ball bearing devised by engineer Sven Wingquist. Because the firm machined each bearing to tightly specified dimensions, a worn bearing in a textile loom or an automobile axle could be swapped for any new one of the same size without custom fitting. This interchangeability, which manufacturers in dozens of countries ______ by the 1920s, helped make large-scale assembly-line production practical.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸은 관계절 'which manufacturers in dozens of countries ___'에 들어가므로, 주어 manufacturers에 맞는 정동사가 필요하다. D의 'had come to rely on'은 정동사이고, 'by the 1920s'라는 과거 기준 시점까지 완료된 상황을 나타내는 과거완료형이라 문맥에도 맞는다. A의 현재분사 'relying on'은 정동사가 아니어서 관계절이 성립하지 않는다. B의 'having come to rely on'은 완료의 의미는 맞지만 분사형이라 마찬가지로 동사 역할을 할 수 없다. C의 to부정사 역시 정동사가 아니므로 관계절이 불완전해진다.
g.explanation_en: The blank falls inside the relative clause "which manufacturers in dozens of countries ___," so the subject "manufacturers" needs a finite verb. D, "had come to rely on," is a finite verb, and its past perfect tense fits the past reference point "by the 1920s." A, the present participle "relying on," is not a finite verb, so the relative clause is left incomplete. B, "having come to rely on," gets the idea of completion right, but it is still a participle and can't act as the clause's main verb. C, an infinitive, also isn't a finite verb, so the clause stays incomplete.
g.design: 긴 관계절 안에서 주어 뒤에 정동사를 골라야 하는 구조이다. B는 완료의 의미를 담고 있고 A·C도 말이 되는 듯 보여서, 훑어 읽으면 고르기 쉽게 만들었다.

g.passage: In the mid-nineteenth century, British planters in Bengal controlled much of the world's supply of natural indigo, a blue dye extracted from the leaves of Indigofera plants. Their dominance, however, proved fragile: after German chemists developed an inexpensive synthetic version in 1897, the price of indigo produced by the Bengali estates, which had already been weakened by peasant revolts against coercive cultivation contracts, ______ so sharply that many plantations shut down within two decades.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 절의 주어는 단수 명사 'the price'이며, 'of indigo produced by the Bengali estates'와 관계절 'which had ... contracts'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이므로 단수 정동사가 필요하고, 1897년 이후의 과거 사건이므로 과거시제가 맞다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 과거시제이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'estates'나 'contracts'에 이끌린 복수형 'were'라서 단수 주어와 맞지 않는다. C는 복수형인 데다 현재완료여서 과거 서술 문맥에도 어긋난다. D는 분사라 'after'절 뒤의 주절에 정동사가 없게 되어 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this clause is the singular noun "the price." The phrase "of indigo produced by the Bengali estates" and the clause "which had ... contracts" only modify that subject, so you need a singular finite verb, and because the events happened after 1897, it should be in the past tense. That makes A correct. B is past tense, but "were" is plural, so it agrees with the nearby plural nouns "estates" or "contracts" instead of "price." C is also plural, and its present perfect tense doesn't fit a narrative about the past. D is a participle, which would leave the main clause after the "after" clause without a finite verb.
g.design: 수식어구와 관계절로 주어와 동사 사이를 멀리 떼어 놓고, 빈칸 바로 앞에 복수 명사를 두어 수 일치 판단과 시제·정동사 판단을 함께 하도록 했다.

Remarkably, the hierarchy, which brokers compiled from merchants' sales records rather than from tastings of the wines themselves, ______ almost unchanged for more than 160 years, and economists note that an estate's tier still reliably predicts the price its bottles fetch today.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'the hierarchy'이고, 그 뒤에 이어지는 'which ... themselves' 관계절은 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 삽입 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 빈칸 바로 앞의 복수 명사(records, wines)에 맞춘 복수 동사여서 주어 'hierarchy'와 수가 일치하지 않는다. C와 D는 분사 형태라서 'the hierarchy'로 시작하는 절에 정동사가 없게 되고, 그 결과 ', and economists note...'와 연결되는 앞 절이 문법적으로 불완전해진다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this clause is the singular noun "the hierarchy." The relative clause "which ... themselves" just interrupts between the subject and its verb. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, and that makes B correct. A is a plural verb that matches the nearby plural nouns "records" and "wines" instead of the real subject, "hierarchy." C and D are participles, so they leave the clause starting with "the hierarchy" without a main verb. That makes the first clause, which is joined to ", and economists note...", grammatically incomplete.
g.design: 긴 비제한 관계절이 단수 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓고, 빈칸 바로 앞에 복수 명사를 배치해 복수 동사 오답을 유도했다. 분사형 오답 두 개는 절에 정동사가 필요하다는 점을 확인해야 배제할 수 있다.

g.passage: Norway's salmon farms, which produce more than a million metric tons of fish each year, have long been praised as an economic success. Yet economists studying the industry argue that its low market prices conceal real costs: sea lice that breed in crowded open-net pens and spread to wild salmon, along with nutrient waste released into the fjords, ______ by coastal communities and fisheries rather than by the farming companies themselves.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 콜론 뒤 절의 주어는 'sea lice'(복수)이며, 'along with nutrient waste...'는 삽입된 수식어이므로 주어의 수에 영향을 주지 않는다. 또한 이 절에는 정동사가 필요하므로 복수 정동사 C가 정답이다. A는 정동사이지만 바로 앞 단수 명사 'waste'나 'fjords' 근처 구조에 끌린 단수형이라 주어와 수가 맞지 않는다. B와 D는 분사형이라 콜론 뒤 절에 정동사가 없게 되어 불완전한 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The clause after the colon has the subject "sea lice," which is plural. The phrase "along with nutrient waste released into the fjords" is an added modifier, so it doesn't change the number of the subject. That clause also needs a main verb, so the plural main verb in C is correct. A is a main verb, but it's singular, probably pulled that way by the nearby noun "waste," so it doesn't agree with the subject. B and D are participles, which would leave the clause after the colon with no main verb and make it incomplete.
g.design: 긴 'along with' 삽입구가 단수 명사로 끝나 수 일치를 흐리게 하고, 분사 오답으로 정동사 필요성까지 함께 판단하게 했다.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "according to" 뒤 절의 주어는 "the practice"(단수)이고, "of hedging ... 1,000 acres"는 이를 꾸미는 수식어구이다. 이 절에는 정동사가 없으므로 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하며, 따라서 D가 정답이다. B는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "acres"에 맞춘 복수형이라 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다. A의 분사와 C의 부정사는 정동사가 아니어서 절이 완성되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the clause after "according to" is the singular noun "the practice," and the phrase "of hedging ... 1,000 acres" just modifies it. That clause has no main verb yet, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, which makes D the answer. B is a finite verb, but it's plural because it matches the nearby noun "acres" instead of the real subject. A, a participle, and C, an infinitive, aren't finite verbs, so the clause would be left incomplete.
g.design: 긴 전치사 수식어구가 단수 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓았다. 그래서 정동사가 필요하다는 점과 수 일치를 둘 다 판단해야 한다. 바로 앞의 "acres"가 복수형 B를 고르도록 유도한다.

g.explanation: 세미콜론 앞 절의 주어는 복수 명사 "differences"이고, "in pay between jobs in the primary sector... and jobs in the secondary sector"는 이를 꾸미는 긴 수식어구다. 따라서 이 절에는 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하므로 A가 정답이다. C and D are participles, so they'd leave the clause without a main verb, and the part before the semicolon wouldn't be a complete sentence.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'The rebates'이고, 'that ... insurers'와 'typically calculated ... price'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이므로 빈칸에는 복수형 정동사가 필요하다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 정동사이지만 단수형이어서, 가까이 있는 단수 명사 'price'나 'manufacturer' 계열 단어에 맞춘 오류이다. C와 D는 분사 형태여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되고, 그 결과 문장이 완성되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "The rebates." g.design: 주어와 동사 사이에 관계절과 분사구를 길게 끼워 넣고, 빈칸 바로 앞에 단수 명사 'price'를 두어 수 일치를 헷갈리게 했다. 또한 정동사와 분사 중 무엇을 고를지도 판단해야 하도록 두 단계로 설계했다.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: economics and business — Venture capital syndication networks technology hubs and geographic concentration startup funding Silicon Valley dominance

g.passage: Economists have long assumed that the internet would weaken the pull of geography on startup funding: if investors can review pitch decks and hold meetings from anywhere, capital should flow more evenly across regions. Venture capital firms, however, rarely invest alone; they form syndicates, sharing deals with partners they already know and trust. A 2021 analysis of more than 9,000 early-stage deals found that firms based outside major hubs were far more likely to join a syndicate when a lead investor from Silicon Valley or Boston was already involved. ______ the networks that were expected to spread capital outward have tended to route it back through a few established centers.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 마지막 문장은 앞 문장의 연구 결과(외부 투자자가 실리콘밸리·보스턴 주도 투자자를 따라 신디케이트에 참여함)가 실제로 무엇을 의미하는지 요약·해석하는 문장이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 지문 전체에 '기대 vs. 현실'의 대조가 있어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 바로 앞 문장과 마지막 문장은 서로 반대되는 내용이 아니라 같은 방향의 내용이다. B는 마지막 문장이 구체적 사례가 아니라 오히려 앞 사례를 일반화한 결론이므로 맞지 않는다. D는 새로운 유사 현상을 덧붙이는 것이 아니라 같은 현상을 해석하는 문장이므로 부적절하다.
g.explanation_en: The last sentence sums up what the study's finding actually means: if investors outside the hubs mostly join deals led by Silicon Valley or Boston firms, then capital keeps flowing back through those centers. That makes C the answer. A looks tempting because the passage as a whole contrasts expectation with reality, but the sentence right before the blank and the final sentence point in the same direction, so they don't contrast. B is wrong because the final sentence isn't a specific example; it's a general conclusion drawn from the example before it. D is wrong because the final sentence doesn't add a separate, similar phenomenon; it interprets the same one.
g.design: '기대와 반전' 구조 때문에 Nevertheless에 끌리게 했지만, 빈칸 바로 앞 문장과는 요약·해석 관계라서 두 단계로 판단해야 한다. 오답은 모두 같은 전환어 형식으로 맞췄다.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: economics and business — Automated valuation models real estate and algorithmic bias reproducing racial discrimination mortgage lending

g.passage: Automated valuation models (AVMs) estimate a home's worth by analyzing recent sales of comparable properties nearby, and lenders increasingly rely on them because they promise to remove the subjective judgments of human appraisers. Removing the appraiser, however, does not remove history. In neighborhoods where decades of discriminatory lending held down sale prices, the comparable sales an AVM draws on already carry that suppressed value. ______ a model that never considers a homeowner's race can still assign systematically lower valuations to homes in predominantly Black neighborhoods, limiting how much those owners can borrow.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.design: 빈칸 앞은 원인(과거 차별로 억눌린 비교 매매가가 데이터에 내재), 뒤는 그 결과(인종을 고려하지 않는 모델도 낮은 평가)이다. 'never considers race ... can still'의 양보적 어감이 A를, 구체적 사례처럼 보이는 내용이 B를 끌어들이도록 설계했다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 AVM이 참고하는 비교 매매가에 이미 과거 차별로 억눌린 가치가 담겨 있다는 원인을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 때문에 인종을 고려하지 않는 모델도 흑인 다수 지역 주택을 낮게 평가한다는 결과를 제시하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 뒤 문장의 'never considers ... can still'이라는 양보적 표현에 끌리게 하지만, 앞 문장 내용과 대조되는 것이 아니라 앞 문장에서 그대로 이어지는 내용이므로 틀리다. B는 뒤 문장이 구체적으로 보이지만, 앞 문장의 일반적 주장을 보여주는 한 가지 사례가 아니라 그 주장에서 도출되는 결과이다. C는 두 문장이 서로 다른 대상을 비교하는 것이 아니므로 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank gives a cause: the comparable sales an AVM uses already carry values held down by past discrimination. The sentence after the blank gives the effect of that cause: even a model that ignores race undervalues homes in predominantly Black neighborhoods. That makes D the answer. A may look tempting because of the concessive wording "never considers ... can still," but the second sentence follows directly from the first rather than contradicting it. B doesn't work because the second sentence isn't one example of a general claim; it's a consequence of the previous point. C is wrong because the text isn't contrasting two different things.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: economics and business — Supply chain diversification strategy and geographic concentration risk following COVID-19 pandemic manufacturing disruptions

g.passage: After factory shutdowns in 2020 left shelves empty and assembly lines idle, many electronics and apparel firms announced plans to reduce their dependence on a single manufacturing hub. Surveys of procurement managers in the following years showed that a growing share of companies had moved at least some final assembly to plants in Vietnam, Mexico, or India. ______ economists tracing the inputs to those new plants found that most of their circuit boards, fabrics, and specialty chemicals were still shipped from the same handful of suppliers the firms had relied on before, meaning the geographic concentration risk had largely shifted upstream rather than disappeared.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 기업들이 조립 공장을 여러 나라로 옮겨 분산화한 것처럼 보인다는 점을 인정한다. 뒷 문장은 핵심 부품이 여전히 같은 공급처에서 온다는 사실을 들어, 그 분산화가 실제로는 위험을 줄이지 못했다고 반박한다. 따라서 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 공장 이전이 부품 의존을 일으켰다는 인과 관계를 암시하지만, 지문에서 의존은 이전 때문이 아니라 원래부터 이어져 온 것이다. C와 D는 뒷 문장을 앞 내용의 유사 사례나 예시로 만들어 버리는데, 뒷 문장은 앞 내용을 뒷받침하지 않고 오히려 그 한계를 지적한다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence grants that firms seem to have diversified by moving assembly to new countries. The next sentence pushes back: key inputs still come from the same few suppliers, so the risk wasn't actually reduced. A signals this concession followed by a reversal, so A is correct. B suggests that the relocation caused the dependence, but the text says the dependence continued from before and wasn't created by the move. C and D would make the final sentence a parallel case or an example of the earlier claim, when it actually points out that claim's limits.
g.design: There is no contrast word in the passage, so readers have to see that the second sentence undercuts the apparent diversification. B is tempting because the relocation does come first in time, and D is tempting because the sentence contains detailed evidence.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: economics and business — Labor union density decline manufacturing and wage inequality correlation post-industrial region economic stagnation

g.passage: Between 1980 and 2010, the share of manufacturing workers belonging to labor unions in the Ohio River valley fell by more than half as factories closed or relocated. Unions there had long negotiated pay scales that narrowed the gap between the lowest- and highest-paid employees on a factory floor, so their retreat removed one of the main forces keeping wages close together. ______ the difference in earnings between the region's top-earning and bottom-earning tenths of workers grew substantially over those same three decades, even as the local economy stagnated.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 노조가 임금 격차를 줄이는 힘이었고 그 힘이 사라졌다고 말하며, 뒷 문장은 그 결과로 임금 격차가 커졌다고 서술하므로 원인-결과 관계인 B가 정답이다. A는 '경제 침체'와의 대비처럼 보여 끌리지만, 격차 확대는 앞 내용에서 예상되는 결과이지 예상을 뒤집는 내용이 아니다. C는 뒷 문장이 구체적인 수치를 다뤄 예시처럼 보이지만, 앞 문장의 일반론을 보여주는 사례가 아니라 그로부터 생긴 결과이다. D는 두 문장이 대조되는 대상을 다루지 않으므로 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence explains that unions had kept wages close together and that this force disappeared; the next sentence describes the wage gap widening, which follows from that loss. That's a cause-and-effect relationship, so B is correct. A may look tempting because of the mention of stagnation, but a widening gap is exactly what the earlier sentence leads you to expect, not a surprising reversal. C may seem to fit because the final sentence is more specific, but it describes a consequence of the earlier claim, not an example of it. D doesn't work because the two sentences don't set up contrasting situations or groups.
g.design: 어휘 단서 없이 '노조의 임금 압축 기능 상실 → 격차 확대'라는 인과 방향을 파악해야 하며, 구체화(C)와 'even as stagnated'로 인한 양보 착각(A)을 부분 근거 오답으로 배치했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: economics and business — Gig economy platform misclassification independent contractor status and legal labor regulation challenges

g.passage: In 2019, California adopted the "ABC test" for classifying workers. Under this standard, a worker is presumed to be an employee unless the hiring company can prove three conditions, one of which is that the work falls outside the usual course of the company's business. For ride-hailing firms, whose core business is arguably transporting passengers, proving that drivers' work meets this condition appeared nearly impossible. ______ the firms spent more than $200 million backing Proposition 22, a 2020 ballot measure that exempted app-based drivers from the test altogether.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 ABC 테스트상 운전자의 업무가 회사 본업 밖이라고 증명하기가 거의 불가능했다는 점을 말하고, 뒷 문장은 그래서 기업들이 테스트 자체를 피하려고 주민발의안에 거액을 썼다는 결과를 제시하므로 원인→결과를 잇는 C가 정답이다. A는 기업들이 '포기하지 않았다'는 인상 때문에 그럴듯하지만, 발의안 지원은 어려움에 반하는 행동이 아니라 어려움에 대한 대응이므로 대조가 성립하지 않는다. B는 뒷 문장이 앞 문장의 사례인 것처럼 보이게 하지만, 발의안 지원은 증명의 어려움을 보여 주는 예가 아니다. D는 뒷 문장이 앞 내용을 다시 말한 것처럼 만들지만, 뒷 문장은 새로운 사건을 덧붙인다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence says ride-hailing firms could almost certainly not prove that drivers' work falls outside their usual business, and the next sentence describes what the firms did because of that: they paid for a ballot measure that exempted drivers from the test. That is a cause-and-effect relationship, so C is correct. A may look tempting because the firms kept pushing, but backing the measure was a response to the difficulty, not something that happened in spite of it, so there is no contrast. B treats the campaign as an example of the difficulty, but spending on a ballot measure doesn't illustrate how hard the proof was. D treats the last sentence as a restatement, but it actually reports a new event.
g.design: I left out any word that signals the relationship, so the cause-and-effect link has to come from the logic connecting "nearly impossible to prove" and "spending to get an exemption." A gives readers who skim a tempting "they persisted anyway" reading, and B and D each have some surface plausibility.

c.seed: economics and business — Markdown optimization retail algorithms and dynamic price adjustment timing inventory turnover profit maximization

g.passage: For decades, many clothing retailers reduced prices on seasonal merchandise according to a fixed calendar: every winter coat in every store might be marked down 30 percent on the same date in January. Markdown optimization software works differently. It tracks how quickly each item is selling at each individual location and recommends a discount only when that item's sales fall behind the pace needed to clear inventory profitably. ______ a coat that is selling briskly in Denver may stay at full price for weeks, while the identical coat in Atlanta, where demand has stalled, is discounted early.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 소프트웨어가 매장별·품목별 판매 속도에 따라 할인 시점을 정한다는 일반 원리를 설명하고, 마지막 문장은 덴버와 애틀랜타의 같은 코트라는 구체적 사례로 그 원리를 보여 준다. 따라서 예시를 이끄는 D가 정답이다. A는 마지막 문장 안의 두 도시 대비에 끌린 오답으로, 앞 문장과 대조되는 것이 아니라 앞 문장을 구체화하므로 맞지 않는다. B는 원리를 적용한 결과처럼 보이지만, 이 문장은 새로운 결과가 아니라 같은 원리를 사례로 다시 보여 주는 것이다. C는 앞 내용과 반대되거나 예상을 뒤집는 내용이 이어질 때 쓰는데, 여기에는 그런 반전이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence states a general principle: the software discounts an item only where its sales at that location are lagging. The final sentence then shows that principle in action with a specific case, the same coat priced differently in Denver and Atlanta, so D, which introduces an example, is the best choice. A is tempting because the final sentence contrasts two cities, but that sentence doesn't contrast with the previous one; it illustrates it. B might seem to fit because the pricing follows from the principle, but the sentence isn't a new outcome; it restates the same principle as a concrete case. C signals a concession or an unexpected turn, and nothing here reverses or qualifies the earlier claim.
g.design: There are no vocabulary cues. The reader has to see that the last sentence turns the general principle into a concrete case. A and B each fit part of the logic: A matches the city contrast inside the sentence, and B matches the cause-and-effect feel of the pricing.

c.seed: economics and business — Hanseatic League merchant network Baltic grain timber furs monopoly and medieval trade route dominance

g.passage: Unlike the kingdoms with which it traded, the Hanseatic League never had a permanent treasury, a standing navy, or a single governing capital. Its member towns sent delegates to assemblies in Lübeck only irregularly, and many towns simply ignored decisions they disliked. ______ for roughly two centuries, Hanseatic merchants controlled most of the Baltic trade in grain, timber, and furs, and won trading privileges from rulers as far apart as London and Novgorod.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장들은 한자동맹에 상설 재정, 해군, 수도가 없었고 회원 도시들이 결정을 자주 무시했다는 약점을 설명한다. 반면 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그런데도 동맹 상인들이 약 200년 동안 발트해 무역을 장악했다는, 예상과 반대되는 결과를 제시한다. 따라서 양보 뒤 반전을 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 느슨한 조직이 무역 장악의 원인이었다는 인과 관계를 만들어 내는데, 지문은 그런 근거를 제시하지 않는다. C는 무역 장악이 조직적 약점의 한 사례인 것처럼 만들고, D는 성공을 약점 목록에 덧붙이는 정보처럼 다루므로 둘 다 대조 관계를 놓친다.
g.explanation_en: The first two sentences describe the League's weaknesses: it had no permanent treasury, navy, or capital, and its member towns often ignored its decisions. The final sentence then reports a result you wouldn't expect from that description, which is two centuries of control over Baltic trade. A transition that admits the weaknesses and then turns to the opposite outcome fits here, so A is correct. B makes the loose organization the cause of the League's success, but the text gives no reasoning to support that. C treats the trade control as an example of the weaknesses, and D adds the success to the list of weaknesses as if it were more of the same, so both miss the contrast.
g.design: 빈칸 앞뒤에 대조를 알리는 어휘 단서 없이, 조직적 약점에서 의외의 성공으로 넘어가는 흐름만으로 양보 후 반전을 판단하게 했다. 인과(B)와 첨가(D)는 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯하게 들리도록 배치했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: economics and business — Antwerp diamond cutting techniques fifteenth century and gemstone valuation standardization establishing pricing hierarchy

g.passage: In fifteenth-century Antwerp, diamond cutters refined the use of a rotating iron wheel coated with a paste of diamond dust and olive oil, a technique that let them grind precise, symmetrical facets onto stones that had previously been traded largely in their rough state. The innovation had consequences well beyond the workshop______ because a stone's brilliance could now be predictably enhanced, merchants began assigning value according to the quality of its cut as well as its weight, gradually forming a pricing hierarchy that buyers across Europe came to accept.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: The blank follows a long, modifier-heavy first sentence and comes before a second independent clause that opens with a 'because' clause, so students have to find the main clause ('merchants began...') before choosing the boundary. A comma looks plausible because of the 'because' clause, and 'which' looks plausible as a way to add a modifier.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The innovation had consequences well beyond the workshop"는 독립절이다. 빈칸 뒤도 "because ~ enhanced"라는 종속절 뒤에 주절 "merchants began assigning value..."가 오는 독립절이다. 두 번째 절이 앞에서 말한 '영향'이 무엇인지 구체적으로 풀어 주므로, 콜론을 쓰는 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 되고, 뒤에 because가 있어 연결된 것처럼 보이는 함정이다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다. D는 which가 관계절을 시작하지만 그 뒤에 이어지는 because 절과 주절이 관계절 구조에 맞지 않아 비문이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "The innovation had consequences well beyond the workshop," is an independent clause. The text after it is also an independent clause: an introductory "because" clause followed by the main clause "merchants began assigning value..." Since the second clause explains what those consequences were, a colon is the right choice, so B is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice; the word "because" can trick you into thinking the clauses are already linked. C runs the two independent clauses together with no punctuation at all. D opens a relative clause with "which," but the "because" clause and main clause that follow don't fit that structure, so the sentence becomes ungrammatical.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: economics and business — South Sea Bubble 1720 joint-stock company speculation and stock price manipulation financial scandal consequences

g.passage: The directors of the South Sea Company, who had circulated exaggerated reports of profitable trade with Spanish America to push the firm's share price from roughly £128 to nearly £1,000 in a few months, did not anticipate the scale of the public backlash______ the bubble collapsed in the autumn of 1720, Parliament opened an inquiry that confiscated much of the directors' wealth to compensate ruined investors.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 비필수 관계절을 지난 뒤 첫 독립절이 끝나는 지점을 찾고, 'when'이 이끄는 부사절이 두 번째 독립절에 속한다는 점을 확인해야 하는 두 단계 판단이다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The directors ... did not anticipate ... backlash"는 완전한 독립절이고, "when the bubble collapsed ..."는 뒤에 오는 독립절 "Parliament opened an inquiry"를 꾸미는 부사절이다. 따라서 두 독립절 사이에 세미콜론이 필요하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 되고, when절이 앞 절을 수식하는 것처럼 보여 혼란스럽다. B는 문장부호가 전혀 없어 run-on이 된다. D는 세미콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 and를 덧붙여 불필요하고 비표준적인 조합이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "The directors ... did not anticipate the scale of the public backlash," is a complete independent clause. The words "when the bubble collapsed ..." begin a dependent clause that modifies the second independent clause, "Parliament opened an inquiry." Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, so C is correct. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice, and it also makes the "when" clause seem to modify the first clause. B uses no punctuation at all, so it creates a run-on sentence. D puts "and" after the semicolon, which is redundant and isn't standard.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: economics and business — Scottish free banking nineteenth century note-issuing competition and absence of central regulatory control mechanism

g.passage: From 1716 to 1845, Scotland's banks operated with remarkably little official oversight. Lacking a central bank to cap their output, rival institutions such as the Bank of Scotland and the Royal Bank of Scotland printed their own paper notes and routinely accepted one another's notes at regular clearing ______ any bank that issued too many notes soon found competitors returning them for redemption in gold, a pressure that kept each issuer cautious.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 수식구와 주어 뒤에서 두 독립절의 경계를 찾고, 접속부사 'as a result'가 어느 절에 붙는지 의미까지 확인하는 두 단계 판단을 요구한다.
g.explanation: 'Lacking ... exchanges'와 'any bank ... cautious'는 둘 다 독립절이고, 'as a result'는 뒤 절을 이끄는 접속부사이다. 따라서 세미콜론으로 두 절을 나누고 접속부사 뒤에 쉼표를 찍은 D가 맞다. A는 독립절 두 개를 쉼표로만 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 세미콜론을 'as a result' 뒤에 두어서, 결과를 나타내는 이 표현이 엉뚱하게 앞 절에 붙어 버린다. C는 두 절 사이에 문장부호가 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: Both "Lacking ... exchanges" and "any bank ... cautious" are independent clauses, and "as a result" is a transitional phrase that introduces the second clause. So you need a semicolon between the clauses and a comma after the transition, which is exactly what D gives you. A joins two independent clauses with only commas, which makes a comma splice. B puts the semicolon after "as a result," so the transition wrongly attaches to the first clause, even though it describes the result in the second one. C has no punctuation at all between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: economics and business — Japanese silk filature Meiji standardization and export market quality grading competitive advantage textile production

g.passage: In the 1870s, Japanese silk producers faced a problem familiar to many new exporters: buyers in Lyon and New York distrusted the uneven quality of hand-reeled thread. The Tomioka Silk Mill, a government-built filature staffed with French-trained instructors and equipped with steam-powered reeling ______ standardized the thickness and strength of its yarn, and its methods soon spread to private mills across the country.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 'a government-built filature ... machines'는 주어 The Tomioka Silk Mill을 설명하는 비필수 동격어구이며, 앞의 쉼표와 짝을 이루는 쉼표로 닫아야 동사 standardized로 이어진다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 닫는 쉼표가 없어 동격어구가 끝나지 않는다. C는 세미콜론 앞이 주어만 있고 동사가 없는 불완전한 절이라 틀린다. D는 and가 주어와 동사를 갈라 놓아 standardized에 주어가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "a government-built filature ... machines" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject, The Tomioka Silk Mill. It opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma before the verb "standardized." That makes A correct. B leaves out the closing comma, so the appositive never ends. C puts a semicolon after words that have a subject but no verb, so they don't form a complete clause. D adds "and," which cuts the subject off from its verb and leaves "standardized" without a subject.
g.design: Option B is tempting because the long appositive hides the subject. Students must find the comma that opens the appositive and then see that the verb comes after the blank. Options C and D look natural if a student skims and mistakes the appositive for a complete clause.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: economics and business — Cork wine stopper manufacturing Portugal and market monopoly dominance in beverage industry supply chain

g.passage: Portugal produces roughly half of the world's cork, and for much of the twentieth century its manufacturers set the terms of trade for winemakers everywhere. In the early 2000s, however, Corticeira Amorim, the family-owned company that controls a large share of global cork stopper output, faced a serious threat______ winemakers, alarmed by reports of a musty contaminant known as cork taint, were switching to screw caps and synthetic closures in growing numbers.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Corticeira Amorim ... faced a serious threat"는 동격 삽입구가 있지만 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "winemakers ... were switching ..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이며 그 위협이 무엇인지 설명한다. 따라서 앞 절을 구체화하는 독립절을 이끄는 콜론을 쓴 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D의 "which"는 관계절을 만들지만, 뒤에 "winemakers ... were switching"이라는 완전한 절이 와서 관계대명사가 들어갈 자리가 없으므로 문법에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "Corticeira Amorim ... faced a serious threat," is an independent clause even though an appositive interrupts it. The text after the blank, "winemakers ... were switching ...," is also an independent clause, and it explains what the threat was. A colon correctly introduces an independent clause that explains the one before it, so B is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the two clauses, which makes a run-on sentence. D adds "which," but the words after it already form a complete clause, so the relative pronoun has no role in that clause and the sentence becomes ungrammatical.
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구와 빈칸 뒤 쉼표 삽입구 때문에 주절의 경계가 잘 보이지 않는다. 쉼표, 부호 없음, 관계사 형태의 오답이 각각 그럴듯하게 보이도록 구성했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: economics and business — Swiss watchmaking precision manufacturing and temporal standardization enabling railway schedule coordination infrastructure

g.passage: By the 1870s, Swiss watchmakers in the Jura valleys had shifted from workshop craft to standardized production, turning out interchangeable movements accurate to within seconds a day. Railway companies across Europe, struggling to coordinate trains that crossed dozens of local time zones, quickly became major ______ conductors carrying these watches could synchronize departures to the minute, making tightly timed connections between lines possible for the first time.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 주어(Railway companies ... time zones) 뒤 첫 번째 독립절은 "buyers"에서 끝나고, 그 뒤 "conductors ... could synchronize"는 주어와 동사를 갖춘 두 번째 독립절이다. 콜론은 독립절 뒤에 쓰여 앞 절을 설명하는 내용(철도회사가 왜 주요 구매자가 됐는지)을 이끌 수 있으므로 C가 정답이다. B는 독립절 두 개를 쉼표만으로 이어 comma splice가 된다. A는 with가 뒤를 전치사구로 만들지만 동사 could synchronize가 남아 문법이 깨진다. D는 which가 사물 buyers를 가리킬 수 없고, 뒤에 이미 주어 conductors가 있어 관계절로도 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The long subject (Railway companies ... time zones) leads to a first independent clause that ends at "buyers," and "conductors ... could synchronize" is a second independent clause with its own subject and verb. A colon can follow an independent clause to introduce an explanation (here, why the railways became major buyers), so C is correct. B joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. A turns what follows into a prepositional phrase with "with," but the verb "could synchronize" is left without a proper structure. D's "which" can't refer to the people "buyers," and since the clause already has its own subject, "conductors," it can't work as a relative clause.
g.design: 긴 삽입 수식어가 주절 동사를 가려 절 경계를 놓치기 쉽게 했고, 오답 A·D는 연결어로 그럴듯하게 보이나 뒤 절의 주어+동사 구조와 충돌한다.

c.instruction:

g.passage: In the 1880s, the Jena optical firm founded by Carl Zeiss guarded its new glass formulas as closely as any patent. One competitor—a small Munich workshop that had quietly hired two of the firm's former lens polishers______began advertising microscope objectives with nearly identical optical properties, and Zeiss's managers soon suspected that trade secrets had traveled south with the workers.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 긴 수식어가 들어간 동격 삽입구가 대시로 열려 있어, 주어와 동사 사이 경계를 찾고 문장부호를 짝맞춤으로 확인하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. 쉼표와 세미콜론은 경계처럼 보여 끌리는 오답이다.
g.explanation: "One competitor" 뒤의 동격 삽입구는 대시로 시작하므로 같은 대시로 닫아야 주어 "One competitor"와 동사 "began"이 이어진다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. C는 삽입구 끝에 쉼표를 써서 앞의 대시와 짝이 맞지 않는다. B의 세미콜론은 독립절 두 개를 나누는 부호인데, 빈칸 앞에는 독립절이 없고 주어와 동사만 갈라 놓게 된다. A의 ", and"는 "began"을 앞의 "had quietly hired"와 나란한 동사로 만들어 주절의 동사가 사라지므로 문장이 완성되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The appositive describing "One competitor" opens with a dash, so it has to close with a matching dash. That way the subject "One competitor" connects cleanly to its verb "began," which makes D correct. C ends the appositive with a comma, and a comma doesn't pair with the opening dash. B uses a semicolon, which belongs between two independent clauses, but nothing before the blank is an independent clause, so the semicolon would just cut the subject off from its verb. A's ", and" turns "began" into a second verb running parallel to "had quietly hired" inside the appositive, so the sentence's main subject is left without a main verb.

g.passage: Each week at the Mombasa Tea Auction, brokers representing buyers from Pakistan, Egypt, and the United Kingdom compete for tea grown by thousands of Kenyan smallholder farmers. The auction's core feature, an open bidding system in which every lot is sold to whoever submits the highest offer ______ lets prices track shifts in global demand instead of being fixed in private deals with a single buyer. Economists credit this transparency with raising the revenue that farmer cooperatives earn per kilogram of leaf.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 주어 'The auction's core feature' 뒤에 쉼표로 시작된 비필수 동격어구가 'offer'에서 끝나고, 주동사 'lets'가 이어진다. 동격어구는 여는 부호와 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 세미콜론이 주어와 동사 사이를 끊어 앞부분이 독립절이 아니게 된다. C의 대시는 여는 쉼표와 짝이 맞지 않는다. D는 'and'를 넣어 주어 'feature'에 주동사가 없게 만든다.
g.explanation_en: The subject "The auction's core feature" is followed by a nonessential appositive that opens with a comma and ends at "offer." The main verb "lets" comes right after it. An appositive must close with the same mark that opened it, so a comma is needed, which makes A correct. B is wrong because the semicolon cuts the subject off from its verb, and the words before it aren't an independent clause. C is wrong because a dash can't close a phrase that opened with a comma. D is wrong because adding "and" leaves the subject "feature" without a main verb.
g.design: 긴 동격어구 뒤에서 주어-동사 연결을 확인하고(1단계), 여는 부호와의 짝을 맞춰야(2단계) 풀린다. 오답 B와 C는 절 경계처럼 보이는 부호를 써서 훑어 읽는 학생을 끌어들인다.

c.seed: economics and business — Filipino coconut copra trade colonial extraction and economic dependency pattern agricultural production

g.passage: Under American colonial rule in the early twentieth century, Filipino farmers in provinces such as Quezon and Laguna shifted large tracts of land to coconut cultivation, drying the meat into copra for export to oil mills in the United States. The trade, which brought steady cash to many rural households, also deepened a troubling ______ the islands supplied raw copra cheaply, while the more profitable work of pressing it into oil and soap took place abroad.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The trade ... also deepened a troubling dependency"는 삽입구(which절) 뒤에서도 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤 내용은 그 '의존'이 무엇인지 구체적으로 설명하므로 콜론이 알맞다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표로만 이어서 쉼표 연결 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 '쉼표+and'로 문법상 연결은 되지만, and는 두 사실을 대등하게 나열할 뿐이어서 뒤 절이 '의존'을 풀어 설명한다는 관계를 보여 주지 못한다. 게다가 이미 while로 대조가 이어지는 문장이라 흐름이 어색해진다.
g.explanation_en: Look at what comes before the blank: "The trade ... also deepened a troubling dependency." Even with the "which" clause in the middle, that is a complete independent clause. What follows the blank explains exactly what that dependency was, so a colon is the right choice, which makes B correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, so it's a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the two clauses, so it's a run-on. D is grammatical, but "and" just lists the two ideas side by side. It doesn't show that the second clause explains the "dependency." It also makes an awkward chain with the "while" contrast later in the sentence.
g.design: 긴 비필수 which 삽입구로 주절 완결성 판단을 어렵게 하고, 문법상 가능한 쉼표+and 오답과 논리 관계(설명)를 비교하게 했다.

c.seed: economics and business — Kuapa Kokoo chocolate cooperative Ghana and farmer ownership revenue distribution model supply chain

g.passage: Founded in 1993, Kuapa Kokoo is a Ghanaian cooperative whose members are cocoa farmers. Unlike growers who simply sell beans to outside buyers, the cooperative's members also hold a substantial share of Divine Chocolate, a company that turns their cocoa into finished bars. As a result, farmers do not just receive a price for their harvest; they are entitled to a portion of the profits generated further along the supply chain, and they hold seats on the company's board. Observers note that this arrangement ______ the usual division between those who grow a crop and those who benefit from its sale.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 농민이 수확물 가격만 받는 게 아니라 하류 공급망의 이익을 나누고 이사회 자리도 가진다고 설명하므로, 재배자와 판매 수익자 사이의 일반적 구분을 흐린다는 C가 정답이다. A는 '구분'이라는 말에만 반응하면 그럴듯하지만, 이 구조는 구분을 강화하는 게 아니라 약화한다. B는 관찰자가 언급하는 맥락과 맞아 보이지만, 사업 구조는 무언가를 기록하는 주체가 아니며 구조가 그 구분에 미치는 영향을 나타내지 못한다. D는 구분이 사라진다는 느낌과 비슷해 보이지만, 감춘다는 것은 구분이 그대로 남아 있되 보이지 않는다는 뜻이어서 실제로 구분이 바뀐다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that the farmers don't just get paid for their harvest. They also share in profits made further along the supply chain and sit on the company's board. That means the usual line between growers and the people who profit from sales is being erased, so C, "blurs," is the answer. A might look right if you only notice the word "division," but this arrangement weakens that division instead of strengthening it. B fits the idea of observers commenting, but a business structure doesn't record anything, and "documents" says nothing about how the structure changes the division. D can feel close because the division seems to fade, but "conceals" means the division is still there and just hidden, while the text describes it actually changing.
g.design: 독자는 두 정보를 연결해야 한다. 하나는 농민이 이익을 나누고 이사회에 참여한다는 점이고, 다른 하나는 '일반적 구분'이라는 표현이다. A와 D는 구분이라는 말이나 구분이 흐려진다는 인상에 부분적으로 기대어 있어 정답과 비교해야만 배제된다. 네 선택지는 모두 같은 문장 틀에 들어가는 타동사로 구성했다.

g.passage: In 1892, Daniel Swarovski patented an electric machine that could cut and polish glass stones far more precisely and quickly than skilled workers grinding each piece by hand. The invention did not make crystal jewelry any more brilliant than the finest handmade pieces, but it allowed his Austrian firm to produce consistently faceted stones in enormous quantities at a fraction of the former cost. Historians therefore argue that Swarovski's real advantage was not superior artistry but a capacity to ______ sparkling ornaments, turning what had been a luxury for the few into an affordable accessory for a growing middle class.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 Swarovski의 기계가 품질을 높인 것이 아니라 대량·저가 생산을 가능하게 해 소수의 사치품을 중산층도 살 수 있는 물건으로 바꿨다고 설명하므로, '널리 누구나 접근 가능하게 하다'라는 뜻의 D가 정답이다. A는 기계가 정밀하게 연마했다는 내용과 연결되어 보이지만, 지문은 더 빛나게 만든 것은 아니라고 분명히 밝히며 장점은 품질 향상이 아니었다고 말한다. B는 크리스털 유리가 보석을 모방한다는 배경지식에 기대지만, 지문의 초점은 접근성과 비용이지 모방이 아니다. C는 장신구를 '보여 준다'는 뜻으로 말은 되지만, 사치품을 저렴한 물건으로 바꾸는 과정을 설명하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says Swarovski's machine didn't make the stones better. Instead, it let the firm make huge numbers of them cheaply, which turned a luxury for a few people into something the middle class could afford. That makes D, "democratize" (to make widely available), the correct answer. A may look right because the machine cut stones precisely, but the text clearly says the stones were no more brilliant, so improving quality was not the advantage. B relies on the idea that crystal imitates gems, but the passage is about cost and access, not copying. C makes sense in general, but "showcase" doesn't explain how a luxury became an affordable accessory.
g.design: 독자가 정밀 절단이라는 단서만 훑어보면 refine을 고르게 함정을 넣었고, 정답을 고르려면 두 정보를 연결해야 한다: 품질은 향상되지 않았다는 점과 소수→중산층으로 바뀌었다는 점. 오답들도 정답과 같은 타동사 형태이며, 질문에는 정답과 겹치는 단어가 없다.

c.seed: economics and business — Rhodesian tobacco sanctions global trade embargo and agricultural export collapse economic disruption

g.passage: After Rhodesia's unilateral declaration of independence in 1965, the United Nations imposed sanctions that barred member states from buying the colony's tobacco, then its most valuable export. Growers did not stop planting, however; instead, traders relabeled shipments and routed them through neighboring ports so that buyers abroad could not easily trace their origin. Economic historians therefore argue that the embargo ______ Rhodesian tobacco sales rather than ending them: exports fell sharply and prices dropped, but a reduced, hidden trade continued for more than a decade.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: briefly interrupted and then fully restored
g.explanation: 지문은 제재 이후 수출이 급감했지만 원산지를 숨긴 채 줄어든 '은밀한' 거래가 10년 넘게 지속되었다고 말하므로, 판매를 숨겨진 형태로 몰아넣고 줄였다는 A가 정답이다. B는 수출 급감이라는 부분과는 맞지만 'rather than ending them'과 거래 지속이라는 사실에 모순된다. C는 거래가 계속되었다는 점과만 맞을 뿐, 수출 감소와 거래의 은밀함에 어긋난다. D는 일시적 중단이라는 점이 그럴듯해 보이지만, 거래가 완전히 회복되었다는 근거가 없고 오히려 규모가 줄어든 채 숨겨져 있었다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says exports fell sharply, yet a reduced, hidden trade went on for more than a decade, so the embargo pushed sales into concealment and shrank them. That makes A correct. B fits the sharp decline, but it contradicts "rather than ending them" and the fact that trade continued. C matches only the continuation of trade; it ignores both the decline and the secrecy. D might look reasonable because there was a disruption, but nothing in the text says the trade was fully restored—it stayed smaller and hidden.
g.design: To get this right, you have to connect two pieces of information: the sharp drop in exports and the hidden trade that kept going. Each wrong answer matches only one of these pieces.

g.passage: After Croatia's independence in the 1990s, its large shipyards, once sustained by state orders, faced global competitors in South Korea and China that could build vessels more cheaply. Successive governments covered the yards' losses with subsidies and loan guarantees rather than forcing deep restructuring. Economists who studied the sector argue that this support was not neutral: by shielding managers from the consequences of missed deadlines and cost overruns, it ______ the very inefficiencies that later made privatization so difficult, since buyers were reluctant to take on yards whose problems had grown for years.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 보조금이 경영진을 결과로부터 보호했고, 그 결과 문제가 수년간 커져 민영화가 어려워졌다고 말한다. 따라서 보조금이 비효율을 '굳히고 고착시켰다'는 뜻의 B가 가장 정확하다. A는 보조금이 비효율을 드러냈다는 뜻이 되는데, 보호해서 결과를 가렸다는 문맥과 반대다. C는 보조금이 손실을 메웠다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, '상쇄했다'면 비효율이 줄었어야 하므로 문제가 커졌다는 내용과 맞지 않는다. D는 비효율이 이전 체제에서 왔을 수 있다는 점에서 부분적으로 맞아 보이지만, 지원 자체가 그 비효율을 만든 원인이라는 논지를 담지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the subsidies shielded managers from consequences, and the yards' problems kept growing for years, which made privatization hard. So the support made the inefficiencies firmly established and harder to remove, and that is what B means. A would mean the subsidies exposed the inefficiencies, but shielding managers hid the consequences instead. C is tempting because subsidies did cover losses, but offsetting the inefficiencies would mean they shrank, and the text says they grew. D fits the idea that the problems came from the old system, but it doesn't say what the support did to the inefficiencies, and that effect is the whole point of the argument.
g.design: To get this right, you have to link two pieces of information: the support protected managers, and the problems grew for years. C and D each match part of the text, so you can only rule them out by reading the whole sentence closely.
