c.seed: economics and business — SKF ball bearing standardization Sweden and precision manufacturing component interchangeability industrial production

g.passage: In the early twentieth century, Swedish engineer Sven Wingquist's company SKF produced ball bearings to tightly controlled dimensions, so that a bearing made in one factory could replace a worn bearing made in another without any filing or refitting. For machine builders, this precision was not a mere refinement but a ______ of large-scale production: assembly lines that depended on parts fitting on the first try could not run at all if each bearing had to be adjusted by hand.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 베어링마다 손으로 조정해야 했다면 조립 라인이 아예 돌아갈 수 없었다고 말한다. 따라서 정밀도는 대량 생산이 가능하기 위한 필수 조건이었고, C가 정답이다. A는 정밀도와 생산이 관련 있다는 점은 맞지만, 정밀도를 생산의 원인이 아니라 생산에서 생겨난 결과로 뒤집어 놓는다. B는 정밀 가공과 대량 생산이 서로 대립한다는 뜻이 되어, 둘이 서로 의존한다는 지문 내용과 어긋난다. D는 정밀도가 생산의 상징이라는 말로 그럴듯해 보이지만, 정밀도가 없으면 생산이 '아예 불가능하다'는 실질적 필요성을 담지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says assembly lines "could not run at all" if each bearing needed adjusting by hand. That means precision was a requirement that had to exist before large-scale production could happen, so C is correct. A does link precision to production, but it reverses the relationship by making precision a result of production instead of a cause. B would mean that precision and mass production compete with each other, but the text shows that one depends on the other. D sounds reasonable, but calling precision a "symbol" leaves out the practical point: without precision, production would not have been possible at all.
g.design: "not a mere refinement but"와 콜론 뒤의 내용을 연결해야 '필수 조건'이라는 의미가 나오도록 설계했다. 오답 A와 D에는 그럴듯한 연관성을 남겨 두어 비교해야만 배제되게 했고, 오답 B도 문맥상 말이 되도록 했다.

c.seed: economics and business — Bengali indigo cartel monopoly and synthetic dye competition displacing natural pigment market India

g.passage: In the mid-nineteenth century, British planters in Bengal controlled much of the world's supply of natural indigo, and for decades buyers in European textile centers had few alternatives. That dominance proved far less durable than it appeared. After German chemists began mass-producing synthetic indigo in 1897, the factory-made dye sold at steadily falling prices and offered a uniformity of shade that plant-based indigo could not match. Within roughly two decades, Bengal's exports had ______, shrinking to a small fraction of their former volume as mills switched suppliers.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 합성 인디고가 더 싸고 균일해서 공장들이 공급처를 바꿨고, 벵골의 수출이 이전 물량의 작은 일부로 "줄어들었다"고 말하므로, 급격하고 결정적인 하락을 뜻하는 D(collapsed)가 정답이다. A(fluctuated)는 경쟁 때문에 시장이 불안정했다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 오르내림을 뜻할 뿐 일방적인 큰 감소를 나타내지 못한다. B(stabilized)는 생산자가 가격 압박에 적응했다고 볼 수도 있으나, 물량이 줄었다는 서술과 모순된다. C(diversified)는 생산자가 다른 작물로 전환했다고 상상할 수 있지만, 빈칸의 주어는 수출 물량이고 지문은 품목 다양화가 아니라 물량 감소를 말한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says synthetic indigo was cheaper and more uniform, so mills switched suppliers, and Bengal's exports shrank to a small fraction of their former volume. That points to a sudden, severe drop, which makes D (collapsed) the answer. A (fluctuated) sounds plausible because competition can make a market unstable, but it only means rising and falling, not one large decline. B (stabilized) could suggest producers adjusting to price pressure, but it contradicts the shrinking volume the text describes. C (diversified) might make you think of growers switching crops, but the blank is about export volume, and the text describes that volume falling, not a wider range of goods.
g.design: 이 문제를 맞히려면 두 가지를 연결해야 합니다. 첫째, 합성 염료가 시장 우위를 차지했다는 사실이고, 둘째, 빈칸 뒤 분사구가 큰 폭의 감소를 말한다는 점입니다. 오답 A·B·C는 각각 시장 불안정, 적응, 사업 전환이라는 그럴듯한 연상에 기대므로 정답과 비교해 봐야 배제할 수 있습니다.

c.seed: economics and business — Bordeaux wine classification 1855 producer ranking prestige pricing and hierarchical market segmentation

g.passage: In 1855, Bordeaux brokers ranked the region's leading wine estates into five tiers, basing the list largely on the prices each estate's wines had commanded over previous decades. Economists studying the classification note that it has proved remarkably ______: although vineyard ownership, winemaking methods, and even the land itself have changed considerably since then, only one estate has ever been promoted, and the price gaps between tiers have persisted, reinforcing the original hierarchy rather than eroding it.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 소유권·양조법·토지가 바뀌었는데도 승격된 곳이 하나뿐이고 등급 간 가격 차이가 유지되어 위계가 강화되었다고 말하므로, 변화에 저항해 굳어 있다는 뜻의 A(entrenched)가 정답이다. B(influential)는 가격 격차가 유지된다는 점과 일부 맞지만, 콜론 뒤의 핵심인 '변화에도 바뀌지 않음'을 정확히 담지 못한다. C(contested)는 등급이 논란거리일 수 있다는 배경 지식에 기대지만, 지문은 논쟁이 아니라 지속성을 말한다. D(arbitrary)는 등급이 바뀐 현실을 반영하지 못한다는 점에서 그럴듯해 보이지만, 지문은 등급이 과거 가격에 근거했다고 하므로 '임의적'이라는 말과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text says that ownership, winemaking methods, and the land itself have all changed, yet only one estate has been promoted and the price gaps between tiers still hold, so the hierarchy has been reinforced. That describes something firmly fixed and resistant to change, so A ("entrenched") is the answer. B ("influential") fits the idea that prices follow the tiers, but it misses the main point after the colon, which is that the ranking has stayed the same despite change. C ("contested") relies on the idea that rankings tend to cause debate, but the text describes persistence, not dispute. D ("arbitrary") might seem fitting because the ranking no longer matches current conditions, but the text says the list was based on actual price history, so it was not random.
g.design: To answer, students must connect the colon's evidence: change happened, yet the ranking did not move and was even reinforced. B and D each match one partial clue (the price effects, or the mismatch with today), and C is a plausible idea from outside the text that the passage does not support.

c.seed: economics and business — Norwegian salmon farming aquaculture and environmental externality cost marine ecosystem impact

g.passage: Norwegian salmon farms report impressive profits, but economists note that these figures leave out costs borne by others: sea lice spreading from crowded net pens to wild salmon, and waste settling on the fjord floor. Because farm owners do not pay for this damage, market prices for farmed salmon ______ the true cost of production. Norway's 2017 "traffic light" system, which limits growth in regions where lice harm wild fish, was designed partly to correct this gap.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.design: 빈칸을 채우려면 두 정보를 연결해야 한다. 하나는 비용이 다른 이들에게 넘어간다는 점이고, 다른 하나는 그래서 가격이 실제 비용보다 낮다는 점이다. 'profits'와 'costs'만 훑어보면 A를 고르기 쉽고, C와 D는 가격과 비용의 관계를 설명하는 그럴듯한 동사라서 오답으로 배치했다.
g.explanation: 지문에 따르면 양식업자는 바다이(sea lice)와 폐기물로 생기는 피해 비용을 내지 않는다. 그러므로 시장 가격에는 그 비용이 빠져 있어 실제 생산 비용보다 낮게 나타난다. 따라서 '실제보다 낮게 나타내다'라는 뜻의 B가 정답이다. A는 반대로 가격이 비용을 부풀린다는 뜻이라 맞지 않는다. C는 가격이 실제 비용을 드러낸다는 뜻이어서 '격차(gap)'를 바로잡아야 한다는 마지막 문장과 모순된다. D는 가격이 비용을 결정한다는 뜻인데, 지문은 인과관계가 아니라 가격에 일부 비용이 빠져 있다는 점을 말하고 있다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says farm owners don't pay for the damage caused by sea lice and waste. That means market prices leave out part of the cost, so they come in lower than the true cost of production. B fits that meaning, so it is correct. A says the opposite, that prices exaggerate the cost. C would mean prices accurately show the cost, which contradicts the "gap" the last sentence says needs correcting. D suggests prices cause or set the cost, but the passage is about prices missing some costs, not about cause and effect.

c.seed: economics and business — Agricultural commodity futures hedging adoption and farmer price risk management financial security strategy

g.passage: Many economists assume that grain farmers would eagerly use futures contracts, which let a grower lock in a selling price months before harvest. Yet surveys of Midwestern corn producers find that only a minority hedge regularly. Agricultural economist Dana Whitfield argues that this reluctance is not simple ignorance: farmers who hedge and then watch market prices climb above their locked-in price often feel they have lost money, even though the contract did exactly what it was designed to do. For these growers, Whitfield suggests, the memory of a missed windfall ______ the security the hedge provided, making them less willing to hedge the following season.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 헤지가 제 역할을 했는데도 농부들이 놓친 이익만 기억해서 다음 해에 헤지를 덜 한다고 말합니다. 그러니 그 기억이 헤지가 준 안정감을 '가려 버린다'는 뜻이 필요하고, 정답은 C(overshadows)입니다. A(confirms)는 헤지가 '설계대로 작동했다'는 부분과 연결돼 그럴듯해 보이지만, 안정감을 확인해 준다면 농부들이 헤지를 꺼릴 이유가 없습니다. B(replicates)는 놓친 이익의 기억이 안정감을 '그대로 재현한다'는 뜻이 되어 논리가 맞지 않습니다. D(anticipates)는 수확 전에 미리 가격을 고정한다는 시간 흐름과 연결돼 보이지만, 지나간 일의 기억이 안정감을 '예상한다'는 것은 말이 되지 않습니다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the hedge worked as designed, but farmers remember only the profit they missed and so hedge less the next year. The blank therefore needs a word meaning the memory outweighs or hides the security the hedge gave, which makes C (overshadows) the answer. A (confirms) seems to fit because the contract "did exactly what it was designed to do," but if the memory confirmed the security, farmers would have no reason to back away from hedging. B (replicates) would mean the memory reproduces the security, which doesn't make sense. D (anticipates) plays on the idea of locking in prices before harvest, but a memory of something that already happened can't anticipate the security.
g.design: To get the answer, students have to connect two pieces of information: the hedge did work, and farmers became less willing to hedge. A and D each draw on a real detail in the passage, so they can only be ruled out by comparing them against that connection.

c.seed: economics and business — Pharmaceutical drug pricing strategy United States and cost escalation insurance intermediary negotiation failures

g.passage: In the United States, pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) negotiate with drugmakers on behalf of insurers, and they are often paid a share of each drug's list price in the form of rebates. Economist Rena Kaplow argues that this arrangement can ______ the very cost increases PBMs are supposed to restrain: because a higher list price produces a larger rebate, a manufacturer that raises its price may actually win a more favorable place on an insurer's coverage list, so both parties gain when prices climb.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 정가가 오르면 리베이트가 커지고 제조사가 더 유리한 보험 등재 위치를 얻기 때문에 가격이 오를 때 양쪽 모두 이득을 본다고 설명한다. 따라서 이 구조는 가격 인상을 '보상한다'는 뜻이므로 D가 정답이다. A(드러내다)는 이 구조가 비용 문제를 밝혀낸다는 뜻이 되는데, 지문은 문제를 드러내는 것이 아니라 인상을 부추기는 유인을 말한다. B(상쇄하다)는 리베이트가 비용을 줄여 준다는 그럴듯한 연상을 주지만, '가격이 오를 때 양쪽 모두 이득'이라는 결론과 반대된다. C(예측하다)는 문맥상 말은 되지만 인과적 유인이라는 핵심을 담지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that a higher list price brings a bigger rebate and can earn the manufacturer a better spot on the coverage list, so both sides gain when prices rise. That means the arrangement rewards price increases, so D is correct. A ("expose") would mean the system reveals cost problems, but the text describes an incentive that encourages increases, not one that uncovers them. B ("offset") sounds plausible because rebates might seem to cut costs, but it contradicts the point that both parties gain as prices climb. C ("predict") makes grammatical sense but misses the cause-and-effect incentive at the heart of the argument.
g.design: 세미콜론 뒤 인과 설명(리베이트↑→유리한 등재→양측 이득)을 빈칸과 연결해야 하는 두 단계 판단이다. 'offset'은 PBM의 억제 역할만 훑어 읽은 학생을 끌어들이고, 'expose'는 비판적 어조를 노린 매력적 오답이다.

c.seed: economics and business — Venture capital syndication network geographic clustering and startup funding concentration Silicon Valley dominance

g.passage: Economists studying venture capital have long noted that funding is heavily concentrated in a few regions, especially Silicon Valley. A 2019 analysis of investment syndicates—groups of firms that jointly fund a single startup—suggests one reason this pattern persists. Because firms prefer to co-invest with partners they can meet frequently and monitor closely, syndicates tend to form among investors located near one another. Over time, these repeated local partnerships ______ the region's advantage: each new deal strengthens existing ties, making it easier for nearby startups, and harder for distant ones, to attract the next round of capital.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 콜론 뒤에서 거래가 하나 성사될 때마다 기존 유대가 강해지고 지역 스타트업은 자본을 끌어오기 더 쉬워진다고 설명하므로, 반복되는 파트너십이 지역의 우위를 '굳힌다'는 뜻의 A가 정답이다. B는 파트너십이 우위를 드러낸다는 의미로 그럴듯하지만, 지문은 우위가 보여지는 것이 아니라 거래마다 강화되는 과정을 말한다. C는 상쇄한다는 뜻이라 우위가 커진다는 내용과 반대된다. D는 파트너십이 우위보다 먼저 존재했다는 시간 관계만 나타낼 뿐, 지문의 핵심인 인과적 강화 과정은 담지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: After the colon, the text explains that each new deal strengthens existing ties and makes it easier for nearby startups to raise money. So the repeated partnerships firmly reinforce, or entrench, the region's advantage, which makes A correct. B is tempting because the partnerships could show that the advantage exists, but the text describes the advantage growing stronger, not just becoming visible. C means counterbalance, which is the opposite of strengthening. D only says the partnerships came before the advantage in time and misses the cause-and-effect reinforcement the text describes.
g.design: 오답 B(드러내다)와 D(시간적 선행)는 대충 읽으면 부분적으로 맞아 보이게 만들었다. 콜론 뒤의 '강화' 설명을 연결해야만 A를 고를 수 있다.

c.seed: economics and business — Automated valuation models real estate algorithms and racial discrimination bias mortgage lending reproduction

g.passage: Automated valuation models (AVMs), algorithms that estimate home prices from past sales data, are often promoted as a remedy for the subjective judgments of human appraisers. Yet economist Junia Howell and colleagues caution that because these models learn from decades of sales shaped by discriminatory lending, they may ______ the very disparities they were meant to eliminate: homes in predominantly Black neighborhoods, undervalued in the historical record, continue to receive lower estimates from the algorithms.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 AVM이 차별적 과거 거래 데이터로 학습하기 때문에 흑인 거주 지역 주택을 계속(continue) 낮게 평가한다고 말하므로, 기존 격차를 '지속시키다'라는 B가 정답이다. A는 알고리즘이 격차를 드러낼 수도 있다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 지문은 격차를 밝혀내는 것이 아니라 그대로 이어가는 것을 말한다. C는 원래 기대된 역할(격차 제거)과 일치해 훑어 읽으면 고르기 쉽지만, 'caution'과 'continue'가 보여주는 결론과 반대다. D는 부정적 효과라는 점은 맞지만, 지문은 격차가 커진다는 근거 없이 같은 방식으로 이어진다고만 말한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says AVMs learn from sales data shaped by discriminatory lending, so homes in Black neighborhoods "continue to receive lower estimates." That means the models keep existing disparities going, which is why B, "perpetuate," is correct. A might seem plausible because algorithms can reveal bias, but the text describes the models carrying the disparities forward, not uncovering them. C matches what AVMs were promoted to do, so it's tempting if you skim, but it contradicts the warning in "caution" and the word "continue." D does capture the negative effect, but the text never says the disparities get bigger, only that they carry on.
g.design: Distractors draw on partial cues: the models' intended purpose (C), harm without magnitude evidence (D), and algorithms revealing bias (A); only "continue" pins down perpetuate.

c.seed: economics and business — Supply chain diversification strategy manufacturing and geographic concentration risk COVID-19 pandemic disruptions

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Geographic concentration risk arises when a manufacturer relies on suppliers clustered in a single region.
- In early 2020, factory shutdowns in one region halted shipments of electronic components to automakers worldwide.
- A fictional appliance maker, Corvane Industries, sourced 90% of its circuit boards from one province before 2020.
- After the 2020 disruptions, Corvane split its circuit board orders among suppliers in three countries.
- In 2022, when one of those three regions faced port closures, Corvane's production fell by only 8%.
g.question: The student wants to present evidence that Corvane's post-2020 approach reduced its vulnerability. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Before 2020, Corvane Industries obtained 90% of its circuit boards from a single province, an example of geographic concentration risk.
In early 2020, factory shutdowns in one region halted component shipments to automakers worldwide, prompting firms such as Corvane to rethink their sourcing.
Having divided its circuit board orders among suppliers in three countries, Corvane saw production drop by just 8% when port closures struck one of those regions in 2022.
Corvane Industries now orders circuit boards from suppliers in three countries rather than relying mainly on one province.
g.design: 정답은 전략 변화(3개국 분산)와 그 결과(2022년 8% 감소)를 연결해야 하며, D는 전략만 제시해 효과 증거가 빠지고 A·B는 정확한 메모지만 이전 상황·배경만 다룬다.
g.explanation: 목표는 2020년 이후 Corvane의 방식이 취약성을 줄였다는 '증거'를 제시하는 것이므로, 분산 전략과 그 결과를 함께 보여야 한다. C는 3개국 분산과 2022년 항구 폐쇄 때 생산이 8%만 줄었다는 결과를 연결해 목표를 달성한다. A는 2020년 이전의 집중 상태만 설명할 뿐 이후 방식의 효과는 보여주지 않는다. B는 2020년 혼란이라는 배경만 다룬다. D는 바뀐 전략을 정확히 서술하지만, 그것이 실제로 취약성을 줄였다는 증거가 없다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to give evidence that Corvane's post-2020 approach made it less vulnerable, so the sentence needs both the new strategy and its result. C does this: it links the three-country split to the fact that production fell by only 8% during the 2022 port closures. A only describes Corvane's concentrated sourcing before 2020, not whether the later approach worked. B only gives the 2020 disruption as background. D correctly states the new strategy, but it offers no evidence that the strategy actually reduced vulnerability.

c.seed: economics and business — Manufacturing labor union density decline and wage inequality correlation post-industrial economic stagnation

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Union density is the share of workers who belong to a labor union.
- In the United States, union density in manufacturing fell from roughly 39 percent in 1973 to about 9 percent by 2019.
- Over a similar period, the gap between the earnings of high-wage and median-wage male workers widened substantially.
- Economists Bruce Western and Jake Rosenfeld estimated that declining unionization accounts for one-fifth to one-third of the growth in wage inequality among U.S. men from 1973 to 2007.
- Unions tend to compress wages by raising pay for lower- and middle-wage workers more than for top earners.
g.question: The student wants to explain a mechanism by which falling union membership could contribute to greater pay disparity. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In U.S. manufacturing, union density dropped from roughly 39 percent in 1973 to about 9 percent by 2019, while the earnings gap between high-wage and median-wage men widened substantially.
Western and Rosenfeld estimated that declining unionization accounts for one-fifth to one-third of the growth in wage inequality among U.S. men between 1973 and 2007.
Union density, the share of workers belonging to a union, fell sharply in U.S. manufacturing, dropping to about 9 percent by 2019.

Because unions raise pay for lower- and middle-wage workers more than for top earners, the fall in manufacturing union density from roughly 39 percent to about 9 percent likely weakened a force that had kept wages compressed.
g.explanation: 목표는 노조 감소가 임금 격차를 키우는 '작동 원리(메커니즘)'를 설명하는 것이다. D는 노조가 하위·중간 임금을 더 끌어올려 임금을 압축한다는 메모와 노조 조직률 하락을 연결해 그 원리를 제시한다. A는 두 추세가 동시에 나타났다는 상관관계만 보여 줄 뿐 이유는 설명하지 않는다. B는 영향의 크기를 추정한 수치일 뿐 어떻게 작용하는지는 밝히지 않는다. C는 조직률 하락만 언급하고 임금 격차와의 연결이 없다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain a mechanism—how falling union membership could widen pay gaps. D does this by linking the note that unions compress wages (raising lower- and middle-wage pay more than top pay) to the decline in union density, showing why inequality would grow. A only shows that the two trends happened together, which is a correlation, not a mechanism. B gives an estimate of how much the decline contributed, but not how it works. C describes the decline in union density without connecting it to pay disparity at all.
g.design: 오답 A·B는 정확한 메모로 상관관계·영향 크기를 제시해 그럴듯하지만 '메커니즘' 목표에서 벗어나며, 정답은 임금 압축 메모와 조직률 하락 메모를 결합해야 한다. 질문은 'compress' 등 정답 핵심어를 피했다.

c.seed: economics and business — Gig economy platform worker misclassification independent contractor status and legal labor regulation challenges

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Many app-based delivery and ride-hailing platforms classify their workers as independent contractors rather than employees.
- Independent contractors in the United States are generally not entitled to minimum wage, overtime pay, or unemployment insurance.
- In 2019, California passed Assembly Bill 5, which applied the "ABC test": a worker is presumed to be an employee unless the hiring company proves, among other things, that the work is outside the usual course of its business.
- In 2020, California voters approved Proposition 22, which exempted app-based drivers from Assembly Bill 5 while granting them a guaranteed minimum earnings level and some health-care stipends.
- In 2024, the European Union adopted a directive presuming that platform workers are employees when a platform controls how their work is performed.
g.question: The student wants to emphasize that California's approach to classifying app-based drivers shifted within a short period. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In 2019, California's Assembly Bill 5 presumed that most workers were employees, but just a year later, Proposition 22 carved out app-based drivers, offering them minimum earnings guarantees instead of full employee status.

In 2019, California's Assembly Bill 5 presumed that most workers were employees, and in 2024, the European Union adopted a similar presumption for platform workers whose work is controlled by a platform.
In 2020, California's Proposition 22 granted app-based drivers a guaranteed minimum earnings level and some health-care stipends, benefits not generally available to independent contractors.

In 2019, California's Assembly Bill 5 required hiring companies to prove that a worker's tasks fell outside the usual course of their business in order to treat that worker as an independent contractor.
g.explanation: 목표는 캘리포니아의 앱 기반 운전자 분류 방식이 짧은 기간 안에 바뀌었다는 점을 강조하는 것이므로, 2019년 AB5와 2020년 Proposition 22를 연결해 1년 만의 변화를 보여 주는 A가 정답이다. B는 AB5를 정확히 인용하지만 EU와 비교하는 데 그쳐 캘리포니아 내부의 변화가 드러나지 않는다. C는 Proposition 22의 혜택만 설명하고, 이전의 AB5 규정과 대비하지 않아 '변화'가 보이지 않는다. D는 AB5의 ABC 테스트만 설명하므로 한 시점의 규정일 뿐이다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to show that California's way of classifying app-based drivers changed within a short time. A does this by linking the 2019 Assembly Bill 5 to the 2020 Proposition 22, which shows a reversal just one year later. B uses the AB5 note accurately, but it compares California with the European Union instead of showing a change inside California. C describes only what Proposition 22 provided and never contrasts it with the earlier AB5 rule, so you can't see any shift. D explains only AB5's ABC test, which describes the policy at a single point in time.
g.design: 정답은 두 시점의 메모(AB5와 Prop 22)를 결합해야 하고, 오답들은 정확한 메모를 쓰지만 단일 시점만 다루거나 엉뚱한 비교로 빠진다. 모든 선택지는 같은 연도+법령 문장 틀을 쓰고, 정답에는 질문의 'shifted' 같은 표현을 그대로 쓰지 않았다.

c.seed: economics and business — Retail markdown optimization algorithms dynamic price adjustment and inventory turnover profit maximization timing

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Retailers traditionally cut prices on unsold seasonal goods using fixed schedules, such as 30% off after six weeks.
- Markdown optimization algorithms instead adjust prices item by item, using daily sales data to predict how demand will respond to each discount.
- A fixed schedule may cut prices on a sweater that is still selling well, giving away profit unnecessarily.
- An algorithm may delay a markdown on that sweater until its sales actually slow.
- A 2019 industry survey found that apparel retailers using such algorithms raised gross margins on clearance goods by an average of 6 percentage points.
g.question: The student wants to explain why the newer approach can protect profits better than the older one. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Markdown optimization algorithms adjust prices item by item using daily sales data, and a 2019 survey found that apparel retailers using them averaged 6 percentage points higher gross margins on clearance goods.
Markdown optimization algorithms, unlike fixed schedules, can hold off on discounting an item that is still selling well until its sales slow, avoiding giving away profit unnecessarily.
Markdown optimization algorithms, unlike fixed schedules such as 30% off after six weeks, rely on daily sales data to predict how demand will respond to each discount.
Markdown optimization algorithms replace fixed schedules, which may cut prices on a sweater that is still selling well, with item-by-item price adjustments.
g.design: 정답은 메모 3·4를 결합해 '왜' 이익이 보호되는지 인과 메커니즘을 설명한다. A는 결과(수치)만, C·D는 차이점은 말하지만 그 차이가 이익과 어떻게 이어지는지 연결하지 않아 비교가 필요하다.
g.explanation: 목표는 새 방식이 '왜' 이익을 더 잘 지키는지 설명하는 것이므로, 잘 팔리는 상품의 할인을 판매가 둔화될 때까지 미뤄 불필요한 이익 손실을 피한다는 메커니즘을 제시한 B가 정답이다. A는 마진 상승이라는 결과만 보여 줄 뿐 그 이유를 설명하지 않는다. C는 두 방식의 작동 차이만 서술하고 이익과는 연결하지 않는다. D는 고정 일정의 문제를 언급하지만, 새 방식이 그 문제를 어떻게 피하는지는 설명하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain why the newer approach protects profits better, so the answer has to show how it works. B does that: the algorithm holds off on discounting an item that is still selling well, so it doesn't give away profit for no reason. A reports a result (higher margins) but doesn't explain what causes it. C describes how the two methods work differently but never connects that difference to profit. D points out the problem with fixed schedules but doesn't explain how item-by-item adjustment avoids it.
