g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In the 1970s, inexpensive quartz watches from Japan and Hong Kong flooded global markets.
- Swiss watchmakers, who relied mostly on traditional mechanical movements, saw employment in their industry fall from about 90,000 workers in 1970 to roughly 30,000 by the mid-1980s.
- In 1983, the Swiss company SMH (later the Swatch Group) introduced the Swatch, a plastic quartz watch.
- The Swatch used only 51 parts, compared with more than 90 in a typical quartz watch of the time, which allowed it to be assembled by machine.
- Fewer parts and automated assembly let the Swatch sell for a low price while still being made in Switzerland.
g.question: The student wants to explain how the Swatch's design made it possible to manufacture a cheap watch in Switzerland. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Introduced by SMH in 1983, the Swatch was a plastic quartz watch that entered a market already crowded with inexpensive quartz watches from Japan and Hong Kong.
As cheap quartz watches spread in the 1970s, employment in the Swiss watch industry fell from about 90,000 workers in 1970 to roughly 30,000 by the mid-1980s.
With just 51 parts rather than the 90-plus common at the time, the Swatch could be assembled by machine, keeping its price low even though it was produced in Switzerland.
Unlike the traditional mechanical watches Swiss firms had long relied on, the Swatch, launched in 1983, used a quartz movement housed in a plastic case.
g.explanation: 목표는 Swatch의 설계가 어떻게 스위스에서의 저가 생산을 가능하게 했는지, 즉 원인과 결과를 연결해 설명하는 것이다. C는 부품 수 축소(51개)→기계 조립→스위스 생산임에도 저가라는 인과 관계를 메모 두 개를 결합해 제시한다. A는 Swatch의 출시와 시장 상황을 말할 뿐 설계가 비용을 낮춘 방식을 설명하지 않는다. B는 산업 쇠퇴 수치만 전달하며 Swatch 자체가 빠져 있다. D는 설계 특징(쿼츠, 플라스틱)을 언급하지만 그것이 어떻게 저가 생산으로 이어졌는지는 보여 주지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain how the Swatch's design made cheap Swiss manufacturing possible, so the sentence needs to link a design feature to its cost result. C does this by connecting the reduced part count (51) to machine assembly and then to a low price despite Swiss production. A describes the Swatch's launch and its competitive market but never explains how its design lowered costs. B reports the industry's job losses and doesn't mention the Swatch at all. D names design features (quartz movement, plastic case) but doesn't show how they made low-cost production possible.
g.design: 오답 A·D는 Swatch에 관한 정확한 설계/출시 정보를 쓰지만 인과(설계→저비용) 연결이 없어 비교해야 배제되며, B는 맥락 정보로 그럴듯하다. 질문은 'parts/machine' 등 정답 핵심어를 피했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 목표(비교·대조·특징 강조 등)에 맞게 서로 다른 메모를 골라 결합해야 하는 문제. 오답은 정확한 메모를 쓰지만 목표에서 벗어난다.
c.seed: economics and business — Patek Philippe luxury watchmaking Swiss heritage and vertical integration manufacturing maintaining exclusivity positioning

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Patek Philippe is a Swiss watchmaker founded in Geneva in 1839.
- The company designs and produces most of its movements, cases, and dials in its own workshops rather than buying parts from outside suppliers.
- This practice, known as vertical integration, lets the firm control the quality and pace of production.
- Patek Philippe makes only about 70,000 watches per year, far fewer than many large watch brands.
- Keeping output low helps the brand stay exclusive, so its watches often hold or increase their value on the resale market.
g.question: The student wants to explain how the company's manufacturing approach supports its high-end market position. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Founded in Geneva in 1839, Patek Philippe is a Swiss watchmaker that designs and produces most of its movements, cases, and dials in its own workshops.
Patek Philippe makes only about 70,000 watches per year, and its watches often hold or increase their value on the resale market.
Because Patek Philippe makes most of its own parts instead of buying them from outside suppliers, the company is an example of vertical integration.
By making most of its parts in its own workshops, Patek Philippe controls the pace of production, limiting output to about 70,000 watches a year and keeping the brand exclusive.
g.design: 정답은 제조 방식(수직 통합)→생산 통제→소량 생산→희소성이라는 인과 연결을 요구한다. A·C는 제조 방식만, B는 희소성 결과만 다루어 각각 절반만 충족하도록 했다.
g.explanation: 목표는 제조 방식이 고급 시장 지위를 어떻게 뒷받침하는지 설명하는 것이므로, 자체 생산과 희소성을 인과적으로 연결해야 한다. D는 자체 생산으로 생산 속도를 통제해 생산량을 연 약 7만 개로 제한하고 브랜드의 희소성을 유지한다고 설명하므로 정답이다. A는 역사와 자체 생산을 언급하지만 시장 지위와 연결하지 않는다. B는 적은 생산량과 재판매 가치를 제시하지만 제조 방식을 빠뜨렸다. C는 수직 통합을 정의할 뿐 그것이 희소성에 어떻게 기여하는지는 설명하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain how the way the company makes its watches supports its high-end position, so the answer has to connect the manufacturing method to exclusivity as cause and effect. D does this: making parts in-house lets the company control the pace of production, which keeps output at about 70,000 watches a year and keeps the brand exclusive. A mentions the company's history and in-house production but never ties them to its market position. B gives the low output and the resale value but leaves out the manufacturing approach. C only defines vertical integration and doesn't show how it supports exclusivity.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — De Beers diamond cartel monopoly control and vertical integration from mining through retail distribution channels

g.passage: For much of the twentieth century, the De Beers company controlled most of the world's rough diamond supply. Economists have generally credited this dominance to De Beers's ownership of mines and its stockpiling of unsold stones. Business historian Lena Achterberg offers a different explanation: she argues that De Beers's ability to keep prices high depended chiefly on its control of distribution. Specifically, it controlled which cutters and wholesalers were allowed to buy rough stones at its invitation-only "sights." In Achterberg's view, a producer that owned many mines but had no say over who could resell its diamonds would not have been able to hold prices steady.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Achterberg's argument?
options: In years when large independent mines outside De Beers ownership began production, prices stayed stable as long as those mines' output was sold through De Beers's sights, but prices fell once some producers began selling directly to unapproved buyers.
In years when De Beers increased its stockpile of unsold rough stones, prices stayed stable, and they fell in years when the stockpile shrank, regardless of who was allowed to attend the sights.
In years when De Beers acquired additional mines in southern Africa, the number of wholesalers invited to its sights also rose, and the average price of polished diamonds rose slightly.
In years when consumer demand for diamond engagement rings rose in the United States, prices stayed stable even as De Beers reduced the number of cutters invited to its sights.
g.explanation: 아흐터베르크는 가격 유지의 핵심이 광산 소유가 아니라 누가 원석을 재판매할 수 있는지에 대한 통제라고 주장한다. A는 광산 소유와 상관없이 판매 경로(사이트)를 통제할 때는 가격이 유지되고 그 통제가 깨지자 가격이 떨어졌음을 보여 주므로 주장을 가장 직접적으로 지지한다. B는 비축이 가격을 좌우했다는 기존 설명을 지지할 뿐이다. C는 광산 인수와 구매자 확대가 함께 일어나 어느 요인이 가격에 영향을 줬는지 구분할 수 없다. D는 사이트 초대 인원이 바뀌어도 가격이 그대로였음을 보여 주어 유통 통제의 역할을 따로 떼어 내지 못하고, 수요 증가라는 다른 요인도 섞여 있다.
g.explanation_en: Achterberg claims that De Beers kept prices high mainly by controlling who could resell rough diamonds, not by owning mines. Choice A fits best: prices held while outside mines' output went through De Beers's sights, then fell once producers sold to unapproved buyers, so control over distribution, not mine ownership, tracks with price stability. Choice B backs the stockpiling explanation that economists usually give, not Achterberg's. Choice C has mine purchases and wider sight access happening at the same time, so you can't tell which one affected prices. Choice D shows prices staying the same even though sight access changed, and rising demand clouds the picture, so it doesn't isolate the role of distribution control.
g.design: To get the answer, students have to tie the claim's contrast (distribution vs. mines) to a finding that pulls those two factors apart. B, C, and D each mention the sights or prices, which is partly relevant, but none separates the factors in a way that supports her.

issues: answer_leak:질문의 주체·수치를 정답만 반복(정답 2개 고유 일치, 오답 0)

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Champagne wine appellation protection France and geographical indication trademark preventing counterfeit sparkling wine production

g.passage: Since the early twentieth century, French law has restricted the name "Champagne" to sparkling wine made from grapes grown in a delimited region of northeastern France, and the European Union now enforces the name as a protected geographical indication. Economist Margaux Delattre argues that the main economic benefit of this protection is not that it blocks outright counterfeits, which are rare and easily prosecuted, but that it keeps the name meaningful to consumers. In her view, without legal protection, producers elsewhere would label ordinary sparkling wines "champagne," and the word would gradually become a generic term for any bubbly wine, eroding the price premium that genuine Champagne commands.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Delattre's argument?
options: In countries that enforce the Champagne indication, customs officials seize only a few thousand bottles of fake Champagne each year, most of them sold in bottles that copy well-known Champagne houses' labels.

In markets where the Champagne indication was not legally recognized for decades, surveyed shoppers commonly used "champagne" to mean any sparkling wine, and genuine Champagne sold at a smaller premium over other sparkling wines than in markets where the name was protected.

In markets where the Champagne indication is protected, sales of sparkling wines from other regions, such as Italian prosecco, have grown faster over the past two decades than sales of genuine Champagne.

In the Champagne region itself, grape prices paid to growers have risen steadily since the name gained EU protection, as demand from Champagne houses has exceeded the supply of grapes from the delimited area.
g.explanation: Delattre의 주장은 두 단계로 되어 있다. 법적 보호가 없으면 이름이 일반 명사가 되고, 그 결과 가격 프리미엄이 줄어든다는 것이다. B는 보호가 없던 시장에서 이름이 일반 명사로 쓰였고 프리미엄도 작았다고 보여 주므로 두 단계를 모두 뒷받침한다. A는 위조품 문제를 다루지만, 그녀는 위조품 차단이 주된 이익이 아니라고 했으므로 주장의 핵심과 관련이 없다. C는 보호된 시장 안의 경쟁 이야기일 뿐 보호가 있는 시장과 없는 시장을 비교하지 않고, D는 가격 상승을 보여 주지만 그 원인이 이름의 의미 유지라는 점은 드러나지 않고 공급 부족으로 설명된다.
g.explanation_en: Delattre's argument has two links: without protection, the name becomes a generic term, and that loss of meaning shrinks Champagne's price premium. B shows both links at once, because in unprotected markets shoppers used "champagne" for any sparkling wine and the premium was smaller. A is about counterfeits, which Delattre says are not the main benefit, so it misses her central point. C describes competition inside protected markets and never compares protected with unprotected markets. D shows prices rising, but it explains the rise through limited grape supply, not through the name keeping its meaning.
g.design: 정답이 되려면 '일반 명사화'와 '프리미엄 감소'라는 두 연결 고리를 모두 확인해야 한다. 오답 A와 D는 보호나 가격이라는 주제 일부만 맞는 함정으로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 지문에 '한때 ~라고 여겨졌으나(통념)' 다음 'however/but/실제로는' 류의 전환어와 함께 이를 뒤집는 새 증거나 반박 문장을 제시하고, 빈칸이 그 반박된 결과를 표현하도록 한다. 정답은 통념과 정반대 방향의 의미를 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 통념 쪽 단어를 그대로 쓴 것, (2) 전환어를 못 읽고 통념과 같은 방향이지만 강도만 다른 단어, (3) 반박 대상과 무관한 제3의 의미 단어로 구성한다. 전환 지점 앞뒤 문장만으로 답이 결정되게 하고 문장 길이나 어휘 난이도는 중간 수준을 유지한다.
c.seed: economics and business — Wool trade England medieval period and Crown taxation revenue monopoly on raw material export

g.passage: Historians once assumed that the Crown's control over England's raw wool exports in the fourteenth century, which funneled shipments through a few designated "staple" towns where they could be taxed, left the country's merchants largely powerless before royal demands. Recent studies of customs records and loan agreements, however, show that the kings depended so heavily on advances from wool merchants that the merchants could bargain over tax rates and even veto new levies. Far from being subordinate to the Crown, these traders were often ______ in setting royal fiscal policy.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation:
정답 C(influential): 'however' 뒤의 새 증거를 보면 왕은 상인들의 대출에 의존했고, 상인들은 세율을 협상하고 새 세금을 거부할 수도 있었다. 'Far from being subordinate'라는 표현도 통념을 뒤집으므로, 빈칸에는 상인들이 재정 정책에 '영향력이 컸다'는 뜻의 단어가 들어가야 한다.
A(submissive, 순종적인)는 반박된 통념인 '무력한 상인'을 그대로 가리키는 단어다.
B(hesitant, 주저하는)는 전환어를 놓치고 통념과 같은 방향(소극적임)을 약하게 표현한 단어여서, 거부권을 행사했다는 증거와 맞지 않는다.
D(nostalgic, 향수에 젖은)는 권력 관계와 상관없는 제3의 의미다.
g.explanation_en:
Choice C, "influential," is correct. After "however," the passage gives new evidence: the kings relied on loans from wool merchants, and the merchants could bargain over tax rates and even veto new taxes. The phrase "Far from being subordinate" also flips the old view. So the blank needs a word meaning the merchants had real power over royal fiscal policy.
Choice A, "submissive," just repeats the old view of powerless merchants that the passage rejects.
Choice B, "hesitant," comes from missing the shift. It points the same way as the old view (merchants being passive), only more weakly, and it doesn't fit merchants who could veto taxes.
Choice D, "nostalgic," has nothing to do with the power relationship being discussed.
g.design: 통념(상인은 무력했다)을 먼저 제시한 뒤 'however' 다음에 이를 반박하는 증거를 두고, 빈칸이 뒤집힌 결론을 나타내게 했다. 오답은 통념 그대로(submissive), 같은 방향이지만 약한 단어(hesitant), 무관한 의미(nostalgic)로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 지문에 'is not X, but rather Y' 또는 'it isn't that A; instead B' 형태로 부정어 뒤에 대조 표현이 이어지는 문장을 만들고, 빈칸이 그 대조 표현(B) 자리에 오게 한다. 정답은 부정된 개념(X)과 반대 극성을 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 부정어를 무시하고 X와 같은 의미 단어, (2) 부정 구조를 이중으로 잘못 해석해 극성을 다시 뒤집은 단어, (3) 대조 구조와 무관한 유사 발음/철자 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: economics and business — Spice trade Portuguese monopoly sixteenth century and maritime route control dominating Indian Ocean commerce

g.passage: Textbooks often say that after Vasco da Gama's voyage, Portugal took command of Indian Ocean commerce. Using its fortresses at Goa, Hormuz, and Malacca, Portugal required every merchant vessel to buy a license called a cartaz. However, historians who study customs records argue that the Portuguese hold on the spice trade was not airtight but rather ______: Gujarati, Arab, and Acehnese traders regularly slipped pepper past Portuguese patrols to Red Sea ports, and by the 1560s Venice was again importing spices through Alexandria in amounts close to those of the previous century.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 정답 D(porous, 구멍이 많아 새는). 'not airtight but rather ___' 구조에서 빈칸에는 부정된 airtight(빈틈없는)와 반대되는 말이 들어가야 한다. 콜론 뒤의 근거도 이를 뒷받침한다. 상인들이 순찰을 피해 후추를 홍해로 실어 날랐고, 베네치아의 수입량도 예전 수준을 거의 회복했다. 즉 포르투갈의 통제는 허점이 많았다. A(impervious, 아무것도 통과시키지 않는)는 부정어 not을 무시하고 airtight와 같은 뜻의 단어를 고른 오답이다. B(unchallenged, 도전받지 않는)는 'not ... but rather' 구조를 한 번 더 뒤집어 읽어 '완전한 지배'라는 극성으로 되돌아간 오답이다. 게다가 밀무역이 있었다는 근거와 정면으로 모순된다. C(ponderous, 육중하고 둔한)는 porous와 철자·발음이 비슷할 뿐 대조 구조나 '새어 나감'이라는 근거와 관계가 없다.
g.explanation_en: The answer is D, "porous." The sentence follows the pattern "not airtight but rather ___," so the blank needs a word that means the opposite of "airtight." The evidence after the colon supports this: traders routinely slipped pepper past Portuguese patrols, and Venice's spice imports recovered. In other words, Portugal's control had many gaps, so "porous" fits. A, "impervious," ignores the word "not" and simply repeats the idea of "airtight." B, "unchallenged," reads the contrast backward, which brings the meaning back to total dominance, and it contradicts the smuggling evidence. C, "ponderous," looks and sounds like "porous" but means heavy or clumsy. It has nothing to do with the contrast or with goods leaking through.
g.design: Following the recipe, the blank sits in the B slot of a "not X but rather Y" sentence. The distractors are (1) a synonym of the negated X ("impervious"), (2) a word that flips the polarity back to X's side ("unchallenged"), and (3) a word that only looks and sounds like the answer ("ponderous").

c.instruction: 지문을 두 단계(예: 상황 묘사 후 화자의 숙고, 또는 기존 주장 소개 후 저자의 반박/선언)로 구성하고, 빈칸을 두 번째 단계의 시작 지점에 배치해 앞 단계와 다른 서술 기능을 하도록 한다. 정답은 두 번째 단계의 기능(숙고, 반박, 선언 등)에 맞는 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 첫 번째 단계에 어울리는 단어, (2) 두 단계 어디에도 맞지 않는 중립적 단어, (3) 의미는 비슷하나 문장이 요구하는 품사/기능이 다른 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: economics and business — Silk Road caravan trade networks Central Asia and overland merchant routes enabling Eurasian commodity exchange

g.passage: Popular accounts often describe the Silk Road as a single great highway, with lone merchants leading camel caravans all the way from Chang'an to the Mediterranean, carrying silk west and returning with glass and silver. Historian Valerie Hansen ______ this image: drawing on contracts and travel passes found at oasis sites such as Turfan, she argues that most goods moved in short relays between neighboring towns, changing hands many times and rarely making the full journey with any one trader.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation:
지문은 두 단계로 되어 있다. 첫 단계는 실크로드를 하나의 큰 길로 보고 상인 한 명이 전 구간을 오갔다는 통념을 소개한다. 둘째 단계는 Hansen이 문서 증거를 근거로 상품이 짧은 구간씩 릴레이로 옮겨졌다고 주장하는 내용이다. 콜론 뒤의 내용이 통념과 정면으로 어긋나므로, 빈칸에는 그 이미지에 '이의를 제기한다'는 뜻의 contests가 들어가야 한다. 따라서 정답은 A이다.
B(popularizes): 첫 단계의 '대중적 서술'에는 어울린다. 하지만 Hansen은 그 이미지를 퍼뜨리는 쪽이 아니라 뒤집는 쪽이다.
C(recounts): '이야기한다/서술한다'는 중립적인 말이라 Hansen의 반박 기능을 담지 못한다. 그녀는 통념을 다시 들려주는 것이 아니라 반박한다.
D(refutation): 뜻은 '반박'으로 비슷하다. 그러나 명사여서 주어 Hansen 뒤에 필요한 동사 자리에 들어갈 수 없다.
g.explanation_en:
The passage has two stages. The first stage describes a popular view: the Silk Road was one highway, and single merchants traveled its whole length. The second stage gives Hansen's argument, based on documents, that goods actually moved in short relays and changed hands many times. What comes after the colon directly contradicts the popular view, so the blank needs a verb meaning that Hansen disputes that image. "Contests" fits, so the answer is A.
B ("popularizes"): This word suits the first stage, which is about popular accounts. But Hansen is overturning the image, not spreading it.
C ("recounts"): This word is neutral. It means she simply retells the image, which misses the fact that she is arguing against it.
D ("refutation"): The meaning is close, but it's a noun. The sentence needs a verb after the subject "Hansen," so it doesn't fit grammatically.
g.design: 첫 단계(통념 소개) 뒤, 둘째 단계(저자의 반박)가 시작되는 지점에 빈칸을 두었다. 오답은 지시대로 구성했다. popularizes는 첫 단계에 어울리는 단어, recounts는 어느 단계에도 맞지 않는 중립어, refutation은 뜻은 비슷하지만 품사가 다른 단어다.

c.instruction: 지문에 두 변수 사이의 이론적 관계(예: A가 클수록 B도 커진다, 정직한 신호일수록 비용이 크다)를 제시하고, 이 이론을 새로운 구체적 집단이나 사례에 적용했을 때 나올 결론을 빈칸으로 묻는다. 정답은 이론이 제시한 방향을 그대로 새 사례에 적용한 것이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 관계의 방향을 반대로 뒤집기, 원인과 결과를 바꾸기, 이론과 무관한 제3의 요인을 결론으로 제시하기의 실제 오개념을 사용해 만든다.
c.seed: economics and business — Hanseatic League merchant confederation and grain timber fur monopoly Baltic Sea regional trade

g.passage: Economists who study trading cartels argue that a cartel's power to keep prices well above competitive levels depends on how hard it is for buyers to reach other suppliers: the fewer outside sources buyers can turn to, the larger and more durable the cartel's markup. The medieval Hanseatic League, a confederation of merchant towns, long dominated two Baltic trades—grain shipped from Prussian and Livonian ports and furs bought in Novgorod. During the fifteenth century, however, Dutch shippers increasingly sailed directly to the Baltic grain ports and bought from local sellers, whereas furs from Novgorod continued to pass almost entirely through the Hanseatic trading post there. If the economists' argument is correct, one would expect that during this period ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the Hanse's markups on grain should have proved more durable than its markups on furs.
the Hanse's markups on furs should have proved more durable than its markups on grain.
the Hanse's high markups on furs should have been what kept Dutch shippers from entering the fur trade.
the Hanse's markups on grain should have fallen mainly because Baltic harvests grew larger.
g.explanation:
정답 B: 이론은 구매자가 의존할 수 있는 다른 공급원이 적을수록 가격 인상분이 크고 오래 유지된다고 본다. 곡물 무역에는 네덜란드 상인이라는 대안 공급 경로가 생겼지만, 모피는 여전히 거의 전부 한자 상관을 거쳤다. 따라서 모피의 가격 인상분이 곡물보다 더 잘 유지되었어야 한다.
A: 관계의 방향을 뒤집었다. 대안 공급원이 생긴 곡물의 인상분이 오히려 더 잘 유지되었다고 예측한다.
C: 원인과 결과를 바꿨다. 이론에서는 대안 공급원이 적다는 점이 원인이고 높은 인상분이 결과인데, C는 높은 인상분이 경쟁자의 진입을 막았다고 말한다. 게다가 높은 인상분은 경쟁자를 막기보다 끌어들이는 요인이다.
D: 이론과 관계없는 제3의 요인인 수확량을 가져왔다. 지문의 논증은 공급원 접근성에 관한 것일 뿐 수확량은 다루지 않는다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, B: The theory says that the fewer outside suppliers buyers can reach, the larger and longer-lasting a cartel's markup. In the grain trade, Dutch shippers gave buyers another way to get grain. Furs, though, still passed almost entirely through the Hanse's trading post in Novgorod. So the markup on furs should have held up better than the markup on grain.
A gets the relationship backward. It predicts that grain, the trade that gained a new supply route, kept the more durable markup.
C reverses cause and effect. In the theory, having few outside sources is the cause and a high markup is the result. C instead says the high markup kept rivals out. A high markup would also tend to attract rivals, not keep them away.
D brings in a third factor, harvest size, that the theory never mentions. The argument is only about how easily buyers can reach other suppliers.
g.design: I gave a theory linking few alternative suppliers to large, lasting markups and applied it to the Hanse's grain and fur trades, which differed in how easily buyers could reach other suppliers. Each wrong answer uses a different error: one reverses the direction of the relationship, one swaps cause and effect, and one brings in an unrelated third factor. All four choices share the same sentence frame.

c.instruction: 짧은 표나 그래프 하나와 이를 설명하는 가설 문장 하나를 함께 제시하고, 두 정보를 결합해야만 답할 수 있는 결론을 빈칸으로 묻는다. 정답은 시각 자료의 특정 수치와 가설 문장을 연결해야 나오고, 오답 3개는 각각 시각 자료만 보고 가설을 무시한 결론, 가설 문장만 보고 시각 자료를 무시한 결론, 시각 자료의 다른 항목을 잘못 짝지은 결론으로 만든다.
c.seed: economics and business — Antwerp diamond cutting industry fifteenth century and gemstone valuation standardization pricing establishment

g.passage:
In the fifteenth century, Antwerp became a center of diamond cutting, and historian Lieve Marten has examined surviving merchant ledgers to study how stone prices were set. Marten hypothesizes that once Antwerp's cutters adopted the shared standards for facet geometry that guild records show spreading after about 1480, buyers could judge a cut stone by its weight alone, so that the price spread among stones of the same weight should have narrowed noticeably in the decades after the standards took hold. The table shows the ratio of the highest to the lowest price recorded for one-carat cut stones in three periods.

Period | High-to-low price ratio, one-carat stones
1450–1469 | 3.8
1470–1489 | 3.6
1490–1509 | 1.7

If Marten's hypothesis is correct, the ledger data suggest that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the price spread for one-carat stones narrowed steadily in every period, which shows that standardized facet geometry had already shaped prices before 1470.
buyers in the 1470–1489 period were already judging one-carat stones by weight alone, since the guild standards had begun spreading during those years.
the shared facet standards became established practice among Antwerp's cutters mainly in the decades after 1489, not when they first appeared in guild records.
the price spread among one-carat stones was largest in 1450–1469 because buyers in that period valued stones mainly by their weight.
g.explanation: 정답 C: 가설에 따르면 표준이 정착하면 가격 비율이 크게 줄어야 한다. 표에서 1470–1489년에는 3.8→3.6으로 거의 그대로이고, 1490–1509년에야 1.7로 급감한다. 따라서 표준은 1480년경 기록에 처음 나타났지만 실제 정착은 1489년 이후였다고 추론할 수 있다. A: 표만 보고 '꾸준한 감소'로 읽은 결론이다. 3.8→3.6은 미미한 변화이고, 1470년 이전에 표준이 영향을 줬다는 근거도 없다(가설 무시). B: 가설과 1480년이라는 연도만 보고 표를 무시한 결론이다. 1470–1489년의 비율 3.6은 거의 줄지 않았다. D: 1450–1469년 수치를 가설의 메커니즘과 잘못 짝지었다. 가설대로라면 무게만으로 평가할 때 가격 폭은 좁아야 하는데, 그 시기에는 오히려 가장 넓다.
g.explanation_en: Correct answer, C: The hypothesis says the price spread should narrow noticeably once the standards took hold. In the table, the ratio barely changes from 1450–1469 to 1470–1489 (3.8 to 3.6). It only drops sharply in 1490–1509 (1.7). So even though the standards show up in guild records around 1480, they must have become established practice only after 1489. A: This reads the table alone as a "steady" decline and ignores the hypothesis. The drop from 3.8 to 3.6 is tiny, and nothing points to the standards affecting prices before 1470. B: This relies on the hypothesis and the 1480 date but ignores the table. A ratio of 3.6 in 1470–1489 shows the spread had hardly narrowed. D: This pairs the 1450–1469 figure with the wrong mechanism. Under the hypothesis, judging stones by weight alone would make the spread narrow, but in that period the spread was at its widest.
g.design: 가설(표준 정착→가격 폭 축소)과 표의 시기별 수치를 결합해야 실제 정착 시점을 추론하도록 했고, 오답은 표만 본 결론(A), 가설·연도만 본 결론(B), 다른 시기 수치를 잘못 짝지은 결론(D)으로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 하나의 결론이나 가설을 먼저 제시한 뒤, 그것을 뒷받침/약화/무관하게 만드는 추가 사실 하나를 골라야 하는 빈칸 문제를 만든다. 정답은 가설의 핵심 조건을 직접 충족하거나 위배하는 사실이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 표면적으로만 관련 있어 보이지만 실제로는 무관한 사실, 가설과 반대 방향으로 작용하는 사실을 지지 사실인 것처럼 제시한 것, 결론과 무관한 배경 정보를 결론 지지처럼 위장한 것으로 만든다.
c.seed: economics and business — South Sea Bubble 1720 joint-stock speculation and stock price manipulation creating financial market crash

g.passage: In 1720, shares of the South Sea Company rose from about £128 in January to nearly £1,000 by late June before collapsing. One economic historian argues that the rise was driven mainly by deliberate manipulation by company insiders rather than by investors' genuine, if overoptimistic, expectations about the firm's trade prospects. On this view, directors bought shares through intermediaries to push prices up, then sold their own holdings at the peak to buyers they had lured in. The historian's account would be most strongly supported if records showed that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: many smaller joint-stock ventures launched in 1720, some with vague or fanciful business plans, also saw sharp price increases before failing.
the company's directors went on buying shares for their own accounts throughout the summer and kept most of those holdings as the price collapsed in the autumn.
the company's charter, granted in 1711, gave it exclusive rights to British trade with Spanish colonies in South America.
the directors quietly sold large blocks of their personal shares in the weeks just before the price began to fall, while publicly urging investors to keep buying.
g.design: 가설의 핵심 조건(내부자가 가격을 올린 뒤 정점에서 팔아치움)을 직접 충족하는 사실을 정답으로 했다. 오답은 표면적으로만 관련된 사실(다른 거품 회사들), 반대 방향의 사실(이사들이 계속 보유함), 배경 정보(1711년 특허장)로 구성했다.
g.explanation:
정답 D: 역사가의 주장은 이사들이 가격을 끌어올린 뒤 정점에서 자기 주식을 팔고, 끌어들인 투자자들에게 넘겼다는 것이다. 폭락 직전에 몰래 대량 매도하면서 겉으로는 매수를 권했다는 기록은 이 핵심 조건을 그대로 충족한다.
A: 다른 회사들의 거품은 시장 전반에 투기 열기가 있었다는 증거일 수 있다. 오히려 '진짜 낙관론' 설명과 더 잘 맞으며, 이 회사 내부자의 조작을 보여 주지는 않는다.
B: 이사들이 사들인 주식을 폭락 때까지 들고 있었다면 정점에서 팔았다는 가설과 정면으로 어긋난다. 이사들도 실제로 낙관했다는 뜻이 되므로 주장을 약화한다.
C: 무역 독점권은 투자자들이 낙관할 만했던 배경을 설명할 뿐이다. 조작이 있었는지와는 관계가 없고, 오히려 낙관론 설명 쪽에 더 가깝다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, D: The historian claims insiders pushed the price up and then sold their own shares at the peak to the investors they had drawn in. Records showing that directors secretly sold large blocks just before the fall, while publicly urging people to keep buying, match this central claim directly.
A: Bubbles in other companies point to a general mood of speculation across the market. If anything, that fits the "genuine optimism" explanation better, and it says nothing about manipulation by insiders at this company.
B: If directors kept the shares they bought all the way through the collapse, they didn't sell at the peak. That suggests they were also truly optimistic, so this weakens the claim.
C: The trade monopoly only explains why investors had reason to be hopeful. It's background that has nothing to do with manipulation, and it fits the optimism explanation better.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Scottish free banking nineteenth century and note-issuing bank competition without central regulatory authority

g.passage: From the early 1700s until 1845, Scotland had no central bank, and no government agency decided how many banknotes could be printed. Instead, many private banks issued their own notes, and people could take any note back to the bank that issued it and exchange it for gold or silver. Banks also regularly collected the notes of rival banks and returned them to those banks for payment. A bank that printed far more notes than it could back with gold or silver would soon face demands for payment it could not meet. Historians who study this period therefore argue that, even without a regulator, ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: competition among the banks themselves discouraged any one bank from issuing too many notes.
the Scottish government secretly limited how many notes each bank was allowed to print.
banks could print as many notes as they liked because no customer ever asked for gold or silver.
rival banks refused to accept one another's notes, so each bank's notes stayed in its own town.
g.explanation: 지문에 따르면 경쟁 은행들은 서로의 지폐를 모아 발행 은행에 돌려보내 금·은으로 바꿔 달라고 했고, 지폐를 너무 많이 찍은 은행은 감당할 수 없는 지급 요구를 받게 되었다. 따라서 규제 기관이 없어도 은행 간 경쟁이 과잉 발행을 막았다는 A가 논리적인 결론이다. B는 지문의 '정부 기관이 발행량을 정하지 않았다'는 내용과 어긋난다. C는 사람들이 지폐를 금·은으로 바꿀 수 있었고 실제로 지급 요구가 있었다는 점과 모순된다. D는 은행들이 경쟁 은행의 지폐를 모았다는 진술과 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says rival banks collected each other's notes and sent them back for payment in gold or silver, so a bank that printed too many notes would face demands it couldn't meet. That means the competition among banks itself kept them from issuing too many notes, which is choice A. Choice B goes against the statement that no government agency decided how many notes could be printed. Choice C contradicts the point that people could exchange notes for gold or silver and that banks faced demands for payment. Choice D is the opposite of the passage, which says banks did collect their rivals' notes.
g.design: 추론 한 단계(경쟁 은행의 지폐 회수 → 과잉 발행 억제)만 필요하고 단서가 지문에 직접 나온다. 오답은 흔한 오개념(정부의 숨은 통제, 태환 요구가 없었음, 지폐가 유통되지 않음)으로 만들었으며, 지문을 읽으면 바로 배제된다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Meiji Japanese silk filature standardization and export market quality grading competitive textile advantage

g.passage: In the 1870s, Japanese silk exporters faced a problem: buyers in Lyon and New York complained that bales of Japanese raw silk varied widely in thickness and evenness, so the buyers could not predict how the thread would perform on their looms. To address this, mechanized filatures such as the Tomioka mill introduced standardized reeling methods, and exporters began sorting silk into official quality grades before shipment. Because foreign manufacturers could now know in advance what quality they were purchasing, they no longer needed to inspect every bale themselves. Historians therefore conclude that standardization and grading helped Japanese silk win market share mainly because ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: they made Japanese silk cheaper to produce than any silk made in Europe.
they made Japanese silk more reliable and predictable for foreign buyers.
they let Japanese silk exporters skip shipping through Lyon and New York.
they let Japanese silk filatures stop using mechanized reeling methods.
g.explanation: 지문은 구매자들의 불만이 품질의 불균일과 예측 불가능성이었고, 표준화와 등급 분류 덕분에 구매자들이 품질을 미리 알 수 있게 되었다고 말한다. 따라서 B가 결론으로 가장 논리적이다. A는 생산 비용을 다루는데, 지문은 비용에 대해 아무것도 말하지 않는다. C는 시장을 피했다는 내용이라 지문과 반대이며, D는 기계화 공장이 표준 방식을 도입했다는 지문 내용과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says buyers' problem was that Japanese silk varied in quality, so they couldn't predict how it would perform. Standardization and grading fixed this by letting buyers know the quality in advance, so B is the most logical conclusion. A is about production cost, which the passage never mentions. C contradicts the passage, which describes selling to buyers in those markets, not avoiding them, and D contradicts the statement that mechanized filatures introduced the standardized methods.
g.design: 쉬운 난이도에 맞춰 "품질 불균일 문제 → 표준화로 예측 가능해짐"이라는 한 단계 추론만 필요하게 했다. 오답은 같은 문장 틀을 쓰고, 비용 우위라는 흔한 오개념과 지문과 모순되는 내용을 담았다.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 주장과 이유를, 텍스트 2는 같은 주제의 다른 접근을 각각 짧게 제시하되 서로를 언급하지 않게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자라면 텍스트 1의 주장에 어떻게 반응할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 2의 전제에서만 도출되는 반응으로 만들고, 오답 3개는 텍스트 1의 내용을 반복하는 선택지, 텍스트 2의 결론만 되풀이하는 선택지, 텍스트 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점을 끌어온 선택지로 만든다.
c.seed: economics and business — Portuguese cork wine stopper monopoly and market dominance in beverage industry supply chains

g.passage:
Text 1
Portugal supplies roughly half of the world's natural cork, and its largest processors have long dominated the market for wine stoppers. Some analysts argue that this dominance will persist indefinitely: cork oaks take about twenty-five years to yield usable bark, so no rival region can quickly build a competing supply, and Portuguese firms therefore face no serious threat to their position.

Text 2
Market power in an input industry depends less on how hard it is to copy the input than on how easily buyers can do without it. When winemakers in New Zealand and Australia adopted aluminum screw caps in the early 2000s, cork producers lost a large share of those markets within a few years—even though no new cork forests had been planted anywhere.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the analysts' reasoning in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that the long maturation period of cork oaks prevents any rival region from quickly establishing a competing source of bark
By maintaining that aluminum screw caps have already replaced cork as the preferred stopper among most winemakers worldwide
By objecting that the analysts consider only whether others could produce cork and overlook whether buyers could switch to a different kind of closure
By arguing that Portuguese processors could lose their position mainly because rising harvest costs would make their cork too expensive to export
g.explanation: 정답 C: Text 2의 전제는 시장 지배력이 투입물 복제의 어려움보다 구매자가 그것 없이 지낼 수 있는지에 달려 있다는 것이다. Text 1의 분석가들은 '경쟁 코르크 공급을 빨리 만들 수 없다'는 공급 측 장벽만 근거로 삼으므로, Text 2 저자는 대체재(다른 마개)로의 전환 가능성을 간과했다고 반박할 것이다. A: Text 1의 근거를 반복한 것으로, Text 2 저자는 이 사실을 부정하진 않지만 그것이 결론을 뒷받침하지 못한다고 볼 것이므로 '동의'로 반응을 요약할 수 없다. B: Text 2의 사례를 과장해 되풀이한 것. Text 2는 뉴질랜드·호주 시장만 언급했을 뿐 전 세계 대다수의 선호를 주장하지 않는다. D: 수확 비용·수출 가격은 Text 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점이다.
g.explanation_en: C is correct. Text 2's premise is that an input industry's market power depends on whether buyers can do without the input, not on how hard the input is to copy. The analysts in Text 1 rest their case entirely on a supply-side barrier: no one can grow competing cork quickly. So Text 2's author would object that they ignore whether buyers could switch to other closures, as the screw-cap example shows. A just repeats Text 1's reasoning. Text 2's author wouldn't deny that cork oaks take a long time to mature, but would say that fact doesn't prove the conclusion, so "agreeing" doesn't describe the response. B exaggerates Text 2's example. Text 2 mentions only New Zealand and Australia and makes no claim about most winemakers worldwide. D brings in harvest costs and export prices, which Text 2 never discusses.
g.design: The two texts never mention each other. The answer comes only from Text 2's general premise (buyers' ability to substitute) applied to Text 1's supply-only reasoning. Each wrong answer was written to a type: A repeats Text 1, B overstates Text 2's conclusion, and D brings in an issue Text 2 doesn't cover.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 하나의 결론을 이끄는 주장을, 텍스트 2는 그 주장의 핵심 근거를 약하게 만들 수 있는 별개의 관찰이나 연구를 제시한다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자가 텍스트 1의 어느 부분에 가장 이의를 제기할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 1의 결론이 아니라 그 결론이 기대는 가정으로 하고, 오답 3개는 결론 자체, 텍스트 1의 부수적 세부, 텍스트 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분으로 만든다.
c.seed: economics and business — Swiss watchmaking precision manufacturing and temporal standardization enabling railway schedule infrastructure coordination

g.passage:
Text 1
In the 1870s and 1880s, Swiss watchmakers in the Jura valleys adopted interchangeable-part machining, and the cost of an accurate pocket watch fell sharply. Some economic historians argue that this drop made Swiss watches the tool that let European railways run on coordinated timetables: once conductors and stationmasters could each carry a dependable watch, the reasoning goes, lines operated by different companies could finally keep to shared schedules at junctions. On this view, precision manufacturing in Switzerland was a hidden foundation of continental rail integration.

Text 2
Company records from several Swiss and German rail operators of the period show that conductors' watches were seldom trusted to keep time on their own. Staff had to check their watches against station regulator clocks, which received telegraph time signals each morning, and they were punished for drifting even when their watches were accurate. One operator's 1884 rulebook states that "the station clock, not the servant's watch, governs departure." Accurate watches were useful, the records suggest, but the coordination itself was kept in place by the telegraph-linked clock network.
g.question: Based on the texts, which part of the argument in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely dispute?
options: The claim that precision manufacturing in Switzerland was a hidden foundation of continental rail integration
The claim that Swiss watchmaking was concentrated in the Jura valleys during the 1870s and 1880s
The claim that European railways operated by different companies did eventually keep to shared schedules at junctions
The claim that railway staff each carrying a dependable watch was what allowed separate lines to keep to shared schedules
g.explanation:
정답 D: Text 1의 결론(스위스 정밀 제조가 철도 통합의 토대)은 '직원 개개인이 믿을 만한 시계를 갖게 된 것이 시간표 조정을 가능하게 했다'는 가정에 기대고 있다. Text 2는 회사 기록을 근거로, 조정을 실제로 유지한 것은 개인 시계가 아니라 전신으로 시각을 맞춘 역 시계였다고 보여 주므로 바로 이 가정을 겨냥한다.
A: 이것은 결론 자체다. Text 2는 결론이 기대는 근거를 약하게 만들 뿐 결론을 직접 다루지는 않으며, 정확한 시계가 '유용했다'는 점도 인정한다. 근거가 무너지면 결론이 흔들리는 것은 그 결과이지, Text 2가 겨냥하는 지점은 아니다.
B: 쥐라 계곡이라는 지역은 부수적인 세부 사항이고, Text 2는 이 부분을 전혀 다루지 않는다.
C: Text 2도 공유 시간표에 따른 조정이 실제로 이루어졌다고 전제한다(그 조정을 유지한 것이 무엇인지만 다르게 설명한다). 따라서 Text 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분이다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is D. Text 1 concludes that Swiss precision manufacturing was a foundation of rail integration. That conclusion depends on an assumption: that individual staff carrying dependable watches is what let separate lines keep shared schedules. Text 2's company records show the opposite. Staff watches were not trusted on their own, and the telegraph-linked station clocks actually kept the coordination in place. So Text 2 targets this assumption directly.
A is the conclusion itself. Text 2 weakens the reasoning behind it but never addresses it directly, and it even admits that accurate watches were useful.
B is a minor detail (where the watchmakers were located), and Text 2 never mentions it.
C is something Text 2 actually agrees with. It takes for granted that coordinated schedules existed and only explains differently what kept them in place.
g.design: Text 2 brings in rulebook evidence that weakens the link between individual watches and coordination. The correct answer is that underlying assumption. The wrong answers are the conclusion itself, a minor detail, and a point Text 2 shares. The question uses the general word "argument" so it does not echo the key terms of the correct answer.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1의 저자가 좋은 설명이나 해결책의 기준(예: 재현 가능성, 단순성, 장기적 효과)을 분명히 드러내게 쓰고, 텍스트 2는 그 기준과 어긋날 수 있는 결론을 내리게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 1의 저자의 기준에서 텍스트 2의 결론을 어떻게 평가할 것인가'로 한다. 오답 3개는 텍스트 2 저자의 기준으로 평가한 결과, 두 저자의 기준을 섞은 평가, 일반 상식에 따른 평가로 만든다.
c.seed: economics and business — Kenyan tea auction Mombasa and price discovery mechanism for smallholder farmer cooperative revenue

g.passage:
Text 1
Economists studying the Mombasa tea auction, where smallholder cooperatives sell leaf through brokers each week, often ask whether an alternative selling arrangement would "help farmers." Economist Wanjiru Kamau argues that such a claim is credible only if it is tested against what cooperatives earn over several seasons, including years when global prices fall. A gain that appears in a single good season, she contends, may simply reflect market conditions rather than the arrangement itself.

Text 2
In 2022, a group of cooperatives in Kenya's Kericho region bypassed the Mombasa auction and sold directly to a European blender under a fixed-price contract. That year, auction prices slumped, while the contract price held steady, and the cooperatives' revenue per kilogram rose roughly 18 percent above what neighboring auction-selling cooperatives received. Analysts who documented the deal concluded that direct contracts are a better route for smallholders than the auction.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Kamau (Text 1) most likely evaluate the analysts' conclusion in Text 2?
options: She would regard it as premature, since the evidence covers one season whose outcome may owe more to that year's falling auction prices than to the contract itself.
She would regard it as persuasive, since the evidence shows contract revenue exceeding auction revenue by a clear margin in a direct comparison.
She would regard it as partly supported, since the evidence includes a year of falling prices, though the margin of 18 percent seems too small to matter.
She would regard it as doubtful, since the evidence concerns a single European buyer, and buyers commonly abandon fixed-price contracts once they become costly.
g.explanation:
정답 A: Kamau의 기준은 하락기를 포함한 '여러 시즌'의 수입 비교이며, 한 시즌의 이득은 시장 상황 탓일 수 있다고 본다. Text 2는 2022년 한 해, 그것도 경매가가 폭락해 고정가 계약이 우연히 유리했던 해의 자료뿐이므로 Kamau는 결론을 성급하다고 볼 것이다.
B: Text 2 분석가들의 기준(한 해의 수입 차이)으로 평가한 것으로, Kamau의 다년 기준을 무시한다.
C: 두 기준을 섞은 평가. '하락기 포함'이라는 Kamau 기준의 일부만 충족된 것으로 보고, 지문에 없는 18%의 크기 문제를 끌어들였다. 다년 검증이라는 핵심 요건이 빠졌다.
D: 일반 상식(구매자의 계약 파기 가능성)에 기댄 평가로, Kamau가 제시한 기준과 무관하다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer A: Kamau's standard is that you have to compare earnings across several seasons, including years when prices drop, because a gain in one season may just reflect market conditions. Text 2 gives data for only 2022. That was a year when auction prices slumped, which made the fixed-price contract look good by circumstance. So she would call the conclusion premature.
B judges the conclusion by the analysts' own standard, a one-year revenue gap, and ignores Kamau's requirement for multiple seasons.
C mixes the two standards. It gives credit for the falling-price year, which is only part of Kamau's test, and adds a complaint about the size of the 18 percent margin that neither text raises. It misses her main requirement: evidence over several seasons.
D relies on general common sense about buyers backing out of contracts. That is not Kamau's stated standard.
g.design: Text 1에서 다년간·하락기 포함 검증이라는 평가 기준을 분명히 밝혔고, Text 2는 하락기 한 해의 자료만으로 결론을 내린다. 오답은 Text 2의 기준, 두 기준을 섞은 평가, 일반 상식에 따른 평가로 구성했다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Swarovski crystal cutting technology and fashion jewelry mass production Austrian firm innovation competitiveness

g.passage:
Text 1
Swarovski, the Austrian crystal company founded in 1895, became a leader in fashion jewelry largely because of one invention. Daniel Swarovski built an electric cutting machine that could facet glass crystals far faster and more precisely than workers cutting by hand. In this view, the machine alone explains why the firm was able to outcompete its rivals.

Text 2
Swarovski's cutting machine was certainly important, but machines can be copied. Business historians point out that the firm also stayed competitive by keeping its methods secret, working closely with fashion designers in Paris, and constantly developing new colors and coatings. Without these efforts, the cutting technology by itself would not have kept the company ahead for so long.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 about the reason for Swarovski's success?
options: By agreeing that the cutting machine was the only real factor behind the company's ability to beat its competitors
By arguing that the cutting machine mattered but that other business practices were also needed to explain the company's lasting success
By arguing that the cutting machine played no meaningful part in the company's rise in fashion jewelry
By arguing that the cutting machine mattered mostly because it allowed the company to stop working with fashion designers
g.explanation: Text 1은 절단 기계 하나만으로 Swarovski의 성공을 설명할 수 있다고 주장한다. Text 2는 기계가 "certainly important"하다고 인정하면서도 비밀 유지, 디자이너와의 협력, 신제품 개발이 함께 필요했다고 말하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 기계 "by itself"로는 부족하다고 한 점과 어긋난다. C는 Text 2가 기계의 중요성을 인정한 점을 무시한다. D는 Text 2가 디자이너와 긴밀히 협력했다고 한 내용과 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: Text 1 claims that the cutting machine alone explains Swarovski's success. Text 2 agrees the machine was "certainly important" but says secrecy, work with designers, and new product development were also needed, so B is correct. A doesn't work because Text 2 says the machine "by itself" was not enough. C ignores that Text 2 calls the machine important. D contradicts Text 2, which says the firm worked closely with fashion designers.
g.design: Easy: the answer hinges on one direct signal in Text 2 ("certainly important, but... by itself would not"), which shows partial agreement. The wrong answers are the typical mistakes: full agreement, full rejection, and a distortion of Text 2's details.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Swatch quartz watch mass production Switzerland and mechanical watchmaking industry disruption 1970s era

g.passage:
Text 1
In the 1970s, cheap quartz watches from Japan and Hong Kong flooded world markets. Many observers concluded that the Swiss watch industry, built on costly hand-assembled mechanical movements, had simply lost because its products were too old-fashioned for modern buyers.

Text 2
The Swiss industry did shrink sharply during the quartz era, but its recovery suggests the problem was not old-fashioned products alone. In 1983, Swiss firms launched the Swatch, a low-cost quartz watch made with far fewer parts on automated lines. Its success showed that Swiss makers could compete once they changed how watches were manufactured and priced, and the revenue helped preserve traditional mechanical brands.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the observers' conclusion described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that the Swiss industry recovered only after it stopped producing quartz watches altogether
By agreeing that Swiss watchmakers were right to keep relying on hand-assembled mechanical movements
By arguing that the conclusion overlooks how much Swiss success depended on manufacturing methods and pricing
By arguing that the conclusion exaggerates how much the Swiss watch industry shrank during the 1970s
g.explanation: Text 1의 관찰자들은 스위스 산업이 제품이 구식이라서 졌다고 결론짓는다. Text 2는 Swatch가 생산 방식과 가격을 바꾸자 경쟁력을 되찾았다고 하여, 문제가 제품의 구식성만이 아니었다고 반박하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 Swatch 자체가 쿼츠 시계이므로 틀리다. B는 Text 2가 수작업 기계식 의존이 아니라 자동화 생산을 성공 요인으로 보므로 틀리다. D는 Text 2가 산업이 크게 축소되었음을 인정하므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The observers in Text 1 conclude the Swiss lost because their products were old-fashioned. Text 2 says the Swatch succeeded once Swiss firms changed how watches were made and priced, so the problem wasn't just old-fashioned products. That makes C correct. A is wrong because the Swatch itself was a quartz watch. B is wrong because Text 2 credits automated production, not continued reliance on hand assembly. D is wrong because Text 2 admits the industry did shrink sharply.
g.design: Text 2가 Text 1의 결론에 명시적으로 '구식 제품만이 원인이 아니다'라고 반박하는 단일 단서로 풀리게 했고, 정답이 질문 표현과 겹치지 않도록 바꿔 썼다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Patek Philippe luxury watchmaking Swiss heritage and vertical integration manufacturing exclusivity market positioning

g.passage: Patek Philippe, the Geneva watchmaker founded in 1839, manufactures nearly every component of its timepieces in-house, from movements to cases. Industry analysts have long attributed the brand's premium prices to this vertical integration, arguing that controlling production lets the firm guarantee craftsmanship that buyers will pay extra for. Yet several rival Swiss firms are equally vertically integrated, producing their own movements and cases, and their watches typically resell on secondary markets for well below their original retail price. Patek Philippe watches, by contrast, often resell above retail. Notably, Patek Philippe deliberately limits annual output to a small number of watches, far fewer than demand would support, while those integrated rivals expand output as demand grows. Taken together, these observations suggest that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: vertical integration is the main reason Patek Philippe's watches keep their value, since few watchmakers outside Switzerland make their own movements.
rival Swiss firms could match Patek Philippe's resale values simply by producing more of their components in-house.
buyers of luxury watches care more about a watch's resale price than about the quality of its craftsmanship.
in-house production alone may not explain Patek Philippe's pricing power, which could depend partly on its deliberate restriction of supply.
g.explanation: 경쟁사들도 똑같이 수직 통합을 했는데 재판매 가치는 떨어지므로, 수직 통합만으로는 파텍 필립의 가격 프리미엄을 설명할 수 없다. 두 집단을 가르는 차이는 의도적인 생산량 제한이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 분석가들의 기존 주장을 되풀이할 뿐, 지문이 제시한 반증을 무시한다. B는 경쟁사들이 이미 수직 통합을 했다는 점과 모순된다. C는 구매자의 우선순위를 다루는데, 지문은 이를 판단할 근거를 주지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Rival Swiss firms are just as vertically integrated, yet their watches lose value on resale, so vertical integration alone can't explain Patek Philippe's premium. The difference the passage points to is that Patek Philippe deliberately limits how many watches it makes, which is why D is correct. A just repeats the analysts' original claim and ignores the counterevidence the passage gives. B contradicts the passage, because the rivals already make their own components in-house. C makes a claim about what buyers value most, and the passage offers no evidence to support it.
g.design: To answer, students have to combine two facts: rivals are equally integrated yet resell poorly, and only Patek limits supply. A and B both lean on vertical integration, which is partly supported by the passage, so they only fall apart when compared with the evidence about rivals.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Bordeaux wine classification 1855 and producer ranking prestige pricing hierarchical market segmentation system

g.passage: In 1855, Bordeaux wine brokers ranked the region's top châteaux into five tiers, or "growths," based largely on the prices their wines had fetched over previous decades. The ranking has been revised only once since then, yet a wine's tier still strongly predicts its price today. Economists debate why. One possibility is that the 1855 brokers simply identified estates with superior soils, which keep producing better wine. But economist Olivier Gergaud and colleagues noted that many classified châteaux have since bought neighboring vineyard land that was never part of the original ranked estate, and wine from these added parcels sells at the same premium as wine from the original vines. If such wines command the same price despite coming from unranked ground, this suggests that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the 1855 tier itself, rather than the specific land it originally described, accounts for at least part of the price premium.
the soils of the added parcels must be just as superior as those of the original vineyards, since buyers would otherwise pay less.
the 1855 brokers based their tiers on soil quality rather than on the prices that wines had previously fetched.
the classification should be revised more often so that the tiers reflect which châteaux now own the best vineyard land.
g.design: 두 정보(토양 우월성 가설 + 비등급 토지 와인도 동일 프리미엄)를 연결해 등급 명칭 자체의 효과를 추론하게 했다. B는 토양 가설을 그럴듯하게 유지하고, C는 지문 정보와 상충하며, D는 논증 밖 정책 제안이다.
g.explanation: 토양 우월성 가설이 맞다면 원래 등급에 포함되지 않은 땅에서 나온 와인은 같은 프리미엄을 받지 못해야 한다. 그런데 실제로는 같은 가격을 받으므로, 가격의 적어도 일부는 땅이 아니라 등급 자체에서 나온다고 보는 A가 정답이다. B는 토양 가설을 살리려 하지만, 새로 산 땅이 더 좋다는 근거는 지문에 없고 증거가 가리키는 방향과도 반대된다. C는 브로커들이 과거 가격을 기준으로 등급을 매겼다는 지문 내용과 어긋난다. D는 정책 제안일 뿐, 이 증거가 무엇을 시사하는지에 대한 결론이 아니다.
g.explanation_en: If superior soil explained the premium, wine from land outside the original ranked estate shouldn't sell at the same price. But it does, so A is correct: at least part of the premium comes from the tier itself, not the land. B tries to rescue the soil explanation, but nothing in the passage says the added parcels have equally good soil, and the evidence actually points the other way. C contradicts the passage, which says the brokers ranked the châteaux mainly by past prices. D is a policy recommendation, not a conclusion about what this evidence suggests.

c.seed: economics and business — Moroccan argan oil cooperative production and fair trade certification premium pricing smallholder women farmer networks

g.passage:
Text 1
Fair trade certification has transformed argan oil production in southwestern Morocco. Women who once sold raw argan kernels to middlemen for very little now belong to certified cooperatives that press and bottle the oil themselves. Because certified oil sells at a premium in European and North American markets, the cooperatives argue that certification gives these women a reliable route to higher household incomes.

Text 2
Researchers who tracked several certified argan cooperatives found that retail prices did rise sharply after certification, but members' earnings grew far less. Much of the premium went to exporters and cosmetics brands, and some cooperatives paid members by the hour for kernel cracking rather than sharing profits. Certification raised what consumers paid; whether it raised what the women took home depended on how each cooperative divided its revenue.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the cooperatives' argument described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that certification lifts members' incomes, since the evidence shows certified oil sells for more than uncertified oil
By noting that a higher selling price for certified oil does not by itself ensure that the women producing it earn more
By arguing that certification lowered the retail price of argan oil, which cut into the earnings of cooperative members
By claiming that the women would earn more by going back to selling raw kernels to middlemen than by staying in cooperatives
g.explanation: Text 1의 협동조합은 인증 오일이 프리미엄 가격에 팔리므로 여성들의 소득이 오른다고 주장한다. Text 2는 소매가는 크게 올랐지만 조합원 소득 증가는 훨씬 작았고, 이는 수익 배분 방식에 달려 있었다고 말하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 가격 상승이라는 부분적 사실만 근거로 Text 2가 의문을 제기한 결론에 동의하는 것이라 틀렸다. C는 Text 2에서 가격이 '올랐다'고 했으므로 맞지 않는다. D는 원료 판매로 돌아가는 것이 낫다는 주장인데 Text 2는 그런 비교를 하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: In Text 1, the cooperatives argue that because certified oil sells at a premium, certification raises the women's incomes. Text 2 reports that retail prices did rise sharply but members' earnings grew much less, and that the result depended on how revenue was divided, so B is correct. A takes one true detail, the higher price, and uses it to accept the very conclusion Text 2 questions. C is wrong because Text 2 says retail prices rose, not fell. D goes too far: Text 2 never says going back to selling raw kernels would pay better.
g.design: To answer, students have to link Text 1's claim that a higher price means higher income with Text 2's finding that price and earnings drifted apart. A uses the real price rise to tempt students, while C and D misread or stretch Text 2.

c.seed: economics and business — Fairtrade coffee certification premium pricing and smallholder farmer cooperative revenue distribution Latin America

g.passage:
Text 1
Economists who study Fairtrade coffee in Latin America often point to the certification's guaranteed minimum price and its additional social premium as clear gains for smallholders. Because certified cooperatives can sell beans above volatile market rates, the researchers argue, member farmers reliably receive higher incomes than comparable uncertified growers.

Text 2
In a multiyear study of cooperatives in Nicaragua and Peru, economist Lucía Barrantes found that cooperatives did secure higher prices for the certified beans they sold. However, most cooperatives could sell only a fraction of their certified harvest on Fairtrade terms, selling the rest at ordinary prices, and much of the premium went to certification fees and cooperative administration. As a result, the extra money reaching individual farmers' households was often small and uneven from year to year.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Barrantes (Text 2) most likely respond to the economists' conclusion in Text 1?
options: She would argue that the conclusion is mistaken because certified cooperatives in her study generally received lower prices than uncertified growers did.
She would argue that the conclusion is sound because the premium Fairtrade buyers pay is passed directly to member farmers.
She would argue that the conclusion overlooks how the higher prices cooperatives obtain are diluted before they translate into household earnings.
She would argue that the conclusion applies to Peru but not to Nicaragua, where cooperatives sold none of their harvest on Fairtrade terms.
g.explanation: Text 1은 높은 가격이 곧 농민의 확실한 소득 증가로 이어진다고 결론짓는다. Barrantes는 협동조합이 높은 가격을 받은 사실은 인정하지만, 인증 물량 중 일부만 공정무역 조건으로 팔리고 프리미엄이 수수료와 운영비로 빠져나가 가계에 닿는 몫이 작다고 지적하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 협동조합이 더 높은 가격을 받았다고 인정한 점과 모순된다. B는 프리미엄이 수수료와 운영비로 쓰였다는 내용과 반대이다. D는 국가별 차이나 니카라과에서 전혀 팔지 못했다는 내용이 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: Text 1 concludes that higher certified prices reliably mean higher incomes for member farmers. Barrantes agrees that cooperatives got higher prices, but she shows that only part of the harvest sold on Fairtrade terms and that fees and administration used up much of the premium, so households gained little. That makes C correct. A contradicts her finding that cooperatives did get higher prices. B is the opposite of what she found, since the premium went largely to fees and administration. D makes up a difference between the two countries, and Text 2 never says Nicaraguan cooperatives sold none of their harvest on Fairtrade terms.
g.design: To answer, you have to connect two facts: Text 2 admits prices were higher, and it also shows where that money leaked away before reaching farmers. A pulls in skimmers who think "Text 2 disagrees" and stop there. B appeals to readers who notice the agreement about higher prices but miss the rest.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 두 문장 사이 관계(대조·추가·결과·예시)가 명시적 어휘 단서로 분명한 문제. 선택지는 서로 다른 관계를 나타내는 전환어 4개.
c.seed: life science — Hagfish slime production and protein fiber gel defense mechanism against predatory shark attacks

g.passage: When a shark bites a hagfish, the hagfish releases a small amount of slime from glands along its body. Within a fraction of a second, threads of protein in the slime absorb seawater and expand into a thick gel. ______ the shark's mouth and gills quickly fill with the sticky gel, and the predator usually lets go and swims away, gagging.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.design: 앞 문장(점액이 젤로 팽창)이 원인, 뒤 문장(상어 입·아가미가 막혀 놓아줌)이 결과라는 한 단계 인과관계만 파악하면 풀 수 있게 했다. 오답은 예시·대조·추가 관계를 나타내는 흔히 헷갈리는 전환어로 구성했다.
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 점액 속 단백질 실이 바닷물을 흡수해 두꺼운 젤로 팽창한다고 설명하고, 뒤 문장은 그 젤 때문에 상어의 입과 아가미가 막혀 상어가 물러난다고 말한다. 이는 원인과 결과 관계이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 앞 내용의 구체적 사례를 들 때 쓰지만, 뒤 문장은 젤 팽창의 사례가 아니라 그 결과이다. B는 대조를 나타내지만 두 문장은 서로 대립하지 않는다. C는 별개의 정보를 덧붙일 때 쓰므로 뒤 문장이 앞 문장에서 비롯된다는 점을 나타내지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The earlier sentence explains that protein threads in the slime soak up seawater and swell into a thick gel. The next sentence tells you that this gel fills the shark's mouth and gills, so the shark lets go. That is a cause-and-effect relationship, so D is correct. A is used to give a specific instance of the previous idea, but the shark's reaction is a consequence of the gel forming, not an example of it. B signals contrast, and the two sentences don't oppose each other. C just adds a separate fact, so it doesn't show that the shark's reaction is caused by the gel.

c.seed: life science — Vampire bat saliva anticoagulant peptides and host blood feeding physiological adaptation mechanisms

g.passage: Common vampire bats feed only on blood, and they must drink for up to thirty minutes from a single small bite. Normally, blood begins to clot within minutes of a wound, which would stop the flow long before the bat finished its meal. ______ the bat's saliva contains a protein called draculin, which blocks key clotting factors and keeps the blood flowing freely from the bite.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 피가 보통 몇 분 안에 굳어 흡혈이 끝나기 전에 흐름이 멈출 것이라고 말하고, 뒷 문장은 박쥐 침의 단백질이 응고를 막아 피가 계속 흐르게 한다고 말한다. 예상되는 문제와 그것을 막는 사실이 서로 대조되므로 대조를 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 비슷한 내용을 덧붙일 때 쓰는 말인데, 두 문장은 비슷하지 않고 서로 반대된다. C는 앞 내용의 예를 들 때 쓰는데, 침의 단백질은 피가 굳는 현상의 예가 아니다. D는 결과를 나타내는데, 피가 굳는다고 해서 침에 항응고 단백질이 생기는 것은 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence says blood normally clots within minutes, which would stop the flow before the bat finished feeding. The next sentence says the bat's saliva blocks clotting and keeps the blood flowing. These two ideas contrast: one describes an expected problem, and the other shows how that problem is overcome, so A is correct. B is used to add a similar idea, but these two sentences point in opposite directions. C introduces an example, but the saliva protein isn't an example of blood clotting. D shows a result, but blood clotting doesn't cause the saliva to contain an anticoagulant.
g.design: 'Normally... would stop'라는 명시적 단서로 대조 관계 하나만 파악하면 풀리게 했고, 오답은 추가·예시·결과를 나타내는 대표적 전환어로 구성했다.

c.seed: life science — Platyfish live-bearing reproductive strategy and male sexual coercion behavioral ecology adaptation

g.passage: Female platyfish do not lay eggs; instead, they carry fertilized eggs inside their bodies and give birth to live, free-swimming young. This strategy protects developing offspring from predators that might otherwise eat unguarded eggs. Males of the species, however, often try to mate with females that have not chosen them, chasing and nipping at them repeatedly. Researchers have found that females respond by staying close to other fish or hiding among plants. ______ these behaviors reduce how often unwanted males can reach them.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 암컷이 다른 물고기 곁에 머물거나 식물 사이에 숨는다고 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 이 행동 때문에 원치 않는 수컷의 접근이 줄어든다는 결과를 제시한다. 따라서 원인-결과를 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A는 대조를 나타내지만 두 문장은 서로 반대되지 않는다. C는 예시를 나타내지만 뒤 문장은 앞 행동의 사례가 아니라 그 효과이다. D는 유사한 내용을 추가할 때 쓰는데, 뒤 문장은 비슷한 다른 사실이 아니라 결과이다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence says females stay near other fish or hide among plants, and the sentence after the blank tells you what these behaviors lead to: fewer unwanted males reach them. That is a cause-and-effect relationship, so B is correct. A signals a contrast, but the two sentences don't oppose each other. C introduces an example, but the second sentence describes an effect of the behaviors, not an instance of them. D adds a similar point, but the second sentence is a consequence, not a parallel fact.
g.design: "these behaviors reduce"라는 명시적 단서로 앞 행동과 그 효과의 인과 관계가 바로 드러나며, 오답은 대조·예시·유사의 전형적 전환어로 구성했다.

c.seed: life science — Lungfish estivation dormancy and metabolic rate suppression during seasonal drought conditions

g.passage: When the ponds and rivers they live in dry up during seasonal droughts, African lungfish burrow into the mud and enter a dormant state called estivation. Encased in a cocoon of hardened mucus, the fish breathe air and greatly ______ their metabolic rate, using energy so slowly that they can survive for months, or even years, without food or water until the rains return.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 빈칸 바로 뒤에 폐어가 에너지를 아주 천천히 써서 먹이와 물 없이 몇 달을 버틴다고 나오므로, 빈칸에는 대사율을 '낮추다'라는 뜻의 단어가 들어가야 하고 C가 정답이다. A는 '빠르게 하다'라는 뜻이라 에너지를 천천히 쓴다는 내용과 정반대이다. B는 '드러내 보이다'라는 뜻이라 대사율이 어떻게 달라지는지를 전혀 말해 주지 않는다. D는 '원래대로 되돌리다'라는 뜻인데, 이는 휴면 중이 아니라 비가 다시 온 뒤에 일어날 일이다.

When their surroundings lose water, they curl into a compact shape and enter a state called anhydrobiosis, in which their metabolism nearly stops. In this state, a tardigrade can remain ______ for years, showing no visible signs of life, and then become active again within hours of being placed back in water.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 탈수 상태에서 대사가 거의 멈추고 '눈에 보이는 생명의 징후가 없다'고 직접 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 활동하지 않고 휴면 중이라는 뜻의 D가 와야 합니다. A는 '활기찬'이라는 뜻으로 대사가 멈춘 상태와 정반대입니다. B는 '투명한'이라는 뜻의 외형 묘사일 뿐, 활동이 멈춘 상태를 나타내지 못합니다. C는 '공격적인'이라는 뜻으로 행동이 활발하다는 의미를 담고 있어 생명 징후가 없다는 설명과 모순됩니다.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 "eyes"이고, "of a mantis shrimp"는 주어를 꾸미는 짧은 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 복수 동사가 필요하므로 A가 정답이다. B, C, D는 모두 단수 동사(contains, is, has)여서 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "shrimp"를 주어로 착각하게 만드는 오답이다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "eyes." The phrase "of a mantis shrimp" just modifies the subject. Since the subject is plural, the sentence needs a plural verb, so A is correct. B, C, and D all use singular verb forms (contains, is, has). They would only work if the singular noun "shrimp," which sits right before the blank, were the subject, and it isn't.
g.design: 짧은 전치사구 수식어가 끼어든 주어-동사 수 일치 하나만 묻도록 구성했고, 오답은 모두 근접 명사에 맞춘 단수형으로 만들었다.

g.passage: Each winter, the wood frog of North America survives being partly frozen solid. As ice begins to form on its skin, the liver of the frog ______ large amounts of glucose into the bloodstream. This sugar then collects inside the frog's cells, where it helps keep them from freezing and bursting.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 짧은 전치사구(of the frog)가 단수 주어 liver와 동사 사이에 끼어 있는 주어-동사 수 일치 한 가지 규칙만 묻는다. 오답은 모두 frog 또는 복수형에 끌린 복수 동사이다.
g.explanation: 정답은 B이다. 빈칸 동사의 주어는 단수 명사 'the liver'이고, 'of the frog'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이므로 단수 동사 'releases'가 필요하다. 앞 문장의 현재 시제와도 일치한다. A, C, D는 모두 복수 주어에 쓰는 동사형이라 단수 주어 liver와 수가 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The correct answer is B. The subject of the blank is the singular noun "the liver." The phrase "of the frog" only describes the liver, so the sentence needs the singular verb "releases." This verb also fits the present tense used in the rest of the text. Choices A, C, and D are all plural verb forms, so they don't agree with the singular subject "liver."

g.explanation: 빈칸 동사의 주어는 복수 명사 "loops"이다. 그 사이의 수식어 "in the tiny tubes of each kidney"는 주어가 아니다. 따라서 복수 동사 C "pull"이 맞다. A "pulls", B "is pulling", D "has pulled"는 모두 단수 동사여서, 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "kidney"를 주어로 착각할 때 고르게 되는 오답이다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the blank is the plural noun "loops." The phrase "in the tiny tubes of each kidney" only describes the loops, so it isn't the subject. That means the verb has to be plural, and C, "pull," is correct. A ("pulls"), B ("is pulling"), and D ("has pulled") are all singular verbs. They're tempting only if you mistake the nearby singular noun "kidney" for the subject.

c.seed: life science — Archerfish trajectory prediction and refraction compensation for hunting submerged prey underwater

g.passage: Archerfish hunt by spitting jets of water at insects resting on leaves above the surface. Because light bends as it passes from air into water, an insect seen from below is not located exactly where it appears to be. Biologist Mara Lindqvist hypothesizes that archerfish learn to correct for this bending of light through practice, rather than being born with the ability. In her view, a young archerfish's aim should improve only after it has had many chances to shoot at targets.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Lindqvist's hypothesis?
options: Young archerfish raised in tanks hit targets above the water as accurately on their first attempts as adult archerfish do.
Adult archerfish in the wild hit insects more often on sunny days than on cloudy days.
Archerfish shoot larger jets of water at heavy insects than at light insects.
Young archerfish miss most targets at first, but their hit rate rises steadily as they gain more shooting attempts.
g.explanation: Lindqvist의 가설은 물고기가 연습을 통해 빛의 굴절을 보정하는 법을 배우므로, 어린 물고기의 조준은 여러 번 쏴 본 뒤에야 좋아진다는 것이다. D는 처음에는 대부분 빗나가다가 시도가 쌓일수록 명중률이 높아진다고 하므로 가설을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 어린 물고기가 처음부터 정확하다는 내용이라 타고난 능력을 시사하므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다. B는 날씨에 관한 것이고, C는 물줄기의 크기에 관한 것이어서 둘 다 연습을 통한 학습과는 관계가 없다.
g.explanation_en: Lindqvist's hypothesis is that archerfish learn through practice to correct for the bending of light, so a young fish's aim should improve only after many tries. D says young fish miss most targets at first and then hit more often as they get more attempts, so it directly supports the hypothesis. A says young fish are accurate right away, which points to an ability they're born with, so it actually weakens the hypothesis. B is about the weather, and C is about how big the jets are. Neither one has anything to do with learning through practice.
g.design: 쉬운 문항이다. 가설(연습할수록 정확도가 오른다)과 발견을 한 번만 맞춰 보면 풀린다. 오답은 A가 반대 방향의 증거이고, B와 C는 주제는 같지만 가설과 무관한 내용이다. 네 선택지 모두 같은 문장 틀로 썼다.

c.seed: life science — Desert pupfish osmoregulation and hypersaline aquifer adaptation in Death Valley isolated populations

g.passage: Pupfish living in isolated springs and pools in Death Valley face water that can be several times saltier than the ocean. Because salt constantly pulls water out of their bodies, the fish must work to keep their internal fluids balanced, a process called osmoregulation. Biologist Rosa Delgado hypothesizes that pupfish populations in the saltiest pools have evolved more efficient salt-removing cells in their gills than populations living in nearly fresh springs.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Delgado's hypothesis?
options: Pupfish from the saltiest pools, when raised in the same water as pupfish from nearly fresh springs, still pump excess salt out through their gills faster.
Pupfish from the saltiest pools, when observed in the wild, spend more of the day resting near the bottom than pupfish from nearly fresh springs.
Pupfish from the saltiest pools, when measured as adults, are on average slightly smaller in body length than pupfish from nearly fresh springs.
Pupfish from the saltiest pools, when surveyed over several years, live in water whose temperature changes more from season to season than pupfish from nearly fresh springs.
g.explanation: 델가도의 가설은 염도가 가장 높은 웅덩이의 개체군이 아가미의 염분 제거 기능을 더 효율적으로 진화시켰다는 것이다. A는 같은 물에서 키웠는데도 이 물고기들이 아가미로 염분을 더 빨리 내보낸다는 내용이므로 가설을 직접 뒷받침한다. B는 행동 차이에 관한 것일 뿐 아가미 기능과는 관련이 없다. C는 몸 크기에 관한 것이고, D는 염도가 아니라 수온에 관한 것이므로 둘 다 염분 제거 효율을 다루지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Delgado's hypothesis is that pupfish from the saltiest pools have evolved gill cells that get rid of salt more efficiently. Choice A shows that these fish still remove salt through their gills faster even when they're raised in the same water as the other fish, so it directly supports the hypothesis. Choice B is about resting behavior, not how well the gills work. Choice C is about body size, and Choice D is about water temperature instead of salt, so neither one tells you anything about how efficiently the fish remove salt.
g.design: 정답을 고르는 데 필요한 규칙은 하나뿐이다. 가설에 나온 특성인 아가미의 염분 제거 효율을 직접 보여 주는 발견을 고르면 된다. 오답은 모두 같은 문장 틀을 따르며, 사막 물고기에게 그럴듯해 보이지만 가설과 관련 없는 차이(행동, 크기, 수온)를 제시한다.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Hippopotamuses spend much of the day in rivers and lakes but leave the water to graze at night.
- Their skin releases a thick, oily fluid that starts out colorless and turns reddish brown within minutes.
- In 2004, chemist Yoko Saikawa and her team analyzed this fluid.
- They found two pigments in it, which they named hipposudoric acid and norhipposudoric acid.
- These pigments absorb ultraviolet light, which protects the animal's skin from sunburn.
- Adult hippos can weigh more than 1,500 kilograms.
g.question: The student wants to explain how a substance produced by hippos benefits their skin. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Hippos release a thick, oily fluid from their skin, and adults of the species can weigh more than 1,500 kilograms.
Hippos release a skin fluid containing pigments that absorb ultraviolet light, shielding the animals from sunburn.
Hippos release a thick, oily fluid from their skin that was analyzed in 2004 by chemist Yoko Saikawa and her team.
Hippos release a thick, oily fluid from their skin, though they leave the water to graze only at night.
g.explanation: 목표는 하마가 만드는 물질이 피부에 어떤 이점을 주는지 설명하는 것이다. B는 분비액 속 색소가 자외선을 흡수해 햇볕 화상을 막는다고 하여 이점을 직접 제시한다. A는 몸무게라는 무관한 정보를 덧붙인다. C는 누가 언제 분석했는지만 말하고 이점은 언급하지 않는다. D는 야간 섭식 습관을 말할 뿐 피부 보호와 관련이 없다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain how a substance hippos produce benefits their skin. B does this directly: it says the fluid contains pigments that absorb ultraviolet light and protect against sunburn. A adds the hippo's body weight, which has nothing to do with skin. C says who analyzed the fluid and when, but it never states a benefit. D mentions grazing at night, which does not explain how the skin is protected.
g.design: 이 문항은 목표에 맞는 메모 하나(자외선 흡수)만 찾으면 풀리는 easy 문항이다. 네 선택지 모두 분비액으로 시작하는 같은 문장 틀을 쓰고, 오답에는 각각 무관한 메모(몸무게, 분석자, 야간 섭식)를 붙였다.

- 세부 기술 힌트: 목표가 메모 1~2개와 직접 대응하는 문제(예: 한 대상 소개). 오답은 목표와 무관한 메모나 부정확한 진술.
c.seed: life science — Olm salamander transparent skull and eye degeneration in subterranean cave ecosystem adaptation

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The olm (Proteus anguinus) is a salamander that lives in underground caves in southeastern Europe.
- These caves are completely dark.
- Young olms are born with small eyes, but the eyes stop developing and become covered by skin as the animals grow.
- Adult olms cannot see, but they can sense light through their skin.
- Olms can live for more than 100 years.
g.question: The student wants to explain how the olm's eyes change over its lifetime. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The olm, a salamander found in southeastern Europe, lives in underground caves that are completely dark.
The olm can live for more than 100 years, much longer than many other salamanders.
Although olms begin life with small eyes, those eyes stop developing and become covered by skin as the animals mature.
Adult olms can sense light through their skin, even though they live in caves that are completely dark.
g.design: 목표가 눈의 변화를 다룬 메모 하나와 직접 대응하며, 오답은 서식지·수명·피부 감광 등 다른 메모를 활용해 같은 진술문 형식으로 구성했다.
g.explanation: 목표는 올름의 눈이 일생 동안 어떻게 변하는지 설명하는 것이다. C는 어릴 때 작은 눈이 있다가 자라면서 발달이 멈추고 피부로 덮인다는 변화 과정을 보여 주므로 정답이다. A는 서식지만 소개할 뿐 눈의 변화는 언급하지 않는다. B는 수명에 관한 내용이라 목표와 무관하다. D는 성체의 피부 감광 능력만 말하고 눈이 어떻게 변하는지는 설명하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain how the olm's eyes change over its lifetime. C works because it describes the change: olms start with small eyes, and as they grow, the eyes stop developing and get covered by skin. A only describes where olms live and says nothing about their eyes. B is about lifespan, which has nothing to do with the goal. D talks about adults sensing light through their skin, but it doesn't explain how the eyes change.
