- 세부 기술 힌트: 독립절 두 개 사이의 쉼표 스플라이스·접속사 유무, 또는 문장 끝 마침표·세미콜론 선택처럼 절 경계가 한눈에 보이는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: life science — Hummingbird hovering flight and rapid wing rotation generating lift on forward and backward strokes

g.passage: Most birds produce lift mainly on the downstroke, when their wings push down against the air. Hummingbirds are different. As they hover in front of a flower, they rotate their wings sharply at the end of each stroke, turning the wing's upper surface to face downward on the return. This rotation lets the wings generate lift on both the forward and the backward ______ hummingbird can stay almost perfectly still in midair while it feeds.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: strokes, and as a result a
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "This rotation lets ... strokes"와 빈칸 뒤 "a hummingbird can stay ... feeds"는 각각 독립절이다. D는 마침표로 두 절을 나누고, 새 문장 앞에 "As a result,"를 붙여 연결하므로 올바르다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. C는 "and" 뒤의 "as a result"가 문장 중간에 삽입된 연결어인데 뒤에 쉼표가 없어서, 두 번째 절의 주어 "a"와 바로 붙어 버린다. 따라서 표준 문장부호 규칙에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("This rotation lets ... strokes") and the text after it ("a hummingbird can stay ... feeds") are both independent clauses. D is correct because it ends the first clause with a period and starts a new sentence with "As a result," which links the two ideas. A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, so it creates a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between them at all, so it creates a run-on sentence. C has "as a result" as an interrupting transition after "and," but there's no comma after it, so the phrase runs straight into the subject "a." That breaks standard punctuation conventions.
g.design: 독립절 두 개의 경계만 판단하면 되는 easy 문항으로 구성했다. 오답에는 쉼표 스플라이스, 무종지문, 삽입 연결어 뒤 쉼표 누락이라는 전형적 오류를 넣었다.

c.seed: life science — Giraffe cardiovascular system and blood pressure regulation preventing cerebral edema from height differential

g.passage: A giraffe's heart must pump blood about two meters upward to reach the brain, so the animal's blood pressure is roughly twice that of a human. When a giraffe lowers its head to drink, however, that pressure could flood the brain with too much blood. A network of small, elastic vessels at the base of the skull absorbs the sudden ______ valves in the neck veins also keep blood from rushing back toward the head.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 양쪽이 모두 완전한 독립절이라 '쉼표+등위접속사' 규칙 하나만 알면 풀리는 easy 문항으로 만들었다. 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스, 런온, 접속사 뒤에 쉼표를 잘못 찍은 형태처럼 흔히 하는 실수로 구성했다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'A network ... absorbs the sudden surge'와 빈칸 뒤 'valves in the neck veins also keep blood...'는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 독립절 두 개는 쉼표와 등위접속사로 연결할 수 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문장부호도 접속사도 없어 런온 문장이 된다. D는 접속사 뒤에 쉼표를 찍어 문장부호 위치가 잘못되었다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("A network ... absorbs the sudden surge") and the text after it ("valves in the neck veins also keep blood...") are both independent clauses, since each has its own subject and verb. You can join two independent clauses with a comma followed by a coordinating conjunction, so A is correct. B uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C has no punctuation or conjunction at all, so it makes a run-on sentence. D puts the comma after "and" instead of before it, so the punctuation is in the wrong place.

c.seed: life science — Stoat seasonal coat color change and photoperiod-triggered molt from brown to white winter pelage

g.passage: In northern regions, the stoat changes its appearance as the seasons shift. Each autumn, shortening daylight triggers a molt in which the animal's brown summer fur is gradually replaced by a thick white ______ this winter pelage helps the stoat blend in with snow while it hunts voles and other small prey.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Each autumn ... a thick white coat"와 빈칸 뒤 "this winter pelage helps ... prey"는 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 접속사 없이 연결할 때는 세미콜론을 쓰므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 and와 뒤 절의 주어 사이를 잘못 끊는다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("Each autumn ... a thick white coat") form an independent clause, and so do the words after it ("this winter pelage helps ... prey"). When you join two independent clauses without a conjunction, you need a semicolon, so B is correct. A links the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between them at all, so you get a run-on sentence. D adds a comma after "and" that doesn't belong there, because it cuts the conjunction off from the clause it introduces.
g.design: 독립절 두 개의 경계가 분명히 보이게 쓰고, 쉼표 스플라이스, 무종지문, 잘못된 쉼표 배치를 전형적인 오답으로 넣어 세미콜론 규칙 하나만 알면 풀 수 있게 했다.

c.seed: life science — Mudskipper amphibious locomotion and terrestrial respiration through skin water film retention behavior

g.passage: Mudskippers, fish that spend much of their lives out of water on tidal mudflats, face a basic problem on land: their gills tend to collapse when exposed to air. To compensate, the fish periodically roll in shallow puddles, and a thin film of water retained on the skin and inside their enlarged gill chambers ______ them to keep absorbing oxygen as they hop across the mud on their muscular pectoral fins.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞의 복수 명사 'chambers'가 오답 유인이고, 실제 주어는 단수 'film'이다. 따라서 정동사가 필요한지와 주어-동사 일치를 함께 판단해야 한다.
g.explanation: 두 번째 절의 주어는 'a thin film of water'이고, 'retained on the skin and inside their enlarged gill chambers'는 이 주어를 꾸미는 수식어구일 뿐이다. 이 절에는 정동사가 필요하고, 단수 주어 'film'에 맞는 단수 동사 C가 정답이다. A는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'chambers'에 맞춘 형태라서 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다. B와 D는 분사 형태라 정동사 역할을 할 수 없으므로, 'and' 뒤의 절이 동사 없는 불완전한 절이 된다.
g.explanation_en: In the second clause, the subject is "a thin film of water." The phrase "retained on the skin and inside their enlarged gill chambers" only describes that subject. This clause needs a main verb, and that verb must be singular to agree with "film," so C is correct. A is a main verb, but it's plural. It matches the nearby noun "chambers" instead of the real subject. B and D are participles, not main verbs, so either one would leave the clause after "and" without a verb.

c.seed: life science — Basilisk lizard bipedal running and surface tension exploitation for water striding across ponds

g.passage: Biologists filming the green basilisk (Basiliscus plumifrons) with high-speed cameras have shown that the lizard's ability to sprint upright across the surface of a pond, a feat most often performed by juveniles weighing only a few grams, ______ less on surface tension than on a rapid slap-and-stroke motion of its fringed hind feet, which traps a brief pocket of air beneath each step.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: The singular subject "ability" is separated from the blank by a prepositional phrase and an appositive containing the plural nouns "juveniles" and "grams," which tempt readers to choose a plural verb. All four options use the same verb, so the student has to find the true subject to answer.
g.explanation: 이 절의 주어는 단수 명사 "ability"이며, "to sprint ... pond"와 동격구 "a feat ... grams"는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 동사가 필요하고, 과학적 사실을 현재 시제로 설명하므로 D(depends)가 정답이다. A는 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "grams"나 "juveniles"에 맞춘 복수형이라서 틀렸다. B와 C도 각각 have, are를 쓴 복수형이어서 단수 주어 "ability"와 수가 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this clause is the singular noun "ability." The phrase "to sprint ... pond" and the appositive "a feat ... grams" are modifiers that come between the subject and the verb. That means you need a singular verb, and since the passage describes a scientific fact in the present tense, D ("depends") is correct. A is plural because it matches the nearby nouns "grams" or "juveniles," not the real subject. B and C are also plural because they use "have" and "are," so they don't agree with the singular subject "ability."

c.seed: life science — Pangolin scale structure and keratin composition providing predator defense against aggressive attacks

g.passage: Pangolins are the only mammals covered almost entirely in overlapping scales. Made of keratin, the same protein found in human fingernails, the scales of a threatened pangolin ______ into a tight ball, presenting predators such as lions with an armored surface that their teeth and claws can rarely penetrate.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: lock together as the animal curls
locks together as the animal curls
locking together as the animal curls
to lock together as the animal curls
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "pangolin"이 아니라 복수 명사 "the scales"이므로 정동사도 복수형이어야 한다. 또한 "Made of keratin"이라는 수식어가 꾸미는 대상은 비늘이므로 주어를 "the scales"로 둔 구조가 맞다. A는 복수 정동사 "lock"을 써서 주어와 수가 일치하고 문장도 완성되므로 정답이다. B는 정동사이긴 하지만 가까이 있는 "pangolin"에 맞춘 단수형이라 주어 "scales"와 수가 맞지 않는다. C의 분사 "locking"과 D의 부정사 "to lock"은 정동사가 아니어서 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "the scales," not the singular noun "pangolin" that comes right before the blank, so the main verb has to be plural. The opening modifier "Made of keratin" also describes the scales, which confirms that "the scales" is the subject. A uses the plural finite verb "lock," so it agrees with the subject and completes the sentence, which makes it the correct answer. B is a finite verb, but its singular form matches the nearby "pangolin" instead of the actual subject, "scales." C uses the participle "locking" and D uses the infinitive "to lock," and since neither is a finite verb, the sentence would be left without a main verb.
g.design: 긴 수식어와 단수 명사 "pangolin"을 주어와 동사 사이에 두어 수 일치를 헷갈리게 했다. 동시에 정동사인지 아닌지(분사, 부정사)도 판단해야 하는 두 단계 문제로 만들었다.

c.seed: life science — Porcupine quill detachment mechanism and barbed tip geometry facilitating wound penetration and retention

g.passage: Biomedical engineer Woo Kyung Cho and colleagues found that the quills of the North American porcupine, each of which is tipped with hundreds of microscopic backward-facing barbs, ______ into tissue with roughly half the force required for barbless quills of similar size. The same barbs then make the quills difficult to remove, a combination that has inspired designs for surgical staples.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸은 that절의 주어 'the quills'에 대한 정동사 자리이며, 사이의 'each of which ... barbs'는 삽입된 관계절이다. 주어가 복수이므로 복수 정동사가 필요하고, B가 이를 충족한다. A는 정동사이지만 삽입절의 'each'나 'barbs' 근처 단수 표현에 끌린 단수형이라 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C와 D는 분사 형태여서 that절에 정동사가 없게 되므로 문장이 불완전하다.
g.explanation_en: The blank needs the main verb of the that-clause, whose subject is "the quills"; the phrase "each of which ... barbs" is just an interrupting relative clause. Since the subject is plural, it needs a plural finite verb, and B is the one that works. A is a finite verb, but it's singular, probably because "each" inside the interrupting clause pulls you toward it, so it doesn't agree with "quills." C and D are participles, which would leave the that-clause with no main verb at all and make the sentence incomplete.
g.design: 긴 삽입 관계절(each of which...)로 주어와 동사를 분리해 단수 유인(A)을 만들고, 분사형 오답(C, D)으로 정동사 필요 여부까지 판단하게 하는 두 단계 구조.

c.seed: life science — Seahorse prehensile tail and antagonistic muscle arrangement enabling precise grasping of seagrass holdfasts

g.passage: Unlike most fish, seahorses anchor themselves to seagrass by wrapping their tails around the plants' holdfasts. Biomechanists studying the tail have found that its square cross-section resists twisting, but grip strength depends on something else: the arrangement of paired muscle bundles running along opposite sides of each bony tail segment ______ the animal to tighten or loosen its hold with remarkable precision as currents shift.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 콜론 뒤 절의 주어는 단수 명사 'the arrangement'이며, 'of paired muscle bundles running along ... segment'는 수식어구일 뿐이다. 따라서 이 절에는 단수 정동사가 필요하고, 지문이 현재시제로 서술되므로 C(allows)가 정답이다. A는 정동사이지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사(bundles, segment 주변의 복수 표현)에 끌린 복수형이라 주어와 일치하지 않는다. B와 D는 분사 형태라서 콜론 뒤 절에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 문장이 되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: After the colon, the subject of the clause is the singular noun "the arrangement"; the phrase "of paired muscle bundles running along ... each bony tail segment" only modifies it. So the clause needs a singular finite verb, and since the passage is in the present tense, C ("allows") is correct. A is a finite verb, but it's plural, as if it agreed with the nearby noun "bundles," so it doesn't match the actual subject. B and D are participle forms, which would leave the clause after the colon without a main verb, so it wouldn't be a complete sentence.
g.design: A long modifier full of plural nouns separates the singular subject from its verb, so careful readers have to find the real subject and also check that the clause has a finite verb. The plural form and the participle options look plausible if you only skim.

c.seed: life science — Gecko adhesion toe pads and van der Waals force molecular interaction enabling vertical wall climbing

g.passage: The toe pads of a gecko, which are covered in millions of microscopic hairs called setae that each branch into hundreds of even finer tips, ______ the lizard to cling to a vertical pane of glass. The grip comes from van der Waals forces, weak attractions that arise between molecules when two surfaces come into extremely close contact.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 "The toe pads"이고, 콤마 사이의 긴 관계절은 수식어일 뿐이므로 빈칸에는 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하다. 따라서 D "allow"가 정답이다. A "allows"와 C "has allowed"는 정동사이지만 단수형이어서, 바로 앞의 "a gecko"를 주어로 착각할 때 고르게 된다. B "allowing"은 분사라서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 불완전한 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "The toe pads." The long clause set off by commas only modifies it, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject. That makes D, "allow," the correct answer. A ("allows") and C ("has allowed") are finite verbs, but they're singular, so you'd only pick them if you mistook the nearby "a gecko" for the subject. B ("allowing") is a participle, which leaves the sentence without a main verb and makes it incomplete.
g.design: To answer, you have to find the main subject behind a long nonrestrictive clause and also choose between a finite verb and a participle. The singular distractors are tempting because of the nearby noun "gecko."

c.seed: life science — Chameleon tongue projectile launch and muscular acceleration achieving prey capture speeds exceeding body length

g.passage: The tongue of the panther chameleon, which can shoot out to nearly twice the length of the lizard's body and reach insects within a few hundredths of a second, ______ much of its explosive acceleration from elastic collagen sheaths that are stretched like springs before each strike rather than from muscle contraction alone.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "The tongue"이고, 쉼표 사이의 which절은 삽입된 수식어일 뿐이므로 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 와야 한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "insects"에 끌린 복수형이어서 단수 주어 "tongue"과 맞지 않는다. C와 D는 분사 형태이므로 문장에 본동사가 없어 완전한 문장이 되지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The tongue." The which-clause set off by commas is just an interrupting modifier, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject. That makes A the answer. B is a finite verb too, but it's plural, as if it agreed with the nearby noun "insects," so it doesn't match the singular subject "tongue." C and D are participles, so with either one the sentence has no main verb and isn't complete.
g.design: 긴 삽입 관계절 뒤 주어-동사 일치와 정동사 vs 분사 판단을 결합했고, 복수 명사 insects를 빈칸 근처에 두어 B를 유인했다.

c.seed: life science — Archerfish pupil shape and spherical lens geometry compensating for chromatic aberration during underwater hunting

g.passage: To knock insects off overhanging leaves, the archerfish must judge the position of prey seen through water and air, where different wavelengths of light focus at slightly different distances, a distortion known as chromatic aberration. Studies of the fish's eye suggest that its nearly spherical lens, together with a pupil whose shape changes as light levels shift, ______ much of this color-related blurring, allowing the fish to aim its jets of water with remarkable precision.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: that절의 주어는 단수 명사 'lens'이고, 'together with a pupil...'은 삽입된 수식어구일 뿐 주어를 복수로 만들지 않는다. 또한 that절에는 정동사가 필요하므로 단수 정동사인 B가 정답이다. A는 정동사이긴 하지만 'lens'와 'pupil'을 복수 주어로 잘못 읽었을 때 고르게 되는 복수형이다. C와 D는 분사 형태라서 that절에 정동사가 없게 되므로 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the that-clause is the singular noun "lens." The phrase "together with a pupil..." is just an interrupting modifier, so it doesn't make the subject plural. The clause also needs a finite main verb, which is why the singular finite verb in B is correct. A is a finite verb, but it's plural, so you'd only pick it if you mistakenly read "lens" and "pupil" as a compound subject. C and D are participle forms, which would leave the that-clause with no main verb, so the sentence wouldn't be complete.
g.design: 긴 삽입구('together with a pupil whose shape changes...')로 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓았다. 그래서 학생은 정동사가 필요하다는 점과 주어가 단수라는 점을 둘 다 판단해야 한다. 그중 A는 정동사라는 조건만, C와 D는 의미만 맞아 보이게 설계했다.

c.seed: life science — Moray eel pharyngeal jaw system and secondary jaws extracting prey from crevices using dual-jaw mechanism

g.passage: Unlike most fish, which create suction to pull prey into their mouths, moray eels hunt in tight rock crevices where suction is ineffective. Instead, the eels rely on a second set of jaws located in the throat. After the oral jaws seize a fish, the pharyngeal jaws, which rest behind the skull until needed, ______ forward into the mouth, grip the prey, and drag it down toward the esophagus.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'the pharyngeal jaws'이고, 관계절 'which rest behind the skull until needed'는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 수식어이다. 빈칸에는 'grip', 'drag'와 병렬을 이루는 복수 정동사가 필요하므로 C 'launch'가 정답이다. A 'launching'과 B 'to launch'는 정동사가 아니어서 주절에 본동사가 없게 되고 'grip', 'drag'와의 병렬도 깨진다. D 'launches'는 정동사이지만 단수형이라 복수 주어 'jaws'와 수가 맞지 않으며, 바로 앞의 'skull'에 맞춰 잘못 고르기 쉽다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the main clause is the plural noun "the pharyngeal jaws," and the clause "which rest behind the skull until needed" is a modifier that sits between the subject and its verb. The blank needs a plural finite verb that is parallel with "grip" and "drag," so C, "launch," is correct. A, "launching," and B, "to launch," aren't finite verbs, so the main clause would have no main verb, and the parallel series with "grip" and "drag" would break. D, "launches," is a finite verb, but it's singular, so it doesn't agree with the plural "jaws." It's easy to pick by mistake if you match it to the nearby noun "skull."
g.design: 삽입된 관계절과 가까운 단수 명사 skull 때문에 주어를 헷갈리게 만들었다. 정동사가 필요하다는 점과 복수 주어와의 일치를 둘 다 판단해야 하고, 병렬 구조로도 확인할 수 있다.

c.seed: life science — Pistol shrimp shock wave generation and snapping claw cavitation bubble collapse stunning prey fish

g.passage: When a pistol shrimp snaps its enlarged claw shut, a jet of water shoots forward so fast that the pressure behind it drops sharply, forming a cavitation bubble. The bubble, which expands for less than a millisecond before the surrounding water forces it inward, ______ with enough energy to produce a shock wave that can stun a small fish several millimeters away.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The bubble"이고, "which expands ... inward"는 삽입된 관계절이므로 주절에는 정동사가 필요하다. D의 "collapses"는 단수 주어와 수가 일치하는 현재형 정동사로, 앞 관계절의 "expands"와 시제도 맞아 문장을 완성한다. A의 "collapsing"과 B의 "having collapsed"는 분사이므로 정동사 역할을 하지 못해 문장이 불완전해진다. C의 "to collapse"는 부정사라서 역시 주절의 동사가 될 수 없다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the sentence is "The bubble," and "which expands ... inward" is a nonessential relative clause, so the main clause still needs a finite verb. Choice D gives you "collapses," a present-tense finite verb that agrees with the singular subject and matches the tense of "expands," so it completes the sentence. Choices A ("collapsing") and B ("having collapsed") are participles, which can't act as the main verb, so the sentence would be incomplete. Choice C ("to collapse") is an infinitive, and an infinitive can't serve as the main verb either.
g.design: 긴 관계절이 주어와 빈칸 사이에 끼어 있어, 훑어 읽으면 "inward" 뒤에 분사가 이어지는 것처럼 보이게 했다. 주어를 찾고 정동사가 없다는 점을 확인하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다.

c.seed: life science — Dragonfly nymphal predatory jaw mechanism and raptorial appendage deployment during larval aquatic hunting

g.passage: Dragonfly nymphs, which may spend years hunting underwater before emerging as winged adults, rely on a strikingly fast feeding apparatus. The labium of a nymph, a hinged lower mouthpart that stays folded beneath the head until the insect is within striking distance of tadpoles or mosquito larvae, ______ forward in a fraction of a second, its hooked tips clamping onto the prey before it can escape.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The labium'이고, 동격 수식어구가 빈칸 앞까지 이어지므로 빈칸에는 문장의 정동사가 와야 한다. A는 단수 주어에 맞는 정동사이므로 정답이다. B는 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'larvae'에 수를 맞춘 형태지만 실제 주어인 'labium'과 일치하지 않는다. C는 뒤에 나오는 분사구 'clamping'과 형태가 비슷해 보이지만 분사라서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다. D 역시 완료분사라 정동사 역할을 하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The labium," and a long appositive phrase runs between it and the blank, so the blank needs the sentence's main verb. Choice A is a singular main verb, so it is correct. Choice B agrees with the nearby plural noun "larvae," but that noun is not the subject, so it does not agree with "labium." Choice C looks parallel to the later participle "clamping," but a participle leaves the sentence without a main verb. Choice D is a perfect participle, so it also cannot work as the main verb.
g.design: A long appositive phrase ending in a plural noun separates the subject from the verb, so you have to identify the real subject and also see that the sentence needs a main verb. The participle choices seem to fit because of the participle "clamping" later in the sentence.

g.passage: Male fireflies of the genus Photinus, drifting low over fields shortly after sunset, produce flashes in patterns unique to their species. Biologist James Lloyd found that the precise rhythm of these signals, together with the dark intervals that separate one pulse of light from the next, ______ a perched female to recognize a male of her own kind and to answer with a timed flash of her own.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 'that' 뒤 절의 주어는 단수 명사 'rhythm'이다. 'together with ~ the next'는 삽입된 수식어구라서 수에 영향을 주지 않는다. 따라서 단수 정동사가 필요하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 정동사이지만 가까이 있는 복수 명사 'intervals'에 수를 맞춘 복수형이라 틀렸다. C와 D는 분사라 정동사가 아니므로 that절에 본동사가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the clause after "that" is the singular noun "rhythm." The phrase "together with the dark intervals... the next" is an interrupting modifier and doesn't change the subject's number. So the clause needs a singular main verb, which makes B correct. A is a main verb, but it's plural: it agrees with the nearby noun "intervals" instead of the real subject. C and D are participles, not main verbs, so the that-clause would have no main verb.
g.design: 문항은 두 가지를 판단하게 한다. 먼저 정동사가 필요한지 알아야 C와 D가 걸러진다. 다음으로 'together with' 삽입구와 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'intervals'를 지나 실제 주어 'rhythm'을 찾아야 A가 걸러진다.

g.passage: Many midwater fishes hide from predators below them by producing light along their undersides, matching the faint glow that comes down from the surface. Penguins cannot produce light, but they get a similar effect another way. In species such as the emperor penguin, the dense white feathers that cover the belly, which reflect the bright light filtering down through the water, ______ the bird's dark outline when a leopard seal looks up at it from deeper water.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 "feathers"이며, "that cover the belly"와 "which reflect ... water"는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하므로 C "soften"이 정답이다. A는 정동사이지만 빈칸 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "belly"나 "water"에 맞춘 단수형이라 주어와 일치하지 않는다. B는 분사여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다. D 역시 단수형이고, 일반적 사실을 현재 시제로 서술하는 문맥에도 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "feathers." The phrases "that cover the belly" and "which reflect ... the water" just modify it. That means the blank needs a main verb that agrees with a plural subject, so C, "soften," is correct. A is a main verb, but it's singular, so it agrees with nearby nouns like "belly" or "water" instead of the real subject. B is a participle, which would leave the sentence without a main verb. D is also singular, and it doesn't fit a passage that uses the present tense to describe a general fact.
g.design: 이 문항은 복수 주어와 동사 사이에 단수 명사가 든 관계절 두 개를 넣어, 주어-동사 일치와 정동사 여부를 함께 판단해야 하도록 설계했다. 이 소재는 펭귄이 실제로는 빛을 내지 못한다는 사실을 반영해, 빛을 내는 어류와 펭귄의 흰 배 깃털을 대비하는 방식으로 정확하게 서술했다.

g.passage: Elephants produce rumbles at frequencies below the range of human hearing, and these infrasonic calls can travel several kilometers across open savanna. Researchers studying herds in Namibia found that the calls carry farthest in the cool hours after sunset, when a temperature inversion near the ground bends sound waves back toward the earth. The rumbles of a matriarch separated from her family group, recorded by microphones placed throughout the grassland, ______ by relatives up to ten kilometers away.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'The rumbles'이고, 'of a matriarch ... group'과 분사구 'recorded by ... grassland'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 문장에는 복수 주어와 맞는 정동사가 필요하므로 D 'were detected'가 정답이다. A는 정동사이지만 가까이 있는 단수 명사 'matriarch'나 'group'에 수를 맞춘 것이라 주어와 일치하지 않는다. B와 C는 분사형이라 정동사가 아니므로 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "The rumbles." The phrase "of a matriarch... group" and the participial phrase "recorded by... grassland" just modify that subject. So the sentence needs a main verb that agrees with a plural subject, which makes D, "were detected," the answer. A is a main verb, but it agrees with the nearby singular nouns "matriarch" or "group" instead of the actual subject. B and C are participles, not main verbs, so they would leave the sentence without a main verb.
g.design: 긴 전치사구와 분사구가 복수 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓고, 단수 명사들을 동사 가까이에 두어 잘못된 일치를 유도했다. 또 'recorded'를 본동사로 착각하면 분사형 오답이 그럴듯해 보이도록 만들었다.

c.seed: life science — Dolphin echolocation click production and biosonar frequency modulation for underwater navigation obstacle avoidance

g.passage: Bottlenose dolphins navigate murky water by producing rapid clicks in their nasal passages and listening for the returning echoes. Researchers once assumed that each dolphin used a fixed click frequency, much as a ship's sonar emits a single standard pulse. Recordings of dolphins swimming through a test course of suspended nets, however, showed the animals shifting their clicks toward higher frequencies as they approached the thinnest strands, which reflect lower-frequency sound poorly. ______ the dolphins appear to adjust their biosonar to suit the specific obstacle in front of them rather than relying on a single all-purpose signal.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 마지막 문장은 앞 문장에서 관찰한 사실(가는 그물에 다가갈수록 클릭 주파수를 높임)을 일반적인 의미(장애물에 맞춰 생체 음파를 조정함)로 다시 풀어 말한다. 따라서 바꿔 말하기를 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 마지막 문장이 앞의 관찰과 반대되는 내용이 아니라 그 관찰과 일치하므로 맞지 않는다. C는 '고정 주파수' 가정과의 대비만 보고 고르기 쉽지만, 빈칸 바로 앞 문장이 이미 그 가정을 뒤집었기 때문에 마지막 문장은 앞 문장과 대비되지 않는다. D는 과거 가설을 가리키는 것처럼 보이지만, 마지막 문장은 예전의 생각이 아니라 새로 내린 결론이다.
g.explanation_en: The last sentence takes the observation in the sentence before it (dolphins raise their click frequency near thin strands) and restates what it means in more general terms (they tailor their biosonar to each obstacle). So A, which signals a restatement, is correct. B doesn't work because the last sentence agrees with the observation instead of contradicting it. C is tempting if you focus on the earlier "fixed frequency" assumption, but the sentence right before the blank has already overturned that idea, so the last sentence doesn't contrast with it. D might seem to point back to the old view, but the last sentence states a new conclusion, not something researchers believed before.
g.design: 빈칸 앞의 반전(however) 때문에 B나 C를 고르기 쉽게 했다. 하지만 정답을 찾으려면 마지막 문장이 바로 앞 관찰을 다시 풀어 말한 것임을 알아차려야 한다.

c.seed: life science — Migratory bird magnetoreception and geomagnetic field navigation using cryptochromes in retinal photoreceptor cells

g.passage: For decades, researchers suspected that migratory birds such as European robins sense Earth's magnetic field through tiny particles of magnetite in their beaks. Experiments in which the nerve linking the beak to the brain was cut, however, showed that robins could still orient themselves correctly during migration season. ______ attention shifted to the eye, where proteins called cryptochromes in retinal photoreceptor cells react to light in ways that may be altered by the direction of the geomagnetic field.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 부리 신경을 끊어도 방향 감각이 유지되었다는 결과 때문에 연구자들의 관심이 눈으로 옮겨갔으므로, 앞 문장은 원인이고 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 결과이다. 그래서 B가 정답이다. A는 앞뒤 내용이 비슷하다는 뜻인데, 뒤 문장은 앞 실험과 비슷한 사례가 아니라 그 실험 때문에 나온 반응이다. C는 대조를 나타내지만, 부리 가설이 약해졌으니 다른 기관을 살펴보는 것은 예상을 뒤집는 일이 아니라 당연한 다음 단계이다. D는 예시를 나타내지만, 눈의 크립토크롬은 앞 문장의 실험 결과를 보여 주는 예가 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The second sentence explains why the beak idea lost support: robins could still orient themselves after the beak nerve was cut. Researchers then turned their attention to the eye, so that shift is a result of the experiments. That makes B correct. A suggests the two sentences describe similar things, but the shift to the eye is a response to the experiment, not a parallel case. C signals a contrast, yet looking at another organ after the beak hypothesis weakened is the expected next step, not a reversal. D introduces an example, but the cryptochromes in the eye are not an example of the experimental finding.
g.design: 이 문항에는 어휘 단서가 없어서, 실험 결과가 연구 방향 전환의 원인이라는 점을 스스로 추론해야 한다. 앞 문장의 "however"가 대조 전환어인 C를 끌어들이도록 했고, 앞 실험과 뒤 연구가 둘 다 탐구 과정이라는 점이 A를 그럴듯해 보이게 만든다.

c.seed: life science — Vampire squid bioluminescent display and photophore deployment for predator deterrence in deep ocean darkness

g.passage: Many deep-sea animals rely on bioluminescence to lure prey or attract mates, but the vampire squid (Vampyroteuthis infernalis) appears to use its light mainly for defense. When a predator comes near, the squid can light up photophores at the tips of its arms and then release a cloud of glowing mucus that holds blue light for nearly ten minutes. Researchers once assumed the squid's light organs worked like those of many other cephalopod relatives, mainly hiding the animal's silhouette against faint light from above. ______ observations from remotely operated vehicles showed that the squid flashes most intensely only when it is disturbed, a pattern that fits startling or confusing an attacker better than steady camouflage.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.design: 빈칸 앞은 기존 가정(위장), 뒤는 그 가정을 뒤집는 관찰이라 대조 관계가 필요하다. 그런데 앞 문단 전체가 방어용이라는 주장이라 'As a result'나 'In other words'도 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯해 보인다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 연구자들이 예전에 발광 기관이 위장용이라고 가정했다는 내용이고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 교란될 때만 강하게 빛난다는 관찰로 그 가정을 반박한다. 따라서 대조를 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용이라고 연결하지만, 뒤 문장은 앞의 가정과 반대된다. B는 관찰이 가정 때문에 생긴 결과라고 말하는데, 이 관찰은 가정에서 나온 결과가 아니라 가정을 뒤집는 증거다. D는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장을 바꿔 말한 것이라고 하지만, 뒤 문장은 오히려 다른 해석을 지지한다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank describes what researchers once assumed: that the light organs served as camouflage. The sentence after it reports observations that challenge that assumption, since the squid flashes mainly when disturbed. Because these two ideas contrast, C is correct. A treats the two sentences as similar points, but the second one goes against the first. B suggests the observations were caused by the assumption, when they actually overturn it. D presents the second sentence as a restatement, but it supports a different explanation instead of rephrasing the first.

g.passage: Most salamanders lose their feathery external gills and move onto land as they mature. The axolotl, a salamander native to lakes near Mexico City, typically never goes through this metamorphosis, keeping its gills and finned tail throughout its life. It would be easy to assume that such an animal is simply stuck in an immature, juvenile stage. ______ axolotls reach full sexual maturity and reproduce while keeping these larval features, a condition biologists call neoteny.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.design: 빈칸 앞 문장은 '쉽게 가정할 수 있는' 오해를 제시하고 빈칸 뒤에서 이를 뒤집는다. 어휘 단서 없이 가정→반박 관계를 파악해야 한다. 훑어 읽으면 '결과'나 '예시'로 착각하기 쉽다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 아홀로틀이 미성숙한 단계에 '갇혀 있다'고 쉽게 가정할 수 있다고 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 아홀로틀이 실제로는 완전히 성적으로 성숙해 번식한다고 밝힌다. 따라서 흔한 가정을 실제 사실로 바로잡는 D가 정답이다. A는 비슷한 내용을 덧붙일 때 쓰지만 뒤 문장은 앞의 가정과 반대된다. B는 아가미를 유지하는 것이 번식의 원인인 것처럼 만들고, 바로 앞 문장이 오해라는 점도 무시한다. C는 뒤 문장이 앞의 가정을 보여 주는 예시가 아니라 그 가정을 반박하는 내용이므로 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank describes an easy assumption: that axolotls are stuck in an immature stage. The sentence after the blank shows that this assumption is wrong, because axolotls actually become sexually mature and reproduce. A transition that corrects a mistaken belief with the actual fact is needed, so D is correct. A is used to add a similar point, but the second sentence contradicts the assumption rather than agreeing with it. B suggests that keeping gills causes reproduction, and it ignores that the previous sentence is a misconception. C doesn't work because the final sentence isn't an example of the assumption; it refutes it.

g.passage: When the spinal cord of a mammal is severed, glial cells near the injury form dense scar tissue that blocks damaged nerve fibers from reconnecting. In zebrafish, glial cells respond to the same kind of injury in a strikingly different way. ______ they extend long projections across the gap, forming a bridge along which regrowing axons can travel; within about eight weeks, the fish can swim normally again.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 두 번째 문장은 제브라피시의 신경교세포가 '눈에 띄게 다른 방식'으로 반응한다고 일반적으로만 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 방식이 무엇인지(틈을 가로지르는 다리 형성)를 구체적으로 설명하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 둘 다 신경교세포의 반응을 다룬다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 포유류와 '다르다'는 내용이므로 유사 관계가 성립하지 않는다. C는 포유류와의 대조만 보면 맞는 것 같지만, 빈칸 바로 앞 문장과 비교하면 뒤 문장은 반박이 아니라 부연이다. D는 회복이라는 결과가 나오기 때문에 끌리지만, 다리 형성은 '다르게 반응한다'는 사실의 결과가 아니라 그 반응의 내용 자체다.
g.explanation_en: The second sentence only says in general terms that zebrafish glial cells respond in a "strikingly different way." The sentence after the blank tells you exactly what that response is: the cells build a bridge across the gap. So A is correct. B might look reasonable because both sentences are about how glial cells respond, but the point is that the zebrafish response is different from the mammal's, so the two aren't similar. C fits the contrast with mammals, but the sentence right before the blank isn't being contradicted; the new sentence adds detail to it. D is tempting because the fish do recover, but the bridge-building doesn't result from the different response. It is the different response.
g.design: The relationship is general claim followed by specific detail, and no word in the passage signals it. Each wrong answer catches a careless reader in its own way: B links two descriptions of glial cells, C picks up the mammal contrast, and D picks up the recovery outcome.

c.seed: life science — Kangaroo rat kidney concentration and specialized nephron loop producing hypertonic urine

g.passage: The kangaroo rat, a rodent of North American deserts, can survive for long stretches without drinking, obtaining most of its water from the metabolism of dry seeds. Its kidneys contain nephron loops that are exceptionally long relative to the organ's size, reaching deep into the inner medulla and building an unusually steep salt gradient there. ______ the animal's kidneys can pull almost all of the water back out of the fluid passing through them, producing urine roughly four times as concentrated as the most concentrated human urine.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 긴 네프론 고리가 가파른 염분 기울기를 만든다는 구조적 원인을, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 덕분에 물을 거의 다 회수해 진한 소변을 만든다는 결과를 제시하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 뒤 문장이 일반 진술의 한 사례처럼 보일 수 있지만, 실제로는 앞의 구조가 낳는 기능적 결과이지 예시가 아니다. C는 사람 소변과의 비교가 등장해 대조처럼 보이지만, 앞 문장과 대조되는 내용이 아니다. D는 양보 후 반전을 나타내는데, 가파른 기울기와 강한 농축은 서로 상충하지 않고 자연스럽게 이어진다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank describes a structure: very long nephron loops that build a steep salt gradient. The sentence after it describes what that structure makes possible, which is pulling back almost all the water and producing highly concentrated urine. That is a cause-and-effect link, so B is correct. A might look tempting because the second sentence gives specific detail, but it's a result of the structure, not an example of it. C is tempting because of the comparison to human urine, but nothing in that sentence contrasts with the sentence before it. D signals a twist after a concession, yet a steep gradient and strong concentration go together; they don't conflict.
g.design: 이 문항에는 연결어 단서가 없어서, 해부 구조(원인)와 기능(결과)이 어떤 방향으로 이어지는지 스스로 파악해야 한다. 오답 A(구체적 세부 정보)와 C(사람과의 비교)는 표면적으로는 말이 되는 것처럼 보이도록 설계했다.

c.seed: life science — Hippopotamus sweat secretion lipid composition and sunscreen-like protection against ultraviolet radiation

g.passage: Hippopotamuses secrete a thick, reddish fluid from their skin that early naturalists mistook for blood and later researchers assumed was ordinary sweat. Chemical analyses led by Yoko Saikawa revealed that the fluid contains two pigments, hipposudoric acid and norhipposudoric acid, which absorb light across the ultraviolet range and also inhibit the growth of certain bacteria. ______ an animal that spends hours basking on open riverbanks under intense equatorial sun, often with small wounds from territorial fights, carries what amounts to a built-in sunscreen and antiseptic.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 마지막 문장은 앞 문장에서 밝혀진 색소의 화학적 성질(자외선 흡수, 항균)이 하마에게 실질적으로 무엇을 의미하는지 바꿔 말하는 요약·함의이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 첫 문장의 '피나 땀으로 오인'과 대비되는 듯 보이지만, 마지막 문장은 바로 앞의 분석 결과를 뒤집지 않고 그대로 이어 간다. B는 마지막 문장에 하마의 구체적 상황이 나오므로 그럴듯하지만, 이 문장은 일반 원리의 한 사례가 아니라 앞 결과의 의미를 재진술한 것이다. D는 시간 순서를 나타내는데, 이 결론은 분석 이전이 아니라 분석에서 도출된 것이다.
g.explanation_en: The last sentence restates what the pigments' chemical properties (absorbing UV light and fighting bacteria) mean in practice for the hippo, so C is correct. A might seem to fit because it seems to contrast with the early misidentifications, but the last sentence builds on the analysis right before it rather than going against it. B is tempting because the sentence describes a specific hippo situation, but that sentence isn't one example of a broader claim; it restates what the earlier findings mean. D signals that something happened earlier in time, but this conclusion comes from the analysis, not from before it.
g.design: 세부 묘사가 있어 예시(B), 초기 오해 언급으로 대조(A)가 그럴듯해 보이게 하고, 실제 관계는 화학적 발견의 실질적 함의 재진술임을 정독해야 파악되도록 했다.

c.seed: life science — Stoat seasonal coat color change and photoperiod-triggered molt from brown to white pelage

g.passage: In autumn, the stoat (Mustela erminea) in northern regions molts its brown summer coat and grows a white one, a change long assumed to be a response to falling temperatures or the arrival of snow. Laboratory studies, however, have shown that the molt is triggered mainly by day length: stoats kept at constant warm temperatures but exposed to shortening periods of light still turned white on schedule. ______ in years when snowfall comes late, wild stoats can be seen bright white against bare brown ground, conspicuous to both predators and prey.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 털갈이가 눈이 아니라 일조 시간에 의해 촉발된다는 원인을 제시하고, 뒷 문장은 눈이 늦게 와도 흰 털로 바뀌어 눈에 띄는 결과를 서술하므로 인과 관계인 D가 정답이다. A는 흰 털이 불리하다는 점이 앞 내용과 대조되는 듯 보이지만, 실제로는 앞 문장에서 예상되는 결과이므로 양보가 아니다. B도 '맨땅 vs 흰 털'의 대비에 끌리게 하지만 두 문장 사이 관계는 대조가 아니다. C는 야생 관찰이 실험 결과의 사례처럼 보이나, 뒷 문장은 실험 사실의 예시가 아니라 그로부터 생기는 결과이다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence explains the cause: the molt is set off by day length, not by snow or cold. The final sentence describes what follows from that: when snow is late, stoats still turn white and stand out against bare ground. That is a cause-and-effect relationship, so D is correct. A is tempting because being conspicuous seems like a drawback, but this outcome is what the earlier sentence predicts, so nothing is being conceded. B plays on the contrast between white fur and brown ground, but the two sentences themselves aren't in contrast. C might look right because the wild observation seems like an example, but the sentence describes a consequence of the lab finding, not an instance of it.
g.design: Two-step judgment: the reader must see that the visible mismatch looks like a contrast but is actually a consequence of the day-length cause. Choices A, B, and C each have partial appeal (a disadvantage, a color contrast, an observation that looks like an example).

g.passage: Mudskippers, small fish found on tropical mudflats, spend much of their lives out of water, propelling themselves across the mud with their muscular pectoral fins. Their gills, like those of most fish, tend to collapse in air, so the gills alone cannot supply enough oxygen on land. ______ mudskippers rely heavily on their skin, which stays coated in a thin film of water that lets oxygen pass into the dense network of blood vessels just beneath the surface.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.design: 빈칸 앞에서 아가미가 육상에서 충분하지 않다고 한 뒤, 뒤에서 피부라는 대체 수단을 제시하므로 '대체' 관계를 찾아야 한다. Nevertheless(앞 내용의 한계 뒤 반전처럼 보임)와 For example(일반화 뒤 구체화처럼 보임)이 그럴듯한 함정이다.
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 육지에서는 아가미만으로 산소를 충분히 얻을 수 없다고 말하고, 뒤 문장은 대신 피부에 의존한다고 설명하므로 대체 관계를 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 대조를 나타내는데, 피부 호흡은 아가미의 한계를 무릅쓰고 일어나는 일이 아니라 그 한계를 해결하는 방법이므로 맞지 않는다. C는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 사례여야 하는데, 피부 호흡은 아가미가 무너지는 현상의 예가 아니다. D는 두 내용이 비슷해야 하지만 피부는 아가미와 같은 방식으로 작동하는 기관이 아니라 아가미를 대신하는 수단이다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence says the gills alone can't supply enough oxygen on land, and the next sentence describes what mudskippers use in their place: their skin. That replacement relationship makes A correct. B signals contrast, but skin breathing doesn't happen in spite of the gills' limits. It's the way mudskippers get around them. C would make the skin breathing an example of the gills collapsing, and it isn't one. D would mean the two ideas are alike, but the skin isn't described as working like the gills. It takes over the job the gills can't do.

c.seed: life science — Basilisk lizard bipedal running and surface tension exploitation for water striding locomotion

g.passage: Water striders and certain spiders can stand on ponds because of surface tension, the cohesive "skin" formed by water molecules at the surface. Since the green basilisk lizard can sprint across streams on its hind legs, observers long assumed that it relied on the same effect. __Yet surface tension can support only a very small mass for a given foot size, and even a young basilisk is far too heavy to be held up this way.__ Biomechanists James Glasheen and Thomas McMahon found instead that each of the lizard's steps has distinct phases: the foot slaps the surface, then strokes downward, pushing water aside and opening an air-filled pocket, and is pulled out before the pocket collapses. The force produced by these motions, rather than surface tension, keeps the running lizard from sinking.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It offers support for the assumption stated in the previous sentence by showing how the lizard's feet spread its weight across the water.
It gives a reason to doubt an explanation mentioned earlier, preparing the way for the account of the lizard's stepping motion that follows.
It states the central finding of Glasheen and McMahon's research about how the lizard's feet interact with water.
It explains why water striders, unlike basilisk lizards, are light enough to remain on the surface of ponds.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작하며, 앞 문장의 가정(바실리스크가 표면장력을 이용한다)을 도마뱀이 너무 무겁다는 근거로 반박하고, 이어지는 발 디딤 동작 설명으로 넘어가게 하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 이 문장이 그 가정을 지지한다고 보지만, 실제로는 약화시킨다. C는 연구자들의 발견을 가리키는데, 그 발견(때리기·젓기·공기 주머니)은 다음 문장에 나오고 밑줄 문장은 반론일 뿐이다. D는 소금쟁이가 가볍다는 점이 암시되기는 하지만, 이 문장의 초점은 소금쟁이가 아니라 바실리스크에 대한 설명이 왜 실패하는지에 있다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence starts with "Yet" and challenges the assumption from the previous sentence (that basilisks use surface tension) by pointing out that the lizard is far too heavy. It then leads into the stepping-motion explanation that follows, so B is correct. A is wrong because the sentence weakens that assumption rather than supporting it. C is wrong because the researchers' actual finding (slap, stroke, air pocket) comes in the next sentence, while the underlined sentence is only the objection. D is wrong because, although the sentence hints that water striders are light, its focus is on why the explanation fails for basilisks, not on water striders.
g.design: Medium: readers must link the "Yet" sentence back to the assumption and forward to the new account. Two distractors use real nearby content (the research finding, the water-strider contrast) but give the wrong function.

c.seed: life science — Porcupine quill detachment mechanism and barbed tip geometry facilitating wound penetration retention

g.passage: North American porcupines carry roughly 30,000 quills, each tipped with microscopic backward-facing barbs. For decades, researchers assumed these barbs served mainly to anchor a quill once it had entered a predator's skin, making it painful and difficult to pull out. In 2012, however, biomedical engineer Woo Kyung Cho and colleagues measured the force needed to push quills into tissue and found something unexpected. __Quills with intact barbs required about 60 percent less force to penetrate muscle than quills whose barbs had been sanded away.__ The team proposed that the barbs concentrate stress at many small points along the tip, tearing tissue fibers in sequence rather than all at once. The barbs, in other words, appear to help a quill go in easily as well as stay in, a dual function that has since inspired designs for surgical staples and needles.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It provides evidence supporting the long-held view that barbs mainly keep a quill lodged in a predator's skin.
It explains the method by which the researchers removed barbs from quills before testing them.
It presents a finding that shows the barbs serve a purpose beyond the one researchers had traditionally assigned to them.
It describes a practical application of quill geometry that engineers later developed for medical tools.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 미늘이 있는 가시가 조직을 뚫는 데 힘이 훨씬 덜 든다는 결과로, 미늘이 '고정'뿐 아니라 '관통'도 돕는다는 새로운 기능을 보여 주므로 C가 정답이다. A는 미늘의 고정 기능이 언급되긴 하지만, 밑줄 문장은 기존 견해를 뒷받침하는 것이 아니라 관통이라는 다른 기능을 드러낸다. B는 미늘을 갈아 없앤 사실이 문장에 나오지만, 문장의 역할은 방법 설명이 아니라 측정 결과 제시이다. D의 의료 도구 응용은 마지막 문장에서 다루는 내용이다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence reports that barbed quills needed much less force to penetrate tissue. That shows the barbs help with entry, not just anchoring, so C is correct. A is wrong because anchoring is the traditional view, and this result doesn't back it up; it points to a different function. B picks up on the sanded-away barbs, but the sentence states a result, not how the experiment was done. D describes the medical applications, which come up only in the final sentence.
g.design: To pick the answer, students have to link the earlier assumption about anchoring with the new result about penetration. Distractors A and B each use a detail that really appears in the text, so they look partly right.

c.seed: life science — Seahorse prehensile tail and antagonistic muscle arrangement enabling precise grasping behavior

g.passage: Unlike most fish, which use their tails mainly for propulsion, seahorses rely on a prehensile tail to anchor themselves to seagrass and coral branches. Biomechanist Michael Porter and his colleagues found that the tail's flexibility depends on an antagonistic arrangement of muscles running along its bony plates, with one set curling the tail inward while an opposing set ______ this balanced pairing allows a seahorse to adjust its grip with remarkable precision, holding fast in strong currents without crushing delicate stems.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 "with one set ... while an opposing set straightens it"라는 긴 수식구로 끝나는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "this balanced pairing allows..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론만으로 연결할 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이다. A는 쉼표+and가 형식상 가능해 보이지만, 'while' 구 안에 놓여 and가 'straightens'와 병렬되는 동사구처럼 읽히게 되어 뒤 절과의 경계가 흐려지고, 앞 내용의 결과를 제시하는 새 문장으로서 접속이 부자연스럽다. C는 세미콜론 뒤에 불필요한 and와 쉼표를 덧붙여 부적절하다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank is an independent clause that ends with a long "with... while an opposing set straightens it" phrase, and the text after the blank, "this balanced pairing allows...," is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. A semicolon by itself can correctly join two independent clauses, so D is correct. B is a comma splice, since a comma alone can't join two independent clauses. A looks acceptable at first, but placed inside the "while" phrase, "and" reads like it's joining another verb to "straightens," which blurs the boundary with the new clause that states the result. C wrongly adds "and" plus a comma after the semicolon, which is redundant and nonstandard.
g.design: 긴 with/while 수식구 뒤에서 절 경계를 판단하게 하고, 쉼표+and 오답을 그럴듯하게 배치해 비교가 필요하게 했다.

g.passage: Most predatory fish swallow prey by rapidly expanding the mouth cavity, creating suction that pulls food inward. Moray eels, which often hunt inside narrow rocky crevices where such expansion is impossible, rely on a different mechanism. A second set of jaws located in the throat, known as the pharyngeal ______ forward into the mouth, grip the captured prey, and haul it back toward the esophagus.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: "known as the pharyngeal jaws"는 앞의 쉼표와 짝을 이루는 비필수 수식어라서 닫는 쉼표가 필요하다. 동사도 복수 주어에 맞춰야 하므로 두 가지를 함께 판단해야 한다. 오답 C는 쉼표는 맞지만 수 일치가 틀리고, D는 동사는 맞지만 쉼표가 빠졌다.
g.explanation: 주어는 "A second set of jaws"이고, "known as the pharyngeal jaws"는 쉼표로 시작한 비필수 삽입구라서 닫는 쉼표가 있어야 한다. 이 수식어가 끝나면 주어에 이어지는 본동사 launch가 나오고, launch는 grip, haul과 병렬을 이룬다. 따라서 정답은 A이다. B는 세미콜론을 써서 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. C는 쉼표는 맞지만, 단수 동사 launches가 병렬 동사 grip, haul과 맞지 않는다. 이 문장에서는 jaws 전체를 복수로 다루고 있기 때문이다. D는 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 삽입구가 끝나지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject is "A second set of jaws," and "known as the pharyngeal jaws" is a nonessential phrase that opens with a comma, so it needs a closing comma too. Once that phrase ends, the main verb launch follows, and it lines up in parallel with grip and haul. That makes A correct. B uses a semicolon, which cuts the subject off from its verb and leaves a first part that can't stand alone as a clause. C gets the comma right, but the singular verb launches doesn't match the parallel verbs grip and haul. The sentence treats the jaws as plural. D leaves out the closing comma, so the nonessential phrase never ends.

g.passage: When a pistol shrimp snaps its oversized claw shut, a jet of water shoots out so quickly that the pressure behind it plummets, forming a vapor-filled cavitation bubble. The bubble's collapse, which lasts only a few hundred millionths of a ______ a shock wave powerful enough to stun nearby prey and a brief flash of light known as shrimpoluminescence.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The bubble's collapse"이고 본동사는 "produces"이다. 그 사이에 쉼표로 시작한 비필수 관계절 "which lasts only a few hundred millionths of a second"가 끼어 있으므로, 관계절을 닫으려면 쉼표가 하나 더 필요하다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론이 주어와 동사를 갈라 놓아 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. C는 닫는 쉼표가 없어 삽입절이 끝나지 않고, D는 "and it"을 넣어 주어 "collapse"에 본동사가 없는 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The bubble's collapse," and its main verb is "produces." Between them sits a nonessential relative clause that opens with a comma: "which lasts only a few hundred millionths of a second." You need a second comma to close that clause, so B is correct. A puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, which leaves the first part without a complete independent clause. C leaves out the closing comma, so the clause never ends, and D adds "and it," which means the subject "collapse" never gets a main verb.
g.design: To solve this, you have to spot that the clause starting with "which" ends at the blank, then find where the main subject and verb connect. Choices A and D look like reasonable ways to join clauses, so you only rule them out once you see the subject has no verb of its own.

c.seed: life science — Dragonfly nymphal predatory jaw mechanism and raptorial appendage deployment aquatic hunting

g.passage: Dragonfly nymphs, which may spend years underwater before emerging as winged adults, hunt with a hinged lower lip called the labium. Folded beneath the head when at rest, the labium can be shot forward in a fraction of a second to seize a passing tadpole or mosquito larva. Researchers studying the mechanism found that the strike does not depend on muscle contraction ______ energy is stored gradually in stretched cuticle and released all at once, much like a drawn bow launching an arrow.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: "rather"가 앞 절을 수식하는지 뒤 절을 이끄는지 문맥으로 판단한 뒤 독립절 두 개 사이 경계를 고르게 했다. A와 B는 쉼표나 세미콜론을 일부 맞게 써서 비교해야만 배제된다.
g.explanation: "the strike does not depend on muscle contraction alone"과 "energy is stored ... all at once"는 둘 다 독립절이고, "rather"는 뒤 절을 이끄는 접속부사이다. 따라서 두 절 사이에 세미콜론을 두고 "rather" 뒤에 쉼표를 붙인 C가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표로만 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 "rather"를 앞 절에 붙여 버려 세미콜론 뒤 절이 접속부사 없이 시작하고, 앞 절 끝의 "rather"는 문법적으로 어색하다. D는 절 사이에 경계 부호가 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: "The strike does not depend on muscle contraction alone" and "energy is stored ... all at once" are both independent clauses, and "rather" is a transition that introduces the second clause. So you need a semicolon between the clauses and a comma after "rather," which makes C correct. A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, so it creates a comma splice. B attaches "rather" to the first clause, which leaves it dangling awkwardly at the end of that clause and puts the semicolon in the wrong spot. D has no punctuation at all between the clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence.

Penguins cannot make light, but biologists suspect they achieve a similar effect in another way. The emperor penguin's belly plumage, a dense layer of white feathers that scatters downwelling sunlight in roughly the same pattern as the surrounding water______ the bird nearly invisible to leopard seals hunting from the darker depths.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 주어 "The emperor penguin's belly plumage" 뒤에 쉼표로 시작한 동격구(a dense layer ... water)가 이어지므로 이 삽입구는 쉼표로 닫혀야 하고, 이어서 본동사 "makes"가 와야 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론 앞부분에 본동사가 없어 독립절이 아니고, "making"도 본동사가 될 수 없다. B는 본동사는 있지만 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 대시로 닫아 문장부호가 짝이 맞지 않는다. C는 "making"이 분사여서 문장 전체에 본동사가 없다.
g.explanation_en: The subject "The emperor penguin's belly plumage" is followed by an appositive (a dense layer ... water) that opens with a comma, so that appositive has to close with a comma too, and then the main verb "makes" must follow. That makes D correct. A doesn't work: what comes before the semicolon has no main verb, so it isn't an independent clause, and "making" can't serve as the main verb either. B does supply a main verb, but it closes a comma-opened appositive with a dash, so the punctuation doesn't match. C uses the participle "making," which leaves the sentence without any main verb.
g.design: A long appositive separates the subject from the verb. To answer, students have to recognize that the sentence still needs a main verb and that the appositive's opening comma must be matched by a closing comma. A semicolon option and a mismatched dash option serve as tempting partial-truth distractors.

Because such low-frequency waves lose relatively little energy as they move across open savanna, a rumble produced at dusk, when a layer of cool air near the ground helps channel sound, can carry surprisingly ______ researchers in Kenya have documented herds responding to calls made several kilometers away.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 긴 종속절과 비필수 삽입절(when...)을 두어 주절의 경계를 흐리게 했고, 'indeed'가 앞뒤 어디에 붙는지와 두 독립절 연결을 함께 판단해야 한다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'a rumble ... can carry surprisingly far'는 독립절이고, 뒤의 'researchers ... have documented...'도 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 이으려면 세미콜론이 필요하며, 'indeed'는 뒤 절을 여는 접속부사이므로 그 뒤에 쉼표가 붙는다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 접속 오류(comma splice)가 생기고, C는 두 절 사이에 아무 문장부호도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The part before the blank, "a rumble ... can carry surprisingly far," is an independent clause, and so is "researchers ... have documented herds responding...." With no conjunction joining two independent clauses, you need a semicolon, and since "indeed" is a conjunctive adverb opening the second clause, a comma follows it. That makes A correct. B and D join the two clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice, and C puts no punctuation between the clauses at all, so it's a run-on sentence.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: life science — Dolphin echolocation click production and biosonar frequency modulation underwater navigation ability

g.passage: Bottlenose dolphins produce their echolocation clicks not in the larynx but in the phonic lips, a pair of fatty structures tucked just beneath the blowhole______ adjusting the tension of these lips, a dolphin can shift the frequency of its clicks, sharpening its acoustic picture of objects as small as a fish buried in sand.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격구(a pair of ... blowhole)로 끝나는 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'by adjusting ..., a dolphin can shift ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문이며, 'blowhole by adjusting'으로 잘못 읽힐 수도 있다. D는 관계대명사 which를 넣지만, 뒤 절에 이미 주어 a dolphin이 있어 which가 문법적으로 할 역할이 없으므로 비문이 된다.
g.explanation_en: Before the blank you have a complete independent clause that ends with a long appositive ("a pair of fatty structures tucked just beneath the blowhole"). After the blank, "by adjusting..., a dolphin can shift..." is also an independent clause, with its own subject and verb. A semicolon is the right way to join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on, and it could also be misread as "blowhole by adjusting." D adds "which," but the clause after it already has its own subject, "a dolphin," so "which" has no grammatical job and the sentence breaks.
g.design: 긴 동격 수식어가 앞 절 끝을 가려 경계를 놓치기 쉽게 했다. 그리고 쉼표, 무부호, 관계사 오답을 넣어 두 독립절인지 확인해야 정답을 고를 수 있게 했다.

c.seed: life science — Migratory bird magnetoreception and geomagnetic field navigation using cryptochromes retinal cells

g.passage: European robins can keep to a migratory heading even on overcast nights when no stars are visible, so biologists have long suspected that the birds sense Earth's magnetic field directly. Many researchers now credit this ability to cryptochromes, light-sensitive proteins located in specialized cells of the birds' retinas______ when struck by blue light, these proteins are thought to form short-lived molecular pairs whose chemical behavior changes with the angle of the magnetic field, possibly letting the birds "see" magnetic direction.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 긴 동격구(light-sensitive proteins located in...)를 두어 끝까지 하나의 수식어처럼 보이게 했다. 빈칸 뒤가 'when' 부사절로 시작해 수식어가 이어지는 것처럼 보이지만 실제로는 'these proteins are thought...'라는 독립절이므로, 쉼표·관계사·접속사 중 무엇이 맞는지 따져 봐야 한다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤도 'when struck by blue light'라는 도입 부사구 다음에 주어 'these proteins'와 동사 'are thought'가 나오는 독립절이다. 뒤 절은 크립토크롬이 어떻게 작용하는지 설명하므로, 콜론으로 두 절을 연결한 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절 두 개를 이은 쉼표 오류(comma splice)이다. B는 'which' 뒤에 'these proteins'라는 주어가 다시 나와 관계절 문법이 맞지 않는다. D는 쉼표 없이 'and'만으로 두 독립절을 이어 문법에 맞지 않고, 'retinas and when...'으로 읽히면 'retinas'에 무언가가 더 나열되는 것처럼 보여 의미도 흐려진다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank is a complete independent clause. After the blank, the introductory phrase "when struck by blue light" is followed by the subject "these proteins" and the verb "are thought," so that part is also an independent clause. The second clause explains how cryptochromes work, so C is correct because a colon properly connects the two clauses and introduces the explanation. A is wrong because a comma alone joining two independent clauses creates a comma splice. B is wrong because "which" would need to act as the subject of its own clause, but the clause already has the subject "these proteins." D is wrong because "and" without a comma doesn't properly join two independent clauses, and "retinas and when..." makes it sound like something else is being added to "retinas," which muddles the meaning.

c.seed: life science — Vampire squid bioluminescent display and photophore deployment predator deterrence deep ocean

g.passage: The vampire squid (Vampyroteuthis infernalis), a small cephalopod that drifts through oxygen-poor waters hundreds of meters below the ocean's surface, has an unusual way of deterring predators. When threatened, it does not release dark ink as many of its shallow-water relatives do______ it ejects a sticky cloud of glowing mucus from the tips of its arms, a display that may confuse an attacker long enough for the squid to vanish into the surrounding darkness.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "When threatened, it does not release ... do"와 빈칸 뒤 "it ejects ... darkness"는 각각 독립절이므로 두 절 사이에 세미콜론 같은 강한 경계가 필요하고, "instead"는 둘째 절을 여는 접속부사로 뒤에 쉼표가 붙어야 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 "instead"를 쉼표로 감쌌지만 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. B는 첫 절 뒤에 아무 경계 없이 다음 절이 이어져 run-on 문장이 된다. C는 세미콜론을 쓰긴 했지만 "instead" 뒤에 둬서 "instead"가 첫 절 끝에 붙어 버리므로, 대조의 의미가 둘째 절과 이어지지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("When threatened, it does not release ... do") and the text after it ("it ejects ... darkness") are both independent clauses, so they need a strong boundary such as a semicolon between them. "Instead" is a conjunctive adverb that introduces the second clause, so it should come after the semicolon and be followed by a comma, which makes D correct. A sets off "instead" with commas, but a comma alone can't join two independent clauses, so it creates a comma splice. B puts no boundary at all between the clauses, which creates a run-on. C does use a semicolon, but placing it after "instead" attaches the word to the end of the first clause, so the contrast no longer introduces the second clause.
g.design: 긴 동격구와 종속절이 앞에 와서 절 경계를 찾기 어렵게 했고, 모든 선택지를 'instead'와 문장부호 조합이라는 같은 틀로 만들었다. 오답 A와 C는 각각 instead에 쉼표를 붙이거나 세미콜론을 쓰는 식으로 일부만 맞아서, 서로 비교해 봐야 배제할 수 있다.

c.seed: life science — Giraffe cardiovascular system and blood pressure regulation preventing cerebral edema height

g.passage: A giraffe's heart must generate roughly twice the blood pressure of a human heart to push blood up a neck that can exceed two meters in length. Yet when the animal lowers its head to drink, that same pressure could flood the brain with fluid. Researchers studying the animal's circulation have identified one safeguard in particular, the rete mirabile, a dense network of small vessels at the base of the ______ this mesh of branching arteries dampens sudden surges in pressure before blood reaches delicate cerebral tissue.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 'Researchers ... have identified one safeguard ... the rete mirabile, ...'라는 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'this mesh ... dampens ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 뒤 절이 앞에서 언급된 안전장치의 작동 방식을 설명하므로 두 독립절을 잇는 콜론을 쓴 A가 맞다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C의 ', and'는 문법상 가능해 보이지만, 'and'가 앞의 동격구 'a dense network ...'와 병렬을 이루는 것처럼 읽혀 'the rete mirabile'에 대한 설명이 모호하게 이어지므로 앞 문장이 소개한 내용을 풀어 설명하는 관계를 나타내지 못한다. D는 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank is a complete independent clause: "Researchers ... have identified one safeguard ... the rete mirabile, a dense network ... skull." The text after the blank, "this mesh of branching arteries dampens ...," is also an independent clause, and it explains how that safeguard works, so A's colon correctly joins the two clauses and introduces the explanation. B joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C may look acceptable, but "and" just adds the second clause as one more fact instead of showing that it explains the safeguard. It also comes right after the appositive "a dense network ...," which makes the sentence confusing, so a colon fits better. D puts two independent clauses together with no punctuation, which creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: I put a long appositive before the blank so it's hard to see that the first clause is already complete. Choices B and D are classic boundary errors, while C uses a conjunction that looks plausible, so students have to check the context to rule it out.

c.seed: life science — Hummingbird hovering flight and rapid wing rotation generating lift forward backward strokes

g.passage: Unlike most birds, which generate nearly all of their lift during the downstroke, hummingbirds such as the ruby-throated hummingbird (Archilochus colubris) produce lift during both the forward and the backward strokes of each wingbeat ______ the shoulder joint, they flip the wing almost upside down at the end of every forward stroke, so the wing keeps meeting the air at a useful angle as it sweeps back.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , by rapidly rotating their wings at
; by rapidly rotating their wings at
by rapidly rotating their wings at
, which, by rapidly rotating their wings at
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'hummingbirds ... produce lift ... wingbeat'는 독립절이고, 뒤의 'by rapidly rotating ... joint, they flip ...'도 주어 they와 동사 flip을 가진 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 접속사 없이 잇기 때문에 세미콜론이 필요하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 문장부호가 없어 by 구가 앞 절에 붙는 것처럼 읽히지만, 실제로는 두 절이 그냥 붙어 버린 run-on 문장이 된다. D는 관계대명사 which로 절을 시작하는데, 그 절에 이미 주어 they가 있어서 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "hummingbirds ... produce lift ... wingbeat," is an independent clause. The text after it, "by rapidly rotating ... joint, they flip ...," is also an independent clause, with the subject "they" and the verb "flip." Two independent clauses joined without a conjunction need a semicolon, so B is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C has no punctuation, so the "by" phrase seems to attach to the first clause, but the two clauses actually run together into a fused sentence. D starts a relative clause with "which," but that clause already has its own subject, "they," so the sentence is ungrammatical.
g.design: 독립절 경계를 판단하는 문제다. 빈칸 앞 첫 절에는 긴 비필수 수식어와 괄호 학명이 있고, 둘째 절은 도입 전치사구로 시작해 주어 they가 뒤에 나온다. 훑어 읽으면 by 구가 앞 절에 이어지는 것처럼 보이도록 했다.

c.seed: life science — Gecko adhesion toe pads and van der Waals force molecular interaction vertical climbing

g.passage: The toe pads of the tokay gecko, a lizard that can sprint straight up a vertical pane of glass, are lined with roughly half a million bristles called setae, each of which branches into hundreds of nanoscale tips______ these tips press so close to a surface that weak van der Waals attractions between molecules, though individually negligible, add up to a grip strong enough to hold the animal's entire weight.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 동격어구와 관계절 뒤에 절 경계가 오도록 했다. 빈칸 뒤에는 because가 이끄는 종속절과 주절(attractions ... add up)이 함께 있어서, because를 앞 문장에 붙이면 뒤의 주절이 연결어 없이 남는다. 그래서 because절이 문장 끝까지 이어지는지 구조를 끝까지 확인해야 정답을 고를 수 있다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 뒤를 보면 "Because these tips press so close to a surface that ..."이라는 종속절 다음에 주절 "weak van der Waals attractions ... add up to a grip"이 따로 나온다. 따라서 빈칸 뒤 부분은 그 자체로 하나의 완전한 문장이므로, 앞 문장을 마침표로 끝내고 Because로 새 문장을 시작한 C가 정답이다. A와 B처럼 because를 앞 문장에 붙이면 because절은 앞 내용의 이유를 나타내는 것처럼 보이지만, 그 뒤의 주절 attractions ... add up이 접속사 없이 남아 문장이 잘못 이어진다. D도 because를 앞 문장에 붙여 같은 문제가 생기며, 게다가 because 바로 뒤에 쉼표를 넣어 접속사와 그 절을 불필요하게 갈라놓았다.
g.explanation_en: Look at what comes after the blank: a dependent clause ("Because these tips press so close to a surface that...") followed by its own main clause ("weak van der Waals attractions... add up to a grip"). That means everything after the blank is already a complete sentence, so C is correct: it ends the first sentence with a period and starts a new one with "Because." Choices A and B attach "because" to the first sentence. The "because" clause then seems to explain the earlier statement, but the main clause "attractions... add up" is left hanging with no conjunction to connect it. D has the same problem, and it also puts an unnecessary comma right after "because," splitting the conjunction from its clause.

c.seed: life science — Chameleon tongue projectile launch and muscular acceleration prey capture speeds achievement

g.passage: Chameleons catch insects by firing their tongues out of their mouths with peak accelerations of more than 2,000 meters per second squared. That is far faster than any vertebrate muscle can shorten on its own. Biologist Jurriaan de Groot and colleagues found that before a strike, a muscle around the tongue's bony core contracts slowly, stretching elastic collagen sheaths nested inside the tongue. When the chameleon releases the tongue, the sheaths spring back all at once. Because the launch runs on this stored elastic energy instead of on muscle contraction during the strike itself, the tongue's performance ______ the speed limits that normally restrict muscle-powered movement.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문에 따르면 혀의 가속도는 근육이 혼자 낼 수 있는 속도를 훨씬 넘고, 그 이유는 발사할 때 근육 수축 대신 저장된 탄성 에너지를 쓰기 때문이다. 따라서 혀의 성능은 근육 운동에 걸리는 속도 한계를 '우회한다'는 뜻의 D가 정답이다. A(강화하다)는 근육이 미리 수축한다는 내용 때문에 그럴듯해 보이지만, 성능이 한계를 강화한다는 말은 논리에 맞지 않는다. B(반영하다)는 근육이 관여한다는 점에서 부분적으로 맞아 보이지만, 성능이 그 한계를 따른다는 뜻이 되어 지문의 대비와 어긋난다. C(근접하다)는 말은 되지만, 지문은 혀가 한계에 가까워지는 것이 아니라 그 한계를 '훨씬 넘는다'고 말한다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the tongue accelerates far faster than muscle alone can manage, and this works because the launch uses stored elastic energy instead of muscle contraction during the strike. So the tongue's performance gets around the usual speed limits on muscle-powered movement, which makes D, "circumvents," correct. A, "reinforces," might seem tempting because a muscle does contract before the strike, but it makes no sense to say the performance strengthens the limits. B, "reflects," might seem to fit because muscle is involved, but it would mean the performance stays within those limits, which goes against the passage's contrast. C, "approaches," makes sense on its own, but the passage says the tongue goes far beyond the limit, not just close to it.
g.design: To answer, students have to connect two facts: the acceleration is greater than any muscle could produce, and the launch is powered by stored energy rather than by muscle during the strike. A and B pick up on the muscle's role, and C fits a quick reading about being near a limit.

g.passage: In many North American firefly species, males flash a coded sequence while flying, and females perched in the grass reply only after a characteristic delay. Biologist James Lloyd found that females of the predatory genus Photuris exploit this system: they copy the delayed reply of other species' females, drawing in males that they then eat. Because the deception depends on matching a prey species' timing almost exactly, Lloyd's work suggests that a firefly's flash pattern, far from being a random display, is a highly ______ signal that predators must closely imitate to succeed.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 포식자가 먹잇감 종의 응답 타이밍을 '거의 정확히' 맞춰야만 속임수가 성공한다고 말하므로, 신호는 종마다 고유하고 정밀한, 즉 '특정한(specific)' 것이어야 한다. 그래서 A가 정답이다. B(눈에 잘 띄는)는 빛 신호의 성질로 그럴듯하지만, 정확히 흉내 내야 한다는 논리와 연결되지 않는다. C(가변적인)는 정확한 모방이 필요하다는 점과 정반대 내용이다. D(정교한)는 코드화된 순서라는 표현과 부분적으로 맞지만, 핵심은 복잡함이 아니라 종 고유의 정확한 타이밍이다.
g.explanation_en: The text says predators succeed only by matching a prey species' timing almost exactly, so the signal must be precise and unique to each species, which makes "specific" in A correct. B, "conspicuous," does fit a flash of light, but being easy to see doesn't explain why the copy has to be exact. C, "variable," says the opposite: a signal that kept changing would not need to be matched precisely. D, "elaborate," seems to fit the phrase "coded sequence," but the point is not complexity. It is exact, species-distinct timing.
g.design: Distractors B and D each match a surface feature (light display, coded sequence), so students must connect "random" with "match almost exactly" to choose specificity.

g.passage: Archerfish hunt by spitting jets of water at insects perched on leaves above the surface, a strategy that demands sharp vision across both air and water. Researchers studying the fish's eye found that its nearly spherical lens, combined with a pupil whose shape shifts with lighting, helps ______ chromatic aberration, the blurring that occurs when different wavelengths of light focus at slightly different points. Rather than eliminating the distortion entirely, these features reduce it enough that the fish can resolve small, fast-moving prey with remarkable accuracy.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 빈칸에는 눈의 구조가 색수차에 미치는 영향이 들어가야 하고, 마지막 문장에서 이 구조는 왜곡을 '완전히 없애지 않고' '충분히 줄인다'고 했으므로 '완화하다'라는 뜻의 B가 정답이다. A는 왜곡을 줄인다는 방향은 맞지만 '완전히 없애다'라는 뜻이라 'Rather than eliminating ~ entirely'와 모순된다. C는 연구자들이 수차를 밝혀냈다는 맥락과 연결되어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 수차를 드러내는 것은 눈이 하는 일이 아니고 선명한 시력이라는 기능과도 맞지 않는다. D는 흐림을 더 심하게 만든다는 뜻이라 먹이를 정확히 식별한다는 내용과 반대이다.
g.explanation_en: The blank describes what the eye's structure does to chromatic aberration. The last sentence says these features don't eliminate the distortion "entirely" but "reduce it enough," so B, "mitigate" (to lessen), is the answer. A points in the right direction, but it means to wipe out completely, which contradicts "Rather than eliminating the distortion entirely." C might seem to fit because the researchers discovered the aberration, but revealing distortion isn't something an eye's lens does, and it has nothing to do with seeing clearly. D means to make the blurring worse, which is the opposite of the fish resolving prey accurately.
g.design: 오답 A는 방향은 맞지만 정도가 지나쳐서, 마지막 문장의 'not entirely'를 읽어야만 배제된다. C는 연구 맥락과 이어져 그럴듯하게 보이도록 만들었다. 문맥 두 곳을 연결해야 풀 수 있게 설계했다.

g.passage: When a pond dries up, a tardigrade does not simply die of thirst. Instead, it pulls in its legs, loses nearly all of its body water, and contracts into a shriveled form called a tun, in which its metabolism becomes almost undetectable. Biologist Takekazu Kunieda and colleagues have shown that this state is not a slow decline toward death but a ______ one: when water returns, even after years, many tuns swell, resume moving, and feed as if nothing had happened. This capacity has led some researchers to test whether tuns could survive the vacuum and radiation of space, and several have.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞에서는 이 상태를 '죽음으로 향하는 느린 쇠퇴'와 대조하고, 뒤에서는 물이 돌아오면 다시 움직이고 먹이를 먹는다고 한다. 즉 원래 상태로 되돌아갈 수 있다는 점이 핵심이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 터널 상태가 휴면에 가깝다는 점에서 그럴듯해 보이지만, 이미 앞 문장에서 묘사된 내용이라 '쇠퇴가 아니다'라는 대조와 회복을 정확히 표현하지 못한다. B는 툰이 몸을 보호한다는 점에서 부분적으로 맞지만, 다시 살아나는 회복을 짚지 못한다. D는 '느린 쇠퇴'의 '느림'과 대조되지 않고 오히려 같은 의미여서 논리에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The blank sits in a contrast with "a slow decline toward death," and the next part explains that when water returns, tuns swell, move, and feed again. So the key idea is that the state can be undone, which makes C the best answer. A sounds plausible because the tun is barely active, but the earlier sentence already says that; "dormant" doesn't deliver the contrast with decline or point to the recovery. B fits the idea that the tun shields the animal, but it misses the return to normal life that the colon introduces. D doesn't work as a contrast at all: "gradual" basically repeats the "slow" part of "slow decline."
g.design: 오답 A와 B는 툰의 실제 특성(휴면, 보호)과 맞아 부분적 근거가 있지만, 대조 구조와 콜론 뒤의 회복 설명을 연결해야만 배제된다. D는 겉보기에 말이 되지만 대조 논리와 충돌한다.
