c.seed: earth and space science — Monsoon failure Indian summer rainfall deficit El Niño Southern Oscillation climate teleconnection impact

g.passage: Since the late nineteenth century, meteorologists have observed that El Niño events, which warm the surface waters of the eastern tropical Pacific, tend to coincide with deficient summer monsoon rainfall over India; roughly half of India's severe droughts since 1871 have occurred during El Niño years. ______ this climate teleconnection is far from dependable: in 1997, during one of the strongest El Niño events on record, India received near-normal monsoon rainfall, an outcome researchers later attributed partly to unusual warmth in the western Indian Ocean.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 첫 문장은 엘니뇨와 인도 몬순 강수 부족 사이에 관련이 있다는 점을 인정하고, 둘째 문장은 그 관련이 믿을 만하지 않다며 1997년의 반례를 든다. 앞 내용을 인정한 뒤 뒤집는 양보 후 반전 관계이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 1997년이 사례라는 점에서 그럴듯해 보이지만, 앞 문장의 주장을 뒷받침하는 예가 아니라 반대되는 사례이다. B는 인과 관계를 나타내는데, 연관성이 관찰되었다는 사실 때문에 그 연관성이 불안정해지는 것은 아니다. C는 두 문장이 같은 방향의 내용을 덧붙일 때 쓰는데, 둘째 문장은 첫 문장과 대조된다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence grants that El Niño and deficient Indian monsoon rainfall are linked, and the second says this link is unreliable, using 1997 as a counterexample. That is a concession followed by a reversal, so D is correct. A may look tempting because 1997 is an example, but it doesn't support the claim before it. It contradicts that claim. B signals cause and effect, but observing a link doesn't cause the link to be unreliable. C signals that the second sentence adds a similar point, but here the second sentence contrasts with the first.
g.design: There is no "however"-type cue word. To see the concession and reversal, the reader has to compare the link stated in the first sentence with the counterexample in the second. The wrong options "For example," and "Consequently," each match part of the passage on a quick read.

c.seed: earth and space science — Earthquake focal mechanism fault plane rupture geometry and seismic moment magnitude scale determination

g.passage: When seismologists analyze an earthquake, they often construct a focal mechanism, a diagram based on whether the first P waves recorded at distant stations push the ground upward or pull it downward. This pattern narrows the orientation of the fault to two perpendicular candidate planes. The first-motion data alone, though, cannot show which of the two planes actually slipped, since slip on either one would produce the same pattern of pushes and pulls. ______ when the aftershocks that follow a large earthquake line up along a surface matching one of the candidates, researchers can identify that plane as the fault that ruptured.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 초동 자료만으로는 두 후보면 중 실제로 미끄러진 면을 구별할 수 없다는 한계를 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 여진 분포를 이용하면 그 면을 식별할 수 있다고 말한다. 한계를 제시한 뒤 그것을 극복하는 방법으로 넘어가므로 대조를 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 한계 때문에 추가 자료가 필요해 보여 그럴듯하지만, 여진으로 단층면을 찾을 수 있다는 내용은 '구별할 수 없다'는 사실에서 도출되는 결과가 아니다. C는 뒤 문장이 구체적인 사례처럼 보이지만, 구별할 수 없다는 한계의 예가 아니라 오히려 구별에 성공하는 경우이다. D는 두 문장을 비슷한 내용으로 묶지만, 뒤 문장은 앞의 한계와 같은 종류의 내용이 아니라 반대 방향의 내용이다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank describes a limitation: first-motion data alone can't show which of the two candidate planes slipped. The sentence after the blank explains how aftershock patterns can identify that plane. Because the text moves from a limitation to a way around it, the contrast in A is correct. B is tempting because the limitation suggests more data is needed, but being able to identify the fault from aftershocks doesn't logically follow from the fact that the planes can't be told apart. C may look right because the final sentence is specific, but it doesn't give an example of the limitation; it describes a case where the limitation is overcome. D treats the two sentences as parallel, but the final sentence points in the opposite direction from the limitation instead of adding a similar point.
g.design: There's no contrast word in the text, so students have to see the shift from a limitation to a way of resolving it. B and C each have partial support (the limitation motivates more data, and the last sentence is concrete), and they can only be ruled out by comparing the logic of the two sentences closely.

c.seed: earth and space science — Tornado formation supercell mesocyclone rotation and atmospheric instability severe convective weather development

g.passage: Meteorologists have long known that most strong tornadoes form within supercells, thunderstorms containing a deep, persistently rotating updraft called a mesocyclone. Modern Doppler radar can now spot a mesocyclone many minutes before any funnel reaches the ground, giving forecasters an early signal of danger. ______ the majority of supercells with clearly detected mesocyclones never produce a tornado at all, a fact that has pushed researchers to study conditions near the surface, such as low-level wind shear and the temperature of air sinking out of the storm.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장들은 메소사이클론이 토네이도와 관련되고 레이더로 일찍 탐지되어 위험 신호가 된다고 말한다. 빈칸 뒤 문장은 탐지된 메소사이클론 대부분이 토네이도를 만들지 않는다고 하므로, 앞의 기대를 뒤집는 양보 후 반전 관계이다. 그래서 B가 정답이다. A는 뒤 문장을 앞 주장의 사례로 보지만, 뒤 문장은 앞 주장을 뒷받침하지 않고 오히려 한계를 보여 준다. C는 레이더 탐지가 토네이도 미발생의 원인인 것처럼 만들고, D는 두 내용이 서로 비슷하다고 잘못 연결한다.
g.explanation_en: The earlier sentences say that tornadoes are linked to mesocyclones and that radar can spot these early as a sign of danger. The sentence after the blank says most detected mesocyclones never produce a tornado, so it pushes back against what you would expect from that warning sign. This is a concession followed by a reversal, which is why B is correct. A treats the last sentence as an example backing up the earlier point, but it actually shows a limit of that point. C makes radar detection sound like the cause of tornadoes not forming, and D wrongly says the two ideas are alike.
g.design: 빈칸 앞뒤에 대조를 나타내는 단어를 두지 않았다. 학생은 '메소사이클론 탐지=위험 신호'라는 기대와 '대부분 토네이도를 만들지 않음'이라는 사실을 직접 이어 봐야 반전 관계를 알 수 있다. A와 C는 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯해 보이게 만들었다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: earth and space science — Salt marsh accretion sediment deposition and sea level rise vulnerability coastal wetland sustainability

g.passage: Salt marshes can keep pace with rising seas only if sediment deposition, the gradual settling of silt and clay carried in by tides and rivers, raises the marsh surface quickly enough. Over a decade of fieldwork in Louisiana's Barataria Basin, geologist Lena Okafor uncovered a striking contrast in accretion rates______ marshes fed by nearby river diversions gained nearly a centimeter of elevation per year, while isolated marshes gained only a few millimeters.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Over a decade ... in accretion rates"는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "marshes ... gained ... per year, while ..."도 동사 gained를 가진 독립절이다. 뒤 절은 앞에서 말한 '뚜렷한 차이'의 구체적 내용이므로 두 독립절을 잇고 설명을 덧붙이는 콜론을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 with가 뒤를 전치사구로 만들려 하지만 정동사 gained가 남아 있어 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The part before the blank, "Over a decade ... in accretion rates," is an independent clause, and the part after it, "marshes ... gained ... per year, while ...," is also an independent clause because it has its own main verb, gained. The second clause spells out the "striking contrast" mentioned in the first, so a colon, which joins two independent clauses and introduces an explanation, works best, which makes C correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. B puts the clauses together with no punctuation at all, which is a run-on sentence. D adds "with," which should turn the second part into a prepositional phrase, but the main verb "gained" is still there, so the sentence doesn't work grammatically.
g.design: An appositive and a long prepositional opener hide the clause boundary. Students need to see that "gained" is a main verb and that the second clause explains "contrast," so they must both apply the rule and check the context.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

g.passage: During the day, sunlight warms the ground, and rising plumes of heated air churn the lowest kilometer or so of the atmosphere, a region meteorologists call the boundary layer, until temperature and humidity are nearly uniform from the surface to its top______ after sunset, this turbulence collapses, leaving a shallow, stable layer of cool air near the ground beneath a calmer "residual layer" above.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞(During the day ... to its top)과 뒤(after sunset, this turbulence collapses ...)는 각각 독립절이므로 세미콜론으로 나누고 접속부사 however 뒤에 쉼표를 찍은 D가 정답이다. A는 however 양쪽에 쉼표를 두어 삽입어처럼 보이지만 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. B는 절 사이에 아무 경계 부호가 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. C는 세미콜론을 쓰긴 했지만 however 뒤에 두어 however가 앞 절에 붙게 되므로, 대조가 뒤 절을 이끄는 문맥과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank (During the day ... to its top) and the text after it (after sunset, this turbulence collapses ...) are both independent clauses, so D is correct: it separates them with a semicolon and puts a comma after the conjunctive adverb "however." A sets "however" off with commas as if it were an interrupter, but that joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. B has no punctuation marking the boundary between the clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence. C does use a semicolon, but it puts it after "however," which attaches "however" to the first clause even though the contrast is supposed to introduce the second clause.
g.design: The long appositive and the "until" clause hide where the main clause ends. Students have to find the boundary between the two independent clauses and then figure out which clause "however" belongs to; A and C each get part of this right.

c.seed: earth and space science — Glacier surging rapid acceleration sliding and drainage system evolution Greenland ice sheet dynamics

g.passage: Glaciologists studying surge-type glaciers in Greenland have long puzzled over their abrupt shift from sluggish flow to rapid sliding. According to one model, meltwater trapped beneath the ice in a network of poorly connected cavities builds pressure until the glacier lifts slightly off its bed and accelerates______ once those cavities merge into efficient drainage channels, the water escapes, friction returns, and the surge stalls.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "meltwater ... accelerates"와 빈칸 뒤 "once ... the water escapes ... stalls"는 각각 독립절이다. "then"은 등위접속사가 아니라 접속부사이므로 두 독립절을 이으려면 세미콜론이 필요하며, A가 이를 충족한다. B와 C는 쉼표와 then만으로 두 독립절을 연결해 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 run-on 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("meltwater ... accelerates") and the text after it ("once ... the water escapes ... and the surge stalls") are both independent clauses. "Then" is a conjunctive adverb, not a coordinating conjunction, so it can't join two independent clauses by itself. A semicolon has to come before it, and that is what A does. B and C use only a comma with "then," which creates a comma splice. D has no punctuation between the two clauses at all, so it creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: The first clause carries a long modifier ("in a network of poorly connected cavities") and the second clause opens with a subordinate clause beginning "once," so students have to find both main clauses before they can choose the boundary. Choices B and C look acceptable because "then" can be mistaken for a conjunction.

g.passage: Each winter, the Harmattan, a dry northeasterly trade wind that sweeps across the Sahara toward the Gulf of Guinea, lifts fine mineral dust from the Bodélé Depression in Chad ______ settles on farmland in Nigeria and Ghana, where its phosphorus can modestly enrich nutrient-poor soils.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , a portion of that dust later
; a portion of that dust later
a portion of that dust later
, and, a portion of that dust later
g.explanation: 긴 동격구(a dry northeasterly trade wind ... Gulf of Guinea)를 걷어내면 주절은 "the Harmattan ... lifts fine mineral dust ... in Chad"이고, 빈칸 뒤 "a portion of that dust later settles ..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 결합 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 이어 run-on 문장이 된다. D는 등위접속사 and를 쓴 점은 맞지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가 있다.
g.explanation_en: If you set aside the long appositive (a dry northeasterly trade wind ... Gulf of Guinea), the main clause is "the Harmattan ... lifts fine mineral dust ... in Chad." The words after the blank, "a portion of that dust later settles ...," also form an independent clause with its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses, which makes a run-on sentence. D is right to use the conjunction "and," but the extra comma after "and" is incorrect.
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 긴 동격 삽입구와 전치사구를 넣어 절 경계를 찾기 어렵게 했다. 오답 A와 D는 각각 쉼표, 접속사라는 부분적으로 그럴듯한 근거를 가지고 있어서 정답과 비교해야만 걸러진다.

g.passage: Because rising magma heats the rock above it, satellite thermal sensors can sometimes detect warming at a volcano's surface weeks before an eruption. At Mount Etna in Italy, for example, measured heat flow near the summit craters, a value that normally changes very little from one decade to the next, climbed sharply in early 2021______ it rose to roughly ten times its usual level shortly before a series of lava fountains began.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격구(a value that ... next)를 지나면 주절의 동사 climbed가 나오고, 빈칸 뒤 it rose도 독립절이다. 따라서 두 독립절 사이에는 세미콜론 같은 경계가 필요하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 경계 문장부호가 아예 없어 무종지문이 된다. D는 which가 관계절을 시작하는데 뒤에 주어 it이 또 있어 관계절이 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Once you get past the long appositive (a value that ... next), you find the main verb climbed, and the words after the blank, it rose, form a second independent clause. Two independent clauses need a real boundary, so C, with a semicolon, is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B has no punctuation at the boundary at all, so it creates a run-on sentence. D starts a relative clause with which, but the clause already has its own subject, it, so the relative clause is ungrammatical.
g.design: The appositive between the subject and the verb hides where the first clause ends. The wrong answers use a comma splice, a run-on, and a relative pronoun, and each looks plausible if you only skim.

g.passage: At Yellowstone's Old Faithful, eruptions recur at intervals that geologists can predict with surprising accuracy. The explanation lies underground, where groundwater seeps into a narrow conduit and a side chamber, is heated by rock above a magma reservoir, and builds pressure until steam bursts through the vent. Each eruption also leaves behind dissolved silica that hardens into sinter, the pale mineral crust that slowly builds the geyser's ______ the conduit then refills, and the cycle of pressure buildup begins again.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Each eruption also leaves ... builds the geyser's cone"은 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 "the conduit then refills, and the cycle ... begins again"도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 'after each eruption'은 '다시 채워진다'는 뒤 절을 꾸미는 말이므로 마침표로 두 절을 나누고 이 구를 뒤 문장 앞에 두는 D가 맞다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B도 쉼표만으로 두 절을 이어 같은 오류가 생기고, 수식 관계까지 흐려진다. C는 두 독립절 사이에 문장부호가 아예 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "Each eruption also leaves ... builds the geyser's cone," is a complete independent clause. The text after it, "the conduit then refills, and the cycle ... begins again," is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. The phrase "after each eruption" tells us when the conduit refills, so D is correct: it ends the first sentence with a period and starts the next sentence with that phrase. A connects the two independent clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. B has the same comma splice problem and also makes it unclear what the phrase modifies. C puts no punctuation at all between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: 긴 동격 수식어(sinter, the pale mineral crust...) 뒤에서 절 경계를 판단하고, 부사구가 어느 절에 속하는지 문맥으로 확인하게 했다. A와 B는 부사구 처리가 그럴듯해 보이지만 comma splice라서 오답이다.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞 절이 긴 분사구(carrying...)로 끝나고 뒤 절 안에 삽입구(though brief and patchy)가 있어서, 두 독립절의 경계를 정확히 찾아야 풀 수 있게 했다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 "cold water ... rises ... zone"은 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤의 "this upwelling ... helps sustain ..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 접속사 없이 연결하려면 세미콜론이 필요하므로 정답은 A이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 "and" 뒤에 쉼표를 두어 등위접속사 앞에 와야 할 쉼표가 잘못된 자리에 있고, 그 결과 "and, this upwelling, though..."처럼 구두점이 어색하게 끊긴다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("cold water ... rises ... into the sunlit zone") make an independent clause, and the words after it ("this upwelling ... helps sustain ...") make another independent clause with its own subject and verb. When you join two independent clauses without a conjunction, you need a semicolon, so A is correct. B links the clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D puts the comma after "and" when it belongs before the coordinating conjunction, so the punctuation breaks up the sentence in the wrong place.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: earth and space science — Atmospheric dust aerosol optical depth measurement and radiative forcing reduction solar insolation penetration

g.passage: Aerosol optical depth, a measure of how strongly airborne particles such as Saharan dust block sunlight before it reaches the ground, can rise sharply during major dust ______ in June 2020, for example, satellite instruments recorded values over the tropical Atlantic several times above the seasonal average, and the solar energy reaching the ocean surface fell accordingly.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격구를 걷어내면 'Aerosol optical depth ... can rise sharply during major dust outbreaks'는 완전한 독립절이며, 빈칸 뒤 'in June 2020, ... satellite instruments recorded values ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 맞으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. C는 관계대명사 which 뒤에 이미 주어(satellite instruments)와 목적어(values)가 다 있어 which가 문장 안에서 맡을 역할이 없다. D는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다.
g.explanation_en: If you set aside the long appositive, "Aerosol optical depth ... can rise sharply during major dust outbreaks" is a complete independent clause. The text after the blank, "in June 2020, ... satellite instruments recorded values ...," is also independent because it has its own subject and verb. Two independent clauses with no conjunction between them should be joined with a semicolon, so B is correct. A uses only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C adds "which," but the clause after it already has a subject (satellite instruments) and an object (values), so "which" has no job to do in the sentence. D puts the two clauses together with no punctuation, which makes a run-on sentence.
g.design: 긴 동격 수식어 때문에 주절이 끝나는 지점이 잘 안 보이게 했고, 빈칸 뒤에 삽입구 'for example'을 넣어 두 번째 절도 독립절인지 확인해야 풀리도록 했다. 관계사 오답(C)은 얼핏 자연스럽게 읽히도록 만들었다.

c.seed: earth and space science — Sediment core varve chronology annual layer counting and paleoclimate reconstruction glacial meltwater discharge records

g.passage: In glacial lakes, each year typically leaves behind a pair of sediment bands: a coarse, pale layer deposited by summer meltwater and a fine, dark layer that settles under winter ice. By counting these paired bands, known as varves, geologist Gerard De Geer built one of the first year-by-year chronologies of the end of the last ice age. Modern researchers have refined his method in one important ______ the thickness of each summer layer as a rough measure of how much meltwater the retreating glacier released that year.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 뒤에 독립절이 오므로 절 경계 판단과, 앞 절의 'one important way'를 뒤 절이 구체화한다는 문맥 확인이 함께 필요하다. 쉼표 분사구(B)는 문법적으로는 그럴듯해 보여서 비교해 봐야 배제된다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Modern researchers have refined his method in one important way'는 독립절이고, 뒤의 'they now treat ... that year'도 독립절이다. 뒤 절이 '한 가지 중요한 방식'이 무엇인지 구체적으로 설명하므로 콜론을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이은 쉼표 오류(comma splice)이다. B는 문장 자체는 성립하지만, 분사구가 'way'를 정의하는 것이 아니라 주어가 동시에 하는 행동처럼 읽혀 'one important way'가 구체적으로 무엇인지 분명히 연결해 주지 못한다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)으로, 'way they now treat'가 관계절처럼 잘못 읽힌다.
g.explanation_en: The part before the blank, "Modern researchers have refined his method in one important way," is an independent clause, and so is the part after it, "they now treat ... that year." Because the second clause tells you exactly what that "one important way" is, a colon is the right connector, so C is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes it a comma splice. B looks grammatical, but the participial phrase reads like something the researchers are doing at the same time, so it never clearly spells out what the "one important way" is. D runs the two clauses together with no punctuation, which creates a run-on and makes "way they now treat" read like a relative clause by mistake.

c.seed: earth and space science — Scoria cone formation basaltic pyroclastic eruption and cinder cone morphology volcanic landform classification

g.passage: Scoria cones, often called cinder cones, form when gas-rich basaltic magma erupts in fountains that hurl clots of lava into the air. The fragments cool and fall back around the vent, building a steep, symmetrical hill. Because these loose fragments are poorly bonded, volcanologists Kelsey Marrin and Tomás Ibarra note that a young cone's slopes ______ the angle at which piled gravel stops sliding: the sides sit at roughly 30 to 33 degrees, and steeper sections soon slump back to that limit.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 느슨한 파편으로 된 사면이 약 30~33도에 머물고, 더 가파른 부분은 그 한계로 다시 무너진다고 설명하므로 사면 각도는 자갈의 안식각과 '대략 같다'는 뜻의 D가 맞다. A는 '초과하다'인데, 경사가 가파르다는 표현에 끌릴 수 있지만 더 가파른 부분은 무너져 한계로 돌아온다고 했으므로 모순이다. B는 '가리다'로, 각도를 감춘다는 내용은 지문에 없다. C는 '~보다 먼저 존재하다'로, 시간 순서를 말하는 단어라 각도 비교와 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the loose slopes sit at about 30 to 33 degrees and that steeper parts slump back to that limit, so the slopes roughly match the angle at which gravel stops sliding. That makes D, "approximate," the answer. A, "surpass," may tempt you because the cones are called steep, but the text says any steeper section falls back to the limit, so the slopes don't go beyond it. B, "obscure," means to hide, and nothing in the text says the slopes hide the angle. C, "predate," is about which came first in time, which doesn't fit a comparison of angles.
g.design: 'steep', 'steeper' 같은 단어 때문에 A를 고르기 쉽게 했다. 하지만 '경사가 한계로 되돌아온다'는 정보와 연결해야 비로소 D를 고를 수 있도록 두 단계 판단을 요구했다.

c.seed: earth and space science — Salt dome buoyancy diapirism and piercing through overlying sedimentary strata petroleum trap formation mechanism

g.passage: Rock salt is less dense than the sandstones and shales that typically accumulate above it, so a thick salt layer buried deep underground is inherently unstable. Over millions of years, the salt slowly flows upward in columns known as diapirs. Geologists emphasize, however, that the salt does not merely push the overlying strata upward; as a diapir rises, it ______ those layers, cutting through them so that their broken edges end up tilted against the salt's flanks. These sealed, upturned edges are where petroleum often collects, which is why salt domes have long been prime drilling targets.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 염류가 위 지층을 "단지 밀어 올리는 것이 아니라" 그 지층을 "뚫고 지나가" 끊어진 가장자리가 측면에 기울어진다고 설명하므로, 관통한다는 뜻의 A가 정답이다. B는 밀어 올린다는 뜻으로, 지문이 "not merely push upward"라며 대조한 바로 그 의미이므로 맞지 않는다. C는 상승하는 암염이 지층에 압력을 가한다는 점에서 일부 그럴듯하지만, 지층을 잘라 낸다는 내용을 담지 못한다. D는 지층이 사라지고 염류로 대체된다는 뜻이 되는데, 지층은 기울어진 채 남아 석유를 가두므로 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the salt does not merely push the layers upward but cuts through them, which leaves their broken edges tilted against the diapir. That makes A, "penetrates," the right answer. B means lifting, which is exactly the "push upward" idea that the text sets up as the contrast. C fits the idea of pressure from rising salt, but it doesn't capture the cutting-through action. D would mean the layers disappear and salt takes their place, yet the text says the layers stay, tilted, and trap petroleum.
g.design: "not merely push upward"라는 대조 신호와 "cutting through"라는 설명을 연결해야 하는 두 단계 판단이다. 훑어 읽으면 상승 이미지 때문에 B나 C를 고르기 쉽게 만들었다.

c.seed: earth and space science — Barchan dune migration rate wind shear stress and sand grain transport across desert floor progression

g.passage: Barchan dunes, the crescent-shaped mounds found on flat desert floors, migrate downwind as wind lifts sand grains from their gentle windward slopes and deposits them over the crest. Geomorphologist Hezlin Adebayo found that a barchan's migration rate is ______ its size: when she compared dunes exposed to the same winds, small barchans advanced several times faster than large ones, because a smaller dune must move far less sand to shift its whole body forward by a given distance.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 같은 바람 조건에서 작은 바르한이 큰 바르한보다 몇 배 빠르게 이동한다고 하므로, 크기가 커질수록 이동 속도가 줄어드는 관계, 즉 B 'inversely related to'가 정답이다. A는 크기와 속도 사이에 관계가 있다고 연구자가 확인했다는 점에서 맞지 않는다. C는 크기와 속도가 관련 있다는 점은 맞지만, 방향이 반대여서 큰 사구가 더 빠르다는 뜻이 된다. D는 크기가 속도를 측정하기 어렵게 만든다는 뜻인데, 지문은 측정의 어려움이 아니라 명확한 비교 결과를 제시한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says that under the same winds, small barchans advanced several times faster than large ones, so speed goes down as size goes up. That's why B, "inversely related to," is correct. A doesn't work because the researcher found a clear link between size and speed. C does connect size and speed, but it points the wrong way: it would mean larger dunes move faster. D would mean that size makes the migration rate hard to observe, but the text describes a clear comparison, not a problem with measuring.
g.design: To answer, the student has to combine two pieces of information: that size and speed are related, and that the relationship runs in the opposite direction (small dunes move faster). The distractor C catches students who skim and notice only that the two are related, and A catches students who fixate on the "same winds" condition.

c.seed: earth and space science — Permafrost carbon pool thaw release and greenhouse gas feedback loop Arctic climate amplification concern

g.passage: Arctic permafrost holds roughly twice as much carbon as the atmosphere currently does, much of it locked in frozen plant matter that has accumulated over thousands of years. As rising temperatures thaw this ground, microbes break down the material and release carbon dioxide and methane, which trap additional heat and accelerate further thawing. Climate scientist Merritt Turetsky and colleagues caution that because this cycle can ______ itself once underway, emissions from thawing soils may continue to grow even if human emissions are reduced, making the process difficult to halt through policy alone.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.design: 'release', 'warm'처럼 지문 표면 어휘와 연결되는 오답을 두어, 피드백 순환이 스스로 지속된다는 논리(인간 배출 감소와 무관하게 계속 증가)를 연결해야 정답을 고를 수 있게 했다.
g.explanation: 지문은 해빙이 온실가스를 배출하고 그 가스가 다시 해빙을 가속하는 순환을 설명하며, 이 순환이 인간 배출이 줄어도 계속될 수 있다고 한다. 따라서 순환이 일단 시작되면 '스스로를 지속시킨다'는 뜻의 C가 가장 논리적이다. A는 지문에서 가스가 배출된다는 내용과 연결되지만, 순환이 '자기 자신을 배출한다'는 표현은 의미가 성립하지 않는다. B는 온난화와 관련은 있지만, 순환이 '자신을 데운다'는 말은 부정확하며 정책으로 멈추기 어렵다는 지속성의 논리를 담지 못한다. D는 숨긴다는 뜻으로, 배출이 계속 늘어난다는 문맥과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text describes a loop: thawing releases gases, and those gases cause more thawing. It also says emissions may keep growing even if human emissions drop, so the cycle must be able to keep itself going once it starts. That makes C the most logical choice. A ties back to the gases being "released," but a cycle can't sensibly "release itself." B connects to warming, but saying a cycle "warms itself" is imprecise and misses the idea that the process keeps running on its own, which is why it's hard to stop. D means to hide, and that doesn't fit a text about emissions that keep growing.

g.passage: In epithermal ore deposits, gold and silver are carried upward by hot, metal-rich fluids moving through fractures in volcanic rock. Geologist Ana Ruiz and colleagues found that the metals rarely settle out gradually along the length of a fracture. Instead, they ______ abruptly at the depth where pressure drops enough for the fluid to boil: boiling strips dissolved gases from the fluid, the metal sulfides can no longer stay in solution, and dense bands of ore crystallize within a few meters of that zone.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 금속이 서서히 쌓이는 대신 끓는 깊이에서 갑자기 용액 밖으로 빠져나와 광석 띠로 결정화된다고 설명하므로, 용액에서 고체로 '침전하다'는 D가 정확하다. A의 '용해되다'는 금속 황화물이 더 이상 용액에 남을 수 없다는 내용과 정반대이다. B의 '흩어지다'는 갑작스러운 변화라는 점은 맞지만 몇 미터 안에 밀집된 띠가 생긴다는 내용과 충돌한다. C의 '이동하다'는 유체가 위로 움직인다는 점과 연결되지만, 금속이 특정 깊이에서 고체로 굳는다는 핵심을 담지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the metals don't settle out gradually but instead come out of solution suddenly at the boiling depth and crystallize as dense ore bands, so "precipitate" (D) is the precise word. A, "dissolve," is the opposite of what happens, since the text says the sulfides can no longer stay in solution. B, "disperse," fits the idea of a sudden change, but it clashes with the dense bands forming within a few meters. C, "migrate," connects to the fluid moving upward, but it misses the key point that the metals turn solid at one specific depth.
g.design: 두 단계 판단을 요구한다. 먼저 'Instead' 대조를 보고 갑작스러운 변화라는 점을 파악한 뒤, 이것을 '용액에 남을 수 없음'·'결정화' 단서와 연결해야 한다. 훑어 읽는 학생은 B와 C를 고르도록 유도했다.

c.seed: earth and space science — Storm surge overwash and salt marsh platform erosion relative sea level rise vulnerability assessment

g.passage: Coastal geologists assessing salt marsh vulnerability to relative sea level rise have long focused on whether sediment accumulation can keep a marsh platform's elevation in step with rising water. A 2021 study of barrier-backed marshes, however, suggests that storm surge overwash may ______ that picture: although overwash deposits can add sediment to the platform interior, the same surges often erode the marsh edge so severely that the platform's total area shrinks even as its surface rises.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 기존 평가가 고도 유지 여부에만 집중했는데, 월파가 내부에는 퇴적물을 더하면서도 가장자리를 침식해 면적을 줄인다고 말한다. 즉 고도가 높아져도 취약성이 남을 수 있다는 상반된 효과가 기존 관점을 더 복잡하게 만든다는 뜻이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 퇴적물 추가가 고도 유지 관점에 부합하는 듯 보이지만, 'however'와 면적 감소라는 반대 효과와 맞지 않는다. C는 새로운 변수가 더해지는 상황이므로 반대 방향이다. D는 기존 관점의 사례가 된다는 뜻이지만, 지문은 그 관점이 놓친 점을 보여 준다.
g.explanation_en: The text says assessments used to focus only on whether a marsh's elevation keeps up with sea level, but overwash adds sediment to the interior while eroding the edge, so the marsh loses area. Those opposing effects make the old picture more complex, so A is correct. B might look right because the added sediment fits the elevation focus, but "however" and the shrinking area point the other way. C is the opposite, since the study adds a new factor rather than removing one. D would mean the study is an example of the old view, but the text shows something that view leaves out.
g.design: 'however'로 기존 관점과 대조하고, 퇴적 증가와 면적 감소라는 두 정보를 연결해야 정답을 고를 수 있게 했다. 퇴적물 추가 부분만 훑어 읽으면 confirm이나 illustrate를 고르기 쉽게 설계했다.

c.seed: earth and space science — Albedo feedback snow ice melt and reduced solar reflectivity accelerating polar climate warming

g.passage: Fresh snow and sea ice reflect most of the sunlight that strikes them, while open ocean and bare ground absorb far more. Climate scientists note that as polar ice melts, the darker surfaces it exposes take in additional solar energy, which warms the region and causes still more ice to melt. Because each round of melting sets up conditions for the next, this albedo feedback tends to ______ the initial warming rather than merely sustaining it, helping explain why the Arctic has warmed faster than the global average.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 융해가 다음 융해를 부르는 자기강화 과정을 설명하고, '단순히 유지하는 것이 아니라(rather than merely sustaining)'라는 대비와 북극이 더 빨리 따뜻해진다는 결과를 제시하므로 초기 온난화를 '증폭한다'는 B가 정답이다. A는 상쇄한다는 뜻으로 피드백의 방향과 정반대이다. C는 온난화를 '지속시킨다'는 점에서 부분적으로 그럴듯하지만, 지문이 배제한 '단순 유지'와 같은 의미여서 강화의 뜻을 담지 못한다. D는 드러낸다는 뜻으로 얼음이 어두운 표면을 '드러낸다'는 내용과 표면적으로 연결되지만, 온난화에 미치는 영향을 설명하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The text describes a self-reinforcing loop in which each round of melting sets up the next one. It also contrasts the effect with "merely sustaining" the warming and ties it to the Arctic warming faster than the rest of the globe, so B ("amplify") is the right answer. A means to counteract, which runs in the opposite direction from this feedback. C looks reasonable because the warming does continue, but "prolong" is basically the "merely sustaining" idea the text rules out, so it misses the sense of intensification. D echoes the point that melting ice exposes darker surfaces, but "reveal" doesn't describe how the feedback affects the warming.
g.design: To answer, students have to connect the self-reinforcing loop with the "rather than merely sustaining" contrast. C (sustain) and D (exposing surfaces) are partly supported, so students must compare them carefully to rule them out.

g.passage: Along subduction zones, the boundary between two tectonic plates is not uniformly locked. Seismologists have found that certain patches, called asperities, stick firmly and accumulate strain, while neighboring zones of weaker, creeping rock slip gradually. Some researchers argue that these creeping zones act as barriers during a megathrust earthquake: a rupture that begins at one asperity tends to stall when it reaches such a zone rather than spreading along the fault. If this view is correct, the presence of creeping segments would ______ the size of the earthquakes a fault can produce, an implication that matters greatly for estimating regional seismic hazard.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 크리핑 구간이 장벽 역할을 해 파열이 단층을 따라 퍼지지 않고 멈춘다고 설명하므로, 이런 구간은 지진 규모를 '제한'한다는 C가 정답이다. A는 크리핑 구간이 규모 추정에 쓰일 수 있다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 지문은 연구자의 예측이 아니라 구간이 파열에 미치는 물리적 효과를 말한다. B는 장벽이 파열을 멈추게 한다는 내용과 정반대다. D는 크리핑 구간이 정보를 줄 수 있다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 파열을 멈추게 한다는 인과 관계를 담지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says creeping zones act as barriers that make a rupture stall instead of spreading along the fault, so these zones would cap, or limit, how large an earthquake can become. That makes C correct. A sounds plausible because the passage mentions hazard estimates, but the blank describes a physical effect the zones have on ruptures, not a forecast scientists make. B is the opposite of what a barrier does, since stopping a rupture would not make earthquakes bigger. D might seem reasonable because the zones could tell scientists something, but it leaves out the cause-and-effect idea of a rupture being stopped.
g.design: 정답을 고르려면 '장벽→파열이 멈춤'이라는 내용과 '규모'를 연결해야 한다. A와 D는 hazard 추정이라는 문맥을 근거로 끌어들이는 부분 정답형 오답이다.

c.seed: earth and space science — Atmospheric river moisture transport and orographic precipitation extreme rainfall event generation mechanism

g.passage: Atmospheric rivers—long, narrow corridors of water vapor flowing from the tropics—can carry more moisture than the largest rivers on land. Yet over open ocean, many of them produce only modest rain. According to atmospheric scientist F. Martin Ralph and colleagues, the extreme downpours tied to these systems usually begin only when the moist air meets a mountain range: forced upward, the air cools and its vapor condenses quickly. The mountains, in other words, do not supply the water themselves; rather, they ______ the release of moisture that the atmospheric river has already carried far inland.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 산이 수분 자체를 공급하지는 않지만, 공기를 들어 올려 이미 운반된 수증기가 비로 쏟아지게 만든다고 설명한다. 따라서 이미 존재하는 것의 방출을 '촉발하다'라는 뜻의 D(trigger)가 가장 정확하다. A(generate)는 비를 일으킨다는 점에서 그럴듯해 보이지만, '산이 물을 공급하지 않는다'는 대조 구조와 충돌한다. 새로 만들어 낸다는 의미를 담기 때문이다. B(postpone)는 공기가 내륙까지 이동한 뒤 비가 내린다는 점에서 지연처럼 읽힐 수 있으나, 산은 비를 미루는 것이 아니라 시작시키는 역할을 한다. C(conceal)는 수분이 바다 위에서는 드러나지 않는다는 점과 어렴풋이 연결될 뿐, 방출을 '숨긴다'는 뜻이라 문맥과 정반대다.
g.explanation_en: The text says mountains don't supply the water themselves; instead, they force the air upward so that vapor the river already carried condenses into heavy rain. A word meaning "set off the release of something that already exists" fits, so D (trigger) is correct. A (generate) looks tempting because the mountains do cause rain, but it means creating something new, which clashes with the "do not supply the water themselves" contrast. B (postpone) might seem to fit because the rain comes only after the air travels inland, but the mountains start the release rather than delay it. C (conceal) loosely echoes the modest rain over the ocean, but saying the mountains "hide" the release is the opposite of what the text describes.
g.design: '산이 물을 공급하지 않는다; rather' 대조 구조와 이미 운반된 수분이라는 정보를 함께 연결해야 generate를 배제할 수 있도록 설계했다. postpone과 conceal도 지문의 일부 정보에 기대고 있어 겉보기에는 그럴듯하다.

g.passage: In many temperate lakes, summer warming creates a sharp boundary, the thermocline, between a warm surface layer and a cold, dense bottom layer called the hypolimnion. Because the two layers resist mixing, oxygen consumed by bacteria decomposing organic matter in the hypolimnion is not replaced from the surface. By late summer, limnologist Rosa Ferreira found, the bottom waters of the lakes she studied were not merely low in oxygen but entirely ______ it, a condition that allowed phosphorus to escape from sediments into the water.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 산소가 보충되지 않는다고 설명하고, "단지 산소가 적은 것이 아니라 완전히 ~한"이라는 대비 구조를 사용하므로 산소가 전혀 없다는 의미의 A가 정답이다. B는 바닥 생물이 산소에 의존한다는 배경 지식과 연결되어 그럴듯하지만, 산소가 없는 상태를 나타내지 못한다. C는 산소와 관련된 표현이지만 정반대 의미이다. D는 산소가 줄어든다는 흐름과 비슷해 보이지만, 물이 산소에 '의해' 줄어든다는 뜻이 되어 논리가 맞지 않고 "완전히"라는 강조도 표현하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that oxygen in the bottom layer is used up and never replaced. It then sets up a contrast: the water was "not merely low in oxygen but entirely ______ it." That contrast calls for a total lack of oxygen, so A is correct. B might seem tempting because organisms in the water need oxygen, but it doesn't describe oxygen being gone. C means the exact opposite. D seems to match the idea of oxygen loss, but it would mean the water was reduced by oxygen, which doesn't make sense, and it doesn't capture the "entirely" contrast either.
g.design: "not merely ... but entirely" 대비 구조와 산소 고갈 과정을 연결해야 풀리게 했다. 오답은 산소와 연관된 그럴듯한 구(의존, 감소)로 구성했다.

c.seed: earth and space science — Volcanic ash fall distribution plume height dispersion and atmospheric circulation transport distance

g.passage: When a volcano erupts explosively, the height of its ash plume largely determines how far the ash will travel. Ash injected only a few kilometers into the atmosphere tends to settle close to the vent, but ash lofted into the stratosphere can be caught by fast, steady winds and carried across entire ocean basins. For this reason, volcanologist Ana Ribeiro argues that forecasts of ash fall should not rely on distance from the volcano alone; a town far downwind of a towering plume may face a greater hazard than a nearby town upwind of a modest one. In Ribeiro's view, distance from the vent is therefore a ______ indicator of risk, useful only when considered alongside plume height and prevailing wind direction.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: Ribeiro는 화구로부터의 거리가 분연 높이·풍향과 함께 고려될 때에만 '유용하다'고 말하므로, 거리는 위험의 일부만 알려 주는 지표, 즉 B(partial)가 가장 정확하다. A는 거리만 믿으면 안 된다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 거리가 '유용하다'는 진술과 충돌한다. C는 거리만으로 판단하지 말라는 주장과 정반대이다. D는 거리가 전혀 의미 없다는 뜻이 되어 '유용하다'는 단서와 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Ribeiro says distance is useful only when combined with plume height and wind direction, so distance tells part of the story about risk, which makes B (partial) the most precise choice. A looks tempting because she warns against relying on distance alone, but calling distance misleading conflicts with her statement that it is still useful. C contradicts her argument, since she rejects treating distance as enough by itself. D would mean distance hardly matters at all, which also clashes with the word "useful."
g.design: 중간 난이도에 맞춰 두 단서(거리만 믿지 말 것 + 그래도 유용함)를 함께 읽어야 풀리게 했다. A와 D는 첫 번째 단서만 보고 고르기 쉬운 함정이다.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Rivers build landforms by depositing sediment in different settings.
- Overbank deposition occurs when a river floods and spills over its banks onto the surrounding floodplain.
- During overbank flooding, water spreads out and slows, so mostly fine silt and clay settle in thin, widespread layers.
- An alluvial fan forms where a steep mountain stream exits onto a flat valley floor and abruptly loses its confining channel.
- On an alluvial fan, the sudden drop in flow energy causes coarse gravel and sand to be dumped near the fan's apex, and the fan gradually extends outward over time.
g.question: The student wants to contrast the kinds of material left behind in the two depositional settings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

Both overbank deposition and alluvial fans form when moving water loses energy, causing the sediment it carries to settle out.

g.explanation_en: Your goal is to contrast the materials deposited in the two settings. g.question: The student wants to present a drawback of a common dune management approach. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

At Hayle Towans and elsewhere, managers now cut gaps in dune vegetation so that wind can once again move sand across the dunes.
At Hayle Towans, as on many coasts, dunes formed when wind-blown sand was trapped by obstacles such as marram grass and other plants.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- At subduction zones, an oceanic plate sinks beneath another plate, forming a deep trench along the boundary.
- At some margins, such as the Cascadia margin off the Pacific Northwest, sediment scraped off the sinking plate piles up into a thick accretionary wedge, so the overriding plate grows seaward.
- At other margins, such as the Peru-Chile margin, the sinking plate grinds away rock from the underside and front of the overriding plate, a process called subduction erosion.
- Subduction erosion drags overriding-plate material down into the mantle, causing the edge of that plate to retreat landward and the trench to deepen over time.
- Geologists estimate that subduction erosion removes roughly 1.3 cubic kilometers of crust from the world's continental margins each year.
g.question: The student wants to contrast how the overriding plate changes at the two kinds of margins. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: At subduction zones such as the Cascadia and Peru-Chile margins, an oceanic plate sinks beneath another plate, and a deep trench forms along the boundary between them.

At the Peru-Chile margin, subduction erosion drags overriding-plate material into the mantle, and worldwide the process removes roughly 1.3 cubic kilometers of crust from continental margins each year.
At the Cascadia margin, scraped-off sediment builds a wedge that extends the overriding plate seaward, whereas at the Peru-Chile margin, erosion from below makes that plate's edge retreat landward.
At the Cascadia margin, sediment scraped off the sinking plate piles up into a thick accretionary wedge, a feature that forms where the oceanic plate meets the overriding plate.
g.explanation: 목표는 두 유형의 섭입대에서 상부 판이 어떻게 달라지는지 대조하는 것이다. C는 캐스케이디아에서는 부가체로 판이 바다 쪽으로 성장하고, 페루-칠레에서는 침식으로 판 가장자리가 육지 쪽으로 후퇴한다는 점을 whereas로 대비하므로 정답이다. A는 두 지역을 언급하지만 공통점(해구 형성)만 말하고 차이를 보여 주지 않는다. B는 정확한 메모를 쓰지만 섭입 침식 하나만 다루어 대조가 없다. D 역시 부가체만 설명할 뿐 다른 유형과 비교하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to contrast how the overriding plate changes at the two kinds of margins. C does this: at Cascadia the plate grows seaward as a wedge builds up, whereas at Peru-Chile erosion makes the plate's edge retreat landward. A names both margins, but it only describes what they have in common (a sinking plate and a trench), so it shows no contrast. B uses accurate notes but covers only subduction erosion, so there is nothing to compare. D describes only the accretionary wedge and never brings in the other kind of margin.
g.design: To answer, you have to combine notes 2 and 4 and see that the plate moves in opposite directions. A mentions both locations but gives only shared features. B and D each describe one margin accurately, so they look plausible but don't meet the contrast goal. The question avoids the key words of the correct choice (seaward/landward, retreat).

B gets the stratosphere's slow exchange right, but it never gives the troposphere's mixing speed, and it focuses on a result (the lag in CO2 levels) instead. g.passage: Tsunamis travel across the open ocean as shallow-water waves, whose speed depends mainly on water depth: the deeper the water, the faster the wave. As a tsunami approaches a coast, the part of the wave front over shallower water slows down while the part over deeper water keeps moving quickly, so the front bends, or refracts, toward the shallow areas. Oceanographer Lena Marsh has proposed that this bending, not just the overall decrease in depth near shore, explains why some coastal sites see much higher tsunami run-up than nearby sites. In her view, an underwater ridge that extends out from the coast acts like a lens, turning wave energy inward and concentrating it on the stretch of shore where the ridge reaches land.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marsh's hypothesis?
options: During a past tsunami, two coastal sites that had similar near-shore depths showed very different wave heights, and the site with the much higher waves sat at the landward end of a long offshore ridge.
During a past tsunami, wave heights rose steadily at every coastal site as the waves moved from deep water onto the continental shelf, whether or not an offshore ridge was present.
During a past tsunami, instruments in the open ocean showed the waves moving at more than 700 kilometers per hour over the deepest parts of the basin, in line with depth-based predictions.
During a past tsunami, a coastal site at the landward end of an offshore ridge had high waves, but so did a nearby site with no ridge and a much shallower, wider shelf.
g.explanation: Marsh는 수심 감소 자체가 아니라 해저 능선에 의한 굴절 집중이 지역 간 차이를 만든다고 주장한다. A는 근해 수심이 비슷한 두 지점(수심 효과 통제)에서 능선 끝 지점만 파고가 훨씬 높았으므로 가설을 직접 지지한다. B는 능선과 무관하게 수심 감소만으로 파고가 높아졌다는 내용이라 오히려 수심 설명에 부합한다. C는 수심-속도 관계를 확인할 뿐 해안 간 차이나 능선 효과와는 무관하다. D는 능선 없는 지점도 수심이 얕아 파고가 높았으므로 능선의 고유한 역할을 보여 주지 못하고 오히려 약화시킨다.
g.explanation_en: Marsh claims that refraction over an offshore ridge, not simply shallowing water, explains why some sites get much higher run-up than nearby sites. A holds near-shore depth roughly constant between two sites and shows that only the site at the end of a ridge had much higher waves, which isolates the ridge effect and directly supports her view. B shows waves growing at every site regardless of ridges, which fits the simple depth explanation instead. C only confirms that speed depends on depth in the open ocean and says nothing about differences between coastal sites. D shows a site without a ridge getting equally high waves because of a shallow shelf, so it fails to show a unique ridge effect and actually weakens the hypothesis.
g.design: To get this right, you have to notice that the hypothesis contrasts refraction with depth decrease alone. The wrong options each touch real tsunami physics (shallowing, depth-dependent speed, a ridge site with high waves), but none of them controls for depth the way A does.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Soil salinization salt accumulation and water table rise agricultural land degradation arid region problem

g.passage: In many irrigated arid regions, farmland gradually turns white and barren as salts build up in the soil. Some researchers attribute this degradation mainly to the irrigation water itself, which carries dissolved salts that are left behind when the water evaporates. Soil scientist Leila Haddad, however, argues that in the lowland valleys she studies, the primary cause is a rising water table: years of excess irrigation and leaky canals have lifted salty groundwater close to the surface, where capillary action draws it upward and evaporation deposits its salts in the root zone. If Haddad is right, she notes, reducing irrigation volume would matter less than lowering the groundwater itself.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Haddad's argument?
options: Fields irrigated with water containing higher concentrations of dissolved salts showed faster salt buildup than fields irrigated with fresher water, regardless of groundwater depth.

Among fields receiving identical irrigation water, salt accumulation was severe where groundwater lay within two meters of the surface but minimal where it lay deeper, and it declined after drainage wells lowered the groundwater.
Lining the valleys' canals to prevent leakage reduced the total volume of water lost during delivery to farms by nearly a third.
Salt crusts in the valleys were thickest in the hottest months, when evaporation from irrigated fields reached its yearly peak.
g.explanation: Haddad은 염류 축적의 주원인이 관개수 자체가 아니라 상승한 지하수위라고 주장한다. B는 관개수를 동일하게 통제한 상태에서 지하수 깊이에 따라 염류 축적이 달라지고, 지하수위를 낮추자 축적이 줄었음을 보여 주므로 주장을 가장 직접적으로 뒷받침한다. A는 관개수의 염분 농도가 원인이라는 경쟁 가설을 지지하므로 오히려 주장을 약화한다. C는 수로 누수가 줄었다는 사실만 보여 줄 뿐 지하수위나 염류 축적과의 연결이 없다. D는 증발의 역할을 보여 주지만, 증발은 두 가설 모두에서 작용하므로 둘을 구별하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: Haddad argues that salt buildup comes mainly from a rising water table, not from the irrigation water itself. B holds the irrigation water constant and shows that salt buildup depends on how deep the groundwater is. It also shows that buildup dropped once the groundwater was lowered, so B supports her claim most directly. A points to the salt content of irrigation water as the cause, which backs the competing explanation and actually weakens her argument. C only shows that lined canals leaked less water; it doesn't connect that change to the water table or to salt buildup. D shows that evaporation plays a role, but evaporation is part of both explanations, so it can't tell them apart.
g.design: Two steps are needed: first figure out how Haddad's claim differs from the competing hypothesis, then find the finding that controls for irrigation water. C and D share key words with the passage (canal leakage, evaporation) and look relevant on a quick read, but neither tells the two explanations apart.

c.instruction: 지문에 '한때 ~라고 여겨졌으나(통념)' 다음 'however/but/실제로는' 류의 전환어와 함께 이를 뒤집는 새 증거나 반박 문장을 제시하고, 빈칸이 그 반박된 결과를 표현하도록 한다. 정답은 통념과 정반대 방향의 의미를 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 통념 쪽 단어를 그대로 쓴 것, (2) 전환어를 못 읽고 통념과 같은 방향이지만 강도만 다른 단어, (3) 반박 대상과 무관한 제3의 의미 단어로 구성한다. 전환 지점 앞뒤 문장만으로 답이 결정되게 하고 문장 길이나 어휘 난이도는 중간 수준을 유지한다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Polar vortex stratospheric displacement and sudden warming event causing midlatitude weather pattern disruption

g.passage: For decades, many meteorologists treated the stratosphere as largely detached from the weather below: disturbances high above the North Pole were thought to play out there without affecting conditions at the surface. Studies of sudden stratospheric warming events, however, show that when the polar vortex is displaced or split apart, the disruption often works its way downward over several weeks, shifting the jet stream and driving prolonged cold outbreaks into midlatitude regions. Such findings suggest that the two atmospheric layers are far more ______ than earlier models assumed.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation:
정답 C (interconnected): 통념은 성층권이 지표 날씨와 '분리되어(detached)' 있다는 것이었다. 그러나 'however' 뒤의 증거를 보면, 극소용돌이의 교란이 아래로 전파되어 제트기류와 중위도 날씨를 바꾼다. 따라서 두 층은 예전 모델의 가정보다 훨씬 '서로 연결되어' 있다는 결론이 자연스럽다.
A (independent): 반박된 통념을 그대로 담은 단어다. 'far more independent'라고 하면 새 증거와 정반대가 된다.
B (separate): 전환어를 놓치고 통념과 같은 방향(분리)을 고른 경우다. 'independent'보다 강도만 약하게 표현했을 뿐 여전히 증거와 모순된다.
D (turbulent): 소용돌이·교란이라는 소재 때문에 그럴듯해 보이지만, 지문이 다루는 것은 두 층의 '관계'이지 불안정성이 아니므로 반박의 대상과 관계없는 단어다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer C (interconnected): The old view held that the stratosphere was "detached" from surface weather. The evidence after "however" shows that a polar vortex disruption travels downward and changes the jet stream and midlatitude weather. So the logical conclusion is that the two layers are much more linked than earlier models assumed.
A (independent): This word restates the overturned view. "Far more independent" contradicts the new evidence.
B (separate): This choice comes from missing the "however." It points the same way as the old view (separation) and only changes the strength, so it still contradicts the evidence.
D (turbulent): This sounds fitting because of the vortex and disturbances. But the sentence is about how the two layers relate to each other, not how unstable they are, so the word misses the point being disproved.
g.design: "Thought to be detached" sets up the old view. After "however," the downward spread of the vortex disruption overturns it, and the blank expresses the overturned result: the layers are connected. The wrong answers are (1) the old view's word, independent; (2) the same direction with different strength, separate; and (3) an unrelated meaning, turbulent.

c.instruction: 지문에 'is not X, but rather Y' 또는 'it isn't that A; instead B' 형태로 부정어 뒤에 대조 표현이 이어지는 문장을 만들고, 빈칸이 그 대조 표현(B) 자리에 오게 한다. 정답은 부정된 개념(X)과 반대 극성을 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 부정어를 무시하고 X와 같은 의미 단어, (2) 부정 구조를 이중으로 잘못 해석해 극성을 다시 뒤집은 단어, (3) 대조 구조와 무관한 유사 발음/철자 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Magnetosphere compression solar wind dynamic pressure and geomagnetic disturbance index storm severity scale

g.passage: When a burst of dense, fast solar wind strikes Earth, its dynamic pressure squeezes the dayside magnetosphere inward, sometimes pushing the boundary from about ten Earth radii to fewer than seven. Yet space physicists caution that this compression alone does not reliably predict how high a storm will rank on geomagnetic severity scales such as the Kp index. The pressure pulse's influence on storm severity is not self-sufficient but rather ______: only when the interplanetary magnetic field carried by the wind points southward, allowing energy to couple efficiently into the magnetosphere, does a compression typically escalate into a major storm.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 정답 D(conditional): 'not self-sufficient but rather ___' 구조에서 빈칸은 부정된 '자족적(그 자체로 충분함)'과 반대 극성이어야 하며, 콜론 뒤 내용(남향 자기장일 때만 큰 폭풍으로 발전)이 '다른 조건에 달려 있음'을 뒷받침한다. A(self-contained): 부정어를 무시하고 부정된 self-sufficient와 같은 뜻을 고른 오답. B(decisive): 'not'과 'but rather'를 이중 부정으로 잘못 읽어 압력이 다시 결정적이라고 극성을 뒤집은 오답이며, 지문의 '압축만으로는 예측 못 한다'와 모순된다. C(confidential): conditional과 철자·발음만 비슷할 뿐 '기밀의'라는 뜻으로 문맥과 무관하다.
g.explanation_en: D (conditional) is correct. The sentence uses a "not X but rather Y" structure, so the blank has to mean the opposite of "self-sufficient." The text after the colon backs this up: a compression usually becomes a major storm only when the magnetic field points southward. That means the pressure pulse's effect depends on another condition. A (self-contained) skips over the negation and repeats the meaning of the word being rejected. B (decisive) reads the structure as if it flipped twice, so it makes pressure the deciding factor again. That contradicts the text's point that compression alone doesn't predict severity. C (confidential) only looks and sounds like "conditional." It means "secret," which doesn't fit the context.
g.design: I put the blank in the Y slot of a "not self-sufficient but rather ___" sentence. Each wrong answer matches one of the recipe's traps: A ignores the negation and repeats X, B flips the polarity back by misreading a double negative, and C is a lookalike spelling.

c.instruction: 지문을 두 단계(예: 상황 묘사 후 화자의 숙고, 또는 기존 주장 소개 후 저자의 반박/선언)로 구성하고, 빈칸을 두 번째 단계의 시작 지점에 배치해 앞 단계와 다른 서술 기능을 하도록 한다. 정답은 두 번째 단계의 기능(숙고, 반박, 선언 등)에 맞는 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 첫 번째 단계에 어울리는 단어, (2) 두 단계 어디에도 맞지 않는 중립적 단어, (3) 의미는 비슷하나 문장이 요구하는 품사/기능이 다른 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Submarine fan turbidite grading sequence and deep-sea sediment transport canyon channel architecture

g.passage: For decades, sedimentologists read submarine fan deposits through the Bouma sequence: each turbidite bed, the model held, records a single waning turbidity current, grading upward from coarse sand to fine mud as the flow slowed after leaving a canyon channel. Geologist Esther Talbot, however, ______ that this tidy succession is the exception rather than the rule. Her cores from levee-confined channels show beds in which coarse layers recur above fine ones, a pattern she attributes to long-lived flows that surged and slackened repeatedly as they traveled down the channel.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 정답 A(contends): 'however'로 시작하는 둘째 단계는 기존 Bouma 모델에 반박하는 기능을 한다. Talbot은 정돈된 순서가 예외라고 '주장한다'는 의미이며, 뒤 문장의 코어 증거가 그 주장을 뒷받침한다. B(illustrates): 첫째 단계(모델이 단일 흐름을 '보여 준다'는 설명적 서술)에 어울리는 단어로, 반론을 제시하는 기능과 맞지 않으며 '예외'라는 논쟁적 판단을 단순 예시로 바꿔 버린다. C(mentions): 두 단계 어디에도 맞지 않는 중립어로, 통설을 뒤집는 강한 입장을 지나가듯 언급한다는 뜻이 되어 약하다. D(contention): 의미는 비슷하지만 명사여서 주어 Talbot 다음에 동사가 필요한 자리에 문법적으로 들어갈 수 없다.
g.explanation_en: The answer is A, "contends." The word "however" starts the second stage of the text, and that stage pushes back against the Bouma model. Talbot argues that the tidy sequence is the exception, and her core evidence in the next sentence supports that claim. "Contends" fits this act of arguing a disputed position. B, "illustrates," matches the first stage, which describes what the model shows. It doesn't fit a rebuttal, and it treats a debatable judgment as if it were just an example. C, "mentions," is a neutral word that fits neither stage. It's too weak for a claim that overturns the standard view. D, "contention," has a similar meaning, but it's a noun. The slot after the subject "Talbot" needs a verb, so D doesn't work grammatically.
g.design: 지문은 1단계(Bouma 모델 소개)와 2단계(however 이후 저자의 반박)로 나뉘고, 빈칸은 2단계가 시작되는 지점에 있다. 오답은 1단계에 어울리는 단어(illustrates), 어느 단계에도 맞지 않는 중립어(mentions), 뜻은 비슷하지만 품사가 다른 단어(명사 contention)로 구성했다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Atmospheric visibility reduction particulate matter haze formation and air quality index measurement standard

g.passage: Haze forms when tiny airborne particles, such as those released by vehicle exhaust and wildfires, scatter and absorb sunlight, making distant objects harder to see. Researchers in one city measured visibility each afternoon for a year and also recorded the concentration of fine particles in the air. They found that on days with higher particle concentrations, the farthest distance at which a landmark could be clearly seen was consistently shorter. Because the city's air quality index is calculated directly from these same particle measurements, the researchers concluded that on days when the index reports poorer air quality, residents should expect that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: distant landmarks will be visible from farther away than usual.
distant landmarks will be harder to see clearly than usual.
distant landmarks will be equally visible regardless of particle levels.
distant landmarks will be visible only after the particles have fallen to the ground.
g.explanation: 지문은 미세입자 농도가 높을수록 시정 거리가 짧아진다고 말하고, 대기질 지수가 바로 그 입자 측정값으로 계산된다고 밝힌다. 따라서 지수가 나쁜 날은 입자가 많은 날이므로 먼 지형지물이 잘 보이지 않을 것이라는 B가 정답이다. A는 관계를 거꾸로 뒤집은 것이다. C는 지문에서 찾은 일관된 관계를 무시한다. D는 입자가 땅에 떨어지는 과정을 끌어들이는데, 지문은 그 내용을 다루지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says that higher fine-particle concentrations consistently shortened the distance at which landmarks could be seen, and that the air quality index is calculated from those same particle measurements. So a day with a poorer index is a day with more particles, which means distant landmarks will be harder to see, and B is correct. A flips this relationship backward. C ignores the consistent link the researchers found. D brings in particles falling to the ground, which the passage never discusses.
g.design: 이 문항은 '입자가 많으면 시정이 짧고, 지수는 입자로 계산된다'는 한 단계 추론만으로 풀린다. 오답은 관계 역전, 관계 무시, 지문에 없는 과정 추가로 구성했다. 네 선택지는 같은 문장 틀을 쓴다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Glacial isostatic adjustment crustal rebound rate and relative sea level change postglacial shoreline migration

g.passage: During the last ice age, thick ice sheets pressed down on the land beneath them, pushing the crust lower. When the ice melted, the crust began slowly rising again, a process called glacial isostatic adjustment. In parts of Sweden's Gulf of Bothnia coast, the land is still rising by about 8 millimeters per year, while the global sea level is rising by only about 3 to 4 millimeters per year. Because the land there is going up faster than the water, ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the shoreline along this coast is likely creeping inland as the sea gradually covers more of the land.
the sea level along this coast is likely staying exactly the same from year to year.
the shoreline along this coast is likely moving seaward as former seabed becomes dry land.
the land along this coast is likely to start sinking once global sea level stops rising.
g.explanation: 이 해안에서는 땅이 연간 약 8mm 솟아오르는데 해수면은 3~4mm만 오르므로 상대 해수면은 낮아진다. 그 결과 예전 해저가 드러나면서 해안선이 바다 쪽으로 이동하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 해수면 상승만 생각하고 땅이 더 빨리 솟는다는 점을 무시한 오개념이다. B는 두 속도가 같을 때나 성립하는데, 지문에 나온 속도는 서로 다르다. D는 땅의 융기가 해수면 때문이라고 오해한 것으로, 지문은 융기의 원인을 빙하가 녹은 것으로 설명한다.
g.explanation_en: On this coast the land rises about 8 mm per year, but the sea rises only 3 to 4 mm per year, so the sea falls relative to the land. That uncovers former seabed and moves the shoreline seaward, which makes C correct. A looks only at sea-level rise and ignores the fact that the land is rising faster. B would be true only if the two rates were equal, and the passage gives two different rates. D mistakes the cause of the uplift, since the passage says it comes from the melting ice, not from sea level.
g.design: 이 문항은 '땅의 융기 속도와 해수면 상승 속도를 비교한다'는 규칙 하나만 쓰는 1단계 추론이다. 오답은 해수면 상승만 고려하기, 상대적 변화가 없다고 보기, 원인을 착각하기라는 흔한 오개념으로 만들었다.

g.passage:
Text 1
Volcanologists often sort pyroclastic density currents into two types: dense flows that hug valley floors and dilute surges that spread more widely. Some hazard planners argue that maps should focus mainly on valleys, since the dense flows carry most of the material and are therefore the greatest danger to nearby towns.

Text 2
Dilute surges may carry less material, but they can move faster than 100 kilometers per hour and reach temperatures above 300 degrees Celsius. Because they are not confined to valleys, surges can climb over ridges and strike communities that seem safely out of the way. For this reason, hazard maps that ignore surges can leave many residents unprepared.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the planners' view described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that the planners' view is correct, since dilute surges carry less material than dense flows do
By claiming that the planners' view is mistaken, since dense flows move more slowly than any other volcanic hazard
By stating that the planners' view is irrelevant, since temperature matters more than speed in measuring danger
By warning that the planners' view is incomplete, since currents outside valleys can also threaten towns
g.explanation: Text 1의 계획자들은 지도에서 계곡(밀도 높은 흐름)에 주로 집중해야 한다고 주장한다. Text 2는 희석된 서지가 능선을 넘어 계곡 밖 마을을 덮칠 수 있으므로 서지를 무시한 지도는 주민을 무방비 상태로 둔다고 말한다. 따라서 그 견해가 불완전하다고 경고하는 D가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 물질량이 적다는 점은 인정하지만 그 견해에 동의하지는 않으므로 틀렸다. B는 밀도 높은 흐름의 속도를 Text 2가 언급하지 않으므로 틀렸고, C는 Text 2가 온도와 속도를 비교하지 않으므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: In Text 1, the planners say hazard maps should focus mainly on valleys, where the dense flows travel. Text 2 points out that dilute surges can climb over ridges and hit towns outside valleys, so maps that ignore surges leave people unprepared. That means the author of Text 2 would warn that the planners' view is incomplete, so D is correct. A is wrong because Text 2 admits surges carry less material but still doesn't agree with the planners. B is wrong because Text 2 never discusses how fast dense flows move, and C is wrong because Text 2 never ranks temperature above speed.
g.design: 계곡 밖 서지 위협이라는 Text 2의 명시적 단서 하나로 반응을 고르게 했고, 오답은 같은 'By ~ing that the planners' view..., since...' 틀로 흔한 오독을 반영했다.

g.passage:
Text 1
In many estuaries, dense seawater slides upstream along the riverbed beneath lighter freshwater, forming a "salt wedge." Some hydrologists argue that the main factor controlling how far this wedge reaches inland is the daily rise and fall of the tides.

Text 2
Tides do push salt water back and forth, but recent field measurements in several estuaries suggest they are not the main control. When river flow drops during dry seasons, the salt wedge advances far upstream even under ordinary tides. When heavy rains raise river flow, the wedge is pushed back toward the sea. River discharge, not tidal motion, appears to set how far the wedge travels.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim made by some hydrologists in Text 1?
options: By arguing that the claim overstates the role of tides, since the amount of river flow better explains how far the salt wedge extends
By arguing that the claim is correct, since tides alone determine how far the salt wedge extends
By arguing that the claim overlooks the role of seawater density, since density alone determines how far the salt wedge extends
By arguing that the claim is irrelevant, since salt wedges form only in estuaries that have no tides
g.explanation: Text 1의 일부 수문학자들은 염수쐐기가 얼마나 내륙까지 들어오는지를 주로 조석이 결정한다고 주장한다. Text 2는 조석의 영향을 인정하면서도 하천 유량이 줄면 쐐기가 전진하고 늘면 후퇴한다며 하천 유량이 주된 요인이라고 말하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Text 2가 조석이 주된 요인이 아니라고 했으므로 틀리다. C는 밀도가 쐐기를 형성한다는 점은 두 글 모두 받아들이지만 Text 2가 강조하는 요인은 하천 유량이므로 틀리다. D는 Text 2가 조석이 있는 하구에서도 쐐기를 다루므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: In Text 1, some hydrologists claim that tides are the main factor controlling how far the salt wedge reaches inland. Text 2 agrees that tides move salt water, but it shows that the wedge advances when river flow drops and retreats when river flow rises, so it names river discharge as the main control. That makes A the answer. B is wrong because Text 2 directly says tides are not the main control. C is wrong because both texts accept that density forms the wedge, but Text 2 points to river flow, not density, as the key factor. D is wrong because Text 2 talks about wedges in estuaries that do have tides.
g.design: Text 2가 Text 1의 주장을 하천 유량이라는 대안 요인으로 직접 반박한다. 답은 이 한 가지 대비만으로 찾을 수 있고, 오답은 동의, 엉뚱한 요인, 과도한 주장이라는 흔한 오개념으로 구성했다.

g.passage: In the hyperarid core of Chile's Atacama Desert, some soils contain almost no detectable microbial life, even though hardy microbes thrive in salt crusts only a few kilometers away. Researchers once assumed the barren soils simply received too little water. However, a 2015 study found that rare rainstorms there actually killed most resident microbes: cells used to extreme dryness absorbed water so fast that they burst. In addition, the soils hold high concentrations of perchlorates, salts that break down organic molecules when exposed to ultraviolet light. The salt-crust microbes, by contrast, live inside halite (rock salt) that soaks up moisture from humid air slowly and screens out ultraviolet radiation. Taken together, these findings suggest that the barren soils lack life not only because they are dry but also because ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: their perchlorates hold onto atmospheric moisture more slowly than halite does, keeping cells dry between storms.
their sudden wetting and reactive salts damage cells, whereas halite supplies water gradually and blocks the radiation that activates those salts.
their rare rainstorms deliver less total water each year than the humid air supplies to nearby salt crusts.
their microbes break down organic molecules faster than halite-dwelling microbes do when exposed to ultraviolet light.
g.design: 수분의 '양'이 아닌 '공급 방식'과 과염소산염·자외선 작용이라는 두 정보를 연결해야 풀리게 했다. 오답들은 지문 속 요소(수분 흡수 속도, 연간 수분량, 유기물 분해)를 잘못 조합하도록 만들었다.
g.explanation: 지문은 두 가지 위험을 제시한다. 비가 갑자기 내리면 세포가 터지고, 과염소산염은 자외선을 받으면 유기분자를 분해한다. 반면 암염은 수분을 천천히 흡수하고 자외선을 막아 준다. B는 이 두 요인과 암염과의 대조를 함께 담고 있으므로 정답이다. A는 수분을 천천히 흡수하는 성질을 과염소산염에 잘못 갖다 붙였고, C는 '건조함' 즉 물의 양 문제로 되돌아가 '~뿐 아니라'라는 구조와 맞지 않는다. D는 유기분자를 분해하는 주체를 미생물로 잘못 바꾸었다.
g.explanation_en: The passage gives two threats in the barren soils. First, sudden rain makes cells burst. Second, perchlorates destroy organic molecules when ultraviolet light hits them. Halite, on the other hand, lets in moisture slowly and blocks ultraviolet light. B is correct because it pulls both threats together and also captures the contrast with halite. A wrongly gives perchlorates the slow-absorption property that belongs to halite. C goes back to the amount of water, which is just "dryness" again and doesn't fit the "not only... but also" structure. D wrongly says the microbes are the ones breaking down organic molecules.

c.seed: earth and space science — Coriolis effect wind deflection and geostrophic balance upper atmosphere jet stream formation dynamics

g.passage: In the upper atmosphere, air begins moving from regions of high pressure toward regions of low pressure. As it moves, Earth's rotation deflects it through the Coriolis effect—to the right in the Northern Hemisphere. Near the ground, friction with the surface slows the wind, which weakens this deflection and lets air keep flowing partly across pressure lines toward low pressure. Several kilometers up, however, friction is almost absent. There, the deflection keeps growing until it exactly balances the push from the pressure difference, a state called geostrophic balance, in which air flows parallel to the pressure lines instead of across them. Because the temperature contrast between the poles and the tropics produces an especially steep pressure difference at these heights in the midlatitudes, meteorologists conclude that the fast, narrow river of wind known as the jet stream ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: flows mainly from the poles toward the tropics, because air at high altitudes moves directly from high pressure toward low pressure.
is weakest where the pressure difference between poles and tropics is greatest, because friction there increases the Coriolis deflection.
travels largely west to east, roughly parallel to lines of equal pressure, instead of crossing directly from high to low pressure.
forms closer to the ground than at higher altitudes, because surface friction is needed to bring the deflection into balance with the pressure difference.
g.explanation: 지문에 따르면 상층에는 마찰이 거의 없어 지균 균형이 이루어지고, 그 결과 공기는 등압선을 가로지르지 않고 나란히 흐른다. 중위도의 남북 기압 차가 크면 등압선이 대체로 동서 방향으로 놓이므로, 제트기류가 서에서 동으로 등압선과 평행하게 흐른다는 C가 가장 논리적이다. A는 공기가 처음에 고압에서 저압으로 움직인다는 내용만 취하고, 상층에서는 편향이 이를 상쇄한다는 점을 무시한다. B는 기압 차가 클수록 바람이 강하다는 흐름과 반대이고, 상층에는 마찰이 거의 없다는 내용과도 어긋난다. D는 마찰의 역할을 뒤집었다. 지문에서 마찰은 편향을 약하게 만들어 균형을 깨뜨리는 요인이다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says that high in the atmosphere there is almost no friction, so geostrophic balance develops and air flows parallel to the pressure lines instead of across them. In the midlatitudes, the steep pole-to-tropics pressure difference means these lines run roughly east-west, so C, a west-to-east flow parallel to the pressure lines, is the most logical conclusion. A uses only the first step, where air starts moving from high to low pressure, and ignores how the deflection balances that push at altitude. B runs against the passage's logic that a bigger pressure difference produces faster wind, and it also wrongly brings in friction, which is nearly absent up there. D gets friction's role backward: in the passage, friction weakens the deflection and prevents balance rather than creating it.
g.design: 정답을 고르려면 두 정보를 연결해야 한다. 상층에서는 마찰이 없어 등압선과 평행하게 흐른다는 점, 그리고 남북 기압 차 때문에 등압선이 동서 방향으로 놓인다는 점이다. 오답 A와 D는 지문의 일부(고압에서 저압으로의 흐름, 마찰)를 그럴듯하게 재활용하도록 만들었다.

g.passage:
Text 1
After large eruptions, researchers often estimate how much an event will cool global climate by measuring the total volume of ash it ejects. Because fine ash particles can travel thousands of kilometers on high-altitude winds and block incoming sunlight, eruptions that produce the most ash are generally expected to produce the strongest and longest-lasting cooling.

Text 2
Volcanologist Mira Okonjo notes that ash, even the finest grains, tends to clump together and fall out of the atmosphere within days to weeks, so its effect on sunlight doesn't last long. Lasting cooling comes instead from sulfur dioxide that reaches the stratosphere, where it turns into tiny sulfate droplets that can stay aloft for a year or more. An eruption that releases huge amounts of ash but little sulfur, or that never sends its plume high enough, may barely change global temperatures.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Okonjo (Text 2) most likely respond to the approach described in Text 1?
options: She would argue that the approach is reasonable because fine ash travels far enough on high-altitude winds to affect sunlight across the globe for more than a year.
She would argue that the approach underestimates cooling because ash and sulfate droplets together block more sunlight than ash alone.
She would argue that the approach should focus on how far ash travels from the volcano instead of how much ash is ejected.
She would argue that the approach measures a material that leaves the atmosphere too quickly to account for long-term cooling, so it can misjudge an eruption's climatic impact.
g.explanation: Text 1은 화산재의 총량으로 냉각 효과를 추정한다고 말하지만, Text 2의 Okonjo는 화산재가 며칠에서 몇 주 안에 떨어진다고 하고, 오래가는 냉각은 성층권에 올라간 이산화황에서 생긴다고 본다. 따라서 화산재 총량에 기대는 방식은 냉각 효과를 잘못 판단할 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 Text 1의 장거리 이동 내용은 반영하지만, 화산재가 1년 넘게 머문다는 주장은 Text 2와 정면으로 어긋난다. B는 황산염 물방울을 언급하지만, Text 2는 화산재의 역할을 더하라는 것이 아니라 화산재가 오래가는 냉각의 원인이 아니라고 말한다. C는 여전히 화산재를 기준으로 삼기 때문에 Okonjo의 핵심 지적과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Text 1 estimates cooling from the total volume of ash. In Text 2, Okonjo says ash falls out of the air within days to weeks and that lasting cooling comes from sulfur dioxide that reaches the stratosphere. That means an approach based on ash volume can misjudge an eruption's climatic impact, so D is correct. A picks up Text 1's point about ash traveling far, but it claims ash stays aloft for over a year, which directly contradicts Text 2. B mentions sulfate droplets, but Text 2 isn't asking you to add ash's effect on top. It says ash isn't the source of lasting cooling at all. C still uses ash as the measure, so it misses Okonjo's main objection.
g.design: 오답 A·B는 각 지문의 실제 정보를 일부 담고 있어서, 화산재가 얼마나 오래 머무는지와 냉각의 원인이 무엇인지를 서로 연결해 봐야 배제된다. 모든 선택지를 같은 "She would argue that the approach..." 틀로 썼고, 질문에는 정답의 핵심어를 넣지 않았다.
