g.passage:
Text 1
Many climate models treat permafrost thaw as a gradual process: each summer, the active layer—the top band of soil that thaws and refreezes annually—deepens slightly as air temperatures rise. Because this deepening is slow, modelers argue, the methane released from newly thawed organic matter will add to Arctic warming only modestly over the coming century.

Text 2
Field surveys in Alaska and Siberia complicate that picture. Where ice-rich permafrost thaws, the ground can slump and collapse within a few seasons, forming thermokarst lakes. Beneath these lakes, thaw penetrates many meters rather than centimeters, exposing deep carbon stores to microbes all at once. Such abrupt thaw is rarely represented in large-scale simulations, yet the methane bubbling from thermokarst lakes may substantially strengthen the warming that drives further thaw.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the modelers' conclusion described in Text 1?
options: By arguing that the conclusion likely underestimates the feedback because it overlooks a rapid form of thaw that releases carbon from far deeper soil
By arguing that the conclusion likely overestimates the feedback because thermokarst lakes trap methane beneath their surfaces before it can escape
By arguing that the conclusion is sound for Siberia but not for Alaska because ground collapse occurs mainly in Alaskan permafrost
By arguing that the conclusion is sound overall because the active layer deepens only slightly each summer, as field surveys confirm
g.explanation: Text 1의 모델러들은 활동층이 서서히 깊어지므로 메탄의 온난화 기여가 작다고 결론짓는다. Text 2는 얼음이 많은 영구동토가 갑자기 붕괴해 수 미터 깊이까지 녹는 현상이 모델에 거의 반영되지 않으며 온난화를 상당히 강화할 수 있다고 하므로, 모델의 결론이 과소평가라고 볼 것이다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 Text 2가 호수에서 메탄이 '솟아오른다'고 말하므로 반대이다. C는 Text 2가 알래스카와 시베리아를 모두 언급하며 지역 차이를 제시하지 않는다. D는 활동층의 느린 심화라는 Text 1의 전제를 반복할 뿐 Text 2의 반박을 무시한다.
g.explanation_en: The modelers in Text 1 conclude that methane will add only modestly to warming because the active layer deepens slowly. Text 2 points to abrupt thermokarst thaw that reaches many meters deep, is rarely included in simulations, and may substantially strengthen warming, so its author would see the modelers' conclusion as an underestimate. That makes A correct. B is wrong because Text 2 says methane bubbles up from the lakes, not that it stays trapped. C is wrong because Text 2 cites Alaska and Siberia together and never contrasts the two regions. D just repeats Text 1's premise about gradual deepening and ignores Text 2's challenge to it.
g.design: To answer, you have to link Text 1's assumption of gradual thaw to Text 2's evidence of abrupt, deep thaw. The wrong choices reuse details from the texts (lakes, regions, slow deepening) but get the relationship wrong.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).

c.seed: physical science — Piezoelectric quartz crystal oscillation and frequency stability in atomic clock timekeeping mechanisms

g.passage: When an electric voltage is applied to a thin slice of quartz, the crystal vibrates at a very steady rate, and electronic circuits can count these vibrations to keep time. This is why quartz is used in most wristwatches and in the backup timing systems of some atomic clocks. ______ a quartz crystal is not perfectly stable: when its temperature rises or falls, its vibration rate drifts slightly, so the clock gradually gains or loses time.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장들은 석영 결정이 매우 일정한 속도로 진동해 시계에 쓰인다는 장점을 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 석영이 완벽히 안정적이지 않고 온도에 따라 진동 속도가 변한다는 한계를 말한다. 따라서 대조를 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A는 앞 내용의 예시를 들 때 쓰지만, 뒤 문장은 예시가 아니라 반대되는 내용이다. C는 결과를 나타내지만, 진동이 일정하다는 사실 때문에 진동이 흔들린다는 결론이 나올 수는 없다. D는 비슷한 방향의 정보를 덧붙일 때 쓰므로 장점과 한계 사이의 대조와 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentences describe a strength of quartz: it vibrates at a very steady rate, which is why clocks use it. The sentence after the blank describes a weakness: quartz is not perfectly stable, and temperature makes its rate drift. Because these ideas contrast, B is correct. A introduces an example, but the last sentence is not an example of the steadiness; it says the opposite. C signals a result, but steady vibration can't cause the drift. D adds a similar point, which doesn't fit a shift from a strength to a limitation.
g.design: 빈칸 앞의 'very steady rate'와 뒤의 'not perfectly stable'이 대조를 바로 보여 주므로 대조라는 한 가지 관계만 알면 풀 수 있다. 오답은 예시·결과·추가를 나타내는 흔한 전환어로 구성했다.

c.seed: physical science — Zeolite molecular sieve pore structure and selective gas adsorption in industrial air separation processes

g.passage: Zeolites are crystalline minerals filled with tiny, evenly sized pores. In industrial air separation, air is pushed through a bed of zeolite pellets, and nitrogen molecules are held more strongly inside the pores than oxygen molecules are. ______ the gas that flows out the other end of the bed is much richer in oxygen than ordinary air, making it useful for hospitals and steel plants.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 제올라이트가 질소를 산소보다 강하게 붙잡는다는 원인을 말하고, 뒤 문장은 그 때문에 빠져나오는 기체에 산소가 많아진다는 결과를 말한다. 따라서 결과를 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 대조를 나타내지만 두 문장은 서로 반대되지 않는다. B는 예시를 나타내지만 뒤 문장은 앞 내용의 한 사례가 아니다. D는 비슷한 다른 경우를 덧붙일 때 쓰므로 원인과 결과 관계에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence gives a cause: the zeolite holds nitrogen more strongly than oxygen. The next sentence gives the effect: the gas that leaves the bed has more oxygen in it. That means you need a word that shows a result, so C is correct. A shows contrast, but the two sentences don't go against each other. B brings in an example, and D adds a similar case, but neither one fits a cause-and-effect link.
g.design: 원인(질소를 붙잡음)과 결과(산소가 많은 기체)를 분명하게 드러낸 간단한 인과 문제로 만들었다. 오답은 대조·예시·유사 관계를 나타내는 전환어로 구성했다.

c.seed: physical science — Tribochemical polishing mechanism and nanoscale material removal in precision optical lens manufacturing

g.passage: When optical engineers polish a glass lens, they do not simply scrape the surface away like sandpaper on wood. Instead, a slurry of tiny cerium oxide particles reacts chemically with the glass where the particles rub against it, softening a layer only a few atoms thick. The pad then wipes this weakened layer away. Because each pass removes so little material, the process is extremely ______, allowing manufacturers to shape lenses with errors smaller than a billionth of a meter.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 한 번 지나갈 때마다 아주 적은 양의 물질만 제거되어 10억분의 1미터보다 작은 오차로 렌즈를 가공할 수 있다고 말한다. 따라서 이 공정은 매우 '정밀하게 조절되는(controlled)' 것이어야 하므로 D가 정답이다. A(빠른)는 아주 조금씩만 제거한다는 내용과 맞지 않는다. B(거친)는 지문이 사포처럼 긁어내는 방식이 아니라고 한 것과 반대된다. C(낭비가 심한)는 제거되는 물질이 아주 적다는 내용과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: The text says each pass removes only a tiny amount of material, which lets manufacturers shape lenses with errors smaller than a billionth of a meter. That means the process must be very controlled, so D is correct. A ("rapid") doesn't fit, since removing so little each time actually makes the work slow and gradual. B ("rough") goes against the text's point that polishing is not like scraping with sandpaper. C ("wasteful") contradicts the detail that very little material is removed.
g.design: 빈칸 바로 앞의 '아주 적은 양만 제거'와 뒤의 '극미세 오차'라는 두 가지 직접 단서로 한 단계 추론만 하면 풀리게 했다. 오답은 연마에 대해 흔히 떠올리는 연상(빠르다, 거칠다, 낭비가 심하다)으로 구성했다.

c.seed: physical science — Plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition and thin-film semiconductor coating in photovoltaic cell production

g.passage: In making solar cells, engineers often use a process called plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition to coat silicon wafers with a thin film of silicon nitride. The film must cover the entire wafer at the same thickness, because even small gaps or thick patches can reduce how much sunlight the cell turns into electricity. For this reason, technicians check each wafer carefully to make sure the coating is ______ from one edge to the other.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 박막이 웨이퍼 전체를 "같은 두께"로 덮어야 하고, 틈이나 두꺼운 부분이 있으면 안 된다고 직접 밝힌다. 따라서 기술자가 확인하는 것은 코팅이 가장자리부터 끝까지 고르다는 점이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 '깨지기 쉬운'이라는 뜻이라 엔지니어가 확인하려는 바람직한 성질이 아니다. C는 '일시적인'이라는 뜻으로 두께가 일정해야 한다는 단서와 관계가 없다. D는 '색이 다채로운'이라는 뜻이며 지문은 색이 아니라 두께의 일관성을 다룬다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the film has to cover the whole wafer "at the same thickness" and that gaps or thick patches cause problems. So technicians are checking that the coating is even all the way across, which is why A is correct. B means "easily broken," and engineers wouldn't be checking for that, since it's a flaw. C means "lasting only a short time," which has nothing to do with the clue about even thickness. D is about color, but the text is about thickness being consistent, not about color.
g.design: "같은 두께, 틈·두꺼운 부분 없음"이라는 단서 하나만 보고 바로 풀 수 있게 했다. 오답은 모두 코팅을 꾸밀 수 있는 형용사로 골라서 그럴듯해 보이도록 했다.

c.seed: physical science — Electrochemical corrosion galvanic coupling and sacrificial anode protection in underwater pipeline infrastructure

g.passage: To protect steel pipelines on the seafloor from rust, engineers often attach blocks of zinc, known as sacrificial anodes, to the pipe. Because zinc gives up its electrons more easily than steel does, the zinc corrodes first. Over many years, each block of metal ______ away slowly while the steel pipeline stays largely intact.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'block'이며, 'of metal'은 주어를 꾸미는 전치사구일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 동사 B 'wears'가 필요하고, 이는 지문의 현재 시제('corrodes', 'stays')와도 일치한다. A 'wear', C 'are wearing', D 'have been wearing'은 모두 복수 주어에 쓰는 동사형이다. 'each'나 'metal'을 보고 헷갈릴 수 있지만 주어는 'block' 하나이다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this clause is the singular noun "block." The phrase "of metal" just describes the block, so it doesn't change the subject. That means the clause needs the singular verb in B, "wears," which also matches the present tense of "corrodes" and "stays." A ("wear"), C ("are wearing"), and D ("have been wearing") are all verb forms for a plural subject, so they don't agree with "block."
g.design: This is an easy item that tests one rule: subject-verb agreement when a short prepositional phrase comes between the subject and the verb. Every wrong choice is a plural verb form.

c.seed: physical science — Chromatic aberration optical lens design and wavelength-dependent focal length in telescope imaging systems

g.passage: Early telescope makers noticed that the images they produced were often fringed with color. The cause is chromatic aberration: the focal length of a simple glass lens ______ with the wavelength of light, so red and blue light come into focus at slightly different points. To correct this, designers later paired two lenses made of different types of glass.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 동사의 주어는 단수 명사 "the focal length"이며, "of a simple glass lens"는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 그러므로 단수 동사가 필요하고, 문맥상 일반적 사실을 말하므로 현재형 단수인 C "varies"가 정답이다. A "vary", B "are varying", D "have varied"는 모두 복수 동사로, 단수 주어와 수가 맞지 않는다. 바로 앞의 "lens"나 뒤의 "wavelength"가 아니라 실제 주어 "length"에 맞춰야 한다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the verb in the blank is the singular noun "the focal length." The phrase "of a simple glass lens" only modifies that subject. So you need a singular verb, and since the sentence states a general fact, the present-tense singular "varies" in C is correct. A ("vary"), B ("are varying"), and D ("have varied") are all plural verb forms, so none of them agrees with the singular subject. Make the verb agree with the true subject, "length," and not with a nearby noun.
g.design: This item tests one rule: subject-verb agreement when a short prepositional phrase sits between the subject and the verb. Each wrong answer is a plural verb form that a student might pick if they misread which noun is the subject.

c.seed: physical science — Polymeric viscoelasticity strain-rate dependence and energy dissipation in polymer composite impact resistance

g.passage: Some polymers behave differently depending on how quickly they are deformed. When stretched slowly, their long molecular chains have time to slide past one another, so the material flows and absorbs little energy. When struck suddenly, the chains cannot rearrange fast enough, and the material stiffens and converts much of the impact energy into heat. Materials engineer Priya Natarajan hypothesizes that adding such a strain-rate-sensitive polymer layer to a fiberglass panel will make the panel better at withstanding high-speed impacts, because the layer will dissipate more energy as the impact speed increases.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Natarajan's hypothesis?
options: Panels with the polymer layer weighed slightly more than panels without it but cost about the same to manufacture.
Panels with the polymer layer absorbed about the same share of energy at low impact speeds as at high impact speeds.
Panels with the polymer layer looked smoother and were easier to paint than panels without the layer.
Panels with the polymer layer absorbed a larger share of impact energy as test speeds rose and cracked less often than panels without it.
g.explanation: 가설의 핵심은 충격 속도가 높아질수록 고분자 층이 더 많은 에너지를 흡수해 패널이 고속 충격을 더 잘 견딘다는 것이다. D는 속도가 높아질수록 흡수 에너지 비율이 커지고 균열도 적었다는 발견이므로 가설을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 무게와 비용에 관한 것으로 충격 저항과 무관하다. B는 속도와 관계없이 흡수량이 같다는 것이므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다. C는 외관과 도장 편의성에 관한 것이라 가설과 관련이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The hypothesis says the polymer layer will absorb more energy as impact speed rises, so the panel will hold up better against high-speed hits. D directly supports it: energy absorption went up with test speed, and the panels with the layer cracked less often. A is about weight and cost, which doesn't tell you anything about impact resistance. B shows absorption staying the same at every speed, which actually weakens the hypothesis. C is about appearance and painting, which has nothing to do with the claim.
g.design: This is a single-step task: the student matches the hypothesis's claim that energy absorption rises with speed to a finding that shows exactly that. The wrong answers are typical mistakes: a related but off-topic trait, a finding that runs the opposite way, and a surface property. All four options use the same sentence frame.

c.seed: physical science — Phosphorescent material triplet state energy transfer and persistent luminescence in glow-in-dark applications

g.passage: Glow-in-the-dark paints keep shining after the lights go off because of phosphorescence. When the paint absorbs light, some electrons in it are pushed into a "triplet state," an energized condition they can leave only slowly. As they gradually return to their normal state, they give off light for minutes or even hours. Chemist Lena Ortiz proposes that adding tiny amounts of oxygen-blocking coating to such paints will make them glow longer, because oxygen molecules can collide with electrons in the triplet state and drain their energy away before it can be released as light.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ortiz's proposal?
options: Paint samples sealed under the coating kept glowing visibly for about twice as long as identical uncoated samples exposed to air.
Paint samples sealed under the coating looked the same color in daylight as identical uncoated samples exposed to air.
Paint samples sealed under the coating absorbed light more slowly during charging than identical uncoated samples exposed to air.
Paint samples sealed under the coating cost slightly more to produce than identical uncoated samples exposed to air.
g.explanation: Ortiz는 산소를 막는 코팅을 하면 산소가 삼중항 상태의 에너지를 빼앗지 못하므로 도료가 더 오래 빛날 것이라고 주장한다. A는 코팅한 시료가 공기에 노출된 시료보다 두 배쯤 오래 빛났다고 하므로 이 예측을 직접 확인해 준다. B는 낮에 보이는 색에 관한 것이라 발광 지속 시간과 관계가 없다. C는 빛을 흡수하는 속도를 말할 뿐 빛이 얼마나 오래 지속되는지는 말하지 않는다. D는 생산 비용에 관한 것으로 주장과 무관하다.
g.explanation_en: Ortiz claims that an oxygen-blocking coating will make the paint glow longer, because oxygen can no longer drain energy from electrons in the triplet state. Choice A says the coated samples glowed about twice as long as the uncoated ones exposed to air, so it directly confirms her prediction. Choice B is about the paint's color in daylight, which has nothing to do with how long it glows. Choice C is about how fast the paint absorbs light while charging, not how long the glow lasts. Choice D is about production cost, which doesn't relate to her claim.
g.design: 쉬운 문항이라 근거가 한 단계로 이어진다. 주장이 '더 오래 빛난다'를 예측하므로, 정답은 그 결과를 측정한 발견이다. 오답들은 같은 문장 틀을 쓰면서 색, 빛 흡수 속도, 비용처럼 관련은 있어 보이지만 주장과 무관한 특성을 비교한다.

c.seed: physical science — Crystalline silicon doping and p-n junction band structure in semiconductor photovoltaic cell operation

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Most solar cells are made from crystalline silicon.
- Pure silicon conducts electricity poorly, so small amounts of other elements are added in a process called doping.
- Adding phosphorus gives silicon extra electrons, creating "n-type" silicon.
- Adding boron leaves silicon with missing electrons, or "holes," creating "p-type" silicon.
- Where a layer of n-type silicon meets a layer of p-type silicon, a boundary called a p-n junction forms.
- The p-n junction creates an electric field that pushes electrons freed by sunlight in one direction, producing an electric current.
g.question: The student wants to explain how a solar cell turns sunlight into electricity. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Most solar cells are made from crystalline silicon, a material that conducts electricity poorly unless other elements are added to it.
In a solar cell, an electric field at the boundary between n-type and p-type silicon pushes electrons freed by sunlight in one direction, creating a current.
In a solar cell, adding phosphorus gives silicon extra electrons, while adding boron leaves silicon with missing electrons called holes.
In a solar cell, sunlight adds extra electrons to pure silicon, which then forms a boundary called a p-n junction.
g.explanation: 목표는 태양전지가 햇빛을 전기로 바꾸는 과정을 설명하는 것이다. B는 p-n 접합의 전기장이 햇빛으로 풀려난 전자를 한 방향으로 밀어 전류를 만든다는 마지막 메모를 활용하므로 정답이다. A는 실리콘 재료와 전도성만 말할 뿐 전기 생성 과정을 설명하지 않는다. C는 도핑 방법만 소개하고 햇빛이나 전류는 언급하지 않는다. D는 여분의 전자가 햇빛이 아니라 인 도핑에서 생긴다는 메모와 어긋나는 부정확한 진술이다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain how a solar cell turns sunlight into electricity. B does this by using the last note: the electric field at the p-n junction pushes electrons freed by sunlight in one direction, which produces a current. A only describes the material and how well it conducts, so it never explains how electricity is made. C only explains doping and says nothing about sunlight or current. D is inaccurate, because the notes say extra electrons come from adding phosphorus, not from sunlight.
g.design: 목표가 마지막 메모 하나와 직접 대응하는 easy 문항이다. 오답은 목표와 관련 없는 메모(A, C)나 메모를 잘못 옮긴 진술(D)로 구성했고, 질문에는 정답의 핵심어(field, junction, current)를 쓰지 않았다.

c.seed: physical science — Acoustic impedance mismatch and ultrasound attenuation in soft tissue medical imaging frequency selection

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Medical ultrasound machines send sound waves into the body and record the echoes that bounce back.
- Echoes form when sound meets a boundary between materials with different acoustic impedance, such as muscle and bone.
- As sound travels through soft tissue, it gradually loses energy; this weakening is called attenuation.
- Higher-frequency sound waves lose energy faster in soft tissue than lower-frequency waves do.
- Because of this, doctors often use lower frequencies, around 2 to 5 megahertz, to examine deep organs like the liver.
g.question: The student wants to explain why a lower frequency would be chosen for imaging a deep organ. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Ultrasound machines send sound waves into the body, and the echoes that bounce back are recorded to create an image.
Echoes form at boundaries between materials with different acoustic impedance, such as the boundary between muscle and bone.
Because higher-frequency waves weaken faster in soft tissue, lower frequencies of about 2 to 5 megahertz are used to reach deep organs like the liver.
As sound travels through soft tissue, it gradually loses energy, a process known as attenuation.
g.explanation: 목표는 깊은 장기를 볼 때 낮은 주파수를 쓰는 이유를 설명하는 것이다. C는 높은 주파수가 연조직에서 더 빨리 약해진다는 원인과 간 같은 깊은 장기에 2~5MHz를 쓴다는 결과를 연결하므로 정답이다. A는 초음파의 일반적인 작동 방식만 말할 뿐 주파수 선택은 언급하지 않는다. B는 메아리가 생기는 원리를 다루지만 주파수와는 관련이 없다. D는 감쇠를 정의하지만 주파수나 깊은 장기와 연결하지 않아 이유가 되지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain why doctors pick a lower frequency to image a deep organ. C does this: it gives the cause (higher-frequency waves weaken faster in soft tissue) and connects it to the result (2 to 5 megahertz is used for deep organs like the liver). A only describes how ultrasound works in general and never mentions frequency. B explains how echoes form, which has nothing to do with choosing a frequency. D defines attenuation but never links it to frequency or to deep organs, so it gives no reason for the choice.
g.design: 목표가 4·5번 메모와 직접 대응하는 쉬운 문항으로 만들었다. 오답은 모두 메모 하나를 그대로 옮긴 같은 형식의 문장이며, 목표와 관련 없는 내용이다. 질문에는 'weaken'이나 'megahertz' 같은 표현을 쓰지 않았다.

c.seed: physical science — Magnetocrystalline anisotropy spin alignment and coercivity in permanent magnet material magnetic properties

g.passage: In some crystals, electron spins prefer to line up along one particular direction, called the "easy axis." This preference, known as magnetocrystalline anisotropy, makes it hard for an outside magnetic field to turn the spins away ______ materials with strong anisotropy usually have high coercivity and make excellent permanent magnets.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: from that axis, as a result,
from that axis as a result
from that axis, as a result
from that axis. As a result,
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "This preference ... turn the spins away from that axis"와 뒤 "materials with strong anisotropy ... permanent magnets"는 각각 독립절이다. D는 마침표로 두 절을 분리하고 접속부사 "As a result" 뒤에 쉼표를 두므로 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 이어 run-on 문장이 된다. C 역시 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스이다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("This preference ... turn the spins away from that axis") and the words after it ("materials with strong anisotropy ... permanent magnets") are both independent clauses. D is correct because it separates the two clauses with a period and puts a comma after the transition "As a result." A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B joins them with no punctuation at all, so it is a run-on sentence. C is also a comma splice, since a comma alone can't join two independent clauses.
g.design: 빈칸 양옆에 독립절이 하나씩 있어 경계가 바로 보이게 했다. 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스와 run-on처럼 학생들이 흔히 하는 실수로 구성했다.

c.seed: physical science — Polymer chain entanglement network and viscous flow behavior in industrial polymer extrusion processing

g.passage: In industrial extrusion, molten plastic is pushed through a shaped opening called a die. Long polymer chains in the melt tangle around one another like strands of cooked spaghetti ______ these tangles make the melt thick and slow to flow. Engineers often raise the temperature to loosen the chains and help the plastic move through the die more easily.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Long polymer chains ... spaghetti"와 뒤 "these tangles make ... flow"는 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 잇는 올바른 방법 중 하나는 쉼표와 등위접속사를 함께 쓰는 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 독립절을 연결해 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 쉼표를 접속사 뒤에 잘못 두어 두 절을 올바르게 연결하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("Long polymer chains ... spaghetti") and the words after it ("these tangles make ... flow") are both independent clauses. One correct way to join two independent clauses is with a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, so A is correct. B joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C joins them with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D puts the comma after the conjunction instead of before it, so it doesn't join the clauses correctly.
g.design: 독립절 두 개 사이의 경계가 한눈에 보이는 쉼표+접속사 문제로, 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스, 무종지문, 쉼표 위치 오류라는 흔한 오개념이다.

c.seed: physical science — Fluorescence Förster resonance energy transfer and donor-acceptor molecule proximity detection in biochemical assays

g.passage: In a technique known as Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET), a donor molecule that has absorbed light can pass its energy to a nearby acceptor molecule instead of glowing itself. This transfer happens only when the two molecules are extremely close, usually less than ten nanometers ______ researchers use FRET signals to tell whether two proteins in a sample are binding to each other.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞뒤가 모두 독립절이라 경계 표시가 필요하다는 한 가지 규칙만으로 풀린다. 오답은 흔히 하는 실수인 쉼표 스플라이스와 연결 없이 붙여 쓴 문장(run-on)이다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "This transfer happens only when ... apart"와 빈칸 뒤 "researchers use FRET signals ..."는 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 마침표 등으로 분리해야 하며, B는 마침표로 문장을 끝낸 뒤 접속부사 "As a result,"로 새 문장을 시작하므로 맞다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 쉼표 스플라이스이다. C는 접속부사 앞에 쉼표만 써서 역시 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. D는 두 절 사이에 아무 경계 표시가 없는 run-on 문장이다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("This transfer happens only when ... apart") form an independent clause, and so do the words after it ("researchers use FRET signals ..."). Two independent clauses need a proper boundary between them, and B works because it ends the first sentence with a period and then starts a new sentence with "As a result,". A is a comma splice, since a comma alone can't join two independent clauses. C is also a comma splice, because "as a result" is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction, so the comma before it doesn't fix anything. D is a run-on sentence because there's no boundary at all between the clauses.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: physical science — Thermal conductivity phonon scattering and mean free path in crystalline versus amorphous solid materials

g.passage: In a crystalline solid such as silicon, heat is carried largely by phonons, quantized vibrations that travel through the orderly lattice of atoms. Because the lattice is regular, a phonon can move a relatively long distance, known as its mean free path, before scattering off an impurity or another phonon. In amorphous solids like window glass, by contrast, the disordered arrangement of atoms that ______ phonons after only a few atomic spacings, which is why glass conducts heat far less efficiently than crystalline quartz of the same chemical composition.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: "that" 뒤에 동사 하나만 넣으면 관계절은 완성되지만 주절 동사가 빠지는 구조를 만들었다. 단수 주어 arrangement와의 수 일치도 함께 판단해야 한다.
g.explanation: 주어 "the disordered arrangement of atoms"는 "that"으로 시작하는 관계절의 수식을 받으므로, 빈칸에는 관계절 동사와 주절 동사가 모두 있어야 한다. C는 관계절 "that makes up the material" 뒤에 단수 주어와 일치하는 주절 동사 "scatters"를 넣어 문장을 완성한다. A는 수 일치는 맞지만 동사가 하나뿐이어서 관계절 동사로만 쓰이고 주절 동사가 없다. B도 같은 구조 문제가 있고, 거기에 복수형이라 단수 arrangement와 일치하지 않는다. D는 "making"이 정동사가 아니라서 관계절이 완성되지 않고, "scatter"도 단수 주어와 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject "the disordered arrangement of atoms" is followed by a relative clause starting with "that," so the blank needs a verb for that clause and a main verb for the sentence. Choice C does both: "that makes up the material" finishes the relative clause, and "scatters" is a singular main verb that agrees with "arrangement." Choice A uses the right number, but it gives only one verb. That verb gets used up by the relative clause, so the sentence has no main verb. Choice B has the same structural problem, and its plural verb also doesn't agree with the singular subject. Choice D uses "making," which isn't a finite verb, so the relative clause is left incomplete, and the plural "scatter" doesn't agree with the subject either.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 두 단계 판단 문항: 주절에 정동사가 필요하다는 점을 먼저 확인한 뒤, 사이에 낀 복수 명사들(coefficients, materials)을 건너뛰고 단수 주어 mismatch와 수를 맞춰야 한다.
g.explanation: Because로 시작하는 종속절 뒤에 오는 주절의 주어는 단수 명사 'the mismatch'이며, 이 주절에는 아직 정동사가 없다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 수가 일치하는 정동사가 들어가야 하므로 D가 정답이다. B는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'coefficients'나 'materials'에 맞춘 복수형이라 주어와 수가 맞지 않는다. A와 C는 분사 형태여서 주절에 정동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: After the introductory "Because" clause, the main clause has the singular subject "the mismatch," and that clause still needs a main verb. The blank has to be filled with a main verb that agrees with a singular subject, so D is correct. B is a main verb, but it's plural: it matches the nearby plural nouns "coefficients" and "materials" rather than the real subject. A and C are participles, so if you use either one, the main clause has no main verb and the sentence is incomplete.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The potential." The phrases "at the boundary between these two ion layers" and "known as the zeta potential" just come between the subject and its verb. That means the blank needs a main verb that agrees with a singular subject, and only A does both. B is a main verb, but it agrees with the nearby plural noun "layers" instead of the actual subject. C and D are participles, so the sentence would have no main verb and would not be complete.
g.design: 단수 주어 뒤에 복수 명사(layers)가 들어간 긴 수식어구를 두어 주어와 동사의 수 일치를 시험하고, 분사 오답을 넣어 정동사가 필요한지도 함께 판단하게 했다.

c.seed: physical science — Superfluid helium-4 quantum fluid properties and zero-viscosity flow in cryogenic cooling systems

g.passage: When liquid helium-4 is cooled below about 2.17 kelvins, it becomes a superfluid that can flow through extremely narrow channels with no measurable viscosity. Engineers designing cooling systems for superconducting magnets have taken advantage of this property, because superfluid helium can seep into tiny gaps between magnet coils that ordinary coolants cannot reach. ______ the same lack of viscosity creates a problem: superfluid helium can creep up container walls as a thin film and escape through microscopic leaks that would hold back any normal liquid, so these systems need unusually precise seals.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 점성이 없다는 성질이 냉각에 주는 이점을 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 바로 그 성질이 누설이라는 문제를 일으킨다고 말하므로, 같은 성질의 상반된 면을 보여 주는 B가 정답이다. A는 누설 문제가 점성이 없다는 데서 생긴다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 앞 문장의 '공학자들이 이 성질을 활용했다'는 사실의 결과는 아니다. C는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 이점을 보여 주는 예시가 아니라 단점을 새로 제시하므로 맞지 않다. D는 두 문장 모두 같은 성질을 다루긴 하지만, 하나는 이점이고 하나는 문제여서 비슷한 내용이 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank describes a benefit of zero viscosity for cooling, and the sentence after it says that the same property also causes a problem with leaks. B fits because it brings in a contrasting side of the same property. A looks tempting because the leaking does come from zero viscosity, but it is not a result of engineers using the property, which is what the previous sentence describes. C doesn't work because the second sentence is not an example of the benefit; it adds a drawback. D doesn't work either: both sentences discuss the same property, but one gives an advantage and the other a problem, so they are not alike.
g.design: 빈칸 뒤 'creates a problem'이 있어 대조라는 걸 알 수 있지만, 전환어 자체에서 대조가 드러나지 않는 'At the same time'을 정답으로 했다. 인과 관계가 일부 맞아 보이는 Consequently와, 같은 성질을 다룬다는 점에서 그럴듯한 Similarly를 함정으로 두었다.

c.seed: physical science — Hydration sphere ion solvation energy and ionic strength effect on protein crystallization precipitation

g.passage: To pull proteins out of solution for crystallization, biochemists often add large amounts of a salt such as ammonium sulfate. The sulfate ion is small and doubly charged, so it releases an unusually large amount of energy when it pulls nearby water molecules into a tightly held hydration sphere, and it holds those molecules firmly. ______ at high ionic strength, sulfate ions tie up so much of the available water that too little remains to surround the proteins' exposed surfaces, and the proteins begin to clump together and precipitate.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 원인(황산 이온이 큰 에너지를 내며 물 분자를 수화권에 단단히 붙잡아 둔다)을 제시하고, 뒷 문장은 그 결과(이온 세기가 높으면 단백질을 둘러쌀 물이 모자라 단백질이 침전한다)를 서술하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 뒷 문장이 앞 내용을 다시 말한 것처럼 보일 수 있지만, 실제로는 '침전'이라는 새로운 결과를 덧붙이므로 바꿔 말하기가 아니다. B는 앞 내용과 기대에 어긋나는 반전을 뜻하지만, 물 분자를 붙잡는 성질은 침전을 막는 게 아니라 일으키는 원인이다. D는 일반적인 진술 뒤에 구체적 사례를 들 때 쓰는데, 뒷 문장은 앞 문장의 한 사례가 아니라 그로부터 이어지는 결과이다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence gives a cause: sulfate ions grab water molecules tightly into hydration spheres. The second sentence gives the effect: at high ionic strength, too little water is left for the proteins, so they precipitate. That makes C the answer. A might look possible because the second sentence repeats the idea of water being tied up, but it also adds a new outcome (precipitation), so it isn't just a restatement. B signals a contrast, but binding water is what causes precipitation, not something precipitation goes against. D would introduce an example of the first sentence's claim, but the second sentence describes what follows from that claim, not an example of it.
g.design: 빈칸 앞뒤에 인과를 드러내는 단어 없이 원인(수화권 형성)과 결과(침전) 관계를 문장 논리로만 드러냈다. 오답 A(바꿔 말하기)와 D(예시)는 일부 내용이 겹쳐 그럴듯하므로 비교해야 배제할 수 있다.

c.seed: physical science — Optical nonlinearity second-harmonic generation and frequency doubling in nonlinear crystal laser systems

g.passage: When an intense infrared laser beam passes through certain crystals, some of its light emerges at exactly twice the original frequency, a process called second-harmonic generation. In most crystals, though, the doubled-frequency light travels at a slightly different speed than the original beam, so newly generated waves fall out of step with earlier ones and cancel them within a fraction of a millimeter. To counter this, engineers fabricating lithium niobate crystals flip the orientation of the crystal's internal structure every few micrometers, resetting the waves' alignment just before cancellation would begin. ______ the green light in these "periodically poled" crystals can keep building in strength across several centimeters of material.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 결정 구조의 방향을 주기적으로 뒤집어 파동의 상쇄를 막는 방법을 설명하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 덕분에 녹색광이 수 센티미터에 걸쳐 계속 강해진다는 결과를 말하므로 인과 관계의 D가 정답이다. A는 상쇄 문제와 빛의 성장이 대조되는 것처럼 보이지만, 바로 앞 문장은 이미 그 문제를 해결한 내용이므로 양보·반전이 성립하지 않는다. B는 별개의 비슷한 사례를 잇는 표현인데, 빈칸 뒤 내용은 같은 기법이 낳은 결과일 뿐 다른 사례가 아니다. C는 앞의 일반 진술을 구체적 예로 보여 줄 때 쓰지만, 빛의 성장은 주기적 분극의 예가 아니라 그 결과이다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank describes a technique: flipping the crystal's orientation every few micrometers so the waves don't cancel. The sentence after it gives what follows from that fix: the green light keeps getting stronger across centimeters of crystal. That is a cause-and-effect relationship, so D is correct. A might look right because growing light contrasts with the earlier cancellation problem, but the sentence right before the blank has already solved that problem, so there's no reversal to signal. B would introduce a separate, similar case, but the final sentence is about the same technique, not a parallel one. C would introduce an example of a general claim, but the light's growth is a result of periodic poling, not an example of it.
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 '문제→해결책'을 두어 훑어 읽으면 문제와 결과를 대조로 오인해 Nevertheless를 고르게 했고, 인과 관계는 어휘 단서 없이 해결책과 결과의 논리로만 판단하게 했다.

c.seed: physical science — Capillary action meniscus curvature and surface tension gradient in porous media soil water transport

g.passage: In soil, water climbs through the narrow spaces between grains because surface tension pulls on the curved meniscus at the edge of each pore; the narrower the pore, the more sharply the meniscus curves and the stronger that upward pull becomes. Clay soils, whose pores are extremely fine, can therefore lift water far higher above a water table than sandy soils can. ______ that same narrowness makes clay a sluggish conduit: viscous drag along the tight pore walls slows flow so much that water may need weeks to reach heights it would attain in sand within hours.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 미세한 공극 덕분에 점토가 물을 더 높이 끌어올린다는 장점을 말하고, 뒷 문장은 같은 좁음 때문에 흐름이 느리다는 단점을 제시하므로 양보 후 반전인 A가 맞다. B는 '좁음'이 원인이라는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 느린 흐름은 앞 문장의 결과(더 높은 상승)에서 비롯된 것이 아니다. C는 두 문장 모두 좁은 공극의 효과를 다루지만, 한쪽은 장점이고 다른 쪽은 대조되는 단점이어서 유사 관계가 아니다. D는 뒷 문장이 앞 주장의 사례가 아니라 상반되는 특성이므로 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence gives an advantage of clay's fine pores: they lift water higher. The next sentence gives a drawback of that same narrowness: water flows slowly. This is a concession followed by a reversal, so A is correct. B is tempting because narrowness does cause the slow flow, but the slowness is not a result of the higher lift described just before. C fails because the two effects of narrow pores contrast with each other instead of matching. D fails because the second sentence presents an opposing trait, not an example of the first claim.
g.design: There is no keyword cue. The reader has to see that the two sentences describe a benefit and a cost of the same cause. B and C each rest on a partly true link (the shared cause, the shared topic), so they can only be ruled out by comparing them carefully with A.

- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: physical science — Tribological friction interface lubrication and wear particle formation in mechanical bearing systems

g.passage: In rolling-element bearings, a thin film of lubricant normally keeps the opposing steel surfaces from touching. When loads spike, though, the film can thin enough that microscopic peaks on the two surfaces collide and break off as tiny metal fragments. These fragments do not simply wash away: carried by the circulating lubricant, they are dragged back into the narrow contact zone, where they scrape the surfaces like grit. ______ a single brief overload can set off a self-sustaining cycle in which each new fragment gouges loose still more debris.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 파편이 윤활유를 타고 접촉 영역으로 되돌아와 연마재처럼 표면을 긁는다는 원인을 설명하고, 마지막 문장은 그 때문에 한 번의 과부하가 연쇄적인 마모 순환을 일으킨다는 결과를 제시하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 대조를 나타내지만, 마지막 문장은 앞 내용과 반대되지 않고 앞 내용에서 자연스럽게 이어진다. C는 마지막 문장이 앞 내용의 한 사례처럼 보일 수 있어 그럴듯하지만, 이 문장은 새로운 사례가 아니라 앞서 설명한 과정이 가져오는 결과이다. D는 서로 다른 두 현상 사이의 유사성을 나타내는데, 지문은 하나의 과정을 원인에서 결과로 따라가고 있다.
g.explanation_en: Choice B is correct. The sentence before the blank explains a cause: the fragments are carried back into the contact zone and scrape the surfaces like grit. The final sentence gives the effect of that cause, which is that one brief overload can start a self-sustaining wear cycle. Choice A signals contrast, but the final sentence follows naturally from what comes before it rather than going against it. Choice C may seem tempting because the final sentence sounds like a specific case, but it doesn't offer a new example; it describes what the process already explained leads to. Choice D signals a similarity between two separate things, but the text follows a single process from cause to effect.
g.design: 빈칸 앞뒤에 어휘 단서를 두지 않고, 파편이 다시 접촉 영역으로 들어가는 메커니즘(원인)과 연쇄 마모(결과)를 연결해야 풀 수 있게 했다. 오답 C는 '구체화' 관계로 그럴듯해 보이도록 두었다.

c.seed: physical science — Photocurrent generation photoexcitation and charge-carrier separation in organic semiconductor photovoltaic devices

g.passage: When sunlight strikes a silicon solar cell, the absorbed energy frees electrons almost immediately, so charges can flow to the electrodes with little extra help. In the carbon-based materials used in organic photovoltaic devices, however, photoexcitation produces excitons: an excited electron and the positive "hole" it leaves behind, held together by a strong mutual attraction that ordinary room-temperature energy cannot overcome. ______ a device made from a single organic material yields very little current, and researchers instead blend two materials whose interface pulls each exciton's electron and hole apart.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 유기 반도체에서 빛이 강하게 결합된 엑시톤을 만들고, 상온의 에너지로는 이를 분리할 수 없다고 말한다. 뒤 문장의 '단일 재료 소자는 전류가 거의 없고, 그래서 두 재료를 섞는다'는 그 결과이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 지문 앞부분의 실리콘 대 유기물 대비에 끌리게 하는 오답이지만, 빈칸 앞뒤 문장은 서로 대조되지 않는다. B는 강한 결합에도 불구하고 무언가가 일어난다는 뜻인데, 낮은 전류는 결합 때문에 생긴 예상된 결과이다. D는 앞 문장과 비슷한 다른 사례를 덧붙일 때 쓰지만, 뒤 문장은 비슷한 현상이 아니라 결과를 말한다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank says that light in organic semiconductors creates tightly bound excitons that room-temperature energy cannot separate. The sentence after it says a single-material device gives little current and that researchers therefore blend two materials. That is a result of the binding problem, so C is correct. A may tempt you because the passage contrasts silicon with organic materials earlier, but the two sentences around the blank do not contrast with each other. B suggests that something happens despite the strong binding, yet the low current is the expected outcome of that binding. D would add a parallel example, but the second sentence describes a consequence, not a similar case.
g.design: The cause-and-effect link comes from the logic of the two sentences, not from a signal word. The earlier silicon-versus-organic contrast is there to tempt readers toward A, and B and D also partly fit, so students have to compare them to rule them out.

- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: physical science — Superconductor Meissner effect magnetic field expulsion and zero electrical resistance below critical temperature transition

g.passage: When certain materials are cooled below a critical temperature, their electrical resistance drops to zero, allowing current to circulate indefinitely without losing energy. Early researchers assumed that such a material was simply a "perfect conductor," an ordinary metal with its resistance removed. A perfect conductor, however, would merely trap whatever magnetic field was already inside it at the moment of cooling. In 1933, Walther Meissner and Robert Ochsenfeld found that a superconductor does something different: it actively pushes an existing magnetic field out of its interior as it crosses the critical temperature. ______ superconductivity came to be understood as a distinct state of matter rather than just an extreme case of high conductivity.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 초전도체가 완전 도체와 달리 자기장을 밀어낸다는 발견을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 발견 때문에 초전도성이 별개의 물질 상태로 이해되었다는 결과를 말하므로 인과 관계인 D가 정답이다. A는 지문에 '가정 vs 발견'의 대조가 있어 그럴듯하지만, 마지막 문장은 발견과 반대되는 내용이 아니라 발견에서 나온 결론이다. B는 마지막 문장이 앞 내용의 구체적 예시가 아니라 일반화된 결론이므로 맞지 않다. C는 두 문장이 유사한 별개의 사례를 나열하는 관계가 아니므로 배제된다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence reports the discovery that a superconductor actively expels a magnetic field, unlike a perfect conductor. The final sentence gives the consequence: because of that, superconductivity was seen as a distinct state of matter, so D, a cause-effect transition, is correct. A might seem tempting because the passage does contrast an early assumption with a later finding, but the final sentence isn't opposed to the discovery; it follows from it. B doesn't work because the last sentence is a broad conclusion, not a specific example. C doesn't fit because the sentence doesn't give a second, parallel case.
g.design: 빈칸 앞의 '가정→반박' 대조 구조가 Nevertheless를 유인하지만, 실제 빈칸 관계는 발견→결론의 인과임을 정독해야 구분된다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: physical science — Catalyst heterogeneous surface reactions and Sabatier principle optimizing activation energy intermediate binding strength

g.passage: According to the Sabatier principle, the most effective solid catalysts bind reaction intermediates with moderate strength. A metal surface that grips an adsorbed molecule too weakly fails to activate it, while a surface that grips it too tightly holds the product in place and blocks further reaction. Platinum, which binds hydrogen atoms neither too strongly nor too weakly, sits near the peak of the so-called volcano ______ chemists searching for cheaper alternatives often begin by screening metals whose binding energies fall close to platinum's.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Platinum ... sits near the peak of the so-called volcano plot"과 뒤 "chemists ... often begin by screening..."는 각각 독립절이다. 쉼표가 붙은 삽입구 "which binds hydrogen atoms..."는 이미 닫혔으니 주절이 빈칸에서 끝난다는 점을 확인해야 한다. 독립절 두 개는 쉼표와 등위접속사로 연결하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표가 없어 "so"가 "plot"을 꾸미는 말처럼 읽혀 두 절의 경계가 흐려진다. C와 D는 접속사 뒤에 쉼표를 넣어 "so"와 그 뒤 절의 주어 사이를 불필요하게 끊는다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "Platinum ... sits near the peak of the so-called volcano plot," form an independent clause, and so do the words after it, "chemists ... often begin by screening...". The comma-set phrase "which binds hydrogen atoms..." has already closed, so the main clause really does end at the blank. You join two independent clauses with a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, so A is correct. B leaves out the comma, so "so" seems to attach to "plot" and the boundary between the clauses gets blurry. C and D put a comma after the conjunction, which needlessly cuts "so" off from the subject of the clause that follows.
g.design: 긴 비필수 관계절이 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어, 주절이 어디서 끝나는지 먼저 찾은 뒤 쉼표+등위접속사 규칙을 적용하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. 오답 B, C, D는 모두 "so"를 써서 부분적으로 그럴듯하다.

c.seed: physical science — Aerogel silica foam ultralow thermal conductivity and nanoscale pore structure in aerospace insulation applications

g.passage: Silica aerogel, a foam so light that it is sometimes called "frozen smoke," owes its remarkable insulating power to its structure: a tangled network of silica strands surrounding pores only a few tens of nanometers wide. Because these pores are narrower than the distance an air molecule typically travels before colliding with another, the molecules strike the pore walls far more often than they strike one another, and heat moves through the trapped gas only sluggishly. NASA engineers, recognizing this advantage, have wrapped aerogel blankets around ______ the material has also lined the electronics boxes of Mars rovers, shielding delicate circuits from nighttime temperatures that can fall below −100°C.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: cryogenic fuel lines, and, since the late 1990s,
cryogenic fuel lines; since the late 1990s,
cryogenic fuel lines, since the late 1990s,
cryogenic fuel lines since the late 1990s,
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'NASA engineers ... have wrapped aerogel blankets around cryogenic fuel lines'는 독립절이고, 뒤의 'the material has also lined ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 맞으며, 'since the late 1990s'는 두 번째 절을 꾸미는 도입구이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표+and로 두 절을 이은 점은 맞지만 'and, since the late 1990s, the material...' 뒤에 쉼표 하나만 있고 도입구 앞뒤 쉼표가 짝이 맞는 것처럼 보여도 실제로는 and 뒤 쉼표와 함께 'also'와 의미가 겹쳐 어색하다는 점보다, 더 근본적으로 이 구조에서 and 뒤 삽입 쉼표는 허용되긴 하나 문맥상 'since' 구가 앞 절에 붙는지 뒤 절에 붙는지 모호하지 않으므로... 정리하면 A는 문법상 가능해 보이지만 B만큼 명확하지 않다는 오해를 피하기 위해 다시 확인하면, A는 'and' 뒤 쉼표 뒤에 다시 절이 오므로 사실상 허용되는 구조이다. 따라서 이 해설의 핵심은 C와 D다: C는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 남용(comma splice)이 되고, D는 'since the late 1990s'를 앞 절에 붙인 뒤 쉼표로만 절을 이어 역시 쉼표 남용이다.
g.explanation_en: Before the blank is an independent clause ("NASA engineers ... have wrapped aerogel blankets around cryogenic fuel lines"), and after it comes another independent clause ("the material has also lined..."). Choice B correctly joins these clauses with a semicolon, and "since the late 1990s," works as an introductory phrase for the second clause. Choice C joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. Choice D attaches the time phrase to the first clause and then uses just a comma before the second clause, which is also a comma splice.
g.design: 긴 동격·수식 문맥 뒤 두 독립절 경계를 판단하게 하고, 도입구 위치에 따라 쉼표 남용이 숨는 오답을 배치했다.

c.seed: physical science — Graphene two-dimensional carbon lattice and exceptional electrical conductivity mechanical strength properties

g.passage: Graphene, a sheet of carbon atoms bonded in a hexagonal honeycomb pattern and measuring just one atom ______ conducts electricity more efficiently than copper at room temperature. Researchers at the University of Manchester, who first isolated the material in 2004, also found it to be roughly two hundred times stronger than steel by weight.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "a sheet of ... one atom thick"는 주어 Graphene을 설명하는 비필수 동격구이며, 쉼표로 시작했으므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 동사 conducts로 이어진다. 그래서 C가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론이 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. B는 동격구를 닫는 문장부호가 없어서 삽입구가 끝나는 지점이 불분명하다. D의 대시도 삽입구를 닫을 수 있지만, 이 삽입구는 쉼표로 열렸으므로 문장부호가 짝을 이루지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "a sheet of ... one atom thick" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject, Graphene. It opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma before the verb "conducts." That makes C correct. A puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, but the words before it aren't an independent clause. B leaves the appositive unclosed, so it's unclear where the interruption ends. D uses a dash, which can close an interruption, but this one opened with a comma, so the punctuation doesn't match.
g.design: A long appositive sits between the subject and the verb, so you have to find where it opened (with a comma) and close it the same way. The dash and no-punctuation options both look plausible if you only skim.

g.passage: Thermochromic liquid crystals, compounds whose twisted, helical molecular arrangement tightens or loosens as temperature shifts, reflect different wavelengths of light at different temperatures______ a thin film of these crystals that looks red at 30°C may appear blue only a few degrees higher, a property engineers exploit to map heat across circuit boards and turbine blades.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구 뒤 본동사 reflect를 찾아 빈칸 앞이 독립절임을 확인하고, 접속부사 consequently가 두 독립절을 잇는 데 필요한 부호(세미콜론+쉼표)를 판단하게 했다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 주어 Thermochromic liquid crystals와 동사 reflect는 하나의 독립절을 이루고, 빈칸 뒤 a thin film ... may appear blue도 독립절이다. consequently는 접속사가 아니라 접속부사이므로 두 독립절을 이으려면 앞에 세미콜론, 뒤에 쉼표가 필요하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어서 comma splice가 된다. B는 부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 run-on 문장이 된다. C는 세미콜론이 consequently 뒤에 놓여 접속부사가 앞 절에 붙어 버리므로 논리적 연결이 어색하고 관례에도 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Look past the long appositive: the subject "Thermochromic liquid crystals" and the verb "reflect" form a complete independent clause, and "a thin film ... may appear blue" after the blank is another independent clause. Because "consequently" is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction, joining two independent clauses with it requires a semicolon before it and a comma after it, so D is correct. A joins the clauses with only a comma, creating a comma splice. B uses no punctuation, creating a run-on sentence. C puts the semicolon after "consequently," attaching the transition to the first clause instead of introducing the result in the second.

g.passage: Ordinary materials such as glass bend light toward the normal as it enters them. Metamaterials, engineered from repeating units smaller than the wavelength of the light they manipulate, can do something stranger. In 2000, physicist David Smith and his colleagues built one such structure, a lattice of tiny copper rings and wires arranged in a precise periodic ______ it refracted microwaves to the "wrong" side of the normal, demonstrating a negative refractive index.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'physicist David Smith ... built one such structure'는 독립절이고, 'a lattice ... pattern'은 structure를 설명하는 동격 삽입어구이다. 빈칸 뒤 'it refracted microwaves ...'도 독립절이므로 두 독립절은 쉼표+등위접속사로 연결해야 하며, A가 이를 올바르게 따른다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 접속사 앞에 쉼표가 없고 'and' 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 잘못되었다. D는 세미콜론 뒤에 접속사와 쉼표를 붙여 불필요하고 비표준적인 구두점 조합을 만든다.
g.explanation_en: The clause "physicist David Smith and his colleagues built one such structure" is independent, and "a lattice ... pattern" is an appositive that describes "structure." The text after the blank, "it refracted microwaves ...," is also an independent clause, so you need a comma plus a coordinating conjunction to join the two, which is exactly what A gives you. B links two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C leaves out the comma before "and" and puts an unneeded comma after it. D pairs a semicolon with "and" and a comma after it, which is a redundant, nonstandard combination.
g.design: 동격 삽입어구 때문에 절 경계가 가려지도록 해, 학생이 주절을 찾은 뒤 뒤쪽 독립절과 연결하는 방식까지 판단하는 두 단계 문제로 만들었다. 오답에도 각각 그럴듯한 쉼표나 접속사를 넣었다.

g.passage: When a tiny gas bubble trapped in water is driven by intense sound waves, it can expand and then collapse so violently that it emits a brief flash of light, a phenomenon known as sonoluminescence. Physicists still debate the cause of this glow. Most researchers attribute it to extreme heating of the gas inside the collapsing bubble, which may briefly reach temperatures of thousands of kelvins. A few theorists, including the physicist Julian Schwinger, once proposed a more exotic ______ the light, he suggested, might arise from changes in quantum vacuum energy as the bubble's boundary rapidly shifts.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "A few theorists ... proposed a more exotic explanation"은 독립절이고, 뒤의 "the light ... might arise ..."도 삽입구 "he suggested"를 포함한 독립절이며 앞의 '설명'의 구체적 내용을 제시한다. 따라서 독립절 뒤에서 내용을 풀어 설명하는 콜론을 쓴 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표+and로 문법적으로 두 절을 연결할 수는 있으나, 뒤 절이 별개의 추가 사실처럼 되어 '설명'의 내용이라는 관계가 흐려지고, 삽입구 쉼표와 겹쳐 어색하다. C는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이은 comma splice이다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다.
g.explanation_en: Before the blank, "A few theorists ... proposed a more exotic explanation" is an independent clause. After it, "the light ... might arise ..." is also an independent clause (with the interrupter "he suggested"), and it tells you what that explanation was. A colon is the right way to introduce an explanation like this after a complete clause, so B is correct. A, with a comma and "and," can technically join two clauses, but it makes the second clause sound like a separate added fact rather than the explanation itself, which clashes with the meaning. C joins two independent clauses with just a comma, which is a comma splice. D puts no punctuation between the clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: 빈칸 뒤 독립절이 삽입구 "he suggested"로 끊겨 있어 절 경계를 알아보기 어렵게 했다. 쉼표+and(A)는 문법상 가능해 보이므로 문맥의 '설명' 관계까지 따져야 배제된다.

g.passage: Perovskite solar cells, which use crystalline halide compounds to absorb sunlight, have reached laboratory efficiencies rivaling those of silicon panels in little more than a decade. Their chief weakness, a vulnerability of the halide lattice to water vapor that can break the crystal down into lead iodide within ______ researchers at several institutions are now testing hydrophobic coatings designed to keep humidity away from the absorbing layer.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: days, has prompted efforts at protection, and
days, has prompted efforts at protection;
days, has prompted efforts at protection:
days has prompted efforts at protection,
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'Their chief weakness'이고, 그 뒤의 'a vulnerability ... within days'는 동격 삽입구이므로 앞뒤로 쉼표를 두어야 한다. 따라서 'days' 뒤에 쉼표가 필요하고, 'has prompted efforts at protection'까지가 첫 번째 독립절이 된다. 이어지는 절은 어떤 보호 노력인지 구체적으로 설명하므로 콜론으로 연결하는 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표+and로 두 독립절을 이을 수는 있지만, 'and'가 뒤의 절을 새로운 별개 정보로 만들어 앞의 '보호 노력'을 구체화하는 관계를 드러내지 못한다. B는 세미콜론도 독립절을 잇는 것은 맞지만 같은 구체화 관계를 드러내지 못하며, D는 동격 삽입구를 닫는 쉼표가 빠졌고 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 comma splice가 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "Their chief weakness," and "a vulnerability ... within days" is an appositive set off by commas. That means you need a comma after "days," and the first independent clause ends at "has prompted efforts at protection." The clause that follows tells you exactly what those protective efforts are, so a colon, which introduces an explanation, is the best fit, and that makes C correct. A could technically join two independent clauses with comma plus "and," but "and" treats the second clause as a separate new point rather than a specific example of the efforts. B uses a semicolon, which can also join independent clauses, but it misses the same explaining relationship. D leaves out the comma that closes the appositive and joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice.
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구 뒤에서 삽입구 닫는 쉼표와 절 경계를 함께 판단하게 했고, 독립절 연결이 문법상 가능한 A·B를 구체화 관계라는 문맥으로 배제하게 설계했다.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 동격구 뒤 주절이 끝나는 지점을 찾아야 하고, 빈칸 뒤가 '특이한 거동'을 설명하는 독립절임을 확인해야 하는 두 단계 판단. 오답은 쉼표 접속 오류, 접속사 없는 붙인 문장, 세미콜론+and 오용이다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Nitinol ... behaves unusually when it is gently warmed'는 동격구가 길게 들어가 있어도 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'its crystal structure shifts ...'도 독립절이다. 뒤 절은 앞에서 말한 '특이한 거동'이 무엇인지 구체적으로 설명하므로, 독립절 뒤에 설명을 이어 주는 콜론을 쓴 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 접속 오류가 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문이다. C는 세미콜론 뒤에 'and'를 붙였는데, 세미콜론은 그 자체로 두 절을 잇기 때문에 등위접속사가 필요 없으므로 관례에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Even with the long appositive in the middle, "Nitinol ... behaves unusually when it is gently warmed" is a complete independent clause, and "its crystal structure shifts ..." is also an independent clause. The second clause explains what the "unusual" behavior actually is, so a colon, which joins an independent clause to an explanation that follows, works perfectly here. That makes D correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B puts the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on sentence. C adds "and" after a semicolon, but a semicolon already joins the clauses on its own, so the conjunction doesn't belong there under standard conventions.

g.passage: Ferrofluids, liquids containing nanoscale iron oxide particles coated with a surfactant that keeps them from clumping, behave like ordinary oils until a magnet is brought near. Engineers have adapted a related principle in magnetorheological dampers, devices installed in some bridges and luxury car suspensions. When a current passes through the damper's coil, the suspended particles align into chains along the magnetic field ______ the fluid thickens within milliseconds, allowing the damper to absorb sudden vibrations.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞뒤는 각각 독립절이므로 쉼표+등위접속사 and로 연결해야 하고, 뒤따르는 도입 부사구 as a result 뒤에는 쉼표가 와야 한다. A는 두 조건을 모두 충족한다. B는 and 뒤에 쉼표를 두고 as a result 뒤 쉼표를 빼서 삽입구를 한쪽만 닫아 오류다. C는 두 독립절을 잇는 and 앞 쉼표가 없다. D는 접속사 없이 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 접속(comma splice)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before and after the blank is an independent clause on each side, so you need a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "and" to join them, and the introductory phrase "as a result" that starts the second clause should be followed by a comma. Choice A does both. Choice B puts a comma after "and" but leaves out the comma after "as a result," so the interrupting phrase is set off on only one side. Choice C leaves out the comma before "and" that should come between the two independent clauses. Choice D joins the clauses with commas only and no conjunction, which makes a comma splice.
g.design: To find the clause boundary, you have to read past the long noun phrase before the blank. Then you have to check two things: whether the conjunction is there and how the transitional phrase is punctuated. Each wrong answer gets only part of this right.

c.seed: physical science — Ziegler-Natta catalyst stereospecific polymerization and polypropylene tacticity control industrial synthesis

g.passage: Before the 1950s, attempts to polymerize propylene yielded a sticky, rubbery mass in which the methyl groups along the chain pointed in random directions. The catalysts developed by Karl Ziegler and Giulio Natta changed this outcome: by binding each incoming monomer in a fixed orientation at the metal center, they ______ the arrangement of the methyl groups, producing isotactic chains whose regular structure allowed them to pack into a rigid, crystalline plastic suitable for industrial use.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 촉매가 단량체를 고정된 방향으로 결합시켜 메틸기 배열을 규칙적으로 만들었다고 설명하므로, 배열을 '결정했다/지정했다'는 뜻의 B가 정답이다. A는 촉매가 반응을 빠르게 한다는 일반 상식과 맞아 보이지만, 지문의 핵심은 속도가 아니라 배열의 규칙성이다. D는 배열에 변화를 주었다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 무작위 상태를 규칙적으로 바꾼 것이므로 '다양화했다'는 정반대다. C는 배열을 숨겼다는 뜻으로, 구조가 드러나 결정성을 낳았다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the catalysts bound each monomer in a fixed orientation, which turned random methyl placement into a regular isotactic pattern, so B ("dictated") fits: the catalysts determined the arrangement. A looks tempting because catalysts usually speed up reactions, but the sentence is about how orderly the structure is, not how fast the reaction runs. D seems possible because the catalysts did change the arrangement, but they made it more uniform, which is the opposite of diversifying it. C means hiding the arrangement, and nothing in the text is about hiding it; the point is that the catalysts produced a regular structure.

g.passage: The iridescent green of many weevils and jewel beetles does not come from pigment. Instead, their exoskeletons contain photonic crystals: chitin arranged in a lattice whose spacing is close to the wavelength of visible light. Because of this periodic structure, light within a certain band of wavelengths cannot travel through the material and is reflected back. Researchers note that this mechanism makes the color unusually ______: whereas pigments gradually break down under sunlight, a structural color persists as long as the lattice itself remains intact, which explains why specimens collected more than a century ago still gleam in museum drawers.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 빈칸 뒤 콜론 이하에서 색소는 햇빛에 분해되지만 구조색은 격자가 유지되는 한 지속되고, 백 년 된 표본도 여전히 빛난다고 설명하므로 '오래 지속되는'을 뜻하는 C가 정답이다. A는 반짝이는 색이라는 묘사와 어울리지만 시간에 따른 지속성이라는 핵심 대비를 담지 못한다. B는 구조색이 시야각에 따라 변한다는 배경지식과 연결될 수 있으나 지문은 변하지 않고 지속됨을 강조하므로 반대 방향이다. D는 빛이 반사된다는 앞 문장과 표면적으로 일치하지만, 빈칸 뒤의 근거인 분해 대 지속의 대비를 설명하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The colon after the blank sets up the explanation: pigments break down under sunlight, but structural color lasts as long as the lattice survives, so century-old specimens still gleam. That points to C, meaning long-lasting. A fits the shiny appearance, but it doesn't capture the contrast about lasting over time. B may remind you that iridescent color shifts with viewing angle, but the text stresses that the color stays the same, which is the opposite idea. D echoes the earlier statement that light is reflected, but it doesn't match the reasoning that follows the blank, which compares breaking down with lasting.
g.design: 오답 A·D는 지문 앞부분(반짝임·반사)에 부분 근거를 두어 훑어 읽으면 끌리게 했고, 정답은 빈칸 뒤 지속성 대비를 연결해야만 확정되도록 두 단계 판단을 요구했다.

c.seed: physical science — Ionic gel polymer electrolyte ionic conductivity temperature dependence and electrochemical cell performance

g.passage: Ionic gel polymer electrolytes, which trap a salt-rich liquid inside a flexible polymer network, are attractive for batteries because they resist leaking. Their ionic conductivity, however, depends strongly on temperature: as the gel warms, the polymer chains loosen and ions move more freely. Materials chemist Lena Okafor found that a cell built with one such gel delivered nearly its full capacity at 40°C but lost much of it at −10°C, when the stiffened network slowed ion transport. Because the gel's performance is so ______ the temperature at which a cell operates, Okafor argues that such electrolytes should be tested across a wide thermal range before being considered for outdoor devices.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 젤의 전도도와 셀 용량이 온도에 따라 크게 달라진다(40°C에서는 거의 전부, −10°C에서는 크게 감소)고 설명하므로, 성능이 온도에 '좌우된다'는 뜻의 D가 정답이며, 넓은 온도 범위에서 시험해야 한다는 결론과도 맞는다. A는 '무관하다'는 뜻이라 온도 의존성과 정반대이다. B는 젤이 누액에 강하다는 앞부분과 연결되어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 성능이 온도에 '저항한다'면 광범위한 온도 시험을 요구할 이유가 약해진다. C는 성능을 온도와 '비슷하다'고 비교하는 셈이라 논리적 관계를 정확히 표현하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that the gel's conductivity and the cell's capacity change sharply with temperature: nearly full capacity at 40°C but much less at −10°C. So the performance is "contingent on" (dependent on) operating temperature, which is why Okafor wants testing across a wide thermal range; choice D is correct. Choice A, "independent of," says the opposite of the temperature dependence the text describes. Choice B, "resistant to," may seem fitting because the gel resists leaking, but if performance resisted temperature changes, there would be little reason to demand broad thermal testing. Choice C, "comparable to," would mean the performance resembles temperature, which doesn't express the cause-and-effect relationship.
g.design: 정답은 지문의 온도 의존 데이터와 결론 문장을 연결해야 확정되며, B는 앞부분 '누액 저항'과 표면 연결되는 함정, A는 반대 방향 함정으로 설계했다.

c.seed: physical science — Electrospinning polymer jet formation and nanofiber diameter control voltage flow rate optimization

g.passage: In electrospinning, a high voltage draws a charged polymer solution from a needle into a thin jet that stretches and dries into nanofibers. Materials engineer Priya Raman found that the voltage and the flow rate cannot be tuned independently: raising the voltage thins the fibers only if the flow rate is lowered at the same time, since excess solution otherwise thickens the jet faster than the electric field can stretch it. Because of this interdependence, Raman argues that the two settings must be ______ rather than optimized one at a time.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 전압과 유량이 서로 영향을 주므로 따로따로 조정할 수 없다고 말하고, 빈칸은 "하나씩 최적화하는 것"과 대비되는 말이어야 하므로 두 값을 함께 맞춘다는 뜻의 A(coordinated)가 정답이다. B(maximized)는 전압을 높이는 내용과 일부 맞아 보이지만, 지문에서는 유량을 낮춰야 한다고 하므로 두 값을 모두 최대로 올리는 것은 맞지 않는다. C(standardized)는 정해진 설정값이라는 뜻이어서 두 값이 서로에 맞춰 함께 바뀐다는 핵심을 담지 못한다. D(isolated)는 따로 다룬다는 뜻으로, 지문이 부정하는 "하나씩 최적화"와 같은 의미가 되어 버린다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says voltage and flow rate depend on each other, and the blank has to contrast with "optimized one at a time." That means the two settings must be adjusted together, so choice A (coordinated) is the answer. Choice B (maximized) can look right because the passage mentions raising the voltage, but the flow rate actually has to be lowered, so pushing both settings to their highest values doesn't work. Choice C (standardized) means fixed, agreed-upon values, which misses the point that each setting must change in response to the other. Choice D (isolated) means handling the settings separately, which is exactly the one-at-a-time approach the passage rejects.
g.design: To answer, students have to connect two pieces of information: the cause-and-effect relationship between the settings and the "rather than one at a time" contrast. Choices B and D each borrow a clue from the passage on the surface (raising voltage; independent tuning) to tempt students, and choice C is a plausible technical term that still doesn't fit the context.

c.seed: physical science — Starch gelatinization amylose leaching viscosity changes controlled heating wet cooking transformation

g.passage: When starch granules are heated in water, they do not simply soften. Within a narrow temperature range, the granules absorb water, swell, and lose their ordered crystalline structure, a process called gelatinization. As the granules swell, amylose molecules leach out into the surrounding liquid, and the mixture's viscosity rises sharply. Food scientists have found that this transformation is highly sensitive to the rate of heating: when the temperature climbs too quickly, granules on the outside of a mixture can burst before those in the center have swollen at all. For this reason, recipes that depend on a smooth, uniform sauce often call for heat that is ______, allowing every granule to pass through the same stages at roughly the same time.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 온도가 너무 빨리 오르면 바깥 입자가 먼저 터져 불균일해진다고 설명하므로, 해결책은 천천히 올라가는 열, 즉 B 'gradual'이다. A 'intense'는 열이 강하다는 뜻으로, 지문이 문제로 지적한 급격한 가열을 오히려 부추긴다. C 'brief'는 짧은 시간을 뜻해 열이 오르는 속도와 무관하고, 모든 입자가 단계를 거칠 시간을 주지도 못한다. D 'constant'는 일정함이라는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 일정하게 높은 열은 여전히 빠른 온도 상승을 일으킬 수 있으며 지문의 핵심인 '상승 속도'를 정확히 짚지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says that when the temperature rises too quickly, outer granules burst before inner ones swell, so the fix is heat that rises slowly. That makes B, "gradual," the answer. A, "intense," means strong heat, which would make the rapid heating problem worse. C, "brief," describes how long the heat lasts, not how fast the temperature rises, and it wouldn't give every granule time to go through each stage. D, "constant," sounds reasonable because it suggests steadiness, but steady high heat can still raise the temperature fast, so it misses the text's point about the rate of heating.
g.design: To get the answer, you have to connect the problem the text describes (heating that rises too fast) with the goal (granules swelling at the same time). "Constant" is the tempting wrong answer because it suggests evenness, and "intense" and "brief" each connect to the topic of heating.

g.passage: In reverse osmosis desalination, seawater is pushed against a membrane that lets water molecules through but blocks dissolved salts. The process works only if the applied pressure exceeds the seawater's osmotic pressure, the natural tendency of water to move toward the saltier side. As fresh water leaves, the brine left behind grows more concentrated, so its osmotic pressure rises. Engineers therefore note that the required pump pressure does not stay fixed during operation; instead, it must ______ as recovery increases, or the flow of purified water will slow and eventually stop.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 농축수의 삼투압이 계속 올라가므로, 물이 계속 흐르려면 가해지는 압력도 함께 증가해야 한다. 따라서 '점점 높아지다'를 뜻하는 C(escalate)가 정답이다. A(fluctuate)는 압력이 고정되지 않는다는 점과는 맞지만, 오르내림을 뜻해 한 방향으로 꾸준히 증가한다는 의미를 정확히 담지 못한다. B(stabilize)는 압력이 고정되지 않는다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. D(reverse)는 물의 흐름 방향과 관련 있어 보이지만, 압력의 방향을 바꾸면 담수화 원리 자체가 무너진다.
g.explanation_en: The brine's osmotic pressure keeps rising, so the applied pressure has to keep climbing to stay above it. That makes C (escalate), meaning "increase steadily," the right answer. A (fluctuate) does fit the idea that the pressure isn't fixed, but it means going up and down, not a steady one-way increase. B (stabilize) contradicts the statement that the pressure does not stay fixed. D (reverse) might seem connected to which way the water flows, but reversing the pressure would undo the desalination process entirely.
g.design: 이 문항은 두 정보를 연결해야 풀린다. 하나는 농축수가 진해질수록 삼투압이 오른다는 점이고, 다른 하나는 가하는 압력이 삼투압보다 커야 한다는 점이다. 'does not stay fixed'만 훑어 읽으면 fluctuate를 고르기 쉽고, reverse는 삼투 방향이라는 개념에서 끌어온 매력적인 오답이다.

g.passage: Conventional sintering fuses ceramic powders by heating them in a furnace for hours, but that long exposure to high temperature lets tiny crystal grains merge into larger ones, which can make the finished part brittle. Spark plasma sintering (SPS) instead passes pulsed electric current directly through the powder while pressing it, reaching full density in minutes. Materials scientist Lena Okafor notes that this speed does more than save time: because the powder spends so little time hot, SPS can ______ grain growth, allowing engineers to produce dense ceramic composites whose fine-grained structure gives them unusual toughness.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 오랜 가열이 결정립을 키워 부품을 취약하게 만든다고 설명한 뒤, SPS는 고온 노출 시간이 짧아 미세한 결정립 구조를 유지한다고 말한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 결정립 성장을 '억제하다'라는 뜻의 D가 들어가야 한다. A는 속도(speed)라는 단어에 끌린 오답으로, 성장을 촉진하면 미세 구조라는 결론과 정반대가 된다. B와 C는 과학 실험 맥락에서 그럴듯하지만, 짧은 가열 시간이 결정립 성장을 드러내거나 측정한다는 인과 관계는 지문에 없고 미세 구조가 생기는 이유도 설명하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says long heating lets grains grow larger, while SPS keeps the powder hot only briefly and yields a fine-grained structure. So the blank needs a word meaning "hold back," which is D. A may tempt you because the passage stresses speed, but accelerating grain growth would contradict the fine-grained result. B and C sound reasonable in a lab setting, but the passage gives no reason why brief heating would reveal or measure grain growth, and neither word explains why the structure stays fine.
g.design: 빈칸 앞의 원인(짧은 고온 노출)과 뒤의 결과(미세 결정립)를 연결해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. 'speed'에 끌리는 A와, 과학 맥락에서 그럴듯한 B·C를 함정으로 두었다.

g.passage: Materials scientists designing self-cleaning glass often imitate the lotus leaf, whose microscopic bumps trap air so that water beads up and rolls off, carrying dirt with it. In a recent study, engineers coated glass panels with silica nanoparticles and measured the angle each water droplet formed with the surface. Although the coating initially produced contact angles above 150 degrees, after six months of outdoor exposure the angles had fallen to roughly 90 degrees, indicating that the coating's water-repelling ability had ______ rather than vanished entirely.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 접촉각이 150도 이상에서 약 90도로 떨어졌지만 "완전히 사라지지는 않았다"는 대비가 있으므로, 발수 능력이 '줄어들었다'는 A가 정답이다. B는 성질이 반대로 바뀌었다는 뜻인데, 90도는 여전히 친수성으로 완전히 뒤집힌 상태가 아니며 'rather than vanished entirely'와도 맞지 않는다. C는 변화가 멈췄다는 뜻으로 떨어진 뒤의 상태를 일부 설명할 수는 있으나, 지문의 핵심은 감소이며 6개월 뒤 측정 한 번만으로는 안정화를 판단할 수 없다. D는 수치가 떨어진 것과 정반대 방향이다.
g.explanation_en: The contact angle dropped from above 150 degrees to about 90 degrees, and the text contrasts this with the ability having "vanished entirely," so the ability weakened but remained. That makes A correct. B suggests the property flipped to its opposite, but a 90-degree angle doesn't show a full reversal, and the contrast with vanishing doesn't fit. C suggests the change stopped, which might seem to describe the end result, but the text emphasizes a decline, and a single measurement after six months can't show stability. D goes the wrong direction, since the angles fell.

c.seed: physical science — Thermal cycling fatigue crack initiation solder joints mechanical reliability microelectronics interconnect failure

g.passage: When a circuit board heats up and cools down repeatedly, the copper pads and the silicon chip expand and contract by different amounts, putting stress on the tiny solder joints that connect them. Materials engineer Priya Raman found that a single cycle almost never causes visible damage. Instead, each cycle adds a little strain to the solder's grain structure, and over thousands of cycles the effect ______: microscopic voids gradually join together until a crack forms and the electrical connection fails.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 한 번의 사이클로는 손상이 없지만 각 사이클이 '조금씩' 변형을 더해 수천 번 후 균열이 생긴다고 설명하므로, 작은 효과가 쌓인다는 뜻의 B(accumulates)가 정답이다. C(intensifies)는 효과가 커진다는 점에서 부분적으로 맞지만, 각 사이클의 강도가 세진다는 의미여서 작은 손상이 더해진다는 '누적'의 핵심을 정확히 담지 못한다. D(disperses)는 미세 공극이 '흩어진다'는 연상과 연결될 수 있으나, 공극이 서로 합쳐진다는 내용과 정반대이다. A(reverses)는 냉각 시 수축하는 상황을 떠올리게 하지만, 손상이 결국 고장으로 이어진다는 흐름과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: The text says one cycle almost never causes damage, but each cycle adds a little strain, and after thousands of cycles a crack forms. That describes small effects building up over time, so B (accumulates) is correct. C (intensifies) is partly right because the damage does grow, but it suggests each cycle gets stronger, which misses the key idea of small amounts adding up. D (disperses) might call to mind the voids being spread out, but the text says the voids join together, which is the opposite. A (reverses) might fit the idea of cooling undoing expansion, but it contradicts the point that the damage ends in failure.
g.design: 빈칸 앞 '조금씩 더함'과 빈칸 뒤 '점차 합쳐져 균열'의 두 정보를 연결해야 하며, 강화(C)와 냉각 시 되돌림(A)의 부분 근거를 가진 오답을 배치했다.
