g.passage: In microfluidic devices, charged particles suspended in a liquid can be separated by applying an electric field along a narrow channel. Each particle's speed depends largely on its zeta potential, the electrical charge at the boundary between its surface and the surrounding fluid. Engineer Priya Raman found, however, that in channels coated with certain polymers, the fluid itself moved so little under the field that particles with nearly identical zeta potentials, which normally travel together, ended up in clearly separate bands. By reducing the background flow that usually carries all particles along together, the coating ______ small differences in particle motion that would otherwise go unnoticed.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문에 따르면 코팅은 모든 입자를 함께 실어 나르던 배경 흐름을 줄였고, 그 결과 원래 있었지만 '눈에 띄지 않던' 미세한 차이가 뚜렷한 띠로 나타났다. 따라서 이미 있던 차이를 드러냈다는 뜻의 C가 정답이다. A는 코팅이 차이를 새로 만들어 냈다는 뜻이 되는데, 지문은 그 차이가 원래 있었으나 가려져 있었다고 말하므로 틀리다. B는 반대 의미로, 입자들이 분리된 결과와 모순된다. D는 흐름이 줄어든 것과 관련 있어 보이지만, 차이를 안정시켰다는 말은 차이가 눈에 보이게 되었다는 핵심을 담지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the coating cut down the background flow that normally carries all particles along together, so small differences that "would otherwise go unnoticed" showed up as separate bands. That means the coating made differences that already existed visible, so C is correct. A says the coating created the differences, but the passage presents them as already there, just hidden. B means the opposite and conflicts with the particles separating. D may seem to fit because the flow was reduced, but "stabilized" misses the main point: the differences became observable.
g.design: Two steps: link the reduced background flow to the phrase "would otherwise go unnoticed," and see that the differences already existed. "Generated" and "stabilized" each fit part of the context, so they tempt students who skim.

g.passage: Magnetorheological (MR) fluid is a suspension of tiny iron particles in oil. Under normal conditions it flows freely, but when an electromagnetic coil is switched on, the particles line up into chains and the fluid thickens almost instantly, becoming nearly as stiff as a soft solid. Engineers have used this property in dampers that protect buildings from earthquakes. Because the strength of the magnetic field can be adjusted continuously, the damper's resistance is not fixed at one level; sensors detect the ground's motion, and a controller ______ the fluid's viscosity from moment to moment, stiffening it during strong shaking and loosening it during milder tremors.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 자기장 세기를 연속적으로 조절할 수 있어 저항이 한 수준에 고정되지 않으며, 강한 진동에는 굳히고 약한 진동에는 풀어 준다고 설명한다. 따라서 상황에 맞춰 점성을 정밀하게 조정한다는 뜻의 D(calibrates)가 정답이다. A는 '굳힌다'는 부분과는 맞지만 약한 진동 때 풀어 준다는 내용과 충돌한다. B는 점성을 일정하게 유지한다는 뜻이어서 '고정되지 않는다'는 내용과 반대이다. C는 점성이 바뀐다는 점은 맞지만, 단순히 반대로 뒤집는 것이지 진동 세기에 맞춰 단계적으로 조절한다는 뜻을 담지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the field strength can be adjusted continuously, so the damper's resistance is not fixed. The fluid is stiffened during strong shaking and loosened during milder tremors. So the controller precisely adjusts viscosity to match conditions, which makes D (calibrates) the answer. A fits the stiffening part, but it doesn't fit the loosening during mild tremors. B means keeping viscosity unchanged, which goes against the idea that resistance is not fixed. C does suggest change, but it means simply flipping the viscosity to its opposite, not fine-tuning it to how strong the shaking is.
g.design: I gave A and C partial support (stiffening, change), so students have to connect the "continuously adjusted" detail with the two-way strong/mild contrast to rule them out.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Friction-stir welding (FSW) was developed at The Welding Institute in the United Kingdom in 1991.
- In FSW, a rotating tool with a shoulder and a pin is plunged into the seam between two metal plates.
- Friction from the spinning tool softens the metal to roughly 80 percent of its melting point without actually melting it.
- The tool stirs the softened metal from both plates together, forming a solid bond as it cools.
- Conventional fusion welding melts aluminum alloys, which can create porosity and cracks that weaken aircraft joints.
- Because FSW joints avoid these defects, some manufacturers use the process to join fuselage panels in place of thousands of rivets.
g.question: The student wants to explain why friction-stir welding is suited to aircraft construction. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Because friction-stir welding joins aluminum without melting it, it avoids the porosity and cracks of fusion welding, allowing some manufacturers to replace thousands of fuselage rivets.
Because friction-stir welding uses a rotating tool with a shoulder and a pin, it can be plunged into the seam between two metal plates, including aluminum ones.
Because friction-stir welding was developed at The Welding Institute in 1991, it has been studied for decades by manufacturers of many kinds of metal products.
Because friction-stir welding heats metal to roughly 80 percent of its melting point, it softens plates enough for the spinning tool to stir them together.
g.explanation: A는 금속을 녹이지 않는다는 점과 용융 용접의 결함(기공·균열)을 피한다는 점을 연결해 항공기 동체 조립에 적합한 이유를 설명하므로 정답이다. B는 공구 구조를 정확히 옮겼지만 항공기에 적합한 이유는 제시하지 않는다. C는 개발 시기만 말하며 '수십 년 연구'는 메모에 없는 내용이고 항공기와도 무관하다. D는 공정 원리를 설명할 뿐 항공기 접합에서의 이점과 연결하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: A is correct because it links the fact that FSW does not melt the metal to its avoidance of the porosity and cracks caused by fusion welding, which explains why it works for fuselage panels. B accurately describes the tool but never says why that matters for aircraft. C gives only the origin date and adds a claim about decades of study that isn't in the notes, with no link to aircraft. D explains how the process softens and stirs metal, but it doesn't connect this to any advantage in aircraft construction.
g.design: 정답은 '녹이지 않음'과 '결함 회피→리벳 대체'라는 두 메모를 연결해야 하며, 오답은 같은 'Because FSW…' 틀로 정확한 메모를 쓰되 항공기 적합성 목표를 놓친다.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Electrochromic windows change how much light they let through when a small voltage is applied.
- Many such windows use a thin film of vanadium oxide layered between electrodes.
- When voltage drives lithium ions into the vanadium oxide film (a process called intercalation), the film darkens and blocks more light.
- Reversing the voltage pulls the ions back out, and the film becomes clear again.
- Once the film has switched, it holds its tint without drawing additional power.
g.question: The student wants to explain how the film returns to its transparent state. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: When voltage drives lithium ions into a vanadium oxide film, the film darkens and blocks more light from passing through the window.
When the voltage is reversed, lithium ions are pulled back out of the vanadium oxide film, allowing the window to become clear again.
When a vanadium oxide film has finished switching, it keeps its tint without drawing any additional power from the window's circuit.
When a small voltage is applied, an electrochromic window with a vanadium oxide film changes how much light it lets through.
g.explanation: 목표는 필름이 투명한 상태로 되돌아가는 과정을 설명하는 것이다. B는 전압을 반대로 걸면 리튬 이온이 빠져나가 창이 다시 투명해진다는 메모를 사용해 그 과정을 정확히 설명한다. A는 정확한 메모를 쓰지만 투명해지는 과정이 아니라 어두워지는 과정을 설명한다. C는 색이 바뀐 뒤 전력 없이 그 상태를 유지한다는 점만 말할 뿐 투명해지는 원리는 다루지 않는다. D는 빛 투과량이 바뀐다는 일반적인 특징만 소개하며 되돌아가는 과정은 설명하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain how the film becomes transparent again. B does exactly that: it says that reversing the voltage pulls the lithium ions back out of the film, and this lets the window clear. A uses an accurate note, but it describes how the film darkens, which is the opposite process. C only says the film keeps its tint without using extra power, so it never explains how the film clears. D gives a general overview of how the window changes light transmission, but it doesn't describe the return to the clear state.
g.design: 네 선택지 모두 'When ...' 동일 틀에 정확한 메모를 쓰게 하고, 질문은 'reversing/clear' 대신 'returns to its transparent state'로 바꿔 표면 일치를 피했다. A는 같은 이온 메커니즘을 써서 훑어 읽으면 헷갈리게 했다.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Precision optical lenses, such as those in telescopes and lithography systems, require surfaces smooth to within a few nanometers.
- Conventional mechanical polishing removes glass by abrasion: hard particles scratch away material, which can leave microscopic subsurface cracks.
- Tribochemical polishing uses softer particles, such as cerium oxide, that chemically bond with the glass surface during rubbing.
- In tribochemical polishing, the bonded surface atoms are then carried away by the particles, removing material roughly one molecular layer at a time.
- Because it relies on chemical bonding rather than scratching, tribochemical polishing leaves far less subsurface damage than abrasive polishing.
g.question: The student wants to contrast how the two polishing methods take material off a glass surface. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Precision optical lenses require surfaces smooth to within a few nanometers, and tribochemical polishing, which uses cerium oxide particles, can help meet this requirement.
Tribochemical polishing leaves far less subsurface damage than abrasive polishing, making it valuable for lenses in telescopes and lithography systems.
Whereas conventional polishing relies on hard particles scratching glass away, tribochemical polishing works through softer particles that bond chemically with surface atoms and then carry them off.
Tribochemical polishing removes material roughly one molecular layer at a time, as softer particles such as cerium oxide bond with the glass during rubbing.
g.design: 질문은 '재료를 떼어내는 방식의 대조'로 표현하고 정답은 scratching/bonding 어휘를 사용해 표면 일치를 피했다. B는 두 방법을 비교하지만 제거 방식이 아닌 결과(손상)를, D는 제거 방식이지만 한 방법만 다뤄 두 단계 판단이 필요하다.
g.explanation: 정답은 C이다. 목표는 두 연마법이 유리 표면의 재료를 제거하는 '방식'을 대조하는 것인데, C만 기존 연마의 긁어내기(마모)와 마찰화학 연마의 화학 결합 후 운반을 함께 제시한다. B는 두 방법을 비교하지만 제거 방식이 아니라 결과인 표면 아래 손상을 대조한다. D는 제거 방식을 정확히 설명하지만 마찰화학 연마 하나만 다루어 대조가 없다. A는 렌즈 요구 조건과 한 방법만 언급해 목표와 관련이 가장 적다.
g.explanation_en: The answer is C. Your goal is to contrast how the two methods remove material, and only C pairs conventional polishing's scratching action with tribochemical polishing's bonding-then-carrying-away process. B does compare the two methods, but it contrasts their result (subsurface damage), not how they remove material. D accurately describes the removal mechanism, but only for tribochemical polishing, so there is no contrast. A mentions lens requirements and only one method, so it misses the goal entirely.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In a magnetic material, the spins of electrons tend to line up along certain preferred crystal directions, called "easy axes."
- Magnetocrystalline anisotropy is the energy cost of turning those spins away from an easy axis.
- Neodymium-iron-boron (Nd2Fe14B) has a very strong anisotropy, so its spins strongly resist being turned.
- As a result, Nd2Fe14B has high coercivity: a strong opposing field is needed to demagnetize it, making it useful for permanent magnets in electric motors.
- Soft iron has a weak anisotropy, so its spins turn easily, and it loses its magnetization in a weak opposing field.
g.question: The student wants to explain why one material keeps its magnetization better than the other. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Nd2Fe14B is used in permanent magnets for electric motors, while soft iron loses its magnetization in a weak opposing field.
In both Nd2Fe14B and soft iron, electron spins tend to line up along preferred crystal directions called easy axes.
Magnetocrystalline anisotropy is the energy cost of turning spins away from an easy axis, and it is very strong in Nd2Fe14B.

Because its strong anisotropy makes spins resist turning away from easy axes, Nd2Fe14B needs a strong opposing field to demagnetize, whereas soft iron, with weak anisotropy, loses magnetization in a weak one.
g.explanation: 목표는 두 물질을 비교하면서 '왜' 한쪽이 자화를 더 잘 유지하는지 원인을 설명하는 것이다. D는 이방성의 강약(원인)과 탈자에 필요한 자기장 크기(결과)를 두 물질 모두에 대해 연결하므로 목표를 달성한다. A는 두 물질의 차이를 보여주지만 이방성이라는 원인을 빠뜨려 이유를 설명하지 못한다. B는 두 물질의 공통점만 말해 차이를 설명하지 않는다. C는 원인을 정의하지만 Nd2Fe14B 하나만 다루고 자화 유지라는 결과나 비교가 없다.
g.explanation_en: The goal asks you to compare the two materials and explain why one holds its magnetization better. D links the cause (strong versus weak anisotropy) to the result (strong versus weak field needed to demagnetize) for both materials, so it accomplishes the goal. A shows a difference but leaves out anisotropy, so it never explains why. B only states something the two materials share, which doesn't explain a difference. C defines the cause but covers only Nd2Fe14B and never connects it to keeping magnetization or makes a comparison.
g.design: 오답 A와 C는 각각 결과만 또는 원인만 담아 부분적으로 맞고, 원인-결과-대조를 모두 연결해야 정답을 고를 수 있게 했다. 질문은 'anisotropy'나 'coercivity' 같은 핵심어를 피했다.

c.seed: physical science — Zeolite molecular sieve pore structure selective gas adsorption industrial air separation processes

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Zeolites are crystalline minerals whose aluminosilicate frameworks contain channels and cages of uniform, molecule-sized pores.
- Zeolite 5A has pores about 0.5 nanometers wide, large enough to admit both nitrogen and oxygen molecules.
- Zeolite 3A has pores about 0.3 nanometers wide, which admit water molecules but exclude most larger gas molecules.
- In zeolite 13X, charged sodium ions inside the pores attract nitrogen molecules more strongly than oxygen molecules, so nitrogen is held while oxygen passes through.
- Medical oxygen concentrators push air through beds of zeolite 13X to deliver air that is roughly 90 percent oxygen.
g.question: The student wants to explain how a zeolite can separate two gases even when both kinds of molecules fit inside its pores. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Although nitrogen and oxygen molecules both enter the pores of zeolite 13X, sodium ions there bind nitrogen more tightly, letting oxygen flow on ahead.
Because zeolite 3A has pores only about 0.3 nanometers wide, it admits water molecules while keeping out most larger gas molecules.
Although zeolite 5A has pores wide enough to admit both nitrogen and oxygen, zeolite 3A has narrower pores that exclude most gas molecules.
Because zeolite 13X separates nitrogen from oxygen, medical oxygen concentrators use it to produce air that is roughly 90 percent oxygen.
g.design: 질문은 '둘 다 구멍에 들어가는데도 분리되는 원리'를 묻는다. 정답은 13X의 크기 조건과 이온 인력 메모를 함께 묶어야 하고, 오답은 정확한 메모를 쓰되 크기 차이에 따른 분리, 두 제올라이트 비교, 응용 사례로 방향이 어긋나게 만들었다.
g.explanation: 목표는 두 기체가 모두 기공에 들어가는 상황에서도 분리가 일어나는 원리를 설명하는 것이다. A는 질소와 산소가 모두 13X 기공에 들어간다는 점과, 나트륨 이온이 질소를 더 강하게 붙잡는다는 메커니즘을 함께 제시하므로 목표를 달성한다. B는 기공 크기로 분자를 걸러내는 방식이라 '둘 다 들어가는' 조건에 맞지 않는다. C는 두 분자를 모두 받아들이는 5A를 언급하지만 분리 원리는 설명하지 않고 기공 크기만 비교한다. D는 13X의 응용 사례만 말하고, 분리가 어떻게 일어나는지는 설명하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The goal is to explain how a zeolite can separate two gases even when both kinds of molecules fit into its pores. A does this: it says that nitrogen and oxygen both enter zeolite 13X, then gives the mechanism, which is that sodium ions hold nitrogen more tightly. B describes separation by pore size, so it doesn't fit the case where both molecules get in. C mentions zeolite 5A, which admits both gases, but it only compares pore sizes and never explains how a separation happens. D gives a use for zeolite 13X but doesn't explain how the separation works.

c.seed: physical science — Fluorescence Förster resonance energy transfer donor-acceptor proximity detection biochemical assays

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) is a process in which an excited fluorescent molecule (the donor) passes energy to a nearby molecule (the acceptor) without emitting light.
- FRET occurs efficiently only when donor and acceptor are within about 1 to 10 nanometers of each other.
- When FRET occurs, the donor's fluorescence dims and the acceptor glows at its own, longer wavelength.
- Biochemists attach a donor to one protein and an acceptor to another to test whether the two proteins bind.
- If the proteins bind, acceptor emission appears; if they remain apart, only donor emission is detected.
g.question: The student wants to explain how researchers can tell from a FRET assay whether two proteins have come together. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In FRET, an excited donor molecule transfers energy to an acceptor molecule without emitting light, a process that works efficiently only across distances of about 1 to 10 nanometers.

In FRET assays, a donor is attached to one protein and an acceptor to another; light at the acceptor's longer wavelength signals that the proteins have bound, whereas donor emission alone signals that they remain apart.
In FRET assays, biochemists attach a donor to one protein and an acceptor to another, since FRET occurs efficiently only when the two molecules are within about 1 to 10 nanometers.
In FRET, the donor's fluorescence dims while the acceptor glows at its own, longer wavelength, showing that energy has passed between the molecules without light being emitted.
g.explanation: 목표는 FRET 분석에서 두 단백질의 결합 여부를 어떻게 판별하는지 설명하는 것이다. B는 표지 방식과 결합 시/비결합 시 관찰되는 신호를 연결해 판별 방법을 완성한다. A는 FRET의 원리와 거리 조건만 말하고 단백질 분석은 다루지 않는다. C는 실험 설계와 거리 조건은 언급하지만 어떤 신호로 결합을 판단하는지 빠져 있다. D는 FRET이 일어날 때의 형광 변화를 설명하지만 이를 단백질 결합 판별과 연결하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain how researchers tell from a FRET assay whether two proteins have bound. B does this: it describes the labeling setup and then links each possible signal to an outcome, bound or apart. A only explains the basic FRET process and the distance limit, and it never mentions proteins or what the assay shows. C describes the setup and the distance limit but leaves out the signal researchers actually read. D describes the change in fluorescence during FRET but never connects it to deciding whether proteins have bound.
g.design: 정답은 표지 메모와 결과 메모 두 개를 결합해야 하며, C와 D는 각각 그중 절반(설계 또는 신호)만 담아 비교 판단이 필요하다.

c.seed: physical science — Electroplating metal ion reduction cathode surface nucleation jewelry circuit board manufacturing

g.passage: In electroplating, metal ions dissolved in a bath are reduced at a cathode, where they deposit as a thin metal coating. Manufacturers of jewelry and circuit boards have long assumed that the smoothness of a coating depends mainly on how much metal is deposited overall. Materials chemist Lena Hwang proposes a different explanation: smoothness is determined chiefly by the earliest stage of plating, when ions first form tiny clusters, or nuclei, on the bare cathode surface. According to Hwang, when many nuclei form at once and are spread densely across the surface, they merge into an even layer, but when only a few nuclei form, each grows into a separate bump that remains visible even after much more metal has been added.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Hwang's proposal?
options: Coatings that received the largest total amount of deposited metal were generally smoother than coatings that received smaller amounts, regardless of conditions during the first seconds of plating.
Cathodes on which nuclei formed densely in the first seconds of plating took slightly longer to reach a given coating thickness than cathodes on which nuclei formed sparsely.

Coatings of equal total thickness differed sharply in smoothness, and the smoothest ones were those whose cathodes had shown the highest number of nuclei per unit area in the first seconds of plating.
Circuit board coatings plated with copper were rougher on average than jewelry coatings plated with gold, even though both were plated to a similar final thickness.
g.explanation: Hwang의 주장은 증착된 금속의 총량이 아니라 초기 핵 밀도가 매끄러움을 결정한다는 것이다. C는 총 두께를 같게 통제한 상태에서 매끄러움이 초기 핵 밀도와 함께 달라졌음을 보여 주므로 이 주장을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 총량을 중시하는 기존 가정을 지지하므로 Hwang의 주장을 오히려 약화한다. B는 핵 밀도를 다루지만 매끄러움이 아니라 도금 속도에 관한 내용이다. D는 같은 두께에서 매끄러움이 차이 난다는 점을 보여 주지만, 그 차이를 핵 형성과 연결하지 않고 금속 종류의 차이로만 설명한다.
g.explanation_en: Hwang argues that coating smoothness depends mainly on how densely nuclei form at the start, not on the total amount of metal deposited. C keeps the total thickness the same and shows that smoothness tracked early nucleus density, so it directly supports her proposal. A supports the traditional total-amount view, which works against Hwang. B does mention nucleus density, but it links density to plating speed, not to smoothness. D shows that coatings of similar thickness can differ in smoothness, but it never connects that difference to nucleation. Instead, it only points to a difference between metals.
g.design: Two of the wrong answers are partly right: B uses nucleus density, and D holds thickness constant. To pick the answer, students have to connect two facts: thickness is held constant, and smoothness follows early nucleus density. The question avoids repeating the key words from the correct answer.

c.seed: physical science — Photochromic spiro compound isomerization reversible color change UV-activated eyeglass lens technology

g.passage: Photochromic eyeglass lenses darken outdoors because they contain spiro compounds such as spirooxazines. When ultraviolet light strikes one of these molecules, a bond in its ring structure breaks and the molecule unfolds into a flat, colored form called a merocyanine. Indoors, away from UV light, the molecule closes again and the lens clears. Users have long noticed that these lenses stay noticeably lighter on hot summer days than on cold winter days, even in equally bright sunlight. Chemist Lena Haviland proposes that this happens because heat speeds up the closing reaction: at higher temperatures, colored molecules snap back to the colorless form faster, so fewer of them are in the colored form at any one moment, even though UV light opens new molecules at the same rate.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Haviland's hypothesis?
options: Under steady UV exposure, lenses held at 35°C and lenses held at 5°C reached the same maximum darkness, but the 35°C lenses took longer to get there.
When lenses were kept in darkness at a single temperature, the colored form returned to the colorless form at a steady rate that depended on how many colored molecules were present.
Under steady UV exposure, lenses held at 35°C absorbed far less ultraviolet light than lenses held at 5°C, so fewer molecules were opened in the warm lenses.
When UV light was switched off, lenses held at 35°C cleared several times faster than lenses held at 5°C, while both sets of lenses absorbed UV light at the same rate.
g.explanation: Haviland의 가설은 두 부분으로 되어 있다. 열이 닫힘(탈색) 반응을 빠르게 하고, UV에 의한 열림 속도는 온도와 관계없이 같다는 것이다. D는 따뜻한 렌즈가 더 빨리 투명해지면서 UV 흡수량은 같았다는 결과이므로 두 부분을 모두 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 최대 어두움이 같았다고 하므로 따뜻한 날 렌즈가 더 밝다는 현상 자체와 맞지 않는다. B는 닫힘 반응을 설명하지만 온도를 비교하지 않는다. C는 열림 쪽 차이로 현상을 설명하므로 열림 속도가 같다는 가설의 전제와 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en: Haviland's hypothesis has two parts: heat speeds up the closing (fading) reaction, and UV opens molecules at the same rate no matter the temperature. D shows that warm lenses cleared faster while both sets absorbed UV equally, so it directly supports both parts. A says the maximum darkness was the same, which doesn't even match the observation that lenses stay lighter on hot days. B describes the closing reaction but never compares temperatures. C explains the effect through a difference in opening, which goes against the hypothesis's claim that the opening rate stays the same.
g.design: 정답은 가설의 두 요소(열에 의한 빠른 닫힘 + 같은 열림 속도)를 모두 충족해야 한다. 오답은 같은 '조건-결과' 문장 틀로 쓰고, 각각 한 요소만 맞히거나 다른 메커니즘을 내세운다.

c.instruction: 지문에 '한때 ~라고 여겨졌으나(통념)' 다음 'however/but/실제로는' 류의 전환어와 함께 이를 뒤집는 새 증거나 반박 문장을 제시하고, 빈칸이 그 반박된 결과를 표현하도록 한다. 정답은 통념과 정반대 방향의 의미를 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 통념 쪽 단어를 그대로 쓴 것, (2) 전환어를 못 읽고 통념과 같은 방향이지만 강도만 다른 단어, (3) 반박 대상과 무관한 제3의 의미 단어로 구성한다. 전환 지점 앞뒤 문장만으로 답이 결정되게 하고 문장 길이나 어휘 난이도는 중간 수준을 유지한다.
c.seed: physical science — Superfluid helium-four quantum fluid properties zero-viscosity flow cryogenic cooling system applications

g.passage: When helium-4 is cooled below about 2.17 kelvins, it becomes a superfluid that can flow through extremely narrow channels without any measurable friction. Early cryogenic engineers assumed that a liquid with such strange behavior would be too unpredictable to use in practical equipment and treated it as a laboratory curiosity. In practice, however, superfluid helium's ability to carry heat away with remarkable efficiency has made it ______ in systems that cool the superconducting magnets of large particle accelerators, where engineers now rely on it to keep conditions steady.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.design: 'too unpredictable to use…laboratory curiosity'라는 통념을 'In practice, however'로 뒤집고, 빈칸은 반박된 결과(필수적임)를 표현하게 했다. 오답은 통념 그대로(impractical), 같은 방향의 약한 표현(somewhat unreliable), 무관한 제3의 의미(luminous)로 구성했다.
g.explanation:
정답 A(indispensable, 없어서는 안 될). 'however' 뒤 문장을 보면 초유체 헬륨이 열을 매우 효율적으로 운반하고, 엔지니어들이 지금은 조건을 안정적으로 유지하는 데 '의존한다(rely on)'고 되어 있다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '실용성이 없다'는 통념과 정반대인 '필수적인'이 들어가야 한다.
B(impractical, 비실용적인): 반박당한 초기 엔지니어들의 생각을 그대로 옮긴 말이라 전환어 'however'와 맞지 않는다.
C(somewhat unreliable, 다소 신뢰할 수 없는): 전환어를 놓치고 통념과 같은 방향으로 강도만 약하게 한 표현이다. 'rely on'과 충돌한다.
D(luminous, 빛나는): 열 운반이나 실용성과 상관없는 제3의 의미다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is A, "indispensable." After "In practice, however," the text says superfluid helium carries heat away very efficiently and that engineers now rely on it to keep conditions steady. That reverses the early belief that it was too unpredictable to be practical, so the blank needs a word meaning "essential."
B, "impractical," just repeats the early engineers' belief, which the word "however" overturns.
C, "somewhat unreliable," misses the shift and keeps the old view, only in a weaker form. It also contradicts "rely on."
D, "luminous," means "glowing." It has nothing to do with heat transfer or usefulness.

c.instruction: 지문에 'is not X, but rather Y' 또는 'it isn't that A; instead B' 형태로 부정어 뒤에 대조 표현이 이어지는 문장을 만들고, 빈칸이 그 대조 표현(B) 자리에 오게 한다. 정답은 부정된 개념(X)과 반대 극성을 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 부정어를 무시하고 X와 같은 의미 단어, (2) 부정 구조를 이중으로 잘못 해석해 극성을 다시 뒤집은 단어, (3) 대조 구조와 무관한 유사 발음/철자 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: physical science — Piezoelectric quartz crystal oscillation frequency stability and resonant vibration in atomic clock timekeeping mechanisms

g.passage: Engineers who design atomic clocks often describe the quartz oscillator inside them as a kind of flywheel. When voltage is applied, the piezoelectric crystal bends and rebounds at its resonant frequency, and over a span of seconds that rhythm holds remarkably steady. Over days, however, temperature shifts and the slow aging of the crystal cause the frequency to drift. For this reason, the quartz's role in the clock is not autonomous but rather ______: a feedback loop repeatedly compares its output with the fixed transition frequency of cesium atoms and nudges the crystal back into step whenever the two diverge.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 정답 B(subordinate, 종속적인): 'not autonomous but rather ___' 구조에서 빈칸은 부정된 '자율적'과 반대 극성이어야 한다. 콜론 뒤 설명대로 수정 진동자는 세슘 원자의 기준 주파수에 계속 비교·교정되므로 그 기준에 종속된 역할이다. A(self-governing): 부정어를 무시하고 autonomous와 같은 뜻을 고른 오답이다. C(unconstrained, 제약 없는): 부정을 한 번 더 뒤집어 '자율이 아니다 → 제약이 없다'는 식으로 다시 자율 쪽 극성으로 돌아간 오답이며, 피드백 루프가 진동자를 계속 끌어당긴다는 설명과 맞지 않는다. D(subordinal): subordinate와 철자가 비슷하지만 '하위 분류의(분류학 용어)'라는 뜻이라 문맥과 무관하다.
g.explanation_en: B is correct. In the structure "not autonomous but rather ___," the blank needs a word with the opposite meaning of "autonomous." The part after the colon explains that a feedback loop keeps checking the quartz against cesium's fixed frequency and correcting it, so the quartz's role is subordinate, meaning it depends on that reference. A ("self-governing") ignores the negation and simply repeats the meaning of "autonomous." C ("unconstrained") flips the meaning a second time and ends up back on the autonomous side, which contradicts the constant correction described in the text. D ("subordinal") is spelled like "subordinate" but means "relating to a suborder" in biological classification, so it doesn't fit here.
g.design: 빈칸은 'not autonomous but rather' 대조 구조의 B 자리에 놓았다. 오답 셋은 각각 부정을 무시한 동의어(self-governing), 극성을 다시 뒤집은 단어(unconstrained), 철자가 비슷한 단어(subordinal)로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 지문을 두 단계(예: 상황 묘사 후 화자의 숙고, 또는 기존 주장 소개 후 저자의 반박/선언)로 구성하고, 빈칸을 두 번째 단계의 시작 지점에 배치해 앞 단계와 다른 서술 기능을 하도록 한다. 정답은 두 번째 단계의 기능(숙고, 반박, 선언 등)에 맞는 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 첫 번째 단계에 어울리는 단어, (2) 두 단계 어디에도 맞지 않는 중립적 단어, (3) 의미는 비슷하나 문장이 요구하는 품사/기능이 다른 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: physical science — Zeolite molecular sieve pore structure and selective gas adsorption in industrial oxygen-nitrogen air separation

g.passage: Zeolites are crystalline aluminosilicates filled with uniform, molecule-sized pores, and textbooks often call them "molecular sieves": in this account, they separate gases by letting small molecules through and blocking larger ones. For the industrial production of oxygen from air, however, this tidy image ______ how the process actually works. Oxygen and nitrogen molecules differ in size by only a fraction of an angstrom, and the zeolites used in air-separation plants hold on to nitrogen more strongly because nitrogen's larger quadrupole moment interacts strongly with the metal cations lining the pores, not because nitrogen is too large to enter.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation:
지문은 두 단계로 되어 있다. 첫 단계는 제올라이트를 크기로 걸러내는 '체'로 보는 교과서식 설명을 소개하고, 둘째 단계는 'however'로 시작해 그 설명을 반박한다. 산소와 질소는 크기가 거의 같고, 실제 분리는 질소의 사중극자 모멘트와 양이온 사이의 상호작용으로 일어난다. 그러므로 빈칸에는 그 깔끔한 이미지가 실제 원리를 '가린다'는 반박의 동사가 들어가야 하며, 정답은 C 'obscures'이다.
A 'illustrates'(보여 주다)는 첫 단계의 설명적 흐름에는 어울린다. 하지만 'however'로 시작하는 반박과 뒤따르는 반대 근거와는 모순된다.
B 'addresses'(다루다)는 중립적인 단어여서 그 이미지가 실제 원리와 어긋난다는 반박의 기능을 전달하지 못한다.
D 'erroneous'(잘못된)는 의미상으로는 반박에 가깝지만 형용사다. 'this tidy image ___ how the process works' 자리에는 목적어를 받는 동사가 필요하므로 문법적으로 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en:
The text has two stages. First, it presents the textbook picture of zeolites as size-based sieves. Then, starting with "however," it argues against that picture: oxygen and nitrogen are nearly the same size, and the real separation comes from nitrogen's quadrupole moment interacting with the cations in the pores. So the blank needs a verb that pushes back on the picture, saying it hides the real mechanism. That makes "obscures" (C) the correct answer.
- **A ("illustrates")** fits the descriptive first stage. But it contradicts the "however" and the evidence against the picture that follows.
- **B ("addresses")** is neutral. It doesn't say that the image misleads, so it can't do the job of a rebuttal.
- **D ("erroneous")** is close in meaning, but it's an adjective. The blank must be a verb that takes "how the process actually works" as its object.
g.design: The blank opens the second stage, which rebuts the first. The wrong answers are: a word that fits the first stage (illustrates), a neutral word (addresses), and a word with a similar meaning but the wrong part of speech (erroneous, an adjective).

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).

c.seed: physical science — Tribochemical polishing nanoscale material removal and atomic-scale asperity deformation in precision optical lens manufacturing

g.passage: Lens makers often finish glass surfaces with tribochemical polishing, in which a slurry of fine particles rubs against the glass while water in the slurry chemically softens the topmost layer of atoms. Engineers at one optics company tested this process on two identical batches of lenses. Both batches were polished with the same particles, pressure, and time, but the first batch was polished in a completely dry chamber, while the second was polished with water added. Under a microscope, the lenses in the first batch still showed tiny raised bumps, called asperities, that had been bent but not removed, whereas the lenses in the second batch were smooth at the atomic scale. Because water was the only difference between the two batches, the engineers concluded that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the polishing particles, rather than the water, were mainly responsible for removing the asperities from the second batch.
the dry chamber caused the asperities to form on the lenses in the first batch during polishing.
increasing the pressure in the dry chamber would have made the first batch just as smooth as the second batch.
the chemical action of water was needed for the asperities to be removed rather than merely bent.
g.design: 조건이 하나(물 유무)만 다른 통제 실험이라는 단일 규칙으로 결론을 끌어내게 했고, 오답은 같은 'the ... was/were/would' 틀의 전형적 오개념(입자 원인, 돌기 생성, 압력 변수)으로 구성했다.
g.explanation: 두 묶음은 입자·압력·시간이 같고 물의 유무만 달랐으며, 물이 없을 때는 돌기가 휘기만 하고 물이 있을 때만 제거되었다. 따라서 물의 화학 작용이 돌기 제거에 필요하다는 D가 정답이다. A는 두 묶음에서 입자가 같았으므로 결과 차이를 설명하지 못한다. B는 돌기가 연마 중 생겼다는 근거가 없으며, 지문은 돌기가 '제거되지 않았다'고만 한다. C는 압력이 실험에서 바뀌지 않았으므로 압력의 효과를 결론 내릴 수 없다.
g.explanation_en: The two batches had the same particles, pressure, and time; the only difference was water. Without water, the asperities were only bent, and with water they were removed, so D is correct: the water's chemical action was needed for removal. A doesn't work because the particles were the same in both batches, so they can't explain why the results differed. B claims the dry chamber created the asperities, but the text only says they weren't removed. C makes a claim about pressure, which was never changed in the test, so the engineers couldn't conclude anything about it.

c.seed: physical science — Plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition thin-film semiconductor coating and radical species surface reactions photovoltaic production

g.passage: To coat solar cells with thin silicon films, manufacturers often use plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD). In this process, an electric field turns a gas such as silane into a plasma that contains highly reactive fragments called radicals. These radicals land on the cell's surface and bond there, building the film layer by layer. Engineers at one factory found that the film grew only where radicals reached the surface; areas shielded from the plasma by a metal clamp stayed bare. This suggests that if a section of a solar panel is blocked so that no radicals can reach it during PECVD, ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: that section will likely end up without a silicon film.
that section will likely end up with a thicker silicon film than other areas.
that section will likely end up with a film made of metal from the clamp.
that section will likely end up coated once the silane gas cools.
g.explanation: 지문은 라디칼이 표면에 닿아 결합해야만 막이 자라며, 클램프로 가려진 부분은 맨 표면으로 남았다고 말한다. 따라서 라디칼이 닿지 못하는 부분에는 실리콘 막이 생기지 않는다는 A가 정답이다. B는 가려진 부분에 막이 오히려 두껍게 생긴다고 하여 지문의 관찰과 반대이다. C는 클램프의 금속이 막을 이룬다고 하지만 지문에 그런 근거가 없다. D는 가스가 식으면 막이 생긴다고 하지만, 지문에서 막을 만드는 것은 냉각이 아니라 라디칼이다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the film forms only when radicals reach the surface and bond there, and the areas covered by the clamp stayed bare. So a section that no radicals can reach should end up with no silicon film, which makes A the answer. B says the blocked section gets a thicker film, which is the opposite of what the engineers saw. C says the film would be made of metal from the clamp, but nothing in the passage supports that. D says the section gets coated once the gas cools, but in the passage the film comes from radicals, not from the gas cooling.
g.design: 이 문항은 '라디칼이 닿아야 막이 생긴다'는 규칙 하나를 그대로 적용하는 1단계 추론이다. 오답 B, C, D는 정답과 같은 문장 틀로 썼고, 각각 정반대 결과, 클램프에서 물질이 옮겨 온다는 오해, 냉각이 원인이라는 오개념을 담았다.

c.seed: physical science — Electrochemical galvanic corrosion coupling and sacrificial zinc anode protection in submarine steel pipeline infrastructure

g.passage:
Text 1
Engineers often attach blocks of zinc to underwater steel pipelines. Because zinc corrodes more easily than steel, it gives up its electrons first and slowly wears away instead of the pipe. For this reason, some engineers claim that once zinc anodes are installed, a pipeline is protected for its entire working life and needs no further attention.

Text 2
Zinc anodes do shield steel pipelines, but only while the zinc lasts. As the anodes dissolve, they shrink, and when they are used up the steel itself begins to corrode. Divers and remote vehicles must therefore inspect pipelines regularly and replace worn anodes before they disappear completely.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim made by some engineers in Text 1?
options: By agreeing, since zinc corrodes more slowly than steel and therefore lasts as long as the pipeline does
By objecting, since the zinc is gradually consumed and must be checked and renewed for protection to continue
By agreeing, since the steel would only begin to corrode if the zinc were never attached in the first place
By objecting, since zinc offers steel no real protection and engineers should stop using it on pipelines
g.explanation: Text 1의 일부 엔지니어들은 아연 양극을 한 번 설치하면 파이프라인이 수명 내내 보호된다고 주장한다. Text 2는 아연이 녹아 없어지면 강철이 부식되기 시작하므로 정기 점검과 교체가 필요하다고 말하므로, 그 주장에 반대할 것이다. 따라서 정답은 B이다. A는 아연이 강철보다 더 쉽게 부식된다는 내용과 반대이고, C는 아연이 다 소모된 뒤 부식이 시작된다는 Text 2의 요지를 무시한다. D는 Text 2가 아연이 실제로 강철을 보호한다고 인정한 부분과 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en: In Text 1, some engineers claim that once zinc anodes are installed, a pipeline stays protected for its whole life. Text 2 explains that the zinc dissolves over time, and once it is used up the steel starts to corrode, so the anodes need regular inspection and replacement. That means the author of Text 2 would object to the claim, which makes B the answer. A is wrong because zinc corrodes more easily than steel, not more slowly. C ignores Text 2's point that the steel corrodes once the zinc is used up, and D is wrong because Text 2 says zinc does protect steel.
g.design: Easy: Text 2 states its key point directly (zinc runs out, so it must be replaced), and that is enough to reject the claim of lifelong protection. Each wrong answer is a common misconception: zinc lasts as long as the pipe, the anode is permanent once attached, or zinc doesn't protect steel at all.

c.seed: physical science — Chromatic aberration optical wavelength-dependent focal length dispersion and correction in refracting telescope objective lens design

g.passage:
Text 1
Early refracting telescopes had a stubborn flaw. Because glass bends blue light more strongly than red light, a single lens brings different colors to focus at slightly different distances. Many seventeenth-century astronomers concluded that this colored blurring could never be removed from any telescope that used lenses.

Text 2
In the 1750s, optician John Dollond paired a lens of crown glass with a lens of flint glass. The two glasses spread colors by different amounts, so the second lens undid most of the color spreading caused by the first. Such "achromatic" lenses let refracting telescopes form far sharper images, and they are still used today.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the conclusion reached by many seventeenth-century astronomers in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that the colored blurring in refracting telescopes could never be reduced, since glass always bends blue light more than red light
By arguing that the colored blurring was caused mainly by poor craftsmanship rather than by the way glass bends different colors
By pointing out that combining two different kinds of glass in one lens later solved much of the problem those astronomers thought was permanent
By suggesting that the colored blurring mattered little, since astronomers of that era rarely needed sharp images of distant objects
g.explanation: Text 1의 천문학자들은 렌즈 망원경의 색 번짐을 결코 없앨 수 없다고 결론지었다. Text 2는 Dollond가 크라운 유리와 플린트 유리를 결합해 색 번짐을 대부분 상쇄했다고 설명하므로, 그 결론이 틀렸음을 보여 주는 C가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 해결책을 제시하므로 동의하지 않는다는 점에서 틀렸다. B는 Text 2가 원인을 제작 결함으로 돌리지 않으므로 틀렸다. D는 Text 2가 문제의 중요성을 깎아내리지 않고 오히려 더 선명한 상을 강조하므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: In Text 1, many astronomers concluded that the colored blurring in lens telescopes could never be removed. Text 2 explains that Dollond combined crown and flint glass so the second lens canceled most of the color spreading, which shows that conclusion was wrong, so C is correct. A is wrong because Text 2 describes a fix, so it would not agree the problem was permanent. B is wrong because Text 2 never blames craftsmanship; it accepts that glass bends colors differently. D is wrong because Text 2 treats sharper images as an important gain rather than saying the blurring didn't matter.
g.design: Text 1에 명시된 '불가능' 주장을 Text 2의 해결 사례가 직접 반박하는 한 단계 관계만으로 풀리게 했고, 오답은 동의·원인 오해·중요성 축소라는 흔한 오개념을 같은 'By ~ing' 틀로 구성했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: physical science — Polymeric viscoelasticity strain-rate dependent energy dissipation and glass transition temperature in impact-resistant composite materials

g.passage: Many impact-resistant composites contain polymer layers that absorb energy through viscoelastic behavior: when deformed, their long molecular chains slide and rearrange, converting some of the impact energy into heat. This dissipation is greatest near the polymer's glass transition temperature (Tg), the point at which the material shifts from a rigid, glassy state to a softer, rubbery one. Importantly, Tg is not fixed. The faster a polymer is deformed, the less time its chains have to rearrange, so the material behaves as though its Tg were higher. Materials engineer Priya Venkataraman tested a polymer whose Tg, measured under slow loading, is about 40°C below room temperature. In slow bending tests at room temperature, the polymer dissipated little energy, but under high-speed impact at the same temperature, it dissipated far more. These results suggest that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the polymer's slow-loading Tg must have been measured incorrectly, since its energy dissipation at room temperature should not vary with loading speed.
the polymer dissipates more energy under impact mainly because high-speed deformation heats it above its slow-loading Tg.
the polymer would dissipate even more energy in slow bending tests if those tests were conducted at a temperature well above room temperature.
the rapid deformation of an impact raised the polymer's effective Tg close to room temperature, placing the material in its range of greatest dissipation.
g.explanation: 지문은 변형 속도가 빠를수록 유효 Tg가 올라가고, 에너지 소산은 Tg 근처에서 가장 크다고 말한다. 느린 하중에서 Tg는 실온보다 40°C 낮아 실온에서 소산이 적었지만, 충격 시 유효 Tg가 실온 근처로 올라가 소산이 커졌다고 보는 D가 두 정보를 연결한 결론이다. A는 Tg가 고정되지 않는다는 지문 내용과 모순된다. B는 열 발생을 언급하지만, 이 폴리머는 실온에서 이미 느린 하중 기준 Tg보다 높은 온도에 있으므로 원인을 설명하지 못한다. C는 온도를 올리면 Tg에서 더 멀어지므로 소산이 오히려 줄어들 것이라 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says faster deformation raises a polymer's effective Tg and that dissipation peaks near Tg. With slow loading, the Tg sits 40°C below room temperature, so dissipation was low; a fast impact would push the effective Tg up toward room temperature, which explains the much higher dissipation, so D is correct. A contradicts the passage's point that Tg is not fixed. B mentions heating, but at room temperature the polymer is already above its slow-loading Tg, so heating it further can't explain the result. C gets the direction wrong: raising the temperature would move the material even farther from its slow-loading Tg, so dissipation should go down, not up.
g.design: To get the answer, students have to connect two ideas: dissipation peaks near Tg, and fast loading raises the effective Tg. B and C borrow real details from the passage (heat, temperature) but apply them in the wrong direction.

c.seed: physical science — Phosphorescent triplet state energy transfer and persistent luminescence duration in glow-in-dark paint formulations

g.passage: Glow-in-the-dark paints store light energy in long-lived excited states and release it slowly as visible light after the lights go out. In many formulations, this energy is held in "triplet" states of dye or pigment molecules, which emit light only gradually. However, a triplet-state molecule can also hand its energy to a nearby oxygen molecule, which then releases it as heat rather than light. Chemist Rafael Ortiz compared two paints made with the same pigment at the same concentration. In paint X, the pigment particles were dispersed in a resin that oxygen passes through easily; in paint Y, they were sealed in a resin that blocks nearly all oxygen. Both paints absorbed the same amount of light during charging. Ortiz therefore expected that, after charging, ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: paint Y would continue to emit visible light for a longer time than paint X would.
paint X would continue to emit visible light for a longer time than paint Y would, because oxygen supplies paint X with additional stored energy.
paint Y would absorb more light during charging than paint X would and therefore glow brighter.
paint X and paint Y would glow for the same length of time, since they contain identical amounts of the same pigment.
g.explanation: 산소는 삼중항 상태의 에너지를 빛이 아닌 열로 빼앗아 가므로, 산소가 잘 통하는 X는 저장된 에너지를 더 빨리 잃고, 산소가 차단된 Y는 더 오래 빛을 낸다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 산소의 역할을 거꾸로 이해해, 산소가 에너지를 빼앗는 것이 아니라 공급한다고 보았다. C는 두 페인트가 같은 양의 빛을 흡수했다는 조건과 모순된다. D는 안료 조건이 같다는 점만 보고 수지의 차이, 곧 산소 투과성의 차이를 무시했다.
g.explanation_en: Oxygen takes energy away from triplet-state molecules and gives it off as heat, not light. So paint X, whose resin lets oxygen through easily, loses its stored energy faster, while paint Y, which blocks oxygen, should keep glowing longer. That makes A the answer. B gets oxygen's role backward: oxygen drains energy rather than supplying it. C contradicts the passage, which says both paints absorbed the same amount of light. D notices that the pigment is the same in both paints but ignores the key difference between the resins, which is how much oxygen gets through.
g.design: To answer, students have to connect two facts: oxygen drains energy as heat, and the two resins differ in how much oxygen they let through. Each wrong answer is built on one partly true detail from the passage (oxygen is involved, the paints absorbed the same light, the pigment is identical).

c.seed: physical science — Crystalline silicon p-n junction band structure and photoexcitation charge-carrier separation in semiconductor solar cell operation

g.passage:
Text 1
In a crystalline silicon solar cell, sunlight frees electrons by lifting them across silicon's band gap, leaving positively charged holes behind. The decisive step, many textbooks explain, comes next: the built-in electric field at the p-n junction sweeps electrons toward the n-type side and holes toward the p-type side. On this account, the junction's field is what turns freed charges into current, and a cell's performance depends chiefly on how strong that field is.

Text 2
Physicist Rhea Okonjo agrees that the junction separates charges, but she notes that its field fills only a thin depletion region, often less than a micrometer wide. Most light is absorbed far deeper in the wafer, where there is almost no field. Carriers created there must first wander randomly by diffusion until they reach the junction. For this reason, Okonjo argues, how long carriers survive before recombining—rather than field strength—usually limits a cell's efficiency.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Okonjo (Text 2) most likely respond to the textbook account described in Text 1?
options: She would claim that it is mistaken to say that the junction plays any part in separating electrons from holes.
She would claim that it overstates how much the field matters, since most carriers must first get to the junction without help from the field.
She would claim that it gets wrong how sunlight frees electrons, since most light is absorbed deep inside the wafer.
She would claim that it is correct about what limits efficiency but leaves out how thin the depletion region is.
g.explanation: Okonjo은 접합이 전하를 분리한다는 점은 인정하지만, 전기장이 얇은 공핍 영역에만 존재하고 대부분의 캐리어는 확산으로 접합까지 가야 하므로 효율을 제한하는 것은 전기장 세기가 아니라 캐리어 수명이라고 본다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 Okonjo가 접합의 분리 역할을 인정하므로 틀리다. C는 흡수 위치는 언급하지만, Okonjo는 빛이 전자를 해방시키는 방식 자체를 반박하지 않는다. D는 Okonjo가 효율 제한 요인에 대해 Text 1과 정면으로 다르므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: Okonjo accepts that the junction separates charges. But she points out that its field fills only a thin region, so most carriers have to diffuse to the junction first, and she argues that how long carriers survive, not field strength, limits efficiency. That makes B correct. A is wrong because she clearly agrees that the junction separates charges. C is wrong because she mentions where light is absorbed but never disputes how sunlight frees electrons. D is wrong because she disagrees with Text 1 about what limits efficiency.
g.design: To get this right, you have to see that Okonjo partly agrees with Text 1 (the junction does separate charges) but disagrees about what limits efficiency. A and D each misstate one of these two points, and C misuses a detail about absorption depth.

c.seed: physical science — Acoustic impedance mismatch ultrasound attenuation and frequency-dependent soft tissue penetration depth in medical ultrasound imaging

g.passage:
Text 1
Clinicians often assume that the main obstacle to imaging deep organs with ultrasound is reflection at tissue boundaries. Because sound bounces strongly where two materials differ sharply in acoustic impedance, such as where soft tissue meets bone or gas, some textbooks treat these boundaries as the chief reason that echoes from deep structures grow faint. On this view, choosing a different frequency would do little to improve images of a deep liver.

Text 2
Strong reflections at bone or gas boundaries do block sound, but in a typical abdominal scan the beam passes mostly through soft tissues whose impedances are fairly similar. There, the larger loss comes from absorption and scattering, which increase roughly in proportion to frequency. A 10-megahertz beam may lose its usable signal within a few centimeters, while a 3-megahertz beam can reach structures well beyond that depth, though with coarser detail. Sonographers therefore routinely lower the frequency to see deeper organs.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the view presented in Text 1 about imaging a deep liver?
options: By agreeing that boundary reflections are the main cause of weak deep echoes but adding that higher frequencies can partly make up for that loss
By arguing that the impedance differences between soft tissues are actually greater than textbooks suggest, so boundary reflections matter even more than Text 1 claims
By granting that sharp impedance boundaries reflect sound but contending that, along a mostly soft-tissue path, frequency-dependent attenuation matters more, making frequency choice important
By granting that frequency affects image detail but contending that it has no meaningful effect on how deep an ultrasound beam can travel
g.explanation: Text 2는 뼈·가스 경계에서의 강한 반사는 인정하지만, 복부 검사에서는 임피던스가 비슷한 연조직을 주로 지나므로 주파수에 비례하는 흡수·산란이 더 큰 손실이며 주파수를 낮추면 더 깊이 볼 수 있다고 하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 반사가 주원인이라는 데 동의하고, 고주파가 도움이 된다고 해 Text 2와 정반대다. B는 연조직 임피던스가 "fairly similar"하다는 Text 2와 모순된다. D는 주파수가 해상도에 영향을 준다는 부분은 맞지만, Text 2는 주파수가 도달 깊이를 결정한다고 분명히 말한다.
g.explanation_en: C is correct. Text 2 admits that bone and gas boundaries reflect sound strongly. But it points out that an abdominal beam travels mostly through soft tissues with similar impedances, so absorption and scattering, which rise with frequency, cause more of the loss. That means lowering the frequency lets you see deeper. A is wrong on two counts: it agrees that reflection is the main cause, and it says higher frequencies help, which is the opposite of what Text 2 says. B goes against Text 2's statement that soft-tissue impedances are "fairly similar." D gets one part right, since frequency does affect detail, but Text 2 clearly says frequency controls how deep the beam can reach.
g.design: To answer, you have to link two points: Text 2 concedes that boundary reflection happens, yet argues that frequency-dependent attenuation matters more. A and D each pick up a partly true idea from the texts (reflection exists; frequency affects detail), so you can only rule them out by comparing them with the full argument.

- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).

c.seed: technology and engineering — Thermochromic paint temperature-sensitive pigment activation and color-change mechanism in smart building envelope applications

g.passage: Thermochromic paint contains special pigments that change color when they reach a certain temperature. On some experimental buildings, the paint stays dark on cool days, which helps the walls absorb sunlight and warm the rooms inside. When the wall surface heats up past about 25°C, however, the pigments switch and the paint turns nearly white. ______ the walls reflect much more sunlight in hot weather, and less heat passes into the building.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 벽이 뜨거워지면 페인트가 거의 흰색으로 변한다는 원인을, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 때문에 벽이 햇빛을 더 많이 반사하고 열이 덜 들어온다는 결과를 말하므로 인과 관계의 D가 정답이다. A는 앞 내용의 구체적 사례를 제시할 때 쓰지만, 뒤 문장은 사례가 아니라 결과이다. B는 대조나 예상 밖의 내용을 나타내지만, 흰색 표면이 햇빛을 반사하는 것은 예상 가능한 결과이다. C는 비슷한 다른 사실을 덧붙일 때 쓰지만, 뒤 문장은 앞 문장에서 직접 이어지는 결과이다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank gives a cause: when the wall gets hot, the paint turns nearly white. The sentence after the blank gives what happens because of that change: the walls reflect more sunlight and let in less heat. That is a cause-and-effect relationship, so D is correct. A introduces an example, but the second sentence is a consequence, not an example. B signals a contrast or something unexpected, but a white surface reflecting sunlight is exactly what you would expect. C adds a similar but separate point, while the second sentence follows directly from the first.
g.design: 앞 문장의 색 변화(원인)와 뒤 문장의 반사·열 감소(결과)를 명시적으로 배치해 한 단계 인과 판단만으로 풀리게 했고, 오답은 예시·대조·유사 관계의 전형적 전환어로 구성했다.

g.passage: Piezoelectric ceramics are materials that produce an electric charge when they are squeezed or bent. These ceramics can also work in reverse: when an alternating electric voltage is applied to them, they rapidly expand and contract. ______ engineers use them in ultrasonic dental scalers, where the ceramic's fast vibrations shake loose hardened plaque from the surface of teeth.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 세라믹이 전압을 받으면 빠르게 팽창·수축한다는 성질을 설명하고, 뒷 문장은 그 진동 때문에 기술자들이 이 세라믹을 치석 제거기에 쓴다는 내용이다. 따라서 원인과 결과를 잇는 A가 정답이다. B는 대조를 나타내지만 두 문장은 서로 반대되는 내용이 아니다. C는 예시를 나타내지만 치석 제거기는 '팽창·수축한다'는 성질의 한 예가 아니라 그 성질을 활용한 결과이다. D는 예상과 다른 내용이 올 때 쓰는데, 뒷 문장은 앞 문장에서 자연스럽게 이어진다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence explains that the ceramics expand and contract quickly when a voltage is applied, and the next sentence says engineers use them in dental scalers because of those vibrations. So the relationship is cause and effect, and A is correct. B signals contrast, but the two sentences don't say opposite things. C signals an example, but using the ceramics in scalers isn't an example of them expanding and contracting. It's a result of that property. D signals something unexpected, but the second sentence follows naturally from the first.
g.design: 빈칸 앞 문장에 성질이 직접 나오고 뒤 문장이 그 성질의 응용이라 원인-결과가 한 단계로 드러난다. 오답은 대조·예시·양보처럼 흔히 헷갈리는 관계로 구성했다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Microfluidic lab-on-a-chip device and capillary flow manipulation for rapid point-of-care diagnostic blood sample analysis

g.passage: Lab-on-a-chip devices allow doctors to test a single drop of blood in minutes. These devices need no pumps. Instead, the narrow channels in each chip ______ the sample forward through capillary action, the same force that pulls water up a thin straw.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 수식어 'in each chip'이 짧게 끼어든 복수 주어 'channels'와 동사의 수 일치 한 규칙만 묻고, 단수 명사 'chip'에 끌린 단수 동사형을 오답으로 배치했다.
g.explanation: 빈칸의 주어는 'chip'이 아니라 복수 명사 'channels'이므로 복수 동사가 필요하다. B는 복수 현재형이고, 지문의 다른 현재 시제 서술(allow, need)과도 맞으므로 정답이다. A, C, D는 모두 단수 동사형(draws, has moved, is moving)이라 바로 앞의 단수 명사 'chip'에 맞춘 오류이다. 따라서 복수 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the blank is the plural noun "channels," not "chip," so you need a plural verb. B is a plural present-tense verb, and it also fits the other present-tense verbs in the passage ("allow," "need"), so it is correct. A, C, and D are all singular forms ("draws," "has moved," "is moving"). They wrongly agree with the nearby singular noun "chip," so they don't match the plural subject.

g.passage: Engineers have developed a type of self-healing concrete that contains tiny capsules filled with dormant bacteria and nutrients. When a microscopic crack forms and water seeps in, the capsules along the crack ______ open, allowing the bacteria to become active and produce calcium carbonate, a mineral that gradually fills the damaged space.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'the capsules'이고, 'along the crack'은 주어를 꾸미는 전치사구일 뿐이다. 따라서 복수 동사가 필요하며, 앞 절의 'forms', 'seeps'와 맞추어 단순 현재형을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A, B, D는 모두 단수 동사(breaks, has broken, is breaking)라서 바로 앞의 단수 명사 'crack'을 주어로 잘못 본 경우에 고르게 되는 오답이다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this clause is the plural noun "the capsules." The phrase "along the crack" only describes the capsules, so it doesn't change the subject. You need a plural verb, and the simple present matches "forms" and "seeps" earlier in the sentence, so C is correct. A, B, and D all use singular verbs (breaks, has broken, is breaking), which you might pick if you mistook the nearby singular noun "crack" for the subject.

- Reverse osmosis is a process used in many desalination plants to turn seawater into drinking water.
- In reverse osmosis, pumps push seawater against a thin membrane at high pressure.
- The membrane is semipermeable: water molecules can pass through it, but most dissolved salt ions cannot.
- Modern membranes can block more than 99 percent of the salt in seawater.
- The Sorek plant in Israel, opened in 2013, is one of the largest reverse osmosis plants in the world.
g.question: The student wants to explain how the membrane separates fresh water from salt. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Because the membrane lets water molecules through while stopping most dissolved salt ions, the water on the far side is nearly salt-free.
Because the Sorek plant opened in Israel in 2013, it has become one of the largest reverse osmosis plants in the world.
Because many desalination plants use reverse osmosis, seawater can be turned into drinking water in many places.
Because the membrane lets salt ions through while stopping most water molecules, the salt can be collected on the far side.
g.explanation: 목표는 막이 담수와 소금을 어떻게 분리하는지 설명하는 것이며, 이는 반투과성 막에 관한 세 번째 메모와 직접 대응한다. A는 물 분자는 통과하고 염 이온은 막힌다는 메모를 정확히 활용하므로 정답이다. B는 소렉 플랜트에 관한 사실만 전달할 뿐 분리 원리를 설명하지 않는다. C는 역삼투가 널리 쓰인다는 점만 말하고 막의 작동 방식은 설명하지 않는다. D는 물과 염 이온의 역할을 뒤바꿔 메모와 어긋나는 부정확한 진술이다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain how the membrane separates fresh water from salt, and the third note speaks to that directly. A is correct because it uses that note accurately: water molecules pass through the membrane, but most salt ions don't. B only gives facts about the Sorek plant and never explains how the separation happens. C points out that reverse osmosis is widely used but doesn't say how the membrane works. D swaps the roles of water and salt ions, so it contradicts the notes.

g.passage: Engineers testing an artificial gill membrane found that the thin polymer sheet could pull dissolved oxygen from seawater at a steady rate______ the next challenge was separating that oxygen gas cleanly from the water flowing past the membrane.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Engineers ... at a steady rate"와 빈칸 뒤 "the next challenge was ..."는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D의 then은 등위접속사가 아니라 부사이므로 쉼표와 함께 써도 여전히 쉼표 스플라이스다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Engineers ... at a steady rate") and the text after it ("the next challenge was ...") are both independent clauses, since each one has its own subject and verb. A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so B is the answer. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between them, which makes a run-on sentence. D adds "then," but "then" is an adverb, not a coordinating conjunction, so a comma plus "then" is still a comma splice.
g.design: Easy: a clear boundary between two independent clauses with simple wording. The wrong answers are common mistakes (a comma splice, a run-on, and a comma with "then").

g.passage: Some modern cars use magneto-rheological dampers in their suspension systems. These dampers are filled with an oil that contains tiny iron particles. When an electromagnetic coil inside the damper switches on, the particles line up and the fluid becomes much thicker ______ when the coil switches off, the fluid quickly thins again, letting the car ride more softly over bumps.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "When an electromagnetic coil ... becomes much thicker"는 독립절이고, 뒤의 "when the coil switches off, the fluid quickly thins again..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 마침표로 분리해야 하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 "and" 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 "and when..." 구조를 어색하게 끊으므로 관례에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "When an electromagnetic coil ... the fluid becomes much thicker," make up an independent clause. The words after it, "when the coil switches off, the fluid quickly thins again...," are a second independent clause. Two independent clauses like these need to be separated, so the period in C is correct. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between them, so you get a run-on sentence. D adds an unnecessary comma after "and," which breaks up the "and when..." structure for no reason, so it doesn't follow standard conventions.
g.design: 이 문항은 쉬운(easy) 난이도에 맞췄다. 독립절 두 개의 경계가 한눈에 보이고, 쉼표 스플라이스·무종지문·잘못된 쉼표 같은 전형적 오개념을 오답으로 넣었다. 정답 C는 마침표로 두 절을 나누는 규칙 하나만 알면 고를 수 있다.

g.passage: Perovskite solar cells owe much of their promise to a flexible crystal lattice: by substituting bromide ions for some of the iodide ions in that lattice, researchers can widen the material's bandgap and shift which colors of light it absorbs. The ability of these thin films, which are often less than a micrometer thick, to absorb light across precisely chosen wavelengths ______ engineers to stack perovskite layers atop conventional silicon cells, capturing energy that silicon alone would miss.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The ability'이고, 'of these thin films...'와 'to absorb light across precisely chosen wavelengths'는 그 주어를 꾸미는 수식어이다. 따라서 단수 정동사인 D 'allows'가 와야 한다. A와 C는 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'wavelengths'나 'films'에 맞춘 복수 동사여서 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다. B는 분사 'allowing'이라 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 문장이 되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The ability," and both "of these thin films..." and "to absorb light across precisely chosen wavelengths" are modifiers describing it. So the blank needs a singular finite verb, which is D, "allows." A and C are plural verbs that agree with the nearby plural nouns "wavelengths" or "films" instead of the actual subject. B is the participle "allowing," which leaves the sentence with no main verb, so it isn't a complete sentence.

g.passage: In an acoustic levitator, a transducer emits ultrasonic waves toward a reflector, and the reflected waves overlap with the incoming ones to form a standing wave. The tiny polystyrene beads that engineers place near the pressure nodes of this standing wave, where the pressure gradients from surrounding regions push inward from both sides, ______ suspended in midair without touching any surface, allowing researchers to study delicate samples free from container contamination.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'The tiny polystyrene beads'이고, 그 뒤에 관계절('that engineers place...')과 where절이 길게 붙어 있어서 이 문장에는 아직 본동사가 없다. 따라서 빈칸에는 복수 주어에 맞는 정동사가 들어가야 하므로 A(remain)가 정답이다. B는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 단수 명사 'standing wave'나 'surface'에 수를 맞춘 형태라서 복수 주어 beads와 일치하지 않는다. C와 D는 분사형이라 정동사 역할을 할 수 없고, 그러면 문장에 본동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The tiny polystyrene beads." A long relative clause ("that engineers place…") and a where-clause separate it from the blank, and the sentence doesn't have a main verb yet. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject, which makes A ("remain") correct. B is a finite verb, but it's singular, as if it agreed with a nearby noun like "standing wave." It doesn't agree with the plural "beads." C and D are participle forms, so they can't serve as the main verb, and either one would leave the sentence incomplete.
g.design: 긴 관계절과 where절이 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓아서, 정동사가 필요하다는 판단과 복수 주어에 맞는 수 일치 판단을 둘 다 해야 풀 수 있게 했다. 단수 명사가 빈칸 가까이에 있어서 B로 유인한다.

g.passage: In electrospinning, a high voltage draws a charged polymer solution from a needle tip into a thin jet that stretches and dries into fibers before landing on a collector. For air-filtration membranes, engineers at several laboratories have found that the voltage applied across the gap between needle and collector, when raised gradually from about 12 to 20 kilovolts, ______ the average fiber diameter, producing denser webs that trap finer airborne particles.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸은 that절의 주어 "the voltage"에 대한 정동사 자리이며, 주어와 동사 사이에 전치사구와 when 삽입구가 끼어 있다. 주어가 단수이므로 단수 동사 B "reduces"가 맞다. C "reduce"는 바로 앞 "kilovolts"나 "laboratories" 같은 복수 명사에 끌린 오답으로, 주어 "voltage"와 수가 일치하지 않는다. A "reducing"과 D "having reduced"는 분사 형태여서 that절에 정동사가 없어 절이 완성되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The blank is the main verb of the that-clause, whose subject is "the voltage"; a prepositional phrase and a "when" phrase come between the subject and the blank. Because the subject is singular, B, "reduces," is correct. C, "reduce," is tempting because it sits right after plural nouns like "kilovolts" and "laboratories," but it doesn't agree with "voltage." A, "reducing," and D, "having reduced," are participles, so they would leave the that-clause without a finite verb, and the clause would be incomplete.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Shape-memory polymer thermal recovery and pre-programmed deformation enabling self-folding origami-inspired structures

g.passage: Engineers have begun printing flat sheets of shape-memory polymer that can fold themselves into three-dimensional structures. The sheets, which are stretched into a temporary shape while warm and then cooled so that the strain in each hinge region is locked in place, ______ toward their original geometry when reheated, bending along pre-programmed creases much as paper does in the hands of an origami artist.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 주어 "The sheets"는 긴 관계절(which ... locked in place) 뒤에서 본동사를 필요로 하므로, 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사 C "recover"가 정답이다. A "recovering"과 D "having recovered"는 분사라서 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다. B "recovers"는 정동사이긴 하지만 단수형이다. 빈칸 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "place"나 "region", "strain"과 잘못 일치시킨 것이다.
g.explanation_en: The subject "The sheets" is separated from its verb by a long relative clause (which ... locked in place), and the sentence still needs a main verb. C, "recover," is a finite plural verb that agrees with "sheets," so C is correct. A, "recovering," and D, "having recovered," are participles, so they would leave the sentence without a main verb. B, "recovers," is a finite verb, but it's singular. It wrongly agrees with nearby singular nouns like "strain," "region," or "place" instead of the actual subject.
g.design: 긴 관계절이 복수 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어 두 가지를 판단해야 한다. 정동사가 필요한지 확인하고, 동사를 실제 주어와 일치시켜야 한다. B는 정동사라는 점은 맞지만 가까운 단수 명사에 끌리게 만든 오답이다.

- 세부 기술 힌트: 긴 수식어구/도치 뒤의 주어-동사 일치, 병렬 구조, 수식어 위치(dangling modifier), 정동사 vs 분사/부정사 선택처럼 구조 파악이 필요한 문제.
c.seed: technology and engineering — Enzymatic fuel cell glucose biocatalysis and bioelectrochemical oxidation reducing current generation for wearable power

g.passage: Unlike conventional batteries, which store a fixed supply of chemicals, enzymatic fuel cells generate electricity from substances already present in the body. In one wearable prototype developed by bioengineers, a thin patch coated with the enzyme glucose oxidase ______ glucose in a wearer's sweat, releasing electrons that travel through a flexible circuit to power a small sensor.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "a thin patch"이고, "coated with the enzyme glucose oxidase"는 주어를 꾸미는 분사구이다. 그러므로 빈칸에는 문장의 정동사가 와야 하며, 단수 주어에 맞는 D "oxidizes"가 정답이다. A "oxidizing"은 분사여서 정동사가 될 수 없고, 그러면 문장이 완성되지 않는다. B "to oxidize"는 부정사라서 역시 정동사 역할을 할 수 없다. C "that oxidizes"는 관계절을 만들어 주어 "patch"를 꾸밀 뿐이므로, 주절에는 여전히 정동사가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "a thin patch," and "coated with the enzyme glucose oxidase" is a participial phrase that modifies it. That means the blank needs the sentence's main verb, and D, "oxidizes," is a finite verb that agrees with the singular subject. A, "oxidizing," is a participle, so it can't serve as the main verb, and the sentence would be incomplete. B, "to oxidize," is an infinitive, which can't be the main verb either. C, "that oxidizes," creates a relative clause that only describes "patch," so the main clause would still have no verb.
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 분사구 수식어를 두어 "coated"를 동사로 오인하게 만들었다. 그렇게 오인하면 분사·부정사·관계절 선택지도 그럴듯해 보이므로, 주어와 정동사 구조를 확인해야만 정답을 고를 수 있다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Superhydrophobic textile coating lotus leaf mimicry and water repellent treatment applied to rain jacket fabrics

g.passage: Inspired by the microscopic bumps and waxy nanostructures that cause water to bead and roll off lotus leaves, materials engineers have developed superhydrophobic coatings for rain jacket fabrics. The coating, a layer of silica nanoparticles bonded to fluorine-free polymer chains that together mimic the leaf's rough, water-shedding surface, ______ droplets to roll away while carrying off dust and dirt as well.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "The coating"이고, 콤마 사이의 긴 동격구(a layer ... surface)는 주어를 꾸미는 삽입어구일 뿐이므로 문장에는 단수 주어에 맞는 정동사가 필요하다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사(polymer chains, nanoparticles)에 끌려 복수형으로 맞춘 것이어서 주어-동사 일치가 틀린다. C와 D는 분사 형태여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되므로 완전한 문장이 되지 못한다. D는 완료형이어서 그럴듯해 보이지만 마찬가지로 정동사가 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The coating." The long phrase set off by commas (a layer ... surface) is just an appositive describing that subject, so the sentence still needs a main verb that agrees with a singular subject. That makes A correct. B is a main verb, but it's plural because it matches the nearby plural nouns ("polymer chains," "nanoparticles"), so the subject and verb don't agree. C and D are participles, which would leave the sentence with no main verb, so it wouldn't be a complete sentence. D may sound right because it's a perfect form, but it isn't a main verb either.
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구와 그 안의 복수 명사로 주어를 가려, 정동사가 필요한지 판단하고 주어-동사 일치까지 확인하는 두 단계 판단을 요구했다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Spark plasma sintering rapid consolidation and grain refinement in tungsten carbide tool bit manufacturing

g.passage: Unlike conventional hot pressing, which can take hours, spark plasma sintering (SPS) sends pulsed electric current directly through a graphite die and the tungsten carbide powder packed inside it. This rapid heating, which brings the powder to its consolidation temperature within minutes and sharply limits the time that individual carbide grains spend at high temperatures, ______ manufacturers to produce cutting-tool bits with finer grains and greater hardness than older methods yield.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'This rapid heating'이고, 'which ... temperatures'는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 관계절이다. 따라서 문장에는 단수 정동사가 필요하므로 B 'allows'가 정답이다. A와 D는 정동사이긴 하지만, 빈칸 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'temperatures'나 'grains'에 수를 맞춘 복수형이어서 단수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C 'allowing'은 분사라서 정동사가 아니므로, 이것을 넣으면 주절에 동사가 없어 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun phrase "This rapid heating." The clause "which ... temperatures" just interrupts the sentence between the subject and its verb. So the sentence needs a singular finite verb, which makes B, "allows," the correct answer. A and D are finite verbs, but they're plural: they match the nearby plural nouns "temperatures" or "grains" instead of the actual subject. C, "allowing," is a participle, not a finite verb, so with C the main clause would have no verb and the sentence wouldn't be complete.
g.design: 길게 끼어든 관계절의 마지막 부분에 복수 명사를 두어, 훑어 읽는 학생이 동사를 그 명사에 맞추도록 유도했다. 오답에는 수 일치 오류 두 가지와 정동사가 아닌 형태 하나를 넣었다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Microfluidic PCR device miniaturized thermal cycling and polymerase chain reaction amplification in portable genetic testing

g.passage: In a conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) machine, DNA samples sit in plastic tubes inside a heavy metal block that must be repeatedly heated and cooled, and because the block itself is so massive, each temperature shift takes close to a minute. Microfluidic PCR devices avoid this delay: a few microliters of sample are pushed through hair-thin channels that pass back and forth over zones held at fixed temperatures, so only the tiny volume of liquid changes temperature, and it does so in about a second. ______ a full set of thirty amplification cycles, which typically takes more than an hour on a benchtop machine, can be completed on a palm-sized chip in under ten minutes.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 미세유체 장치에서 액체 온도가 약 1초 만에 바뀐다는 원인을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 결과로 전체 30회 증폭이 10분 안에 끝난다는 점을 말하므로 결과를 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 기존 장치와 미세유체 장치의 대비가 지문에 있어 그럴듯하지만, 그 대비는 이미 앞 문장에서 이루어졌고 빈칸 뒤 문장은 앞 문장과 대비되는 내용이 아니라 그 결과이다. B는 예상과 반대되는 내용을 이끌지만, 빠른 온도 변화 뒤에 처리 시간이 짧아지는 것은 예상대로의 결과이다. D는 구체적 수치가 나와 예시처럼 보이지만, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 앞 내용의 한 사례가 아니라 그로 인해 생기는 결과이다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank gives a cause: in a microfluidic device, the liquid changes temperature in about a second. The sentence after the blank gives the effect: all thirty cycles finish in under ten minutes. That makes C, which signals a result, the right choice. A may look tempting because the passage does compare old and new devices, but that comparison already happened in the previous sentence, and the final sentence follows from that sentence instead of contrasting with it. B introduces something unexpected, but a shorter run time is exactly what you'd expect after faster temperature shifts. D may seem to fit because the final sentence has specific numbers, but it describes a result of the earlier claim, not one example of it.
g.design: There's no cue word, so students have to figure out the cause-and-effect relationship between the sentences themselves. A works with the passage's overall comparison, and D fits the concrete numbers, so both must be ruled out by checking how the last two sentences actually connect.
