c.seed: technology and engineering — Ionic liquid electrolyte electrochemical stability and wide operating temperature range in next-generation battery development

g.passage: Ionic liquids, salts that stay liquid at room temperature, are attracting attention as electrolytes for next-generation batteries. Unlike the flammable carbonate solvents used in most lithium-ion cells, many ionic liquids resist breaking down at high voltages and stay liquid from roughly −40°C to above 100°C. ______ the same strong ionic attractions behind this stability also make ionic liquids thick and slow-flowing, so lithium ions move through them sluggishly and batteries that use them charge more slowly.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 이온성 액체의 장점(고전압 안정성, 넓은 작동 온도)을 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 같은 성질이 느린 이온 이동과 느린 충전이라는 단점도 낳는다고 말한다. 장점을 인정한 뒤 한계로 돌아서는 흐름이므로 D가 가장 논리적이다. A는 특성을 하나 더 덧붙이는 것처럼 보이지만, 뒤 문장은 장점을 이어 가는 내용이 아니라 반대 방향의 단점이다. B는 뒤 문장의 '같은 이온 간 인력'을 보고 인과 관계로 착각하게 하지만, 느린 충전은 넓은 온도 범위 같은 장점에서 생기는 결과가 아니다. C는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 장점을 보여 주는 사례가 아니므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence lists the strengths of ionic liquids (stability at high voltage and a wide operating temperature range), and the sentence after the blank says the same property also causes a weakness: slow ion movement and slower charging. The text grants an advantage and then turns to a limitation, so D is the most logical choice. A looks like it adds one more trait, but the next sentence doesn't continue the list of strengths; it goes the opposite way. B might pull you in because the next sentence mentions "the same strong ionic attractions," but slow charging isn't a result of advantages like the wide temperature range. C is wrong because the next sentence isn't an example of the strengths described before it.
g.design: 빈칸 앞뒤에 대조를 알려 주는 어휘 단서를 두지 않았다. 장점을 인정한 뒤 단점으로 돌아서는 흐름을 내용으로만 파악하게 했다. 'same ... behind this stability' 표현이 B(인과)와 A(추가)를 그럴듯하게 만든다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Magnetostrictive material stress-induced magnetic field change and ferromagnetic sensor applications in structural health monitoring

g.passage: Magnetostrictive materials, such as certain iron-gallium alloys, change their magnetization when they are mechanically stressed. Engineers have proposed embedding thin strips of these alloys in bridge girders so that shifts in the strips' magnetic fields would reveal strain building up in the steel. Early prototypes, however, gave inconsistent readings, because the alloys' magnetic response also drifted as the surrounding temperature changed. ______ a team at a Korean research institute paired each sensing strip with an unstressed reference strip made of the same alloy, letting temperature effects cancel out so that only the stress-induced signal remained.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.design: 빈칸 뒤 문장은 앞 문장의 문제(온도 표류)에 대한 해결책이다. 표면적으로 인과처럼 보이는 'As a result'와 재진술로 오인할 수 있는 'In other words'를 함정으로 두어, 두 문장의 관계를 비교해야 고를 수 있게 했다.
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 온도 변화 때문에 판독값이 일정하지 않다는 문제를 말하고, 뒤 문장은 기준 스트립을 짝지어 온도 영향을 상쇄한 연구팀의 방법을 소개하므로 문제에 대한 대응을 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 문제와 뒤 문장이 이어져 있어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 연구팀의 설계는 온도 표류가 저절로 낳은 결과가 아니라 의도적인 해결책이므로 맞지 않는다. C는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장을 다른 말로 바꿔 말하는 게 아니라 새로운 해결책을 더하므로 틀리다. D는 뒤 문장이 앞의 내용과 비슷한 사례가 아니라 그 문제에 대한 대응이므로 적절하지 않다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence describes a problem: temperature drift made the prototypes' readings inconsistent. g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "such modules can harvest energy from almost any hot surface"와 빈칸 뒤 "engineers have mounted them..."는 각각 독립절이므로 둘을 제대로 이어 줄 경계가 필요하다. D는 세미콜론으로 두 절을 나누고 접속부사 consequently 뒤에 쉼표를 찍어 올바르다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절 두 개를 이은 콤마 스플라이스다. C는 "because of this"가 의미상 인과를 나타내 그럴듯하지만, 접속사가 아닌 전치사구이므로 여전히 콤마 스플라이스다. B는 which가 뒤 절의 주어 역할을 하지 못해 "which engineers have mounted them"이 문법적으로 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("such modules can harvest energy from almost any hot surface") and the text after it ("engineers have mounted them...") are both independent clauses, so you need a proper boundary between them. D works because the semicolon separates the two clauses, and the comma after the conjunctive adverb "consequently" is placed correctly. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C may look right because "because of this" shows cause and effect, but it's a prepositional phrase, not a conjunction, so it's still a comma splice. B doesn't work because "which" can't fit into the next clause, which already has its own subject and object, so "which engineers have mounted them" is ungrammatical.
g.design: An introductory adverbial clause and a nonrestrictive modifier come before the main clause, so students have to find both independent clauses first. C is a tempting wrong answer because its cause-and-effect meaning fits the context, but its punctuation is wrong.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Catalytic converter honeycomb substrate structure and precious metal surface reactions reducing vehicle exhaust emissions

g.passage: Inside a catalytic converter, exhaust gases pass through a ceramic honeycomb containing thousands of thin parallel channels. The honeycomb itself does not react with the pollutants; rather, its walls are coated with tiny particles of platinum, palladium, and rhodium, which speed up the conversion of carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides into less harmful gases. Because these reactions occur only where gas molecules touch the metal, engineers design the channel walls to ______ the exposed surface area of the coating, allowing a small quantity of costly metal to treat a large volume of exhaust.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 반응은 기체가 금속에 닿는 곳에서만 일어나고, 적은 양의 금속으로 많은 배기가스를 처리하려는 것이 목적이므로 노출 표면적을 '최대화'한다는 A가 정답이다. B는 표면을 가린다는 뜻이라 반응 접촉을 줄여 목적과 정반대가 된다. C는 코팅을 안정시키는 일이 공학적으로 그럴듯하지만, 지문이 강조하는 '적은 금속으로 많은 양 처리'라는 논리는 표면적이 커져야 성립하므로 맞지 않는다. D는 엔지니어가 표면적을 측정할 수는 있어도, 측정만으로는 처리 효율이 높아지지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The reactions happen only where gas touches the metal, and the goal is to let a little metal treat a lot of exhaust, so the channel walls must make the exposed area as large as possible. That makes A correct. B would hide the surface, which cuts down contact and works against the goal. C sounds like something engineers would care about, but keeping the coating stable doesn't explain how a small amount of metal handles a large volume of exhaust. D is also plausible as an engineering task, but measuring the surface area doesn't make treatment any more effective.
g.design: 문맥을 두 가지 정보에 연결해야 답이 나오도록 했다. 하나는 기체가 금속에 닿는 곳에서만 반응한다는 점이고, 다른 하나는 적은 금속으로 많은 배기가스를 처리한다는 점이다. 오답 C와 D는 공학적으로 그럴듯해서 비교해 봐야만 배제된다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Osmotic power salinity gradient exploitation and membrane potential difference in pressure-retarded osmosis energy generation

g.passage: Pressure-retarded osmosis (PRO) generates electricity where river water meets the sea: fresh water flows through a semipermeable membrane toward the saltier side, raising its pressure enough to spin a turbine. Early pilot plants, however, produced far less power than theory predicted, because salt gradually leaked backward through the membranes and built up inside their support layers. Engineers note that this buildup does not halt the process outright; rather, it ______ the very salinity difference that drives water across the membrane, so output declines steadily instead of stopping all at once.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 염분 축적이 공정을 완전히 멈추게 하지는 않고 출력이 '갑자기 멈추지 않고 꾸준히' 줄어든다고 말하므로, 염도 차이를 점진적으로 약화시킨다는 B "erodes"가 정답이다. A "reverses"는 염분이 역류한다는 내용과 연결되어 그럴듯하지만, 염도 차이 자체가 뒤집히면 물의 흐름이 반대가 되어 '꾸준한 감소'와 맞지 않는다. D "eliminates"는 차이를 줄인다는 방향은 맞지만 완전히 없앤다는 뜻이어서 '공정을 멈추지 않는다'는 내용과 충돌한다. C "conceals"는 차이를 숨긴다는 뜻으로, 실제 물리적 감소와 출력 하락을 설명하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the salt buildup doesn't stop the process outright and that output falls steadily rather than all at once, so the buildup must wear down the salinity difference gradually. That makes B, "erodes," the answer. A, "reverses," might seem to fit because the salt leaks backward, but if the gradient itself were reversed, the water would flow the other way, and that wouldn't be a steady decline. D, "eliminates," points the right way, but it means the difference disappears completely, which contradicts the point that the process doesn't halt. C, "conceals," means hiding the difference, and that doesn't explain an actual physical drop in power.
g.design: "not halt outright"와 "steadily instead of all at once"라는 두 단서를 연결해야 점진적 약화를 고를 수 있게 했다. 방향은 맞지만 정도가 지나친 오답(eliminates)과 '역류'라는 표면 단서에 걸리는 오답(reverses)을 넣었다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Pneumatic artificial muscle nylon polymer contractility and compressed air actuation in biomimetic robotic appendages

g.passage: Engineers designing robotic hands often turn to pneumatic artificial muscles: braided nylon sleeves wrapped around rubber bladders. When compressed air fills the bladder, the sleeve widens and shortens, pulling on a tendon much as a biological muscle does. Early versions, however, were hard to control precisely, because the braid's fibers slid against one another and the muscle's pull varied from one inflation to the next. By coating the nylon fibers with a low-friction polymer, a team at a robotics lab made the muscle's response far more ______: the same air pressure now produced nearly the same contraction every time, allowing a robotic finger to grasp a grape without crushing it.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 초기 인공근육의 문제가 팽창할 때마다 당기는 힘이 달라진 것이었다고 말하고, 코팅 후에는 같은 공기압이 매번 거의 같은 수축을 낳았다고 설명한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 반복해도 같은 결과가 나온다는 뜻의 C가 와야 한다. A는 포도를 쥐는 장면과 연결돼 그럴듯하지만, 지문에서 개선된 점은 힘의 크기가 아니라 일정함이고, 오히려 힘이 세지면 포도가 으스러질 수 있다. B는 섬유끼리 미끄러지는 내용과 연결돼 보이지만, 핵심은 휘어지는 성질이 아니라 반응을 예측할 수 있다는 점이다. D는 반응 속도를 말하지만 지문에는 속도에 대한 근거가 없다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says the early muscles' problem was that their pull changed from one inflation to the next. After the coating, the same air pressure produced nearly the same contraction every time. So the blank needs a word meaning "repeatable," which is C. A might seem to fit because the finger grasps a grape, but the improvement described is steadiness, not strength, and more force could actually crush the grape. B connects to the sliding fibers, but the key point is that the response became predictable, not that the muscle bends more easily. D refers to speed, and nothing in the passage talks about how fast the muscle responds.
g.design: 빈칸 뒤 콜론 설명(같은 압력→같은 수축)과 앞의 문제(매번 다른 힘)를 연결해야 정답이 확정되도록 했다. 오답 A·B는 grasp와 sliding fibers에서 부분 근거를 얻어 비교가 필요하게 만들었다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Holographic display diffractive optical element and wavelength-specific light bending creating three-dimensional image projection

g.passage: Conventional lenses refract all visible light by roughly similar amounts, but the diffractive optical elements used in many holographic displays behave differently. Their microscopic ridges bend each wavelength at its own angle, so red, green, and blue light leaving the same element head in noticeably different directions. Engineers designing such displays therefore cannot treat color as an afterthought: unless the ridge spacing is tuned separately for each color channel, the three components of a projected image will ______, producing a three-dimensional figure fringed with misaligned bands of color.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 회절 소자가 파장마다 다른 각도로 빛을 꺾어 빨강·초록·파랑이 서로 다른 방향으로 간다고 설명하고, 그 결과 색 띠가 어긋난다고 말한다. 따라서 세 성분이 '서로 갈라진다'는 D가 정답이다. B는 빛의 경로를 다루는 단어라 그럴듯하지만, 한 점으로 모인다는 뜻이어서 어긋난 색 띠와 정반대다. A는 색이 강해진다는 뜻이고, C는 색이 약해진다는 뜻인데, 둘 다 밝기 변화를 말할 뿐 방향이 어긋나는 문제를 설명하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says diffractive elements bend each wavelength at a different angle, which sends red, green, and blue light in different directions, and the result is misaligned color bands. So the three components separate, which makes D correct. B sounds tempting because it also describes light paths, but it means coming together, the opposite of misalignment. A means getting stronger and C means getting weaker. Both describe changes in brightness, so neither explains why the colors end up pointing in different directions.
g.design: 빛의 경로를 다루는 오답(converge)과 밝기를 다루는 오답 두 개를 두었다. 정답을 고르려면 '파장마다 다른 각도'라는 정보와 '어긋난 색 띠'라는 결과를 연결해야 한다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Cryogenic energy storage liquid nitrogen phase-change utilization and latent heat capacity in thermal battery systems

g.passage: Most batteries store energy chemically, but engineers developing cryogenic energy storage rely on a physical process instead. When surplus electricity is available, air is cooled until it becomes a liquid and is kept in insulated tanks. Later, the liquid is allowed to warm and boil back into gas, and the rapid expansion drives a turbine. Because a great deal of heat must be absorbed before the liquid can change phase, engineers can ______ this property: by pairing the tanks with a store of material that holds the cold released during the cycle, they recover energy that would otherwise be lost and raise the system's overall efficiency.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 콜론 뒤 내용은 상변화에 필요한 큰 열 흡수라는 특성을 냉열 저장재와 함께 써서 에너지를 회수하고 효율을 높인다는 것이므로, 이 특성을 '이용한다'는 뜻의 A가 정답이다. B는 특성을 결함으로 보고 상쇄한다는 뜻인데, 지문에서는 이 특성이 효율을 높이는 이점으로 쓰인다. C는 계산에 반영하거나 설명한다는 뜻이라 그럴듯하지만, 특성을 적극적으로 활용해 이득을 얻는다는 콜론 뒤 내용을 정확히 담지 못한다. D는 문제로서 맞서 다룬다는 뜻이어서 긍정적인 결과와 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The part after the colon says engineers pair the tanks with a cold-storage material, recover energy, and raise efficiency. That means they actively use the large heat absorbed during the phase change to their advantage, so A is correct. B means offsetting a drawback, but the text treats this property as a benefit, not a flaw. C, meaning to factor in or explain, sounds possible, but it doesn't capture the idea of actively putting the property to use for a gain. D means struggling against a problem, which doesn't fit the positive outcome the text describes.
g.design: To answer, you have to link the property (large latent heat) to what the colon describes (energy recovery and higher efficiency). B and D each fit the idea that the heat is a "problem" in the first half of the sentence, and C sounds technically plausible, so you can only rule them out by reading the whole sentence to its end.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Cryogenic liquid nitrogen thermal storage and phase-change enthalpy recovery in grid-scale energy buffer systems

g.passage: Liquid air energy storage plants cool air until it condenses, store it in insulated tanks, and later let it boil and expand to drive turbines. Early prototypes wasted much of the cold released during that boiling, but engineers at one pilot facility in northern England captured it in beds of gravel and reused it to chill incoming air during the next charging cycle. This recovery did not eliminate the need for compressors and refrigeration, but it ______ the electricity they consumed, raising the plant's round-trip efficiency by roughly a third.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 재활용한 냉기가 압축기·냉동 장치를 없애지는 못했지만 효율을 높였다는 대조 구조이므로, 그 장치들이 쓰는 전력을 '줄였다'는 뜻의 B(curtailed)가 맞다. C(replaced)는 전력을 대체했다는 뜻이 되어 '필요를 없애지 못했다'는 앞 절과 충돌한다. D(redirected)는 냉기가 다른 곳에 쓰였다는 점과 표면적으로 연결되지만, 전력 사용 방향을 바꾼다고 효율이 오르는 것은 아니므로 감소라는 핵심을 놓친다. A(concealed)는 전력 소비를 숨겼다는 뜻으로, 실제 효율 향상과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence sets up a contrast: the recovered cold didn't remove the need for compressors and refrigeration, but it still raised efficiency. So the cold must have reduced the electricity those machines used, which makes B (curtailed) the answer. C (replaced) would mean the electricity was substituted entirely, and that clashes with the statement that the machines were still needed. D (redirected) might seem to fit because the cold was put to new use, but changing where electricity goes wouldn't raise efficiency, so it misses the idea of a reduction. A (concealed) means hiding the consumption, which doesn't match a real gain in efficiency.
g.design: "did not eliminate ... but"이라는 대조와 효율 상승을 함께 읽어야 '부분적 감소'가 도출되도록 했다. replaced와 redirected는 각각 '전력 절감'과 '냉기 재사용'에 부분적으로 기대고 있어, 비교해야만 배제된다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Holographic diffractive optical element wavelength selectivity and coherent light reconstruction in three-dimensional display projection

g.passage: Engineers designing holographic displays often rely on diffractive optical elements, thin films etched with microscopic interference patterns that bend incoming light to reconstruct a three-dimensional image. These elements are highly wavelength selective: a pattern recorded for green laser light diffracts green light efficiently but redirects red or blue light only weakly and at the wrong angles. For this reason, a display that must reproduce full color cannot simply ______ a single element; instead, designers stack separate layers, each tuned to one of the three laser wavelengths, so that every color is reconstructed in the correct position.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문에서 소자 하나는 한 파장만 효율적으로 회절시키므로, 풀컬러 디스플레이는 단일 소자에 '의존할' 수 없고 대신 여러 층을 쌓는다고 했다. 따라서 'instead'와 대조를 이루는 C가 정답이다. A는 보정이라는 공학적 맥락에 어울려 보이지만, 문제는 보정이 아니라 단일 소자로는 세 색을 감당할 수 없다는 점이다. B는 제작을 뜻하는데, 단일 소자를 만드는 것 자체가 불가능하다는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 빛과 관련되어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 단일 소자에 빛을 비추는 것 자체는 가능하며 지문이 문제 삼는 핵심이 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says each element diffracts only one wavelength efficiently, so a full-color display can't rely on a single element and instead stacks several layers. That contrast with "instead" makes C the answer. A sounds right in an engineering context, but the problem isn't adjusting the element; one element just can't handle three colors. B means making the element, and the passage never says a single element can't be made. D fits the topic of light, but shining light on one element is possible, and that isn't the problem the passage describes.
g.design: I placed related engineering verbs (A, B, D) as distractors so that a quick read seems to fit. Only by connecting the wavelength-selectivity clue to the contrast with "instead" does C become clear.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Pneumatic artificial muscle nylon fiber contractility and compressed air actuation mimicking biological muscle tissue mechanics

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- A McKibben actuator is a type of pneumatic artificial muscle first developed in the 1950s for use in orthotic devices.
- It consists of an inflatable rubber bladder surrounded by a sleeve of braided nylon fibers.
- When compressed air fills the bladder, the braided sleeve widens and shortens, pulling on whatever is attached to its ends.
- Biological muscle tissue also shortens and thickens as it contracts, which is why engineers say the actuator mimics muscle.
- Unlike biological muscle, which can shorten by roughly 40 percent of its resting length, a typical McKibben actuator shortens by only about 25 percent.
g.question: The student wants to point out a limitation of the device relative to the tissue it imitates. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Like biological muscle tissue, a McKibben actuator shortens and thickens as it contracts, pulling on whatever is attached to its ends.
A McKibben actuator, first developed in the 1950s for orthotic devices, shortens by about 25 percent when compressed air fills its rubber bladder.
Because its braided nylon sleeve widens and shortens when air fills the bladder, a McKibben actuator behaves much as biological muscle tissue does.
Although a McKibben actuator contracts in a musclelike way, it shortens by only about 25 percent of its length, whereas biological muscle can shorten by roughly 40 percent.
g.explanation: 목표는 이 장치가 모방하는 생체 근육보다 못한 점(한계)을 지적하는 것이다. D는 액추에이터의 수축률(약 25%)과 생체 근육의 수축률(약 40%)을 대비해 한계를 분명히 보여 준다. A와 C는 정확한 메모를 쓰지만 둘의 유사점만 강조해 한계를 드러내지 못한다. B는 25%라는 수치를 언급하지만 근육의 40%와 비교하지 않아 그것이 한계인지 알 수 없다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to show a way the device falls short of the muscle tissue it copies. D does this by contrasting the actuator's roughly 25 percent shortening with muscle's roughly 40 percent. A and C use accurate notes but only point out similarities, so they don't show any limitation. B gives the 25 percent figure but never compares it with muscle, so you can't tell from that sentence that it's a shortcoming.
g.design: To get it right, you have to link two notes: the actuator's figure and the muscle's figure. B looks right if you skim because it includes the 25 percent figure but leaves out the comparison. A and C use accurate notes about similarities, so they miss the goal.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Catalytic converter platinum-palladium coating and nitrogen oxide reduction catalysis in automotive exhaust aftertreatment systems

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Gasoline engines produce nitrogen oxides (NOx), carbon monoxide (CO), and unburned hydrocarbons as exhaust pollutants.
- A three-way catalytic converter contains a ceramic honeycomb coated with precious metals.
- In the coating, platinum and palladium mainly speed up oxidation, turning CO and hydrocarbons into carbon dioxide and water.
- Rhodium, a third metal in the coating, mainly speeds up reduction, splitting NOx into nitrogen and oxygen.
- Rhodium's reduction of NOx works best when the engine burns fuel and air at a nearly exact chemical balance.
g.question: The student wants to contrast the jobs that different metals perform inside a catalytic converter. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Whereas platinum and palladium mainly oxidize CO and hydrocarbons into carbon dioxide and water, rhodium mainly reduces NOx into nitrogen and oxygen.
Whereas gasoline engines emit NOx, CO, and hydrocarbons, a three-way catalytic converter uses a ceramic honeycomb coated with precious metals.
Whereas rhodium reduces NOx into nitrogen and oxygen, it works best when the engine burns fuel and air at a nearly exact chemical balance.
Whereas platinum and palladium are precious metals in the coating, they mainly speed up oxidation of CO and hydrocarbons into carbon dioxide and water.
g.explanation: 목표는 서로 다른 금속이 맡는 역할을 대조하는 것이다. A는 백금·팔라듐의 산화 기능과 로듐의 환원 기능을 나란히 놓아 두 금속군의 역할을 정확히 대조한다. B는 엔진 배출물과 변환기 구조를 연결할 뿐 금속별 역할을 비교하지 않는다. C는 로듐 하나의 기능과 작동 조건만 다루므로 다른 금속과의 대조가 없다. D는 백금·팔라듐만 설명하고 로듐과의 대조가 빠져 있다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to contrast the jobs that different metals do. A sets platinum and palladium's oxidation of CO and hydrocarbons against rhodium's reduction of NOx, so it contrasts two groups of metals directly. B links the engine's pollutants to the converter's structure but never compares what the metals do. C deals only with rhodium, covering its function and the conditions it needs, so there's no second metal to contrast it with. D describes only platinum and palladium and leaves rhodium out, so it doesn't contrast anything.
g.design: All four choices share the same "Whereas…" contrast frame and use accurate notes. Only A contrasts two different metals' roles, so you must check what each choice actually compares instead of just spotting the contrast word.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Osmotic power pressure-retarded osmosis and salinity gradient exploitation for renewable hydroelectric-alternative energy generation

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Osmotic power generates electricity from the difference in salt concentration between freshwater and seawater.
- In pressure-retarded osmosis (PRO), freshwater passes through a semipermeable membrane into pressurized seawater, increasing the volume on the seawater side.
- The added volume of pressurized water is then used to spin a turbine.
- Unlike solar and wind power, osmotic power can run continuously, regardless of weather or time of day.
- In 2009, the Norwegian company Statkraft opened the world's first PRO prototype plant in Tofte, Norway.
- The Tofte plant was shut down in 2013 because its membranes produced too little power per square meter to be commercially viable.
g.question: The student wants to present an advantage of osmotic power while also acknowledging an obstacle to its adoption. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Osmotic power, which can run continuously regardless of weather, was first tested at a prototype plant that Statkraft opened in Tofte, Norway, in 2009.
Although osmotic power can run continuously regardless of weather, the Tofte prototype closed because its membranes yielded too little power per square meter to be commercially viable.
Although the Tofte prototype closed in 2013, osmotic power uses the salt difference between freshwater and seawater, pushing freshwater through a membrane to spin a turbine.
Because freshwater passes through a membrane into pressurized seawater, osmotic power adds volume that spins a turbine, an approach first tested in Norway in 2009.
g.explanation: 목표는 삼투 발전의 장점과 보급을 막는 장애물을 함께 제시하는 것이다. B는 날씨와 상관없이 계속 가동된다는 장점과, 막의 출력이 낮아 상업성이 없었다는 장애물을 함께 담아 목표를 이룬다. A는 장점은 말하지만 장애물 대신 시범 발전소가 문을 연 사실만 덧붙인다. C는 발전소 폐쇄는 언급하지만 그 원인이 빠져 있고, 뒤따르는 내용도 장점이 아닌 작동 원리이다. D는 작동 원리와 역사만 설명할 뿐 장점도 장애물도 제시하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to present an advantage of osmotic power and also an obstacle to its adoption. B does both: it gives the advantage (the plant can run continuously regardless of weather) and the obstacle (the membranes produced too little power to be commercially viable). A states the advantage, but instead of an obstacle it only adds that a prototype plant opened. C mentions that the plant closed but leaves out why, and the rest of the sentence explains how the process works rather than giving an advantage. D only covers how the process works and its history, so it gives neither an advantage nor an obstacle.
g.design: To answer, students have to link the continuous-operation note to the note on why the plant closed. A and C each use part of the goal, so they look partly right. D is an accurate sentence that is off-goal. Every option uses the same sentence frame.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Tribological plasma vapor deposition coating and adhesion enhancement reducing tool wear in metal machining operations

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Cutting tools used in metal machining wear down from friction and heat at the point where the tool meets the workpiece.
- Physical vapor deposition (PVD) is a process in which a hard material, such as titanium aluminum nitride, is vaporized in a vacuum chamber and condensed onto a tool as a thin film.
- Plasma-assisted PVD bombards the tool surface with ionized gas before and during coating, which cleans the surface and helps the film bond more tightly.
- In a 2019 trial, uncoated carbide drills lasted an average of 410 holes in hardened steel before needing replacement.
- Identical drills given a plasma-assisted PVD coating lasted an average of 1,150 holes under the same conditions.
g.question: The student wants to emphasize how much the treatment affected the drills' service life. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In plasma-assisted PVD, ionized gas strikes the tool surface before and during coating, cleaning it so that the titanium aluminum nitride film bonds more tightly.
In a 2019 trial, carbide drills given a plasma-assisted PVD coating lasted an average of 1,150 holes in hardened steel before needing replacement.
In a 2019 trial, drills with a plasma-assisted PVD coating lasted an average of 1,150 holes in hardened steel, nearly triple the 410 holes managed by identical uncoated drills.
In a 2019 trial, uncoated carbide drills, which wear down from friction and heat, lasted an average of 410 holes in hardened steel before needing replacement.
g.explanation: 목표는 처리(코팅)가 드릴 수명에 미친 영향의 크기를 강조하는 것이므로, 코팅된 드릴과 코팅되지 않은 드릴의 수치를 함께 비교해야 한다. C는 1,150개와 410개를 나란히 제시하고 '거의 세 배'라고 차이를 밝혀 목표를 달성한다. A는 코팅이 더 잘 붙는 원리를 설명할 뿐 수명 변화는 보여주지 않는다. B는 코팅된 드릴의 수치만 있어 비교 기준이 없으므로 영향의 크기를 알 수 없다. D는 코팅되지 않은 드릴의 수치만 제시해 처리의 효과를 보여주지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to emphasize how much the coating changed the drills' service life, so you need both numbers side by side. C does this: it gives 1,150 holes against 410 holes and describes the gap as nearly triple. A explains how the plasma helps the coating bond, but it says nothing about how long the drills lasted. B gives only the coated drills' result, so there's nothing to compare it with, and you can't tell how big the effect was. D gives only the uncoated drills' result, so it doesn't show what the treatment did.
g.design: B와 D는 실험 수치를 정확히 쓰지만 한쪽 수치만 담아서, 두 수치를 비교해야 하는 목표를 채우지 못한다. 질문에 'coating'이나 'triple' 같은 말을 쓰지 않아 정답이 질문과 표면적으로 겹치지 않게 했다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Flexoelectric effect mechanical bending strain and electric polarization in ultrathin polymer piezoelectric sensor devices

g.passage: Flexoelectricity is the generation of electric polarization by a strain gradient, as when a material is bent so that one surface is stretched while the opposite surface is compressed. Unlike ordinary piezoelectricity, which responds to uniform strain, flexoelectric output depends on how sharply strain changes across a material's thickness, and because bending a thinner film produces a steeper gradient, the effect should grow stronger as films get thinner. Materials engineer Hana Okafor and colleagues built bending sensors from ultrathin films of a polymer that is only weakly piezoelectric. They argue that in their thinnest films, the voltage the sensors produce comes mainly from flexoelectricity rather than from the polymer's piezoelectric response.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor and colleagues' argument?
options: Under the same bending, the sensors' voltage output stayed roughly the same whether the films were 500 nanometers or 50 nanometers thick.
When the films were stretched uniformly along their length without being bent, the sensors produced a small but measurable voltage.
Sensors made from a strongly piezoelectric ceramic produced more voltage under bending than the polymer sensors did at every film thickness tested.

As film thickness was reduced from 500 nanometers to 50 nanometers under the same bending, voltage output per unit of applied bending rose sharply, while output under uniform stretching stayed nearly constant.
g.explanation: 이 주장은 가장 얇은 필름에서 나오는 전압이 주로 압전 효과가 아니라 굴곡 전기(flexoelectricity)에서 온다는 것이다. 굴곡 전기는 변형 기울기에 반응하므로 필름이 얇아질수록 강해져야 하고, 균일한 변형에 반응하는 압전 효과는 두께와 상관없이 비슷해야 한다. D는 굽힘에 대한 출력은 두께가 줄수록 크게 늘었지만 균일 인장에 대한 출력은 거의 그대로였음을 보여 주므로, 늘어난 출력이 굴곡 전기에서 왔다는 것을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 두께에 따라 출력이 변하지 않았다는 결과이므로 오히려 주장을 약화한다. B는 압전 반응이 존재한다는 것만 보여 줄 뿐 어느 효과가 주도하는지는 알려 주지 않고, C는 이 고분자 안에서 두 효과를 비교하지 않으므로 관련이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The claim is that in the thinnest films, the voltage comes mainly from flexoelectricity rather than piezoelectricity. Flexoelectricity responds to strain gradients, so it should get stronger as films get thinner. Piezoelectricity responds to uniform strain, so it should stay about the same at any thickness. D shows that the bending output rose sharply as the films got thinner while the output from uniform stretching barely changed, which points directly to flexoelectricity as the source of the extra voltage. A actually weakens the claim, since the output didn't change with thickness. B only shows that some piezoelectric response exists, not which effect dominates. C compares the polymer to a different material, so it says nothing about the two effects inside the polymer.
g.design: 학생은 두 정보를 연결해야 한다. 두께가 줄면 굴곡 전기가 커진다는 점과, 균일 인장으로 압전 효과를 따로 분리해 볼 수 있다는 점이다. 오답 B와 C는 그럴듯한 관련 데이터를 담고 있어서 꼼꼼히 비교해야 배제된다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Thermoelectric Seebeck module temperature gradient conversion and semiconductor junction voltage generation for waste heat recovery

g.passage: Thermoelectric generators convert heat directly into electricity through the Seebeck effect: when one side of a semiconductor junction is hotter than the other, charge carriers drift from the hot side toward the cold side, producing a voltage. Engineers have proposed attaching such modules to factory exhaust pipes to recover waste heat. Materials scientist Lena Okafor argues, however, that in many industrial installations the main limit on power output is not the semiconductor material itself but the heat sink on the cold side. Because heat flows through the module continuously, she contends, a poorly cooled cold side warms up until the temperature difference across the junction shrinks, and the voltage falls with it.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's claim?
options: When identical modules on the same exhaust pipe were fitted with larger fins on the side away from the pipe, the gap in temperature between their two faces grew and their power output rose substantially.
When modules made of a newer semiconductor alloy replaced older modules on the same exhaust pipe, their power output rose substantially even though the cooling hardware was unchanged.
When identical modules were placed on exhaust pipes carrying hotter gas, the temperature of the face touching the pipe rose and the modules produced more voltage than those on cooler pipes.
When identical modules on the same exhaust pipe were fitted with larger fins on the side away from the pipe, the factory's overall energy costs declined over the following year.
g.design: 정답은 '냉각 측 개선→온도차 증가→출력 증가'의 인과 고리를 모두 보여야 하며, 오답 B는 재료 쪽 개선으로 주장을 약화, C는 온도차-전압 관계만 확인할 뿐 냉각 측과 무관, D는 같은 개입이지만 결과 지표가 모호하다.
g.explanation: Okafor는 출력의 주된 한계가 반도체 재료가 아니라 냉각 측 방열에 있다고 주장한다. A는 같은 모듈에서 냉각 측 방열만 개선했더니 온도차가 커지고 출력이 늘었다는 것으로, 주장의 인과 고리 전체를 직접 뒷받침한다. B는 재료를 바꿔 출력이 늘었다는 것이므로 오히려 재료가 한계라는 쪽을 시사해 주장을 약화한다. C는 온도차가 클수록 전압이 높다는 일반 원리만 보여 줄 뿐 냉각 측이 한계라는 점과는 관련이 없다. D는 같은 개입이지만 공장 전체 에너지 비용은 다른 요인에도 좌우되므로 모듈 출력이나 온도차에 관해 직접 알려 주지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Okafor claims that the main limit on output is the cold-side heat sink, not the semiconductor material. Choice A changes only the cooling on identical modules and shows that the temperature difference grew and power rose, which confirms every link in her reasoning. Choice B shows that changing the material raised output, which suggests the material is the limit, so it actually weakens her claim. Choice C only confirms the general rule that a bigger temperature difference gives more voltage; it says nothing about the cold side being the bottleneck. Choice D uses the same fix, but a factory's overall energy costs depend on many other factors, so it tells you nothing direct about the modules' output or temperature difference.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: technology and engineering — Nanocellulose fiber reinforcement and biodegradable polymer matrix composites in sustainable food packaging applications

g.passage: Polylactic acid (PLA) is a biodegradable plastic made from plant starch, and food companies have tested it as a replacement for petroleum-based packaging. One problem is that pure PLA film lets oxygen pass through it fairly easily, and oxygen causes packaged foods such as nuts and cheese to spoil faster. Engineers at a materials lab added tiny nanocellulose fibers, made from wood pulp, to PLA film. In tests, the reinforced film allowed about 60 percent less oxygen to pass through than pure PLA film of the same thickness. These results suggest that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: nanocellulose fibers would make PLA film break down more slowly once it is thrown away.
nanocellulose fibers could help PLA packaging keep certain foods fresh for a longer time.
nanocellulose fibers would make PLA film cheaper to produce than petroleum-based film.
nanocellulose fibers could allow PLA packaging to be made from materials other than plant starch.
g.explanation: 지문은 산소가 음식을 빨리 상하게 하고, 나노셀룰로스를 넣은 필름이 산소 투과를 약 60% 줄였다고 말한다. 따라서 이 필름이 음식을 더 오래 신선하게 유지할 수 있다는 B가 자연스러운 결론이다. A는 분해 속도에 대한 정보가 지문에 없다. C는 비용을 전혀 다루지 않으며, D는 PLA의 원료를 바꾸는 것이 아니라 섬유를 첨가한 것일 뿐이므로 근거가 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text tells you that oxygen makes foods spoil faster and that the nanocellulose-reinforced film let about 60 percent less oxygen through. Putting those two facts together, the film should help keep foods fresh longer, so B is correct. A is wrong because the text says nothing about how fast the film breaks down. C is wrong because cost is never discussed, and D is wrong because the fibers were added to PLA, not used to replace the plant starch it is made from.
g.design: 추론 한 단계짜리 문제: 산소가 있으면 음식이 상하고, 섬유를 넣으면 산소가 덜 통한다는 두 사실을 연결하면 된다. 오답은 모두 같은 문장 틀을 쓰되, 지문이 다루지 않는 성질(분해 속도, 비용, 원료)을 끌어들인다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: technology and engineering — Chromogenic photochromic smart glass and light-triggered opacity transition reducing solar heat gain through building fenestration

g.passage: Photochromic smart glass contains special molecules that change shape when struck by ultraviolet light. When the sun is bright, these molecules darken the glass, blocking much of the sunlight that would otherwise pass through a window and warm the room. When the sun goes down or clouds cover it, the molecules return to their original shape and the glass becomes clear again. Engineers testing the glass in an office building found that rooms with photochromic windows stayed noticeably cooler on sunny afternoons than identical rooms with ordinary windows. Because air conditioners must work harder when sunlight heats a room, these results suggest that installing photochromic windows ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: would make rooms darker at night than ordinary windows do.
would raise the amount of heat that enters a building on cloudy days.
could lower the energy a building uses for cooling on sunny days.
could stop ultraviolet light from changing the molecules in the glass.
g.explanation: 지문은 해가 강할 때 유리가 어두워져 방이 더 시원했고, 햇빛이 방을 데우면 에어컨이 더 많이 일해야 한다고 말한다. 따라서 이 창문은 맑은 날 냉방에 드는 에너지를 줄일 수 있다는 C가 정답이다. A는 틀렸다. 밤에는 유리가 다시 투명해지므로 일반 창문보다 더 어둡게 만들지 않는다. B는 흐린 날 유리가 투명해진다는 사실을 열이 더 들어온다는 뜻으로 잘못 확대한 것이다. D는 자외선이 분자의 모양을 바꾸는 것이 유리의 작동 원리라는 지문 내용과 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the glass darkens in bright sun, which kept rooms cooler, and that air conditioners must work harder when sunlight heats a room. Putting these together, the windows could lower the energy used for cooling on sunny days, so C is correct. A is wrong because the glass turns clear again at night, so it wouldn't make rooms darker than ordinary windows. B misreads the fact that the glass is clear on cloudy days as meaning more heat gets in, which the text never says. D contradicts the text, because ultraviolet light changing the molecules is exactly how the glass works.
g.design: 추론 한 단계(냉각 효과 + 냉방 부담 → 에너지 절감)로 풀리는 easy 문항이다. 오답은 지문에 나온 세부 내용(밤, 흐린 날, 자외선)을 잘못 적용한 흔한 오개념으로 만들었다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: technology and engineering — Magnetostrictive material stress-induced magnetic field alteration enabling ferromagnetic bridge structural health monitoring sensors

g.passage:
Text 1
Engineers have long relied on strain gauges glued to steel bridge girders to detect dangerous loads. Researchers now propose exploiting magnetostriction instead: when a ferromagnetic material such as structural steel is stressed, its internal magnetic domains shift, measurably altering the field around it. Because the girder itself becomes the sensor, proponents argue, bridges could be monitored continuously without attaching fragile gauges that peel or corrode, making the approach ready to replace conventional methods on existing spans.

Text 2
Field trials of magnetostrictive monitoring on older steel bridges have produced encouraging but uneven results. The magnetic signal does track stress, yet it also drifts with temperature and with the steel's prior loading history, so identical stresses can yield different readings on cold and warm days or before and after a heavy truck passes. Until engineers can separate these influences, the method is best treated as a supplement to established gauges rather than a substitute for them.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the proponents' conclusion described in Text 1?
options: By rejecting it, since field trials showed that the magnetic properties of steel do not change in response to stress.
By endorsing it, since field trials confirmed that the girder can serve as its own sensor in all weather conditions.
By questioning it, since attaching magnetic sensors to girders would be as fragile and prone to corrosion as using strain gauges.
By questioning it, since factors other than stress also affect the magnetic signal, making the method unreliable as a standalone replacement.
g.design: 두 텍스트를 연결해 Text 1의 '대체 가능' 결론과 Text 2의 '보완으로만' 입장을 대조하게 했고, A·C는 '반박/의문'이라는 방향은 맞지만 근거가 틀린 부분적 오답으로, B는 '고무적'이라는 표현을 훑어 읽은 경우를 노린 오답으로 설계했다.
g.explanation: Text 2는 자기 신호가 응력을 반영하긴 하지만 온도와 하중 이력에 따라서도 변한다고 지적하며, 이 방법을 기존 게이지의 대체가 아닌 보완으로 써야 한다고 말한다. 따라서 Text 1의 '대체할 준비가 됐다'는 결론에 의문을 제기할 것이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 신호가 응력을 '추적한다'고 인정한 내용과 모순된다. B는 Text 2가 결과를 '고르지 않다'고 했고 날씨에 따른 변동을 문제 삼았으므로 틀렸다. C는 반응 방향은 맞지만, 부착 센서가 약하다는 근거는 Text 2에 없다.
g.explanation_en: Text 2 admits that the magnetic signal tracks stress, but it points out that the signal also shifts with temperature and with the steel's loading history. That's why the author says the method should supplement established gauges, not replace them. So the author would question Text 1's claim that the method is ready to replace conventional methods, which makes D correct. A is wrong because it contradicts Text 2's statement that the signal does track stress. B is wrong because Text 2 calls the results uneven and points to readings that change between cold and warm days. C gets the reaction right, but Text 2 never says the sensors are fragile or likely to corrode.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Ionic liquid electrolyte wide electrochemical stability window and temperature-independent conductivity in solid-state battery development

g.passage:
Text 1
Battery engineers have grown enthusiastic about ionic liquids—salts that remain liquid near room temperature—as electrolytes for next-generation cells. Their wide electrochemical stability window means they resist breaking down even at high voltages, allowing pairing with energy-dense electrodes. Proponents also claim their conductivity stays essentially constant across temperatures, so a battery using them would perform as well on a frozen morning as on a summer afternoon.

Text 2
Materials chemist Ines Varga agrees that ionic liquids tolerate high voltages far better than conventional carbonate electrolytes, a genuine advantage for solid-state hybrid designs. Her measurements, however, tell a different story about cold conditions. Because ionic liquids are highly viscous, their ion mobility falls sharply as temperature drops; in her test cells, conductivity at −10°C was less than a fifth of its value at 25°C.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Varga (Text 2) most likely respond to the proponents' claims described in Text 1?
options: She would accept their point about resistance to breakdown at high voltage but dispute their assertion about performance in the cold.
She would accept their assertion about performance in the cold but dispute their point about resistance to breakdown at high voltage.
She would accept both of their claims but argue that viscosity makes ionic liquids too costly to manufacture.
She would dispute both of their claims, arguing that carbonate electrolytes outperform ionic liquids in every condition.
g.explanation: Text 1의 지지자들은 두 가지를 주장한다. 고전압에서 잘 분해되지 않는다는 점과 전도도가 온도에 거의 영향을 받지 않는다는 점이다. Varga는 첫째 주장(고전압 내성)에는 동의하지만, 측정 결과 −10°C에서 전도도가 5분의 1 미만으로 떨어졌으므로 둘째 주장은 반박한다. 따라서 정답은 A이다. B는 동의하는 주장과 반박하는 주장을 뒤바꿨고, C는 저온 성능 반박을 놓친 채 지문에 없는 비용 문제를 끌어왔으며, D는 Varga가 고전압 측면에서 이온성 액체가 낫다고 인정한 점과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: The proponents in Text 1 make two claims: ionic liquids resist breakdown at high voltage, and their conductivity barely changes with temperature. Varga agrees with the first claim, but her measurements show conductivity at −10°C falling below a fifth of its 25°C value, so she disputes the second. That makes A the answer. B flips which claim she accepts and which she disputes. C misses her objection about cold performance and brings in a cost issue that neither text mentions. D contradicts her statement that ionic liquids handle high voltages better than carbonate electrolytes.
g.design: To answer, students have to pull apart the two claims in Text 1 and work out Varga's stance on each one. B uses the same sentence frame with the stances reversed, which catches students who skim, and C and D each start from something partly true in Text 2.
